questionEn: Which Surah contains the primary Qur'anic verse detailing the obligatory steps of Wudu and Tayammum?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah
Surah Al-Ma'idah
Surah An-Nur
Surah Al-Muzzammil
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:6) commands believers to wash the face, hands up to the elbows, wipe the head, and wash the feet up to the ankles when rising for prayer.

questionEn: According to the Hadith of the Prophet ﷺ, what fraction of faith (Iman) is purification (Taharah)?
optionsEn: One-third of faith
Half of faith
One-quarter of faith
All of faith
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ stated: 'Purification is half of faith (At-tuhuru shatrul-iman),' highlighting the foundational role of cleanliness in a believer's life.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ describe as the 'key to Salah'?
optionsEn: Facing the Qiblah
Reciting Al-Fatihah
Purification (Taharah)
The Adhan
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The key to prayer is purification; its consecration (opening) is Takbir, and its conclusion is Taslim.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:6, up to which anatomical landmark must the arms be washed during Wudu?
optionsEn: The wrists
The mid-forearms
The shoulders
The elbows
explanationEn: Allah commands washing the hands and arms 'ila al-marafiq' (up to and including the elbows), and the Prophet ﷺ consistently washed past his elbows.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:6, up to which point must the feet be washed during Wudu?
optionsEn: The mid-shins
The ankles (ka'bayn)
The toes only
The knees
explanationEn: The Qur'an specifies washing the feet 'ila al-ka'bayn' (up to and including the two ankle bones on each foot).

questionEn: What warning did the Prophet ﷺ give upon seeing companions leave dry spots on the backs of their heels during Wudu?
optionsEn: Repeat only the feet
Woe to the heels from the Fire
Their prayer is merely disliked
Wipe them with dust
explanationEn: He ﷺ called out loudly twice or thrice: 'Woe to the heels from the Hellfire!' emphasizing thorough washing of the entire foot including the heels.

questionEn: Which phrase is recommended to utter before beginning Wudu?
optionsEn: Alhamdulillah
SubhanAllah
Bismillah
Allahu Akbar
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught: 'There is no complete Wudu for one who does not mention the name of Allah (say Bismillah) over it.'

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ refrain from making the Miswak obligatory before every Salah?
optionsEn: Miswak wood was scarce
It was only for Ramadan
Water alone suffices
Out of fear of causing hardship to his Ummah
explanationEn: He ﷺ said: 'Were it not that I might overburden my Ummah, I would have commanded them to use the Siwak with every Wudu (or every prayer).'

questionEn: What is the maximum number of times each limb may be washed in a single Wudu according to the Sunnah?
optionsEn: Five times
Three times
Seven times
Four times
explanationEn: After demonstrating Wudu by washing each limb three times, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever adds to this has done wrong, transgressed, and acted unjustly.'

questionEn: Which companion narrated the detailed Hadith showing the Prophet ﷺ performed Wudu washing each limb once, twice, and three times on different occasions?
optionsEn: Bilal ibn Rabah (RA)
Abdullah ibn Zayd / Ibn Abbas / Uthman (RA)
Salman al-Farisi (RA)
Abu Dharr (RA)
explanationEn: Sahih al-Bukhari records narrations from Ibn Abbas (once), Abdullah ibn Zayd (twice), and Uthman ibn Affan (three times), proving one wash is obligatory and three is complete Sunnah.

questionEn: What is the Arabic term for rinsing the mouth with water during Wudu?
optionsEn: Istinshaq
Istinthar
Madmadah
Mas'h
explanationEn: Madmadah is swirling water inside the mouth and spitting it out, whereas Istinshaq is drawing water into the nostrils.

questionEn: What is the Arabic term for blowing water out of the nose after drawing it in during Wudu?
optionsEn: Madmadah
Tathlith
Takhlil
Istinthar
explanationEn: Drawing water into the nose is Istinshaq, and expelling it with a gentle blow using the left hand is called Istinthar.

questionEn: What special instruction did the Prophet ﷺ give to Laqit ibn Sabirah regarding Istinshaq when one is fasting?
optionsEn: Skip rinsing the nose altogether while fasting
Do not sniff water too deeply while fasting
Use warm water only while fasting
Sniff water seven times while fasting
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told him: 'Perform Wudu thoroughly, run water between the fingers, and draw water deeply into the nose—unless you are fasting.'

questionEn: What is 'Takhlil al-Asabi' in the context of Wudu?
optionsEn: Drying the fingers with a cloth
Interlacing and washing between the fingers and toes
Trimming the nails before prayer
Removing rings only during Ghusl
explanationEn: Takhlil al-Asabi' is running water and fingers between the fingers and toes (often using the little finger for the toes) to ensure water reaches all skin.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ wipe his head during Wudu according to the Hadith of Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA)?
optionsEn: From the back to the front only
Only over the forehead
Starting from the front of the head to the nape of the neck, then returning to the front
Wiping only the right side of the head
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Zayd narrated that the Prophet ﷺ passed both wet hands from the front hairline to the nape of his neck and brought them back to where he started.

questionEn: How many times did the Prophet ﷺ wipe his head in the standard narration of his Wudu?
optionsEn: Three times with fresh water each time
Twice
Seven times
Once
explanationEn: In the authentic descriptions of the Prophet's ﷺ Wudu (such as Uthman's and Ali's narrations), the head is wiped once, unlike the washed limbs which are washed up to three times.

questionEn: According to the Hadith of Ibn Abbas (RA), what did the Prophet ﷺ do regarding his ears during Wudu?
optionsEn: Wiped them with a dry towel
Washed them three times with cupped handfuls
Skipped the ears completely
Wiped inside the ears with his forefingers and behind them with his thumbs
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ wiped the inside folds of his ears with his index fingers and the outer backs of his ears with his thumbs.

questionEn: Which famous statement explains why the ears are wiped using the same wetness as the head (according to several schools)?
optionsEn: The ears are part of the face
The ears are part of the head (Al-udhunani min ar-ra's)
The ears require separate Ghusl
The ears are washed like the arms
explanationEn: The narration 'Al-udhunani min ar-ra's' ('The two ears are part of the head') underpins the practice of wiping the ears immediately after wiping the head.
reference: Sunan Ibn Majah 443; Sunan Abi Dawud 134

questionEn: Which hand or foot did the Prophet ﷺ love to begin with when performing Wudu and putting on sandals?
optionsEn: The left
Either randomly
The right (Tayammun)
Both simultaneously
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ loved starting from the right in purifying himself, combing his hair, putting on his sandals, and in all his affairs.

questionEn: Approximately how much water did the Prophet ﷺ typically use for a complete Wudu?
optionsEn: One Sa' (about 2.5–3 liters)
Ten liters
A full bucket
One Mudd (about two cupped handfuls / ~0.6–0.75 liters)
explanationEn: Anas (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ used to perform Wudu with one Mudd of water and Ghusl with one Sa' to five Mudds, modeling extreme conservation of water.

questionEn: Even when standing beside a flowing river, what did the Prophet ﷺ warn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) against during Wudu?
optionsEn: Speaking during Wudu
Using cold water
Washing the face first
Extravagance and wasting water (Israf)
explanationEn: When Sa'd asked if there can be wastefulness in Wudu, the Prophet ﷺ replied: 'Yes, even if you are beside a flowing river.'

questionEn: What spiritual reward is promised to the believer who recites the Shahadah after completing Wudu carefully?
optionsEn: A mansion in Firdaws immediately
All eight gates of Paradise are opened for them to enter whichever they wish
Exemption from voluntary fasting
Reward of 100 prayers
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ promised that whoever completes Wudu well and says 'Ash-hadu an la ilaha illallah wahdahu la sharika lah wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh' has all eight gates of Jannah opened for them.

questionEn: What additional supplication is recorded in Jami' at-Tirmidhi right after the Shahadah following Wudu?
optionsEn: Rabbi zidni ilma
HasbunAllahu wa ni'mal-wakil
Allahumma-j'alni minat-tawwabina waj'alni minal-mutatahhirin
SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi
explanationEn: The supplication asks Allah: 'O Allah, make me among those who constantly repent and make me among those who purify themselves.'

questionEn: What happens to a believer's minor sins as the water drips from their face, hands, and feet during Wudu?
optionsEn: They are postponed until Friday
They require Sadaqah to erase
Nothing changes until Salah starts
Every minor sin committed by those limbs is washed away with the water or last drop
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that when a Muslim washes their face, hands, and feet in Wudu, every sin looked at, grasped, or walked toward departs with the water or the last drop of water.

questionEn: How will the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ recognize his Ummah on the Day of Resurrection according to Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim?
optionsEn: By carrying prayer mats
By the color of their garments
By their native language
By the radiant light on their foreheads, hands, and feet from Wudu (Al-Ghurr al-Muhajjalun)
explanationEn: He ﷺ explained that his followers will be called 'Al-Ghurr al-Muhajjalun'—shining with radiant whiteness on their faces, arms, and feet from the traces of Wudu.

questionEn: What two-rak'ah prayer did Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) consistently offer that caused the Prophet ﷺ to hear his footsteps ahead of him in Paradise?
optionsEn: Two rak'ahs before Fajr only
Two rak'ahs immediately after every Wudu (Tahiyyat al-Wudu)
Two rak'ahs at sunset
Two rak'ahs inside the Hijr
explanationEn: Bilal (RA) explained that whenever he performed Wudu at any hour of day or night, he prayed as much as Allah decreed for him right afterward.

questionEn: What does 'Muwalah' (continuity) mean among the conditions or acts of Wudu?
optionsEn: Performing Wudu facing the Qiblah
Using warm water
Washing each limb consecutively without long pauses that let the previous limb dry in normal weather
Doing Wudu silently
explanationEn: Muwalah means performing the steps of Wudu in continuous succession without an undue interruption during which the previously washed limb would dry under moderate conditions.

questionEn: What does 'Tartib' refer to in Wudu?
optionsEn: Washing each limb three times
Drying the limbs afterward
Using a specific vessel
Performing the obligatory steps in the sequence mentioned in Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:6
explanationEn: Tartib is observing the Qur'anic order: face, then arms to elbows, then wiping the head, then washing the feet to the ankles.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Wudu with water-resistant nail polish or thick paint that prevents water from reaching the nail or skin?
optionsEn: Only Ghusl is affected, not Wudu
Wudu is valid if one wipes over it
Wudu is valid for travelers only
Wudu is invalid because water must reach the nail/skin underneath
explanationEn: Any impermeable barrier (like thick paint, wax, or standard waterproof nail polish) that blocks water from contacting the skin or nail invalidates Wudu unless removed.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim 243, what did the Prophet ﷺ command a man who left a dry spot the size of a fingernail on the top of his foot after Wudu?
optionsEn: Just wet that spot and pray
Go back and perform Wudu properly again
Perform Sujud al-Sahw
Wipe over the spot with sand
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ saw a dry spot the size of a dirham/fingernail on his foot and ordered him: 'Go back and perform your Wudu thoroughly.'

questionEn: Which action is universally agreed by scholars to nullify Wudu?
optionsEn: Trimming fingernails
Eating cooked lamb
Passing wind or any discharge from the two private passages
Looking at a non-Muslim
explanationEn: Anything exiting the front or rear private passages (urine, stool, wind, etc.) is a consensus nullifier of Wudu.

questionEn: If a person in prayer feels a slight sensation in their stomach and suspects they passed wind, what rule did the Prophet ﷺ establish?
optionsEn: Leave the prayer immediately to be safe
Repeat Wudu after finishing the rak'ah
Offer two prostrations of forgetfulness
Do not leave the prayer unless they hear a sound or detect an odor
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught: 'He should not leave [his prayer] unless he hears a sound or smells an odor,' establishing the fiqh principle that certainty is not overridden by doubt.

questionEn: According to authentic Hadith in Sahih Muslim, eating the meat of which animal specifically requires performing Wudu afterward?
optionsEn: Camel meat
Beef
Mutton
Fish
explanationEn: When asked if Wudu is required after eating mutton, the Prophet ﷺ said 'If you wish'; when asked about camel meat, he ﷺ said: 'Yes, perform Wudu after eating camel meat.'

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the ruling on Wudu after eating cooked food in general (as his final practice)?
optionsEn: It always breaks Wudu
It does not break Wudu; the Prophet ﷺ prayed after eating cooked mutton without renewing Wudu
It breaks Wudu only at night
It requires rinsing the mouth seven times
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated that the last of the two commands from the Prophet ﷺ was not performing Wudu after eating what was touched by fire (cooked food).

questionEn: Which type of sleep breaks Wudu according to the Prophetic Sunnah?
optionsEn: Closing one's eyes briefly while attentive
Blinking during Qiyam
Deep sleep in which consciousness is lost so one would not notice if wind passed
Resting one's head for five seconds while sitting upright and fully aware
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ explained: 'The eye is the drawstring of the rear passage; whoever sleeps must perform Wudu,' whereas light dozing while seated firmly without losing awareness did not break the Companions' Wudu.

questionEn: What happens to Wudu if a person laughs aloud (Qahqahah) during prayer according to the majority vs Hanafi school?
optionsEn: All schools say it breaks Wudu
No school says it invalidates Salah
Only silent smiling breaks Wudu
It invalidates Salah by consensus, and in the Hanafi school it also breaks Wudu
explanationEn: Laughing out loud invalidates prayer by scholarly consensus; the Hanafi school additionally holds that audible laughter inside Salah breaks Wudu based on mursal narrations.

questionEn: Does breast-feeding an infant or changing a baby's diaper without touching one's own private parts break the mother's Wudu?
optionsEn: No, neither breaks Wudu (though hands should be washed of impurity)
Yes, touching a baby always breaks Wudu
Only nursing a boy breaks Wudu
Only changing a diaper requires Ghusl
explanationEn: Breastfeeding or touching a child does not nullify Wudu; if impurity gets on the hands, washing the impurity off suffices without repeating Wudu.

questionEn: Which two fluids are distinguished in Hadith when Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) asked Miqdad (RA) to inquire about urethral discharge?
optionsEn: Blood and sweat
Madhy (pre-seminal fluid, requiring Wudu & washing) and Many (semen, requiring Ghusl)
Wady and water
Tears and saliva
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that Madhy (thin fluid from arousal) requires washing the private part and performing Wudu, whereas Many (semen) requires full Ghusl.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when asked if a person may touch the Qur'an (Mushaf) without Wudu?
optionsEn: No restriction exists
Only men need Wudu
None should touch the Qur'an except one who is pure (Tahir)
Wudu is only needed for Surah Al-Baqarah
explanationEn: In his letter to the people of Yemen via Amr ibn Hazm, the Prophet ﷺ wrote: 'None should touch the Qur'an except one who is pure,' echoing Surah Al-Waqi'ah 56:79.

questionEn: May a person who is in a state of minor impurity (without Wudu, not Janabah) recite the Qur'an from memory?
optionsEn: No, recitation from memory is strictly forbidden without Wudu
Only in Ramadan
Only after Tayammum
Yes, reciting from memory without touching the Mushaf is permissible
explanationEn: Scholars agree that someone without Wudu (minor ritual impurity) may recite Qur'an from memory and remember Allah freely; the Prophet ﷺ remembered Allah in all states.

questionEn: Which three obligatory acts require Wudu according to Islamic jurisprudence?
optionsEn: Salah, Tawaf around the Ka'bah, and touching the Mushaf
Fasting, Zakah, and Sadaqah
Dhikr, Dua, and entering a home
Giving Salam, eating, and sleeping
explanationEn: Wudu is required for Salah, Tawaf (which the Prophet ﷺ likened to Salah except speaking is permitted), and touching the physical Mushaf.

questionEn: How many prayers can a Muslim offer with a single Wudu as long as nothing invalidates it?
optionsEn: Only one prayer
As many prayers as they wish until Wudu is broken
Maximum two prayers
Only Fard prayers, not Sunnah
explanationEn: On the Day of the Conquest of Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ prayed all five daily prayers with a single Wudu, showing it was permissible.

questionEn: What reward did the Prophet ﷺ promise for renewing Wudu when one is already in a state of Wudu (Wudu 'ala Wudu)?
optionsEn: It is forbidden as a waste of water
It erases previous prayers
Ten good deeds (or 'Light upon Light') are recorded for them
It counts as an extra obligatory prayer
explanationEn: While not obligatory, renewing Wudu for a new prayer is praised in narrations as 'light upon light,' though one should still conserve water.

questionEn: What is the minimum obligation when someone wakes up from nighttime sleep before dipping their hand into a shared vessel of water?
optionsEn: Dip the right hand first
Use sand first
Perform Ghusl first
Wash both hands outside the vessel three times before dipping them in
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ commanded: 'When one of you wakes from sleep, let him not dip his hand into the vessel until he washes it three times, for he does not know where his hand spent the night.'

questionEn: What is the term for washing the private parts with water after relieving oneself?
optionsEn: Istinja'
Istijmar
Istikhdam
Istighfar
explanationEn: Istinja' refers to cleansing the private passages with pure water after urination or defecation, whereas Istijmar uses clean stones or dry absorbent materials.

questionEn: What minimum number of clean stones (or wipes) did the Prophet ﷺ prescribe when performing Istijmar without water?
optionsEn: One stone
At least three stones (and an odd number if more are needed)
Exactly seven stones
Two stones
explanationEn: Salman al-Farisi (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ forbade cleaning oneself with fewer than three stones, and taught that cleansing should end on an odd number.

questionEn: Which two materials did the Prophet ﷺ explicitly forbid using for Istijmar (dry cleansing)?
optionsEn: Leaves and wood
Pebbles and cloth
Animal dung (rawth) and bones
Sand and clay
explanationEn: He ﷺ forbade using dung because it is impure/filth, and bones because they are the food of our believing brothers among the Jinn.

questionEn: Which hand did the Prophet ﷺ forbid using to touch the private part during urination or to clean oneself after relieving oneself?
optionsEn: The left hand
Both hands
Either hand
The right hand
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ commanded: 'When any of you drinks, let him not breathe into the vessel; when he relieves himself, let him not touch his private part with his right hand nor clean himself with his right hand.'

questionEn: What dua is Sunnah to recite before entering the restroom (toilet)?
optionsEn: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika minal-khubuthi wal-khaba'ith
Ghufranak
Bismillahi tawakkaltu alAllah
Subhanaka Allahumma
explanationEn: Saying 'Bismillah, Allahumma inni a'udhu bika minal-khubuthi wal-khaba'ith' seeks Allah's protection from male and female devils.

questionEn: What concise word did the Prophet ﷺ say upon exiting the restroom?
optionsEn: Allahu Akbar
Ghufranak (Your forgiveness, O Allah)
Astaghfirullah al-Azim
Alhamdulillahi Rabbil-Alamin
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) narrated that whenever the Prophet ﷺ exited the restroom, he would say 'Ghufranak' ('I seek Your forgiveness').

questionEn: Which foot is Sunnah to step in with when entering the restroom, and which when exiting?
optionsEn: Right foot in, left foot out
Right foot for both
Left foot in, right foot out
Left foot for both
explanationEn: In Islamic etiquette, the right foot is favored for noble places like the Masjid, while the left foot enters the restroom first and the right foot exits first.

questionEn: In open spaces, what direction did the Prophet ﷺ forbid facing or turning one's back toward while relieving oneself?
optionsEn: East
North
West
The Qiblah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'When you go to relieve yourselves, neither face the Qiblah nor turn your backs to it; rather face east or west [for people in Madinah].'

questionEn: Why were the inhabitants of Quba' praised by Allah in Surah At-Tawbah 9:108 ('Men who love to purify themselves')?
optionsEn: They combined water with stones (or followed stones with water) for thorough cleansing
They built marble baths
They washed their clothes daily
They fasted every Monday
explanationEn: When asked why Allah praised their purification, the people of Quba' replied that they used water after relieving themselves.

questionEn: How does one purify a garment or surface contaminated by urine, according to the Hadith of the Bedouin who urinated in the Masjid?
optionsEn: Scrape it with a stick
Pour a bucket of water over it
Burn the garment
Wash it with soil seven times
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told his companions to leave the Bedouin until he finished, then commanded them to pour a bucket of water over the spot.

questionEn: What distinction did the Prophet ﷺ teach regarding purifying clothing touched by the urine of an exclusively breastfed infant?
optionsEn: Both boy and girl require seven washes
Neither needs any water
A baby girl's urine is washed, while a baby boy's urine (before solid food) is sprinkled with water
Both must be boiled
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The urine of a baby girl is washed, and the urine of a baby boy is sprinkled with water,' provided the boy has not yet begun eating solid food.

questionEn: How must a vessel licked by a dog be purified according to Sahih Muslim?
optionsEn: Rinse once with warm water
Wipe with a dry cloth
Wash three times with soap
Wash it seven times, the first (or one) of them with earth/soil
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ stated: 'The purification of the vessel of one of you, if a dog licks it, is to wash it seven times, the first of them with dirt/earth.'

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about a cat drinking from a water vessel?
optionsEn: It is not impure; cats are among those who go around among you
It must be washed seven times
It must be thrown away
Only the top layer is impure
explanationEn: When Kabshah bint Ka'b held a vessel for Abu Qatadah while a cat drank from it, he cited the Prophet ﷺ: 'It is not najis (impure); it is one of those that go around among you.'

questionEn: What is the ruling on seawater for Wudu and Ghusl according to the Hadith of the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: It is invalid because it is salty
Its water is purifying and its dead sea creatures are halal
It is valid only for Tayammum
It may only be used in extreme drought
explanationEn: When sailors asked about making Wudu with seawater, the Prophet ﷺ replied: 'Its water is purifying (Tahur), and its dead creatures are lawful (Halal).'

questionEn: When asked about the Well of Buda'ah in Madinah, what fundamental rule about water purity did the Prophet ﷺ declare?
optionsEn: Still water is always impure
Only rainwater is pure
Water is pure and nothing makes it impure (unless its color, taste, or smell is altered by impurity)
Well water must be boiled first
explanationEn: He ﷺ said: 'Indeed water is pure; nothing makes it impure,' which scholars explain means water remains pure unless an impurity changes its color, taste, or odor.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the purity of a believer's body when Abu Hurayrah (RA) stepped away because he was in Janabah?
optionsEn: A Muslim in Janabah is physically impure
Do not shake hands until Ghusl
Stay at home until Ghusl
SubhanAllah! Indeed, the believer does not become impure (Al-mu'min la yanjus)
explanationEn: When Abu Hurayrah felt too shy to sit beside the Prophet ﷺ while in Janabah, the Prophet ﷺ reassured him: 'Glory be to Allah! The believer never becomes physically impure.'

questionEn: If the lower hem of a woman's long dress touches dry impurity on the street and then drags over clean dry ground afterward, how is it purified according to Hadith?
optionsEn: What comes after (clean ground) purifies it
She must burn the hem
She must perform Ghusl
She must cut off the hem
explanationEn: Umm Salamah (RA) asked the Prophet ﷺ about a woman's trailing garment passing over dirty and clean ground; he ﷺ said: 'What comes after it purifies it.'

questionEn: What should a worshipper do if they notice dirt or impurity on the sole of their shoes before or when entering the Masjid?
optionsEn: Throw the shoes away
Rub them against the clean ground/earth and inspect them
Wash them seven times with soap
Pray barefoot without checking
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed that when one comes to the Masjid, they should check the underside of their sandals; if they see filth, they should wipe it on the earth and then pray in them.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ respond when Jibril informed him during Salah that there was impurity on his sandals?
optionsEn: He restarted the prayer from the beginning
He left the Masjid immediately
He took off his sandals during the prayer and continued without restarting
He performed Sujud al-Sahw
explanationEn: When Jibril alerted him during prayer, the Prophet ﷺ quietly removed his sandals, placed them to his left, and completed his prayer.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a worshipper discovers an impurity on their garment ONLY after finishing the prayer, without knowing it was there beforehand?
optionsEn: The prayer is invalid and must be repeated
They must repeat all prayers of that day
They must perform Ghusl
The prayer is valid and need not be repeated, because the Prophet ﷺ did not restart his prayer when alerted
explanationEn: Scholars (including Malikis/Hanbalis and many Shafi'is) rule that if someone prays unaware of impurity and discovers it only after Salah, the prayer remains valid.

questionEn: How does tanning (Dibagh) affect the skin of a dead animal (other than dog/pig) according to Sahih Muslim?
optionsEn: When the hide is tanned, it becomes pure
It remains permanently impure
Only sheep skin becomes pure
It requires burial
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whenever a hide is tanned, it is purified,' making tanned leather usable for water skins, shoes, and prayer mats.

questionEn: What is the Arabic term for major ritual impurity requiring a full-body bath (Ghusl)?
optionsEn: Hadath Asghar
Janabah (Hadath Akbar)
Istinja'
Najasah Hukmiyyah
explanationEn: Minor impurity requiring Wudu is Hadath Asghar, whereas major ritual impurity requiring Ghusl—such as Janabah, menstruation, or postpartum bleeding—is Hadath Akbar.

questionEn: Which of the following causes Ghusl (full ritual bath) to become obligatory?
optionsEn: Passing wind
Falling asleep while seated
Discharge of semen (Many) or marital intercourse, and ending of menstruation/postpartum bleeding
Eating camel meat
explanationEn: Ghusl becomes obligatory upon ejaculation of semen with pleasure, marital intercourse (even without ejaculation), completion of menstruation (Hayd) or postpartum bleeding (Nifas), and upon embracing Islam (according to many scholars) or death.

questionEn: When Umm Sulaym (RA) asked whether a woman must perform Ghusl if she sees a wet dream, what did the Prophet ﷺ reply?
optionsEn: Never
Only perform Wudu
Only on Fridays
Yes, if she sees fluid (discharge)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ answered: 'Yes, if she sees water (fluid),' establishing the same rule for men and women regarding nocturnal discharge.

questionEn: In the Prophet's ﷺ complete Sunnah method of performing Ghusl from Janabah (as narrated by Aishah and Maymunah RA), which step comes first after washing the hands and private part?
optionsEn: Performing a complete Wudu as for prayer
Pouring water over the feet first
Washing the back first
Drying the hair
explanationEn: First he ﷺ washed his hands, then washed his private area with his left hand, then performed a full Wudu (sometimes delaying washing the feet until the end), then poured water over his hair/head three times, then over the rest of his body.

questionEn: How many times did the Prophet ﷺ pour water over his head to ensure it reached the roots of his hair during Ghusl?
optionsEn: Once
Three times
Five times
Seven times
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) reported that he ﷺ ran his wet fingers through his hair until he was sure water reached the skin of his scalp, then poured water over his head three times.

questionEn: When Umm Salamah (RA) asked if she must undo her tightly braided hair for Ghusl of Janabah, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
optionsEn: Yes, always undo all braids
You must cut it
No, it suffices to pour three handfuls of water over your head so it covers your body
Only undo half of them
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told her: 'No, it is enough for you to pour three handfuls of water over your head, then pour water over yourself, and you will be purified.'

questionEn: Does a person who performs an obligatory Ghusl (such as for Janabah) with intention need to perform a separate Wudu afterward in order to pray?
optionsEn: Yes, Ghusl never suffices for Wudu
Only if it is before Dhuhr
Only for men
No, an obligatory Ghusl removes both major and minor impurity (provided one didn't break Wudu after Ghusl)
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ did not perform Wudu after Ghusl, because the complete ritual bath already encompasses Wudu.

questionEn: For which weekly worship did the Prophet ﷺ say Ghusl is 'Wajib (strongly incumbent) upon every adult Muslim'?
optionsEn: On Friday (for Jumu'ah)
On Monday
On Wednesday
On Thursday
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ stated: 'Ghusl on Friday is incumbent upon every person who has reached puberty,' emphasizing cleanliness and dignity for the weekly gathering.

questionEn: Why should a person who is in a state of Janabah perform Wudu before going to sleep if they delay Ghusl until Fajr?
optionsEn: So they don't have to do Ghusl at Fajr
It is Sunnah (recommended) to sleep in a state of minor purification
Sleep is invalid without Wudu
Because Wudu replaces Ghusl
explanationEn: When Umar (RA) asked whether one may sleep while in Janabah, the Prophet ﷺ replied: 'Yes, if he performs Wudu first.'

questionEn: Is a fasting person's fast valid if they wake up at Fajr in a state of Janabah and perform Ghusl after Fajr begins?
optionsEn: No, their fast is broken
They must make up the day
Yes, their fast is completely valid
Only in voluntary fasts
explanationEn: Aishah and Umm Salamah (RA) reported that Fajr sometimes entered while the Prophet ﷺ was in Janabah from marital intimacy, and he ﷺ would perform Ghusl and fast.

questionEn: Which act is forbidden for a person in a state of major ritual impurity (Janabah) until they perform Ghusl?
optionsEn: Eating or drinking
Greeting others with Salam
Sleeping
Performing Salah, Tawaf, and reciting Qur'an
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ would recite the Qur'an in all situations except when in a state of Janabah; Salah and Tawaf are likewise prohibited until Ghusl (or Tayammum if excused) is performed.

questionEn: What distinguishes Hayd (menstruation) from Istihadah (irregular non-menstrual bleeding) regarding prayer?
optionsEn: A woman does not pray during Hayd and does not make up missed prayers, whereas during Istihadah she performs Wudu for each prayer and prays normally
Both require stopping Salah
Neither prevents Salah
Both require making up missed prayers
explanationEn: As the Prophet ﷺ taught Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh (RA), Hayd is recognized menstrual blood during which Salah is paused without make-up, while Istihadah is bleeding from a vein during which she cleanses herself, makes Wudu for each prayer time, and prays.

questionEn: When a woman becomes pure from Hayd or Nifas before the time of a prayer ends, what is the ruling?
optionsEn: She waits until the next day
She performs Ghusl and prays that prayer (and some scholars add the preceding combined prayer if Asr/Isha)
She only prays starting at Fajr
She only makes Wudu
explanationEn: Once bleeding ceases and she becomes pure before a prayer's time expires, she performs Ghusl and offers that prayer within its time.

questionEn: What is 'Tayammum' in Islamic purification law?
optionsEn: Washing only the right side
Wiping over leather socks
Dry ritual purification using clean earth/dust when water is unavailable or harmful to use
Using rosewater for Wudu
explanationEn: Tayammum (literally 'intending') is wiping the face and hands with clean earth (Sa'id Tayyib) in place of Wudu or Ghusl when water is lacking or cannot safely be used.

questionEn: Which Sahabi's lost necklace incident led to the revelation of the verse of Tayammum?
optionsEn: Khadijah (RA)
Fatimah (RA)
Hafsah (RA)
Aishah (RA)
explanationEn: During a journey when Aishah (RA) lost her necklace and the army stopped without water, Allah revealed the verse of Tayammum, prompting Usayd ibn Hudayr to say: 'This is not your first blessing, O family of Abu Bakr!'

questionEn: According to the Hadith of Ammar ibn Yasir (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari, which parts of the body are wiped in the Prophetic method of Tayammum?
optionsEn: Only the face and the hands (up to the wrists) with a single strike on the earth
The entire body including the feet
The face, arms to the elbows, head, and feet
The neck and ears
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ struck the earth once with his palms, blew off excess dust, and wiped his face and the backs of his hands; he told Ammar: 'It would have been enough for you to do like this.'

questionEn: Why did Ammar ibn Yasir (RA) originally roll his whole body in the dust when he was in Janabah without water?
optionsEn: He was playing
He reasoned by analogy that if Wudu requires partial washing and Tayammum wipes face/hands, then Ghusl must require rolling the whole body in dust
Someone told him to do so
He was hiding from enemies
explanationEn: Ammar analogized Tayammum for Janabah to Ghusl; the Prophet ﷺ gently smiled and corrected him, teaching that one strike for face and hands suffices for Janabah as well.

questionEn: Which condition makes Tayammum permissible even when water is physically present?
optionsEn: Feeling slightly lazy
Disliking tap water
Illness or injury where using water would cause harm or delay healing, or extreme cold with no means to heat water
Running two minutes late for work
explanationEn: When Amr ibn al-As (RA) feared dying from extreme cold if he performed Ghusl at Dhat as-Salasil, he performed Tayammum and led prayer; the Prophet ﷺ approved his understanding of 'Do not kill yourselves' (An-Nisa 4:29).
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 334; Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab at-Tayammum)

questionEn: What happens to a person's state of Tayammum the moment clean water becomes available and usable?
optionsEn: It stays valid for 24 hours
It stays valid for 3 days
It never breaks
Tayammum is nullified once water is found and accessible
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Clean earth is the Muslim's Wudu even if he does not find water for ten years; when he finds water, let him touch his skin with it.'

questionEn: If two travelers prayed with Tayammum due to no water, and then found water BEFORE the prayer time expired, what did the Prophet ﷺ validate when one repeated and the other did not?
optionsEn: Both were praised: one followed the Sunnah (no repeat needed) and the other earned double reward
Both prayers were invalid
Only the one who repeated was forgiven
Both had to fast three days
explanationEn: To the one who did not repeat, he ﷺ said: 'You have hit the Sunnah and your prayer sufficed you'; to the one who repeated, he ﷺ said: 'For you is double reward.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:6, what phrase describes the clean earth used for Tayammum?
optionsEn: Ma'an Ma'inan
Sa'idan Tayyiban
Turaban Aswad
Hijaran Muharran
explanationEn: Allah says 'fatayammamu sa'idan tayyiban'—'then seek clean, pure earth/soil/surface.'

questionEn: Which unique privilege did Allah grant the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his Ummah regarding the earth itself?
optionsEn: Every mountain is gold
Earth never holds impurity
The entire earth has been made a place of prostration (Masjid) and a means of purification (Tahur)
Travelers never need to pray
explanationEn: He ﷺ said: 'I have been given five things not given to any prophet before me... the earth has been made for me a place of prostration and a means of purification.'

questionEn: How long is a resident (non-traveler) permitted to wipe over their leather socks (Khuffayn) during Wudu?
optionsEn: Three days and three nights (72 hours)
One week
One prayer only
One day and one night (24 hours)
explanationEn: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) narrated: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed three days and nights for the traveler, and one day and one night for the resident.'

questionEn: How long is a traveler permitted to wipe over their Khuffayn or thick socks (Jawrabayn) during Wudu?
optionsEn: Three days and three nights (72 hours)
24 hours
Only during the flight/ride
Five days
explanationEn: A traveler may wipe over their Khuffayn for up to 72 hours (three days and three nights) from the first wipe (or first minor impurity after putting them on).

questionEn: What prerequisite must be fulfilled BEFORE putting on Khuffayn or socks in order for wiping (Mash) over them to be valid?
optionsEn: They must be white
The feet must be put into them while in a complete state of Wudu (purity)
One must be inside a Masjid
One must be traveling
explanationEn: When Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah bent to pull off the Prophet's ﷺ leather socks during Wudu, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Leave them, for I put them on while my feet were in a state of purity.'

questionEn: Which part of the Khuff (leather sock) is wiped during Wudu according to the Hadith of Ali (RA)?
optionsEn: The sole (bottom) only
Both the top and the bottom equally
The upper surface (top) only
The heel only
explanationEn: Ali (RA) famously remarked: 'If the religion were based on mere opinion, the bottom of the khuff would deserve wiping more than the top; yet I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wipe over the top of his khuffs.'

questionEn: Can wiping over Khuffayn replace washing the feet during an obligatory Ghusl from Janabah?
optionsEn: Yes, always
Yes, for travelers
Yes, for 24 hours
No; during Ghusl the socks must be removed so water washes the entire body including the feet
explanationEn: Safwan ibn Assal (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ allowed them not to remove their khuffs for three days except in the case of Janabah (when Ghusl is required).

questionEn: If a person wipes over their Khuffayn and later removes the socks while still in Wudu, what is the ruling according to many scholars (e.g., Ibn Taymiyyah vs Hanbali/Shafi'i)?
optionsEn: Scholars differ: some rule Wudu remains valid until broken, while others require washing the feet or renewing Wudu
All scholars agree Ghusl is required
They must do Tayammum
They cannot pray until next day
explanationEn: There is a classical scholarly difference: some hold that removing the khuff breaks the Wudu (requiring washing feet or renewing Wudu), while others hold Wudu remains valid until a nullifier occurs.

questionEn: What is 'Mash 'ala al-Jabirah' in Islamic purification?
optionsEn: Wiping over a prayer mat
Wiping with wet hands over a cast, splint, or bandage covering a wound during Wudu or Ghusl
Wiping over a hat
Wiping over jewelry
explanationEn: When a limb has a cast or bandage (Jabirah) that cannot be removed or washed without harm, one washes the healthy parts and wipes gently with a wet hand over the bandage/cast.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 336 (hadith of the wounded man)

questionEn: In the Hadith of the companion with a fractured skull during a cold night, why did the Prophet ﷺ rebuke those who told him he must wash his wound in Ghusl?
optionsEn: They told him to use seawater
They forgot to give him a towel
Because washing the wound caused his death when wiping over a bandage or Tayammum was sufficient
Because they delayed Fajr
explanationEn: Upon learning he died from washing the head wound, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'They killed him, may Allah punish them! Why did they not ask when they did not know? It would have sufficed him to do Tayammum and bind/wipe over his wound.'

questionEn: When does the 24-hour or 72-hour wiping period for Khuffayn begin according to the majority of jurists?
optionsEn: From the moment the socks are purchased
From the moment the socks are put on
From the time of Fajr
From the first wipe after breaking Wudu (or first minor impurity after putting them on)
explanationEn: Most jurists count the 24h/72h window from the first time one wipes after breaking Wudu (or from the first minor impurity after wearing them in purity), not simply from when they were put on.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about wiping over a turban ('Imamah) during Wudu according to Sahih Muslim?
optionsEn: He wiped over his forelock and over his turban
He never wore a turban
He removed it every single time
He washed it with soap
explanationEn: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ performed Wudu and wiped over his forelock, his turban, and his leather socks.

questionEn: How does a Muslim who suffers from a continuous excuse (like chronic urinary incontinence or continuous bleeding) maintain purity for Salah?
optionsEn: They are excused from Salah permanently
They wash the area, use protection, and perform a fresh Wudu after each prayer time enters, then pray as much as they wish within that time
They perform Ghusl five times a day
They pray once a week
explanationEn: A person with a continuous discharge (Ma'dhur) performs Wudu once the time for each prayer begins; any involuntary discharge during that prayer time does not invalidate their Wudu for that time.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Wudu with water left over by a woman (or spouse) in a shared vessel?
optionsEn: It is strictly forbidden
It is valid only for travelers
It is completely permissible; the Prophet ﷺ and his wives performed Wudu and Ghusl from the same vessel
It requires boiling
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) and Aishah (RA) confirmed that the Prophet ﷺ and his wives bathed and made Wudu together from the same vessel, and he ﷺ used water from a vessel after Maymunah (RA).

questionEn: What does 'Fitrah' refer to in the famous Hadith mentioning five natural practices of cleanliness?
optionsEn: Fasting Ramadan
Facing Makkah
Reciting Surah Al-Fatihah
Circumcision, shaving pubic hair, trimming the mustache, clipping nails, and plucking armpit hair
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ listed these five practices as part of the Fitrah (pure natural disposition) of cleanliness taught to all prophets.

questionEn: What is the maximum time limit Anas ibn Malik (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ set for leaving nails, mustache, armpit, and pubic hair untrimmed?
optionsEn: Forty nights
Seven days
Six months
One year
explanationEn: Anas (RA) said: 'A time limit was set for us regarding trimming the mustache, clipping the nails, plucking armpit hair, and shaving pubic hair: not to leave them for more than forty nights.'

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ warn against failing to protect oneself from splashes of urine ('Istibra' / avoiding urine traces)?
optionsEn: It ruins sandals
Most punishment in the grave is because of carelessness regarding urine
It cancels Hajj
It makes food haram
explanationEn: Passing two graves, the Prophet ﷺ said both were being punished—one for gossip/backbiting, and the other because he did not shield himself from urine.

questionEn: What is the ruling on drying one's limbs with a towel after Wudu?
optionsEn: Strictly forbidden
Obligatory before prayer
Permissible (Mubah), though leaving water to drip is also Sunnah
Invalidates Wudu
explanationEn: Although Maymunah (RA) mentioned the Prophet ﷺ shook water off after Ghusl without using a cloth on one occasion, other narrations mention he had a towel for Wudu; scholars agree drying is permissible.

questionEn: Which tree's twigs are traditionally used to make the authentic Miswak (Siwak)?
optionsEn: Olive tree
Date palm
Cedar tree
Arak tree (Salvadora persica)
explanationEn: The Arak tree (Salvadora persica) has natural antibacterial fibers and was the Prophet's ﷺ favored wood for cleaning the mouth before prayer and upon waking.

questionEn: According to Aishah (RA), what was the very first thing the Prophet ﷺ would do whenever he entered his house?
optionsEn: Use the Miswak (clean his teeth)
Eat dinner
Take a nap
Change his cloak
explanationEn: Shurayh asked Aishah (RA) what the Prophet ﷺ started with when entering his home, and she answered: 'With the Siwak (Miswak).'

questionEn: When praying after having performed Wudu, what should a person do if they are uncertain whether they broke their Wudu or not?
optionsEn: Assume their Wudu is still valid because certainty is not removed by mere doubt
Assume their Wudu is broken automatically
Perform Tayammum just in case
Repeat the last two prayers
explanationEn: The foundational fiqh maxim 'Al-yaqin la yazulu bish-shakk' (certainty is not negated by doubt) stems directly from the Hadith instructing not to leave Salah without clear proof.

questionEn: Conversely, if someone knows for certain they broke their Wudu earlier and doubts whether they renewed it afterward, what is their state?
optionsEn: They are in a state of Wudu
They must perform Wudu, because the last state known with certainty was impurity
They can wipe over their socks
They may pray without Wudu
explanationEn: Applying the same certainty rule in reverse: if impurity is certain and renewed Wudu is doubtful, one remains in impurity until Wudu is performed with certainty.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Wudu with water that has been heated by the sun (Mushammas) or heated on a stove?
optionsEn: Both are strictly haram
Only cold water is valid for Wudu
Warm or heated water is valid for Wudu as long as it remains pure water
Heated water invalidates Ghusl
explanationEn: Clean water remains purifying whether cold or warmed; Umar (RA) used heated water for Ghusl and Wudu, and moderate warmth aids thorough washing in cold weather.

questionEn: Which Sahabi reported seeing the Prophet ﷺ perform Wudu and run his wet fingers through his thick beard (Takhlil al-Lihyah)?
optionsEn: Abu Hurayrah (RA)
Bilal (RA)
Zayd ibn Thabit (RA)
Uthman ibn Affan (RA)
explanationEn: Uthman ibn Affan (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ used to run his wet fingers through his beard during Wudu.

questionEn: If a person has a thin beard through which the skin of the jaw is visible, what must they do when washing their face in Wudu?
optionsEn: Wash so that water reaches the skin beneath the hair
Only wipe the tips of the beard
Skip the beard
Cut the beard
explanationEn: Because the face is defined as the visible skin area, when a beard is light/thin enough to show the skin underneath, water must reach the underlying skin.

questionEn: What are the anatomical boundaries of the 'face' (Wajh) that must be washed during Wudu?
optionsEn: From the eyebrows to the nose only
Vertically from the normal hairline to the bottom of the chin/jaw, and horizontally from ear to ear
Only the cheeks and forehead
From the crown of the head to the collarbone
explanationEn: Jurists define the face as spanning lengthwise from the usual hairline at the forehead down to the bottom of the chin, and widthwise from one ear lobe/edge to the other.

questionEn: When washing the arms in Wudu, should the hands (palms/fingers) also be washed again up to the elbows even if one already washed the hands three times at the start?
optionsEn: No, start only from the wrists
Only wash the left hand
Yes, washing from the fingertips up to and including the elbows is obligatory in that step
Only wipe the hands
explanationEn: The initial handwashing before Wudu is Sunnah; the Qur'anic command 'wash your hands/arms up to the elbows' requires washing from the fingertips through the elbows.

questionEn: If a person wears a tight ring on their finger during Wudu or Ghusl, what should they do?
optionsEn: Never wear rings at all
Leave it tight without moving it
Only wash the ring
Move/twist the ring so water reaches the skin underneath it
explanationEn: Narrations from Abu Rafi' and Ibn Umar indicate the Prophet ﷺ would move his ring during Wudu so water would reach the skin beneath it.

questionEn: How does a person with an amputated forearm (say below the elbow) perform the arm-washing step of Wudu?
optionsEn: Wash whatever remains of the arm up to and including the elbow
Skip that arm and do Tayammum for it
Wash only the opposite arm twice
Do Ghusl instead
explanationEn: Based on 'Fear Allah as much as you are able' (At-Taghabun 64:16), one washes the remaining portion of the limb up to the elbow.

questionEn: What is the ruling on wiping the neck (back of the neck) during Wudu?
optionsEn: An obligatory pillar of Wudu
Not established as a Sunnah of Wudu (though wiping the nape while returning the hands over the head is part of head wiping)
Invalidates Wudu
Obligatory only in Ghusl
explanationEn: Scholars like Ibn al-Qayyim and An-Nawawi noted there is no authentic Hadith establishing separately wiping the neck as a Sunnah of Wudu.

questionEn: What is the ruling on using a small amount of water from a modern spray bottle or sink in an airplane restroom to perform Wudu carefully?
optionsEn: Invalid because it is not from a basin
Invalid unless a liter is poured
Valid, as long as water flows/coats the obligatory limbs thoroughly without leaving dry spots
Forbidden in airplanes
explanationEn: As long as pure water flows over and covers the washed limbs (face, arms to elbows, feet to ankles) and wipes the head, Wudu is valid even with minimal water.

questionEn: According to the Hadith of Abu Hurayrah (RA), what did the Prophet ﷺ say about extending the radiance (Ghurrah) of Wudu beyond the minimum boundaries?
optionsEn: It is strictly prohibited
It cancels Wudu
It applies only to the feet
Whoever among you is able to lengthen his radiance (by washing slightly past the elbows/ankles), let him do so
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah (RA) washed well above his elbows and ankles and cited the Prophet ﷺ encouraging believers to lengthen their Ghurrah and Tahjil.

questionEn: Which type of water is classified as 'Tahur' (pure and purifying)?
optionsEn: Water in its natural state—rain, river, spring, well, sea, and melted snow/hail—unchanged by impurities
Rosewater mixed with heavy syrup
Soap suds without flowing water
Vinegar and fruit juice
explanationEn: Pure natural water (Ma' Mutlaq)—including rain, snow, hail, sea, spring, and well water—is both pure in itself and capable of removing ritual impurity.

questionEn: In the opening dua of Salah ('Allahumma ba'id bayni...'), what three pure substances did the Prophet ﷺ ask Allah to wash away his sins with?
optionsEn: Milk, honey, and olive oil
Water, snow, and hail (Al-ma'i wath-thalji wal-barad)
Rain, river, and sea water
Earth, wind, and dew
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ supplicated: 'O Allah, wash away my sins with water, snow, and hail,' symbolizing complete, cool, soothing purification.

questionEn: Why does Islamic law consider Zamzam water valid for Wudu and Ghusl (while avoiding using it for Istinja' out of reverence)?
optionsEn: Because Zamzam is only for drinking
Because Zamzam cannot remove impurity
Because it is pure water (Tahur) by nature; the Prophet ﷺ made Wudu with it, though scholars advise against using it to wash filth out of honor
Because Zamzam is seawater
explanationEn: Ali (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ called for a bucket of Zamzam water, drank from it, and performed Wudu with it.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Wudu with rainwater that has slightly changed color from clean tree leaves or natural earth/mud?
optionsEn: It is impure
It can only be used for Istinja'
It invalidates Ghusl
It remains pure and purifying (Tahur) because the alteration came from clean natural elements, not Najasah
explanationEn: Water altered naturally by soil, algae, or fallen leaves without losing its fluidity remains Tahur (pure and purifying) by scholarly consensus.

questionEn: Can pure liquid like milk, tea, or orange juice be used instead of water for Wudu?
optionsEn: No; if water is unavailable or harmful, one performs Tayammum rather than using other liquids
Yes, milk is valid
Yes, juice is valid in travel
Yes, if warmed
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:6 specifies water, and in its absence prescribes Tayammum with clean earth—never substitute beverages.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach if a fly falls into a vessel of drink or water?
optionsEn: Throw the entire pot away immediately
Immerse it completely and then remove/discard it, for one wing carries disease and the other its cure
Boil it for one hour
Perform Ghusl if you touched it
explanationEn: This Hadith also confirms that dead insects without flowing blood (like flies, mosquitoes, bees) do not render water or food ritually impure.

questionEn: Why does a dead fish or dead locust NOT make water impure according to Islamic jurisprudence?
optionsEn: Only when cooked
Only in the ocean
Because dead sea creatures and locusts are halal/pure, and creatures without flowing blood do not cause impurity
Because fish have scales
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Two dead animals and two types of blood have been made lawful for us: fish and locusts, and liver and spleen.'

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ advise regarding a mouse that fell into clarified butter (ghee)?
optionsEn: Throw all of it away regardless of solidity
Eat it as is
Wash the mouse and keep the ghee
If it is solid, discard the mouse and what is around it and eat the rest; if it is liquid, do not go near it (or discard/use for non-food if impure)
explanationEn: This Hadith illustrates how impurity spreads through liquids, whereas in solid fats it stays localized around the contact spot.

questionEn: How are droppings and urine of animals whose meat is lawful to eat (like sheep, goats, cows, and camels) classified by many jurists (e.g., Malikis/Hanbalis)?
optionsEn: Pure (Tahir), as the Prophet ﷺ allowed praying in sheep pens and prescribed camel milk/urine for the Uraynah tribe
Major impurity worse than dog saliva
Requires seven washes with soil
Prohibited even to look at
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Pray in sheep pens, but do not pray in camel resting places [due to their restlessness, not impurity],' and permitted the Uraynah men to drink camel milk and urine as medicine.

questionEn: Which two animals are universally agreed by scholars to be ritually impure in their flesh even when alive or dead (notably swine)?
optionsEn: Horses and donkeys
Pigs (swine) and dogs (in saliva/body per majority)
Cats and rabbits
Camels and gazelles
explanationEn: The Qur'an describes the flesh of swine as 'rijs' (filth/impure) in Al-An'am 6:145, and Sahih Muslim 279 commands seven washes including earth for a dog's saliva.

questionEn: What did Asma bint Abi Bakr (RA) receive as instruction from the Prophet ﷺ when she asked about menstrual blood on a garment?
optionsEn: Throw the dress away
Wipe it with a dry tissue only
Scrape it off, rub it with water, sprinkle/wash it, and then pray in it
Soak it in milk
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught a practical three-step removal: scrape away the dried trace, rub it with water using the fingertips, rinse it clean, and then the garment is fit for Salah.

questionEn: If a trace/faint stain of menstrual blood remains on a garment even after thorough washing with water, is the garment still pure for Salah?
optionsEn: No, the dress must be burned
No, you must cut out that piece
Only if dyed black
Yes; when Khawlah bint Yasar asked about a lingering trace, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Water suffices you, and its trace does not harm you'
explanationEn: Once the substance of the impurity has been washed away thoroughly, a faint residual discoloration that refuses to fade does not affect the purity of the garment.

questionEn: How did Aishah (RA) purify dried semen (Many) from the Prophet's ﷺ garment?
optionsEn: She scraped it off when dry (and washed it when wet)
She discarded the garment
She washed it seven times with earth
She applied perfume over it without cleaning
explanationEn: Sahih Muslim records Aishah (RA) scraping dried semen off his garment with her fingernails and washing fresh spots with water, showing its physical purity (or ease of removal) according to scholars.

questionEn: Is normal human sweat, saliva, or tears from a Muslim or non-Muslim considered ritually impure (Najis)?
optionsEn: Yes, sweat breaks Wudu
No, human sweat, saliva, and tears are pure (Tahir)
Only tears are impure
Only sweat during fasting is impure
explanationEn: Human bodily secretions such as sweat, tears, mucus, and saliva are pure, and they do not nullify Wudu or taint clothing.

questionEn: Does touching a spouse affectionately or kissing one's spouse without discharge break Wudu according to the authentic narration of Aishah (RA)?
optionsEn: Always breaks Wudu in all four schools
Requires Ghusl
Aishah (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ kissed one of his wives and went out to prayer without performing Wudu (though Shafi'is differ)
Breaks Wudu only in Ramadan
explanationEn: This is a well-known point of scholarly nuance: Aishah (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ kissed a wife and prayed without renewing Wudu, while the Shafi'i school holds skin-to-skin contact between non-mahram spouses breaks Wudu based on Al-Ma'idah 5:6.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ clarify regarding touching one's own private part during Wudu or prayer?
optionsEn: It is always Harām
It requires Ghusl
It invalidates all fasts
Direct skin contact with the private part without a barrier breaks Wudu according to the Hadith of Busrah bint Safwan (RA)
explanationEn: Busrah bint Safwan (RA) narrated: 'Whoever touches his private part, let him perform Wudu,' while Talq ibn Ali's narration treats unintentional/non-desirous touch differently—leading to respectful scholarly discussion.

questionEn: If a person eats or drinks something after performing Wudu (other than camel meat or anything intoxicating), does it break Wudu?
optionsEn: No, eating normal halal food or drinking water/milk/coffee does not break Wudu (rinsing mouth with water after fatty food like milk is recommended)
Yes, eating anything breaks Wudu
Only sweet foods break Wudu
Only drinking cold water breaks Wudu
explanationEn: After drinking milk, the Prophet ﷺ rinsed his mouth saying 'It has fat in it,' without repeating Wudu.

questionEn: Does a minor cut or nosebleed break Wudu according to the majority of Hadith scholars (Malik, Shafi'i) vs the Hanafi school?
optionsEn: All schools say every drop breaks Wudu
In the Shafi'i/Maliki view blood outside the two passages does not break Wudu; in the Hanafi view flowing blood that leaves the wound site breaks Wudu
Both require Ghusl
Neither allows prayer that day
explanationEn: Umar (RA) prayed while his wound bled, and Al-Hasan said Muslims continued praying with their wounds; meanwhile Hanafi jurists consider flowing blood from a wound a nullifier.

questionEn: Does clipping one's fingernails, trimming a mustache, or getting a haircut break Wudu?
optionsEn: Yes, always
Yes, only haircuts
No, cutting hair or nails does not break Wudu
Only if done on Friday
explanationEn: Nothing in Qur'an or Sunnah makes hair or nail trimming a nullifier of Wudu; Ibn Umar and others confirmed Wudu remains completely intact.

questionEn: If someone wears regular cotton or wool socks (Jawrabayn) that cover the ankles and puts them on in a state of Wudu, did the Prophet ﷺ wipe over Jawrabayn (thick socks) and sandals?
optionsEn: No, never
Only leather boots in winter
Only during Hajj
Yes, Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ performed Wudu and wiped over his socks (Jawrabayn) and sandals
explanationEn: Several Companions—including Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Anas, and Abu Umamah—also wiped over thick socks, forming the basis for wiping over thick non-transparent socks today.

questionEn: How should one physically wipe over their socks (Khuffayn or Jawrabayn) during Wudu?
optionsEn: Pass wet fingers from the tips of the toes toward the shins/ankles along the top of the socks once
Wash the socks under the tap until soaked
Wipe only the heel
Wipe the bottom of the socks
explanationEn: Al-Mughirah (RA) described seeing the Prophet ﷺ place his wet hand on the top of his khuffs near the toes and draw it upward toward the shin once.

questionEn: What happens if a traveler's 72-hour period for wiping over Khuffayn expires while they are still in a state of Wudu?
optionsEn: They must perform Ghusl
They must remove the socks and wash their feet (or renew Wudu) before praying again (and in one view, expiration ends the wiping concession immediately)
They can extend it to 7 days
They switch to Tayammum
explanationEn: Once the 24h (resident) or 72h (traveler) limit expires, the concession of wiping ends and the feet must be washed when renewing Wudu (or immediately according to most scholars).

questionEn: If a person puts on one sock after washing the right foot, and THEN washes the left foot and puts on the left sock, may they wipe over those socks later?
optionsEn: Yes, always
Only if traveling
According to the majority of jurists, both feet must be washed FIRST before putting on either sock so that the socks are donned in complete purity
Only the right sock may be wiped
explanationEn: Because Wudu is not complete until both feet are washed, the majority require finishing washing both feet before slipping on the socks so each sock is worn after complete purity.

questionEn: If a person has a small hole in an otherwise wearable sock, is wiping over it permitted according to scholars like Sufyan ath-Thawri and Ibn Taymiyyah?
optionsEn: Never under any circumstance
Only if sewn with gold thread
Only for 1 hour
Yes, because the Companions' khuffs often had tears/holes from travel yet the Prophet ﷺ never set a condition that they be 100% hole-free
explanationEn: While some schools require the sock to cover the foot without large holes exposing skin, others note that poor Companions routinely traveled with patched or torn footwear without restriction.

questionEn: If a person is wearing two pairs of socks (say thin inner socks and thicker outer socks) put on together in purity, which pair do they wipe over?
optionsEn: The outer pair (and if the outer pair is later removed, scholars differ on whether the inner stays valid)
Must remove both
Must wipe between the two pairs
Cannot wipe at all
explanationEn: Wiping applies to the uppermost layer covering the foot; scholars recommend keeping that outer layer on if possible until Wudu is renewed.

questionEn: What is the minimum obligation (Fard) in Ghusl according to all four Sunni schools of jurisprudence?
optionsEn: Using fragrant soap and shampoo
Intending purification and ensuring water reaches every accessible part of the outer body and hair (plus rinsing mouth and nose in Hanafi/Hanbali schools)
Pouring water seven times
Facing Makkah in the shower
explanationEn: The core pillar of Ghusl is intention and washing the entire external body with water; the Hanafi and Hanbali schools also count rinsing the mouth and nose (Madmadah and Istinshaq) as obligatory in Ghusl.

questionEn: For which occasions is Ghusl a recommended Sunnah (Mustahabb) rather than strictly obligatory?
optionsEn: Before every Fajr prayer
Before entering a grocery store
Before Eid prayers, before entering Ihram for Hajj/Umrah, and after washing a deceased body
After waking from a midday nap
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ or his Companions modeled Ghusl for Ihram, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, entering Makkah, standing at Arafah, and after bathing the deceased.

questionEn: According to the Hadith of Abu Hurayrah (RA), what Sunnah act is prescribed for one who has just finished washing a deceased Muslim?
optionsEn: Fast three days
Pay Zakah
Shave the head
Perform Ghusl (and whoever carries the bier should perform Wudu)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever washes a dead person, let him take a bath (Ghusl); and whoever carries him, let him perform Wudu'—which most scholars classify as strongly recommended (Mustahabb).

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about bathing in stagnant (non-flowing) water while in a state of Janabah?
optionsEn: None of you should bathe in stagnant water while in a state of Janabah
It is the best method of Ghusl
It doubles the reward
It is only for summer
explanationEn: To keep shared still pools clean for others, the Prophet ﷺ prohibited immersing oneself in stagnant water while in Janabah; rather one should scoop water out of it.

questionEn: Is it permissible for a person to perform Ghusl or Wudu without clothes inside a private, enclosed bathroom?
optionsEn: Strictly forbidden
Yes, it is permissible when completely private (and Allah has even more right to modesty when uncovered unnecessarily)
Invalidates Ghusl
Only allowed at night
explanationEn: Prophet Musa (AS) and Prophet Ayyub (AS) bathed privately unclothed as narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari, showing it is permissible in private while covering before others is obligatory.

questionEn: What is the ruling on using a clean marble tile, stone wall, or dusty rock for Tayammum when natural soil/sand is unavailable (e.g., in a hospital bed)?
optionsEn: Never allowed
Requires soil imported from Makkah
Permissible according to many jurists (e.g., Hanafis and Malikis) because 'Sa'id' includes anything of the earth's natural surface such as stone, sand, or mineral surfaces
Only wood is allowed
explanationEn: Hanafi and Maliki scholars define 'Sa'id' broadly as any pure surface of earthly origin—sand, dust, clay, or clean unglazed stone/marble—even if no visible dust clings to the hand.

questionEn: If a person performs Tayammum because water is completely unavailable and then prays, and water becomes available AFTER the prayer is finished, must they repeat that prayer?
optionsEn: Yes, always
Yes, twice
Only if it was Fajr
No, their prayer was valid and fulfilled its obligation at that time
explanationEn: As confirmed in the Hadith of the two travelers (Abu Dawud 338), a prayer validly performed with Tayammum does not need to be repeated if water is found afterward.

questionEn: Can a person who is in Janabah (major impurity) perform Tayammum when water is unavailable or dangerously cold?
optionsEn: Yes; Tayammum substitutes for both Wudu and Ghusl in times of necessity
No, Tayammum only replaces Wudu
Only if they fast a day
Only in Makkah
explanationEn: Both the Hadith of Ammar ibn Yasir (Sahih al-Bukhari 338) and Imran ibn Husayn (Sahih al-Bukhari 344) prove that Tayammum purifies a person from Janabah until water is found.

questionEn: What does the Hadith of Imran ibn Husayn (RA) teach about a man who stood aside from congregational prayer because he was in Janabah and had no water?
optionsEn: He was told to go home
The Prophet ﷺ handed him clean earth/said: 'Upon you is clean earth (Tayammum), for it suffices you'
He was ordered to pray without any purification
He was fined
explanationEn: When the man said 'Janabah has befallen me and there is no water,' the Prophet ﷺ replied: 'Use clean earth, for that is sufficient for you.'

questionEn: If a person has just enough drinking water on a desert journey to survive and keep their animals alive, should they use it for Wudu or keep it for drinking and do Tayammum?
optionsEn: Use all of it for Wudu even if they die of thirst
Throw it away
Preserve the water for drinking/survival and perform Tayammum for Salah
Skip Salah completely
explanationEn: Preserving human and animal life takes precedence in Shariah; when water is needed to prevent severe thirst, one is legally considered lacking water for Wudu and uses Tayammum.

questionEn: What if a person fears that searching for water or delaying to buy water will cause the prayer time (e.g., Fajr before sunrise) to expire completely—may some scholars allow Tayammum?
optionsEn: Never under any scholar
Always regardless of whether water is at home
Only on airplanes
Scholars like the Hanafis and Ibn Taymiyyah permit Tayammum if water is absent nearby and waiting would cause the entire prayer time to pass (while others require seeking water first)
explanationEn: Jurists debate whether fear of time expiring (e.g. waking minutes before sunrise with no water immediately accessible) permits Tayammum; Ibn Taymiyyah and the Hanafis allow it in narrow windows, whereas the majority prioritize seeking available water.

questionEn: When someone has a wound on one arm that cannot get wet, how do they purify themselves for Salah?
optionsEn: Wash all healthy limbs as normal in Wudu, and wipe over the bandage/wound or perform Tayammum for the unwashed limb
Skip Wudu completely
Wash the wound with salt water
Wait until the wound heals in weeks before praying
explanationEn: Islamic law combines ease with obedience: wash the unaffected limbs, wipe over any dressing (Jabirah), or do Tayammum for the injured spot if wiping directly causes harm.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah 2:222, what two groups of believers does Allah declare that He loves?
optionsEn: The wealthy and the travelers
Those who constantly repent (At-Tawwabin) and those who purify themselves (Al-Mutatahhirin)
The poets and merchants
The builders and farmers
explanationEn: Allah says: 'Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves'—linking inner spiritual purity (Tawbah) with outer physical purity (Taharah).

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say Allah's acceptance of any Salah depends upon when a person stands to pray without purification?
optionsEn: Allah accepts half of it
Allah accepts it if the person gives charity
Allah does not accept Salah without purification (nor charity from stolen wealth)
Allah accepts only Sunnah prayers without Wudu
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah does not accept prayer without purification, nor charity from misappropriated wealth (Ghulul).'

questionEn: What happens to a person's state if they intentionally pray without Wudu while knowing they are not in Wudu (despite being able to make Wudu)?
optionsEn: They get minor reward
It is merely disliked
It counts if they pray in congregation
Their prayer is invalid and it is a grave sin of disrespecting worship
explanationEn: Purification is a prerequisite (Shart) for the validity of Salah; knowingly praying without Wudu or Tayammum renders the prayer invalid.

questionEn: If someone forgets they were without Wudu, prays Salah, and remembers after finishing, what must they do?
optionsEn: Perform Wudu and repeat that Salah, because purification is an indispensable condition
Nothing, forgetfulness excuses conditions too
Only pay Fidyah
Only make Sujud al-Sahw
explanationEn: Unlike unawareness of minor physical impurity on clothes, praying without ritual Wudu means a core condition was absent, so one makes Wudu and repeats the prayer without sin for the mistake.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ recommend making Wudu when one becomes angry?
optionsEn: To wash away tears
Because anger comes from Shaytan (created from fire), and fire is extinguished with water
To delay speaking until midnight
Because anger breaks Wudu
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ advised: 'Anger comes from the devil, and the devil was created from fire, and fire is only extinguished with water; so when one of you becomes angry, let him perform Wudu.'

questionEn: What happens to the three knots Shaytan ties at the back of a sleeper's head upon waking, remembering Allah, performing Wudu, and praying?
optionsEn: They stay tied all week
Only fasting unties them
Remembrance unties the first knot, Wudu unties the second knot, and Salah unties the third knot—leaving one energetic and pure-spirited
Wudu unties all three at once
explanationEn: Sahih al-Bukhari records this vivid encouragement for Fajr: Dhikr upon waking, Wudu, and Fajr prayer untie all three knots of sluggishness.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach Al-Bara' ibn Azib (RA) to do right before lying down to sleep at night?
optionsEn: Eat a full meal
Run around the block
Drink three cups of water
Perform Wudu as you do for prayer, lie on your right side, and recite the bedtime supplication
explanationEn: Going to bed with Wudu is a beloved Sunnah; if one passes away that night, they die upon Fitrah.

questionEn: What special blessing does an angel invoke for a believer who goes to sleep in a state of Wudu (tahir)?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, forgive Your servant, for he went to sleep in a state of purity'
'O Allah, double his wealth'
'O Allah, wake him at noon'
'O Allah, grant him travel'
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) narrated that whoever spends the night in purity has an angel in their inner garment praying for their forgiveness every time they stir.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Wudu before going to sleep if one wishes to sleep in purity, vs performing Wudu only for Salah?
optionsEn: Performing Wudu before sleep is obligatory
Performing Wudu before sleep is a recommended Sunnah, whereas Wudu for Salah is obligatory
Both are obligatory
Neither is Sunnah
explanationEn: Sleeping in Wudu is a rewarding Mustahabb practice, whereas Wudu before Salah is Fard (obligatory).

questionEn: What is the 'Qullatayn' measurement mentioned in Hadith regarding large bodies of water?
optionsEn: Two tiny cups
Two drops of rain
Two large jars (approx. 160–200+ liters) — a volume that does not easily carry impurity unless its traits change
Two rivers
explanationEn: When asked about desert water holes visited by animals, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'When water reaches two Qullahs, it does not carry impurity (khubth),' meaning small impurities do not corrupt large volumes unless color/taste/smell changes.

questionEn: Which liquid is considered pure (Tahir) even though consuming it is forbidden unless it turns naturally into vinegar?
optionsEn: Fresh milk
Honey
Zamzam water
Grape wine (Khamr) is debated: majority hold it ritually impure based on 'Rijs' in 5:90, though pure once transformed into vinegar
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:90 calls intoxicants 'rijs' (abomination/filth); if wine turns naturally into vinegar without tampering, it becomes pure and lawful.

questionEn: Are modern alcohol-based hand sanitizers and perfumes considered ritually impure (Najis) such that one cannot pray after applying them?
optionsEn: Many contemporary scholars rule synthetic/industrial ethanol in perfumes and sanitizers is pure (not Khamr beverage), though avoiding any doubt or rinsing if preferred is cautious
They always require Ghusl
They break Wudu immediately
They permanently ruin clothes
explanationEn: Contemporary fiqh councils clarify that 'rijs' in Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:90 refers to spiritual/moral abomination or drinkable wine, not medical rubbing alcohol or cologne.

questionEn: How does one purify a large carpet or floor tile contaminated by urine in a Masjid or home without ruining the carpet?
optionsEn: Burn the carpet
Blot/remove the wetness, pour clean water over the spot and absorb/dry it until no smell, color, or substance of urine remains
Sprinkle perfume only
Turn the carpet upside down
explanationEn: Just as the Prophet ﷺ ordered a bucket of water poured over the Masjid floor, pouring clean water and blotting/extracting it until the impurity's traits vanish purifies carpets.

questionEn: When performing Wudu in cold weather despite physical discomfort—what did the Prophet ﷺ call 'Isbagh al-Wudu 'ala al-makarih'?
optionsEn: A minor mistake
Something forbidden
One of the great acts (Kaffarat) by which Allah erases sins and raises ranks
Only for soldiers
explanationEn: He ﷺ asked: 'Shall I not tell you that by which Allah erases sins and elevates degrees? Performing Wudu thoroughly despite hardship, taking many steps to the Masajid, and waiting for the next prayer after a prayer.'

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Wudu for someone who experiences repeated intrusive whispers (Waswasah) claiming they missed a spot or broke Wudu?
optionsEn: Repeat Wudu ten times until relieved
Stop praying
Perform Ghusl every time
Ignore the whisper completely, act only on certainty, and seek refuge in Allah from Shaytan
explanationEn: Scholars emphasize that yielding to Waswasah strengthens it; the cure is strictly following the Sunnah once with normal water and refusing to repeat limbs without clear certainty.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ gently handle a companion (or himself) who felt distracted or doubted during purification or prayer?
optionsEn: With clear certainty rules ('no leaving unless hearing a sound or smelling an odor') and moderation in water
By commanding endless repetition
By prohibiting congregation
By forbidding questions
explanationEn: Islamic law is built on ease ('Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship,' 2:185), giving objective standards to silence anxiety.

questionEn: Is it permissible for someone else (like a caregiver) to assist an elderly or disabled person in performing Wudu or Tayammum?
optionsEn: Never; Wudu is void if assisted
Yes; helping a sick or elderly person wash their limbs or wipe for Tayammum is completely valid and rewarded
Only family members of the same age
Only in Makkah
explanationEn: Even the Prophet ﷺ had companions like Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah pour water for him during Wudu; assisting those unable to wash themselves fulfills their purification.

questionEn: What should a bedridden hospitalized Muslim do if they are physically unable to use water AND have no one to assist them with Tayammum?
optionsEn: Skip prayer permanently
Wait until discharged next month
Pray in whatever state they are in, for Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity
Pay a fine
explanationEn: Known as 'Faqid at-Tahurayn' (one lacking both water and earth), such a patient prays on time without delaying Salah, because Salah is never dropped as long as consciousness remains.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Wudu while wearing waterproof cosmetics, cream, or lotion?
optionsEn: All moisturizers invalidate Wudu
Only oil invalidates Wudu
Cosmetics break Wudu automatically
Waterproof barrier products (heavy wax/silicone makeup) that block water from skin must be removed, whereas absorbed lotions that allow water to wet the skin do not block Wudu
explanationEn: The criterion is physical: if the substance forms an impermeable film preventing water from contacting the skin, it must be removed; if absorbed so water wets the skin, Wudu is valid.
