questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about using a vessel made of gold or silver for eating, drinking, or performing Wudu?
optionsEn: It is prohibited to eat or drink from gold and silver vessels (and scholars prohibit using them for Wudu too, though Wudu water in them still cleanses if used sinfully)
It is Sunnah for Eid
It doubles the reward of Wudu
Only silver is forbidden
explanationEn: Hudhayfah (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ forbade drinking and eating from gold and silver vessels, saying: 'They are for them in this world and for you in the Hereafter.'

questionEn: Is it permissible to use clean brass, copper, plastic, ceramic, or stainless-steel vessels for Wudu water?
optionsEn: Only clay pots are valid
Yes, any clean vessel other than gold and silver is permissible
Only glass
Only stone basins
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ performed Wudu from leather waterskins, brass bowls (Tawr), wooden bowls, and stone basins.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ cover water vessels at night before going to sleep?
optionsEn: To keep water warm
So no one sees them
Out of hygiene and prophetic protection against pests, dust, and seasonal contagion, while mentioning Allah's name
Because uncovered water breaks Wudu
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated the Prophet ﷺ commanded covering vessels and tying waterskins at night while saying 'Bismillah,' protecting food and Wudu water alike.

questionEn: What is the difference between 'Wudu' (minor ablution) and 'Ghusl' (major bath) regarding wiping the head?
optionsEn: In both, you only wipe the head
In Ghusl you only wipe the head, never wash it
In Wudu you wash the hair to the scalp; in Ghusl you only wipe
In Wudu you wipe over the head with wet hands, whereas in Ghusl you pour water so it thoroughly washes the hair and scalp
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:6 commands wiping the head ('wamsahu bi-ru'usikum') in Wudu, whereas for Janabah it commands full purification ('fattahharu') by washing the entire head and body.

questionEn: When a woman finishes wiping her head during Wudu and is wearing a Hijab/headscarf in a public place where non-mahram men are present, how do many jurists guide her?
optionsEn: She may wipe over her forelock/part of the head under the scarf and wipe over the headscarf (Khimar) if removing it exposes her, as Umm Salamah (RA) did
She must skip Salah until home
She must uncover fully in public
She must wash the scarf in a bucket
explanationEn: Narrations from Umm Salamah (RA) and ruling principles of removing hardship allow wiping over the front of the head and continuing over the Khimar when in public spaces.
reference: Al-Mughni (Ibn Qudamah); Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the purity of a deceased Muslim?
optionsEn: A dead Muslim is impure
The Muslim never becomes impure, alive or dead (Ibn Abbas RA)
Only martyrs are pure
Anyone who touches a deceased Muslim must do Tayammum
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) explicitly stated: 'Your dead do not become impure!'—the ritual washing (Ghusl al-Mayyit) is an act of honor and worship, not because the believer's body became Najis.

questionEn: Does vomiting unintentionally or coughing up phlegm break Wudu?
optionsEn: All schools agree any phlegm breaks Wudu
Only phlegm requires Ghusl
Phlegm does not break Wudu; for full-mouth vomiting scholars differ (Hanafis/Hanbalis say a mouthful breaks Wudu, while Shafi'is/Malikis say it does not)
Both require Tayammum
explanationEn: Scholars agree mucus/phlegm does not nullify Wudu, whereas they hold differing interpretations of Hadith narrations regarding whether vomiting a mouthful breaks Wudu.

questionEn: According to the Hadith of the Prophet ﷺ, which act requires performing Wudu if one washed their hands only after eating, vs before/after eating?
optionsEn: Eating dates breaks Wudu
Drinking water breaks Wudu
Using a spoon breaks Wudu
Washing hands before and after meals is called 'barakah (blessing) of food,' not ritual Wudu for Salah
explanationEn: In Arabic Hadith ('Al-wudu' qabla at-ta'am wa ba'dahu'), the word 'wudu' literally means washing the hands and mouth for cleanliness and blessing, not the prayer ablution.

questionEn: Which limb in Wudu requires washing ALL the way around, including the underside, arches, heels, and between every toe?
optionsEn: The feet
Only the big toe
Only the shins
Only the tops of the feet
explanationEn: Because people sometimes rush and splash only the top of the foot, the Prophet ﷺ warned specifically about dry heels and instructed running the little finger between the toes.

questionEn: In the Hadith of Al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad (RA), which finger did he observe the Prophet ﷺ using to clean between his toes during Wudu?
optionsEn: His thumb
His little finger (Khinsir)
His middle finger
His index finger
explanationEn: Al-Mustawrid (RA) narrated: 'I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rub between his toes with his little finger when performing Wudu.'

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Wudu inside a modern bathroom that contains both a sink and a toilet?
optionsEn: Strictly forbidden
Invalidates Wudu
Permissible; one may say Bismillah silently in the heart (or verbally before entering) and complete Wudu normally at the sink
Requires doing Tayammum afterward
explanationEn: Scholars clarify that when sinks and toilets share one room, Wudu at the sink is fully valid, and saying Bismillah silently in the heart or aloud just outside preserves reverence.

questionEn: What is 'Istibra'' in the etiquette of purification?
optionsEn: Washing the eyes with water
Saying Allahu Akbar before Wudu
Drying the face after Ghusl
Ensuring all residual drops of urine have ceased before performing Istinja' and Wudu
explanationEn: Istibra' means waiting briefly or taking gentle natural care after urinating so remaining drops do not soil clothes or invalidate Wudu right afterward.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 216 (chapter on shielding from urine)

questionEn: If a person notices a slight dampness later and suspects it might be a drop of urine, what practical Sunnah did Ibn Abbas (RA) and other Companions recommend to defeat anxiety?
optionsEn: Sprinkle a little clean water on the outside/inside of the undergarment after Wudu so any noticed coolness is attributed to that water unless proven otherwise
Take a full shower ten times a day
Stop drinking water
Burn the garment
explanationEn: Reported from the Prophet ﷺ (in Abu Dawud 168) and practiced by Ibn Umar, sprinkling water over the garment (Nadh) gives psychological relief against Satanic whispers of urine leakage.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 168; Sunan Ibn Majah 464

questionEn: What is the ruling on praying on a clean piece of cloth, carpet, wood, grass, or bare earth without a special 'prayer rug'?
optionsEn: Invalid without a patterned prayer mat
Completely valid as long as the surface itself is free from physical impurity (Najasah)
Only valid in Makkah
Only valid for voluntary prayers
explanationEn: A prayer rug is not a religious requirement; any clean ground or surface suffices because the whole earth was made a Masjid for this Ummah.

questionEn: Which two places did the Prophet ﷺ explicitly forbid offering Salah inside (unless necessary/excused)?
optionsEn: Living rooms and kitchens
Parks and gardens
Graveyards (except Janazah) and restrooms/bathrooms
Libraries and schools
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ stated: 'All of the earth is a Masjid except the graveyard and the bathhouse/restroom.'

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ forbid praying in camel resting/watering pens (Ma'atin al-Ibil) while permitting prayer in sheep pens?
optionsEn: Because camel hair is Najis
Because sheep are louder
Because camels eat grass
Because camels can be startled and unruly (and narrations link them to harshness/devils), disturbing the worshipper's tranquility
explanationEn: When asked about praying in sheep pens, he ﷺ said yes; when asked about camel pens, he ﷺ forbade it—not due to impurity of their dung, but due to distraction and danger.

questionEn: Which garment restriction did the Prophet ﷺ explain when asked about praying in a single garment (Thawb)?
optionsEn: None of you should pray in a single garment with nothing over his shoulders (must cover the shoulders if able, along with the Awrah)
You must wear at least three layers
Only white garments are valid
Belts are prohibited
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ instructed covering at least the area between navel and knees and draping part of the cloth over the shoulders if large enough.

questionEn: Is it permissible for a Muslim to wear a garment made by a non-Muslim or purchased new from a market without washing it first for Salah?
optionsEn: No, every garment must be washed seven times first
Yes; everything is presumed pure (Tahir) by default unless actual impurity is known with certainty
Only cotton is pure
Only handmade clothes are pure
explanationEn: The legal maxim in Islamic law is that all things—garments, floors, vessels—are pure by default until clear evidence of Najasah is established; Umar (RA) even performed Wudu from a Christian woman's water skin.

questionEn: If a person has a surgical stoma bag or urinary catheter, how do scholars advise them to pray?
optionsEn: They are excused from prayer forever
They must remove the medical device for every prayer
They treat it like the ruling of Istihadah/Ma'dhur: clean the external area if feasible, perform Wudu for each prayer time, and pray with the sealed bag
They only pray once a week
explanationEn: Islamic bioethics applies the Ma'dhur concession so patients with ostomy bags or catheters never abandon Salah and suffer no undue hardship.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Wudu with water that a donkey or mule has drunk from (Su'r al-Himar)?
optionsEn: It requires seven soil washes
It makes Wudu punishable
It breaks fasting

The Prophet ﷺ and Companions were asked about animals drinking from open water; most scholars regard their leftover saliva as pure (while Hanafis classify it as doubtful/Mashkuk, advising Tayammum if no other water exists)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about water in deserts visited by beasts and riding animals and replied: 'To them belongs what they drank, and to us belongs what remains—pure and purifying.'

questionEn: When performing Wudu, what is the Sunnah way to wipe the head if one has long hair reaching down the back?
optionsEn: Wipe from the front hairline to the back of the skull/nape and return to the front without needing to wipe all the way down hanging braids
Soak the entire length of the hair
Wash the braids with shampoo
Shave the head
explanationEn: Wiping applies to the head (the scalp/skull area), not hanging hair beyond the neck; full hair soaking belongs to Ghusl, not Wudu.

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:6 conclude the verse commanding Wudu, Ghusl, and Tayammum?
optionsEn: 'Allah commands severe hardship upon you'
'Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful'
'Perform ablution only in Madinah'
'Water is forbidden in winter'
explanationEn: The conclusion reminds believers that every rule of purification—including concessions like Tayammum—is an expression of Allah's mercy and favor.

questionEn: According to Sahih al-Bukhari, why did the Prophet ﷺ carry a small staff ('Anazah) or sit by a spear when praying outdoors?
optionsEn: To defend against birds
To draw lines in the sand
As a Sutrah (barrier) in front of him so passersby would not walk directly between him and his spot of prostration
To measure shadow length only
explanationEn: While technically a Salah etiquette, placing a Sutrah preserves the sanctity and cleanliness of the worshipper's prayer space outdoors.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Wudu with water that was used once before to wash off minor impurity (Ma' Musta'mal) when fresh water is available?
optionsEn: Always preferred over tap water
Impure like sewage
Required on Fridays
Scholars agree it is physically pure (Tahir), though most jurists say it cannot be used again to lift ritual impurity if fresh water is available
explanationEn: Water dripping from Wudu limbs (Ma' Musta'mal) is physically clean—the Companions even vied for drops of the Prophet's ﷺ Wudu water—though jurists distinguish its fitness for a second ritual Wudu.

questionEn: What does 'Taharah Ma'nawiyyah' (inner spiritual purification) refer to alongside physical Wudu?
optionsEn: Purifying the heart from shirk, hypocrisy, envy, malice, and sins through Tawbah and sincerity
Washing clothes with scented detergent
Polishing the shoes
Using only cold water
explanationEn: Scholars note that physical Taharah prepares the body to stand before Allah, while inner Taharah purifies the soul so the heart truly connects in Salah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the superiority of Miswak-accompanied prayer over prayer without Miswak (in narrations reported by Aishah RA)?
optionsEn: No difference
Prayer after using the Siwak has seventy times greater virtue than prayer without it (reported in Ahmad/Ibn Khuzaymah, authenticated by several scholars)
Only twice the reward
Applies only to Fajr
explanationEn: Using the Miswak cleans the mouth before reciting Allah's words; the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The Siwak is a purification for the mouth and a means of pleasing the Lord.'

questionEn: If a person washes their face, arms, wipes their head, and washes their feet in reverse order (starting with the feet and ending with the face), is their Wudu valid according to the majority (Shafi'i and Hanbali)?
optionsEn: Yes, order never matters in any school
Only valid at night
No, because Tartib (following the Qur'anic sequence) is an obligatory pillar of Wudu in the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools (whereas Hanafis/Malikis count it a strong Sunnah)
Requires Ghusl afterward
explanationEn: Shafi'i and Hanbali jurists cite the Qur'anic order plus the Prophet's ﷺ lifelong consistency ('Start with what Allah started with') to require Tartib; Hanafis and Malikis consider Wudu valid even out of order though neglecting Sunnah.

questionEn: During which landmark event in the Prophet's ﷺ life were the five daily prayers made obligatory?
optionsEn: Al-Isra wal-Mi'raj (the Night Journey and Ascension)
The Pledge of Al-Aqabah al-Kubra
The Conquest of Makkah
The Farewell Pilgrimage at Arafah
explanationEn: Unlike other acts of worship revealed on earth through Jibril (AS), the five daily prayers were prescribed directly during the Prophet's ﷺ ascension to the heavens in Al-Isra wal-Mi'raj, underscoring their supreme status.

questionEn: How many daily prayers were initially prescribed during the Night of Ascension before being reduced to five?
optionsEn: Ten prayers
Fifty prayers
Twenty-five prayers
Forty prayers
explanationEn: Allah initially prescribed fifty daily prayers; upon the repeated advice of Prophet Musa (AS) to ask for ease for the Ummah, Allah reduced them to five in performance while retaining the reward of fifty.

questionEn: When Allah reduced the fifty daily prayers to five, what reward did He promise for those who perform the five faithfully?
optionsEn: The reward of five prayers only
The reward of ten prayers
The reward of fifty prayers
The reward of seventy prayers
explanationEn: Allah declared that His decree does not change: the five daily prayers remain fifty in reward on the scale of good deeds, multiplying each prayer tenfold.

questionEn: Which prophet advised Prophet Muhammad ﷺ during the Mi'raj to return to Allah and request a reduction in the number of daily prayers?
optionsEn: Prophet Ibrahim (AS)
Prophet Isa (AS)
Prophet Yusuf (AS)
Prophet Musa (AS)
explanationEn: Prophet Musa (AS), whom the Prophet ﷺ met at the sixth heaven, urged him to ask Allah for lightness because he had tested the Children of Israel before and knew human weakness.

questionEn: In the famous hadith narrated by Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA), what did the Prophet ﷺ describe as the 'pillar' (amud) of Islam?
optionsEn: Salah (the ritual prayer)
Zakah (obligatory charity)
Fasting in Ramadan
Jihad in Allah's path
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA) that the head of the matter is Islam, its supporting pillar is Salah, and its peak is striving in the path of Allah.

questionEn: What will be the very first deed a servant is called to account for on the Day of Resurrection?
optionsEn: Honoring one's parents
The Salah (prayer)
Paying Zakah
Recitation of the Qur'an
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that the first action a servant is held accountable for on the Day of Judgment is Salah; if it is sound, the rest of one's deeds succeed, and if it is ruined, one fails and loses.

questionEn: According to Surah An-Nisa (4:103), how has Salah been prescribed upon the believers?
optionsEn: As a voluntary spiritual retreat
Only during times of peace and safety
At fixed, appointed times (kitaban mawqutan)
Once a week on the day of gathering
explanationEn: Allah states in Surah An-Nisa 4:103 that prayer has been decreed upon the believers as an obligation tied to fixed, scheduled times.

questionEn: Which verse of the Qur'an highlights that establishing Salah restrains a believer from immorality and wrongdoing?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:45
Surah Ta-Ha 20:14
Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:2
Surah Al-Ankabut 29:45
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ankabut 29:45 declares: 'Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater.'

questionEn: To what did the Prophet ﷺ compare the five daily prayers in terms of purifying a believer from sins?
optionsEn: A flowing river at one's door in which one bathes five times a day
Rain falling gently on barren soil every morning
A polished mirror reflecting morning sunlight
Fresh spring water stored in a sealed vessel
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ asked his Companions whether any dirt would remain on a person who bathed five times daily in a river outside his door, then explained that the five prayers similarly wash away sins.

questionEn: Which type of sins are expiated by performing the five daily prayers and Jumu'ah to Jumu'ah?
optionsEn: All sins including major sins without repentance
Minor sins, provided major sins are avoided
Only errors made while traveling
Only sins of the tongue
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ explicitly qualified the expiation between the five daily prayers and from Jumu'ah to Jumu'ah with the condition 'so long as major sins are avoided.'

questionEn: When Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) asked the Prophet ﷺ which deed is most beloved to Allah, what did the Prophet ﷺ mention first?
optionsEn: Striving in the path of Allah
Being dutiful to one's parents
Performing Salah at its appointed time
Giving charity in secret
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ ranked performing prayer at its proper time as the foremost beloved deed to Allah, followed by dutifulness to parents and then striving in Allah's cause.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:238), believers are commanded to guard the prayers and especially 'Salat al-Wusta' (the Middle Prayer). Which prayer did the Prophet ﷺ identify as Salat al-Wusta?
optionsEn: Fajr prayer
Dhuhr prayer
Maghrib prayer
Asr prayer
explanationEn: During the Battle of the Trench, the Prophet ﷺ specifically identified Salat al-Wusta as the Asr prayer when the enemy's siege delayed them from praying it until after sunset.

questionEn: What severe warning did the Prophet ﷺ give regarding a person who deliberately misses the Asr prayer?
optionsEn: It is as though he has lost his family and all his wealth
He must fast three consecutive days in expiation
His Wudu becomes invalid for the rest of the day
He cannot lead any congregational prayer for a year
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ compared missing the Asr prayer to losing one's family and property, and in another narration stated that the deeds of whoever abandons Asr become null and void.

questionEn: Which two prayers did the Prophet ﷺ refer to as 'al-Bardayn' (the two cool prayers), promising Paradise to whoever guards them?
optionsEn: Maghrib and Isha
Fajr and Asr
Dhuhr and Asr
Fajr and Isha
explanationEn: Fajr and Asr are called al-Bardayn because they fall during the cooler parts of the morning and late afternoon. The Prophet ﷺ promised that whoever observes them enters Paradise.

questionEn: Which two prayers did the Prophet ﷺ describe as the heaviest upon the hypocrites?
optionsEn: Dhuhr and Asr
Asr and Maghrib
Fajr and Isha
Maghrib and Fajr
explanationEn: Fajr and Isha occur during darkness when people rest in their beds and when insincere worshippers are unseen, making them heaviest upon hypocrites; the Prophet ﷺ noted they would crawl to them if they knew their reward.

questionEn: What spiritual reward is promised to one who prays Isha in congregation followed by Fajr in congregation?
optionsEn: The reward of fasting an entire month
The reward of performing one Umrah
Forgiveness of all past and future sins
Standing in night prayer for half the night for Isha, and the entire night for Fajr
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that praying Isha in congregation equals standing half the night in worship, and praying Fajr in congregation equals standing the entire night in worship.

questionEn: Under whose special protection (dhimmah) does a person enter when they perform the Fajr prayer?
optionsEn: The protection of Allah Himself
The protection of the Prophet's ﷺ household
The protection of the angels of mercy alone
The protection of the Muslim ruler
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ stated that whoever prays the morning (Fajr) prayer is under the protection (dhimmah) of Allah, warning people not to violate Allah's covenant of protection.

questionEn: During which two daily prayers do the angels of the night and the angels of the day meet and take shifts?
optionsEn: Dhuhr and Maghrib
Fajr and Asr
Maghrib and Isha
Dhuhr and Isha
explanationEn: Angels of the night and day succeed each other in shifts, gathering together at Fajr and Asr, after which the ascending angels report to Allah that they left His servants praying and found them praying.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ looked at the full moon and promised believers they would see their Lord on the Day of Judgment without crowding, which two prayers did he urge them never to miss?
optionsEn: The prayers after sunset and at midnight
Dhuhr and Jumu'ah
The prayer before sunrise (Fajr) and the prayer before sunset (Asr)
Witr and Tahajjud
explanationEn: Immediately after telling the Companions they would see their Lord as clearly as the full moon, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'If you are able not to be overcome regarding a prayer before sunrise and a prayer before sunset, do so.'

questionEn: What value did the Prophet ﷺ assign to the two Sunnah rak'ahs performed before the obligatory Fajr prayer?
optionsEn: Equal to one month of voluntary fasting
Equal to feeding sixty poor people
Equal to praying at Masjid al-Aqsa
Better than the entire world and everything in it
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ described the two brief Sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr as 'better than the world and whatever is in it,' showing why he never abandoned them even while traveling.

questionEn: What is meant by 'Ibrad' in relation to the Dhuhr prayer?
optionsEn: Delaying Dhuhr slightly in intense heat until the scorching heat subsides
Performing Wudu with cold water before Dhuhr
Praying Dhuhr on cool marble floors
Shortening Dhuhr to two rak'ahs during summer travel
explanationEn: Ibrad is the Prophetic Sunnah of delaying Dhuhr slightly during extreme summer heat so worshippers do not suffer distress, as the Prophet ﷺ explained that intense heat is from the raging breath of Hellfire.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ advise delaying Dhuhr slightly when the daytime heat becomes severe?
optionsEn: Because the sun stands still at midday in summer
Because the intensity of heat is from the breath (fayh) of Hellfire
Because shadows disappear completely in summer
Because workers cannot leave their fields before mid-afternoon
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'When the heat becomes intense, cool down by delaying the prayer, for the severity of heat is from the breath of Hellfire.'

questionEn: According to the Hadith of Jabir (RA), what stands directly between a believer and disbelief (kufr) or polytheism (shirk)?
optionsEn: Neglecting voluntary charity
Breaking a promise
Abandoning the Salah
Delaying Hajj without an excuse
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ stated: 'Between a man and shirk and kufr is the abandonment of Salah,' emphasizing the grave danger of neglecting the daily prayers.

questionEn: At what age did the Prophet ﷺ instruct parents to begin commanding their children to perform Salah?
optionsEn: Age five
Age ten
Age twelve
Age seven
explanationEn: Parents are instructed to command their children to pray when they reach seven years of age to cultivate the habit early, and to discipline them gently over neglecting it at age ten.

questionEn: If a Muslim oversleeps or genuinely forgets an obligatory prayer until its time passes, what is the required expiation?
optionsEn: Praying it as soon as one wakes up or remembers it
Fasting one day for each missed prayer
Giving food to ten needy people
Waiting until the same prayer time the next day to pray both together
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ declared: 'Whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, its expiation is to pray it as soon as he remembers it,' with no other penalty required.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ dislike sleeping before the Isha prayer and engaging in idle conversation after it?
optionsEn: Because sleeping before Isha breaks Wudu automatically
Out of concern that sleeping beforehand might cause missing Isha and talking afterward might cause missing Fajr
Because conversing at night invalidates the Isha reward
Because angels depart from homes where people talk after Isha
explanationEn: Scholars explain that the Prophet ﷺ disliked sleeping before Isha lest one sleep past its time, and disliked idle talk after Isha lest one stay up late and miss Fajr or Qiyam al-Layl.

questionEn: In Surah Ta-Ha (20:14), what purpose did Allah give Prophet Musa (AS) when commanding him to establish Salah?
optionsEn: For protection from Pharaoh's armies
To distinguish Israel from Egypt
For Allah's remembrance (li-dhikri)
To earn leadership over his tribe
explanationEn: Allah addressed Musa (AS) at the sacred valley of Tuwa saying: 'Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.'

questionEn: Which Surah opens its description of the successful believers by mentioning their humility (khushu') in Salah?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah
Surah Al-Anfal
Surah Al-Ma'un
Surah Al-Mu'minun
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mu'minun begins with: 'Certainly will the believers have succeeded: they who are during their prayer humbly submissive,' and concludes their traits in verse 9 with guarding their prayers.

questionEn: What criticism does Surah Al-Ma'un (107:4-5) level against those who are heedless (sahun) of their prayer?
optionsEn: They neglect their prayers' proper times and lack sincerity, praying only to be seen
They recite too loudly during silent prayers
They perform Wudu without using scented water
They stand too close together in congregational rows
explanationEn: Commentators note that being 'heedless of their prayer' in Surah Al-Ma'un refers to delaying prayers beyond their prescribed times, performing them carelessly, and showing off rather than seeking Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Ibrahim (14:40), what special supplication did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) make regarding Salah?
optionsEn: To be exempt from praying while traveling
To make himself and his descendants steadfast establishers of Salah
To pray only inside Masjid al-Haram
To double the reward of Friday prayer
explanationEn: Prophet Ibrahim (AS) prayed: 'My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.'

questionEn: In Surah Ta-Ha (20:132), alongside enjoining prayer upon one's family and remaining steadfast in it, what does Allah remind the believer regarding provision (rizq)?
optionsEn: Provision increases only through trade after Fajr
Prayer replaces the need to seek livelihood
Allah does not ask the believer for provision; rather, Allah provides for him
Provision is tied exclusively to praying Dhuhr early
explanationEn: Allah says in Surah Ta-Ha 20:132: 'And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast therein. We ask you not for provision; We provide for you, and the good outcome is for righteousness.'

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Baqarah (2:45) instruct believers to seek help in facing life's trials?
optionsEn: Through wealth and alliances
Through travel and migration
Through silence and fasting alone
Through patience and Salah
explanationEn: Allah commands: 'And seek help through patience and prayer; and indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive.'

questionEn: Which two traits did Luqman (AS) advise his son to combine immediately after commanding him to establish Salah?
optionsEn: Enjoining good, forbidding wrong, and bearing adversity with patience
Building mosques and digging wells
Memorizing poetry and learning astronomy
Fasting Mondays and giving gold in charity
explanationEn: In Surah Luqman 31:17, Luqman counsels his son: 'O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you.'

questionEn: In the Hadith of the five pillars narrated by Ibn Umar (RA), where does establishing Salah rank after the Shahadah (testimony of faith)?
optionsEn: Fifth
Second
Third
Fourth
explanationEn: Islam is built upon five pillars: testifying that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is His Messenger, establishing Salah, paying Zakah, performing Hajj, and fasting Ramadan.

questionEn: What happens to the reward of a person who guards the five daily prayers with proper Wudu, timing, bowing, and prostration, according to the hadith of Ubadah ibn as-Samit (RA)?
optionsEn: He is exempt from Zakah for that year
He is guaranteed worldly wealth
He has a promise (ahd) from Allah to enter Paradise
His family members are excused from accountability
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ stated that Allah has obligated five prayers, and whoever perfects their Wudu, prays them on time, and completes their bowing, prostration, and humility has a binding promise from Allah to forgive him and admit him to Paradise.

questionEn: During the final illness of the Prophet ﷺ, what repeated counsel did he emphasize to his Ummah as his soul was departing?
optionsEn: Conquering distant lands
Memorizing genealogy
Compiling his personal belongings
Guarding the Salah and treating those under one's care kindly
explanationEn: Among the Prophet's ﷺ final parting words to his Ummah were: 'As-Salah, as-Salah (the prayer, the prayer), and fear Allah regarding those whom your right hands possess.'

questionEn: Which Qur'anic passage links the times of glorifying Allah to the morning, evening, late afternoon, and noon?
optionsEn: Surah Ar-Rum 30:17-18
Surah Al-Kawthar 108:2
Surah Al-Fatihah 1:5
Surah Al-Ikhlas 112:1-4
explanationEn: In Surah Ar-Rum 30:17-18, Allah mentions glorifying Him when you enter the evening (Maghrib/Isha), when you enter the morning (Fajr), in the late afternoon (Asr), and when you reach noon (Dhuhr).

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say happens to a believer's sins when he stands up to pray?
optionsEn: They remain recorded until Hajj
They are placed upon his head and shoulders and fall off every time he bows or prostrates
They transfer to the Imam leading the prayer
They disappear only after completing twenty rak'ahs
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ explained that when a servant stands to pray, his sins are brought and placed on his head and shoulders, and each time he performs Ruku' or Sujud, they fall away from him.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say distinguishes the covenant between believers and unbelievers?
optionsEn: Wearing specific garments
Knowing the Arabic alphabet
Establishing the Salah
Fasting on the first day of Muharram
explanationEn: Buraydah (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The covenant that distinguishes between us and them is the prayer; whoever abandons it has fallen into disbelief.'

questionEn: How does Allah describe the state of people who come after the prophets and abandon prayer while following desires in Surah Maryam (19:59)?
optionsEn: They will be given extra time to repent after death
They will only miss optional rewards
They will still lead the believers on the Sirat
They will meet destruction (ghayyan) unless they repent and do righteous deeds
explanationEn: Surah Maryam 19:59 warns that generations who neglected prayer and pursued lusts will encounter 'ghayy' (evil perdition/a valley in Hellfire), followed in verse 60 by an exception for those who repent and believe.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ instruct Muslims to do regarding the five daily prayers before any major hardship or distress?
optionsEn: Turn immediately to Salah for solace and relief, as he used to say 'Give us comfort through it, O Bilal'
Postpone prayer until the distress completely passes
Combine all five prayers into one session
Pray silently in one's mind without physical movement
explanationEn: Whenever a serious matter troubled the Prophet ﷺ, he hastened to prayer, and he used to tell Bilal (RA): 'Establish the prayer and give us comfort through it.'

questionEn: In the narration of Abu Dharr (RA), if a person prays Fajr and Asr with full devotion, what ultimate blessing is mentioned in connection with seeing Allah?
optionsEn: A palace built of coral in Madinah
Nothing will deprive him of gazing upon Allah's Countenance without crowding on the Day of Resurrection
Immunity from physical fatigue in old age
Exemption from questioning in the grave
explanationEn: In the hadith of Jarir ibn Abdullah (RA), the Prophet ﷺ connected guarding the prayers before sunrise (Fajr) and before sunset (Asr) with not being deprived of seeing Allah's Face in the Hereafter.

questionEn: Who descended from heaven to lead the Prophet ﷺ in prayer over two consecutive days at the Ka'bah to teach the earliest and latest boundaries of all five prayer times?
optionsEn: Angel Mika'il (AS)
Angel Israfil (AS)
Angel Jibril (AS)
Angel Malik (AS)
explanationEn: Jibril (AS) led the Prophet ﷺ at the earliest limit of each prayer on the first day and at the latest limit on the second day, then declared: 'The time for prayer is between these two limits.'

questionEn: What distinguishes Fajr Sadiq (the true dawn), which marks the start of the Fajr prayer, from Fajr Kadhib (the false dawn)?
optionsEn: Fajr Sadiq is a vertical pillar of light that disappears quickly
Fajr Sadiq appears only in the western sky
Fajr Sadiq is accompanied by complete brightness like midday
Fajr Sadiq spreads horizontally along the eastern horizon and steadily brightens
explanationEn: Fajr Kadhib is a vertical streak resembling a wolf's tail followed by darkness, whereas Fajr Sadiq spreads horizontally across the eastern horizon and steadily increases until sunrise.

questionEn: During Fajr Kadhib (the false dawn), what is the Islamic ruling regarding Fajr prayer and Suhoor for fasting?
optionsEn: Fajr prayer is not yet valid, and eating Suhoor remains permissible
Fajr prayer becomes obligatory immediately, and Suhoor becomes forbidden
Only Sunnah of Fajr is valid, not the Fard
Both Fajr and Maghrib may be prayed
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ clarified that the vertical false dawn neither prohibits food and drink for the fasting person nor marks the entrance of Fajr prayer time; only the horizontal true dawn does.

questionEn: When does the prescribed time for the Fajr prayer come to an end?
optionsEn: When the sun reaches the height of a spear
As soon as the upper edge of the sun begins to rise above the horizon
Twenty minutes after sunrise
At the zenith (Zawal)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ explicitly stated in the comprehensive hadith of prayer times: 'The time of the morning prayer (Fajr) is from the appearance of dawn so long as the sun has not begun to rise.'

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about a person who manages to complete one full rak'ah of Fajr before the sun rises?
optionsEn: The prayer is completely invalid and must be repeated later
It counts only as a voluntary prayer
He has caught the Fajr prayer within its time, and must complete the second rak'ah
He must perform Sujud al-Sahw twice at the end
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that whoever catches one rak'ah of Fajr before sunrise has caught the Fajr prayer in time, though intentionally delaying Fajr until sunrise is sinful.

questionEn: What does the term 'Ghalas' refer to in the Prophetic practice of praying Fajr?
optionsEn: Praying Fajr right before the sun rises
Praying Fajr silently on Fridays
Combining Fajr with Dhuhr while traveling
Praying Fajr early while some pre-dawn darkness still lingers
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to pray Fajr in Ghalas (early dawn while darkness still remained), such that believing women wrapped in their cloaks returned home unrecognized in the dim light.

questionEn: How do scholars reconcile the hadith 'Brighten (Asfiru) with the Fajr prayer, for its reward is greater' with the Prophet's ﷺ regular practice of praying Fajr early in Ghalas?
optionsEn: Start in Ghalas after verifying true dawn and prolong recitation until daylight begins to brighten, or ensure certainty of dawn
Wait until after sunrise before beginning Fajr
Pray Fajr in Ghalas only in winter and after sunrise in summer
Pray one rak'ah in darkness and the second rak'ah after sunrise
explanationEn: Many scholars explain that the Prophet ﷺ began Fajr early in Ghalas and recited long surahs so he finished as light spread (Isfar), while others (like the Hanafis) recommend Isfar especially so people arrive safely and dawn is unmistakable.

questionEn: What astronomical event marks the exact beginning of the Dhuhr prayer time?
optionsEn: When the sun reaches its highest point directly overhead
Zawal—when the sun passes its meridian/zenith and begins declining westward
When shadows reach twice the height of objects
Exactly at 12:00 PM clock time year-round
explanationEn: Dhuhr begins at Zawal, the moment the sun crosses the meridian and begins leaning toward the west, causing shadows to lengthen eastward.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse refers to the decline of the sun (Duluk ash-Shams) as a marker for daily prayer times?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Fatihah 1:4
Surah Al-Muzzammil 73:2
Surah Al-Isra 17:78
Surah Al-Alaq 96:1
explanationEn: Surah Al-Isra 17:78 instructs: 'Establish prayer at the decline of the sun (from its meridian) until the darkness of the night, and the recitation of dawn.'

questionEn: According to the majority of jurists (Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali), when does the time of Dhuhr end and Asr begin?
optionsEn: When the sun turns pale yellow
When an object's shadow reaches half its height
Exactly three hours after Zawal
When an object's shadow equals its own height (in addition to any shadow present at Zawal)
explanationEn: In the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) and the Jibril (AS) narration, Dhuhr lasts until a man's shadow becomes equal to his height (plus the zenith shadow, fay' az-zawal), at which point Asr begins.

questionEn: In the Hanafi school of jurisprudence, when does the Asr prayer time begin?
optionsEn: When an object's shadow becomes twice its height (beyond the zenith shadow)
When an object's shadow equals half its height
Thirty minutes after sunrise
As soon as the sun turns bright red
explanationEn: While Imam Abu Yusuf and Imam Muhammad aligned with the 1x shadow boundary, the relied-upon view attributed to Imam Abu Hanifah places the end of Dhuhr and start of Asr at twice the object's height (beyond the zenith shadow).

questionEn: What is 'Fay' az-Zawal' when calculating the start of Asr using shadows?
optionsEn: The darkness just before sunset
The minimum shadow an object already casts at exact solar noon (zenith), which must be subtracted or added as the baseline
The shadow cast by the Ka'bah at midnight
The reflection of clouds before rain
explanationEn: Outside the tropics on most days of the year, an upright stick still casts a short northward shadow at solar noon; that baseline shadow (fay' az-zawal) is excluded when measuring when the shadow grows by 1x the stick's height.

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim 612, until what point does the preferred/choice time (waqt al-ikhtiyar) of Asr continue?
optionsEn: Until the sun sets completely
Until shadows reach three times object height
So long as the sun has not turned yellow (isfirar)
Until the moon appears in the eastern sky
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The time for Asr continues as long as the sun has not turned yellow.' Delaying beyond yellowing without excuse is severely censured, though the time of necessity extends until sunset.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ describe the person who delays Asr until the sun turns yellow and is low between the horns of Shaytan, then quickly pecks four rak'ahs?
optionsEn: As a cautious traveler
As a pious ascetic
As a forgetful beginner
As performing the prayer of a hypocrite
explanationEn: Anas (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ called delaying Asr until the sun is nearly setting and rushing through four rapid prostrations without remembering Allah except a little 'the prayer of the hypocrite.'

questionEn: If a person begins Asr late and completes one full rak'ah before sunset, what is the ruling on his Asr prayer?
optionsEn: He has caught Asr in its time and must finish the remaining three rak'ahs
His prayer is invalid and turns into Maghrib
He must restart Asr from the beginning after Maghrib
Only one rak'ah counts and the rest are Nafl
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever catches one rak'ah of Asr before the sun sets has caught Asr,' meaning the prayer counts as timely (ada') rather than missed (qada'), though intentional delay until sunset is sinful.

questionEn: What defines the exact onset of the Maghrib prayer time?
optionsEn: When the sun turns orange near the horizon
When the entire disk of the sun disappears below the horizon
Twenty minutes after sunset
When the first stars become visible
explanationEn: Maghrib enters the moment the entire solar disk sets below the horizon, regardless of remaining twilight glow in the sky.

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim 612, what celestial sign marks the end of Maghrib and the start of Isha?
optionsEn: The disappearance of the yellow glow only
The rising of the full moon
The disappearance of the twilight (al-shafaq)
Two hours exactly after sunset
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The time of the sunset (Maghrib) prayer continues so long as the twilight (al-shafaq) has not disappeared.' Once it disappears, Isha begins.

questionEn: What does 'al-Shafaq' refer to according to the majority of scholars when determining the end of Maghrib and start of Isha?
optionsEn: The pale blue haze at noon
The green glow over the ocean
The blackness of midnight
The red twilight glow remaining on the western horizon after sunset
explanationEn: The majority of scholars (Malik, Shafi'i, Ahmad, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad) define al-shafaq as the red afterglow on the western horizon, while Imam Abu Hanifah took the precaution of the white glow that follows it.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about hastening the Maghrib prayer versus delaying it until stars fill the sky?
optionsEn: His Ummah will remain upon sound nature (fitrah) so long as they do not delay Maghrib until the stars appear densely
Maghrib should always be delayed until forty stars appear
Hastening Maghrib is only for travelers
Delaying Maghrib doubles its reward
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ praised praying Maghrib promptly after sunset and warned against delaying it until the stars mesh across the sky (ishtibak an-nujum).

questionEn: According to the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) in Sahih Muslim, when does the preferred/choice time (waqt al-ikhtiyar) of Isha end?
optionsEn: Two hours after sunset
At the middle of the night (Islamic midnight)
At dawn (Fajr)
One hour after sunset
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ stated: 'The time of the night prayer (Isha) is up to half of the night (nisf al-layl).' While many scholars consider the time of necessity to extend until Fajr, intentionally delaying Isha past Islamic midnight is prohibited or strongly disliked.

questionEn: How is 'Islamic midnight' (the end of Isha's choice time) calculated?
optionsEn: Always 12:00 AM on the wall clock
Six hours after Dhuhr
The exact midpoint between sunset (Maghrib) and true dawn (Fajr)
The midpoint between sunset and sunrise
explanationEn: In Islamic law, the night begins at sunset (Maghrib) and ends at true dawn (Fajr Sadiq); therefore, Islamic midnight is halfway between Maghrib and Fajr, which varies by season.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ refrain from making it a regular rule to delay the Isha prayer until a third or half of the night?
optionsEn: Because the mosque lamps lacked oil
Because Jibril (AS) prohibited delaying Isha
Because Isha becomes invalid after the first third of the night
Out of compassion so as not to impose hardship on his Ummah
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ once delayed Isha until late at night while the Companions waited, he remarked: 'Were it not that I would overburden my Ummah, I would have commanded them to pray it at this hour.'

questionEn: On the second day when Jibril (AS) taught the Prophet ﷺ the latest times of prayer, at what point did he lead him in Isha?
optionsEn: When one-third of the night had passed
Just before sunrise
Immediately at sunset
At the last sixth of the night
explanationEn: In the narration of Jibril (AS) leading the Prophet ﷺ, on the second day he prayed Isha when the first third of the night had passed, establishing the upper limit of its preferred period.

questionEn: What is the ruling on the time between the disappearance of Fajr (sunrise) and Zawal (solar noon)?
optionsEn: It belongs to the Fajr prayer time
No obligatory daily prayer has its scheduled time during this morning period
It is the time for Dhuhr prayer
It is the time for Witr prayer
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ stated in Sahih Muslim 612 that when the sun rises, refrain from prayer until it rises higher; there is no Fard prayer prescribed between sunrise and Zawal (though Duha is a cherished Sunnah).

questionEn: If a menstruating woman's bleeding stops just enough time before sunset to say Takbirat al-Ihram (or pray one rak'ah), what is the majority view on her prayers for that day?
optionsEn: She owes no prayers for that day
She must make up Fajr, Dhuhr, and Asr
She must perform Asr (and according to many jurists, Dhuhr as well since Dhuhr and Asr share a combined time in excuse)
She waits until the next day to resume praying
explanationEn: Jurists agree she catches Asr if purified before sunset; Hanbalis, Malikis, and Shafi'is (following reports from Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf and Ibn Abbas) also hold she prays Dhuhr with Asr, and similarly Maghrib with Isha if purified before Fajr.

questionEn: In high-latitude regions during summer where twilight (Shafaq) never fully disappears between sunset and Fajr, how did the Prophet's ﷺ guidance in the Hadith of Dajjal instruct Muslims to handle prayer times?
optionsEn: Skip Isha and Fajr for the entire summer
Pray all five prayers together once a week
Wait until autumn to make up the prayers
Estimate (qadru) the prayer times based on normal days or the nearest moderate latitudes
explanationEn: When the Companions asked how to pray during a day like a year at the time of Dajjal, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Estimate for it its due measure (qadru lahu qadrahu),' forming the basis for scholars' fatwas on abnormal high-latitude prayer schedules.

questionEn: What is the ruling on deliberately praying an obligatory prayer before its prescribed time enters?
optionsEn: It is invalid and does not discharge the obligation, even if performed in congregation
It is valid as long as it is within fifteen minutes of the time
It is valid for travelers only
It is merely disliked (Makruh) but valid
explanationEn: Entry of the prescribed time is a strict prerequisite (Shart) for the validity of an obligatory prayer (Surah An-Nisa 4:103); praying before the time enters is invalid and must be performed again once the time begins.

questionEn: According to the majority of scholars, what is the ruling on performing an obligatory prayer before its time if one mistakenly thought the time had already entered?
optionsEn: It counts as the Fard prayer due to good intention
It counts only as a voluntary (Nafl) prayer, and the Fard must still be prayed once the time actually enters
One must give expiation of feeding a poor person
It counts as valid if the Adhan had been mistakenly called
explanationEn: Because the condition (Shart) of time entry was absent, the prayer does not count as the obligatory Fard; rather, the person is rewarded for a voluntary prayer and must perform the Fard when its true time begins.

questionEn: At what exact point is solar noon (the moment just before Zawal) determined?
optionsEn: When an object's shadow is longest
When the sun rises 45 degrees above the eastern horizon
When the sun reaches its highest point in the sky and shadows reach their shortest length before shifting east
When the moon aligns with the western horizon
explanationEn: Before midday, shadows shrink westward; at exact solar noon (istiwa), the shadow stops shrinking; the instant the shadow begins growing eastward marks Zawal and the entry of Dhuhr.

questionEn: Why does the duration between Fajr and sunrise vary significantly between summer and winter in temperate latitudes?
optionsEn: Because the sun changes its speed around the earth
Because Fajr is fixed at 5:00 AM only in winter
Because Maghrib replaces Fajr in winter
Because the earth's axial tilt alters the angle at which the sun approaches the eastern horizon, changing twilight duration
explanationEn: Because prayer times follow true astronomical positions of the sun (dawn depression angle, zenith, shadow length, sunset, twilight depression angle), seasonal tilt changes both day length and twilight duration.

questionEn: If a person is uncertain whether the time of a prayer has ended or whether it is still within the time, what principle applies?
optionsEn: One does not pray a Fard until reasonably certain its time has entered; once in time, certainty persists until proven ended
Always assume the time has passed and skip it
Flip a coin to decide between two prayers
Wait until the next day to pray both
explanationEn: In Islamic legal maxims, certainty is not removed by doubt: one must be reasonably certain (by Adhan, reliable timetable, or observation) that a prayer time has entered before praying it.

questionEn: Which prayer's time starts immediately when Dhuhr's time ends without any gap between them?
optionsEn: Fajr
Asr
Maghrib
Isha
explanationEn: Dhuhr and Asr are consecutive with no gap between them (the end of Dhuhr is the start of Asr), just as Maghrib and Isha are consecutive (the disappearance of twilight ends Maghrib and begins Isha).

questionEn: Which two pairs of daily prayers have an intervening period between them during which no Fard prayer time is active?
optionsEn: Dhuhr and Asr, and Maghrib and Isha
Asr and Maghrib
Fajr to Dhuhr (between sunrise and Zawal), and Isha to Fajr (if Isha ends before dawn, or only Fajr-to-Dhuhr if Isha extends to Fajr)
Dhuhr and Maghrib only
explanationEn: Between sunrise (end of Fajr) and Zawal (start of Dhuhr) there is no obligatory prayer time; similarly, in the view that Isha's true end is Islamic midnight, there is an interval from midnight until Fajr.

questionEn: When praying Fajr in a dark room without a clock, what physical sign outside confirms that Fajr Sadiq has entered?
optionsEn: A faint vertical cone of light in the west
Complete disappearance of all stars
Dew forming on grass at midnight
A horizontal band of white light spreading along the eastern horizon
explanationEn: Fajr Sadiq appears as a horizontal white light spreading north-to-south along the eastern horizon (described in Qur'an 2:187 as the 'white thread of dawn distinct from the black thread of night').

questionEn: How does Surah Hud (11:114) instruct regarding establishing prayer at the two ends of the day and approaches of the night?
optionsEn: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and the early hours of the night, for good deeds erase bad deeds
Pray only at sunrise and midnight
Pray twice a week at sunset
Establish prayer only after sunset
explanationEn: Surah Hud 11:114 commands establishing prayer at the two ends of the day (Fajr, Dhuhr/Asr) and in the near parts of the night (Maghrib and Isha), affirming that good deeds drive away evil deeds.

questionEn: If a person is at the top of a tall skyscraper or high mountain where the sun is still visible even though people at street level below have seen it set, when does Maghrib begin for the person at the top?
optionsEn: When street-level clocks reach sunset time
When the sun actually disappears from his own elevated horizon
Thirty minutes before street-level sunset
At solar noon
explanationEn: Because prayer and fasting boundaries depend on each person's observed horizon, someone on a high mountain or tall tower who still sees the sun above the horizon must wait until it sets from their vantage point.

questionEn: On an airplane flying westward (chasing the sun), if the sun stays above the horizon for many hours longer than normal, how do the prayer times apply to passengers?
optionsEn: They follow the departure city's clock regardless of sun position
They are excused from all prayers while airborne
They follow the actual position of the sun outside the aircraft as each time enters
They pray all five prayers at boarding
explanationEn: Jurists agree that passengers on a plane pray according to the actual astronomical signs outside the aircraft—Zawal, shadow/afternoon, sunset, and dawn—because times are tied to the sun's movement relative to the worshipper.

questionEn: What is the ruling on praying Isha before its time enters simply because someone has a long shift or early flight and fears missing it?
optionsEn: Permissible anytime after Maghrib Adhan
Permissible for workers in hospitals
Permissible once the sky turns dark blue
Impermissible to pray before Isha enters, though a legitimate traveler may combine Maghrib and Isha (Jam' Taqdim) at Maghrib time
explanationEn: A resident may not pray Isha before its time begins; only those with a valid Shar'i concession for combining prayers (such as a traveler or in severe hardship/rain where Jam' is valid) may perform Jam' Taqdim at Maghrib time.

questionEn: How did Jibril (AS) pray Maghrib on both the first and second days when teaching the Prophet ﷺ the boundaries of prayer times?
optionsEn: At the exact same time—immediately when the sun set—signifying the urgency and narrow preferred focus of Maghrib
Once at sunset and once at midnight
Once before sunset and once after Fajr
Only on the first day
explanationEn: In Jibril's (AS) two-day demonstration (Abu Dawud 393, Tirmidhi 149), he prayed Maghrib at the exact same moment right after sunset on both days (while Ibn Amr's hadith in Muslim 612 clarifies Maghrib's full window extends until twilight disappears).

questionEn: What is the astronomical solar depression angle commonly used by major Islamic bodies (such as Umm al-Qura and MWL) to mark Fajr Sadiq and Isha?
optionsEn: 0 degrees below the horizon
Between 15 and 19 degrees below the horizon (commonly 18 degrees in MWL / 18.5 in Umm al-Qura)
45 degrees below the horizon
90 degrees below the horizon
explanationEn: While jurists look to visual true dawn and disappearance of twilight, standard astronomical calculations approximate Fajr Sadiq and Isha when the sun is roughly 15° to 18.5° below the horizon.

questionEn: Which term describes the preferred early period of Asr before the sun turns yellow, versus the period after it turns yellow?
optionsEn: Waqt al-Fajr vs Waqt al-Dhuhr
Waqt al-Qada vs Waqt al-Nafl
Waqt al-Ikhtiyar (choice time) vs Waqt al-Darurah (time of necessity)
Waqt al-Istiwa vs Waqt al-Zawal
explanationEn: Scholars distinguish between Waqt al-Ikhtiyar (when one may freely choose to pray Asr, before yellowing) and Waqt al-Darurah (from yellowing until sunset, sinful to delay to without excuse, yet valid if prayed then).

questionEn: Why is the time of Dhuhr sometimes called 'al-Ula' (the first prayer) in early Islamic narrations?
optionsEn: Because it was revealed first in Makkah
Because it has only one rak'ah
Because women pray it first before men
Because it was the very first prayer Jibril (AS) led the Prophet ﷺ in after Isra wal-Mi'raj
explanationEn: Jibril (AS) first descended to teach the Prophet ﷺ the prayer times at Dhuhr (right after Zawal), which is why several early narrations refer to Dhuhr as 'al-Ula' (the first).

questionEn: If a person enters the masjid when the sun has just set, hears the Maghrib Adhan, and delays praying Maghrib until the red twilight vanishes without excuse, what happens?
optionsEn: Maghrib's time has expired and he has sinned by delaying it past its window, so he must pray it immediately as Qada
Maghrib merges automatically into a 7-rak'ah Isha
It remains within Maghrib's preferred time
He is excused if he was talking in the courtyard
explanationEn: Once the red twilight vanishes, Maghrib's prescribed window closes and Isha begins. Delaying Maghrib past twilight without an excuse (like travel/rain combining) is a sin requiring repentance and immediate Qada.

questionEn: When praying in congregation during summer's extreme heat in Makkah or Madinah, what should an individual do if the mosque prays Dhuhr right at Zawal rather than waiting for Ibrad?
optionsEn: Refuse to join the congregation and pray alone later
Join the congregation in the mosque, since praying in congregation takes precedence over individual Ibrad
Pray Asr instead of Dhuhr with them
Sit in the back row without joining until an hour later
explanationEn: Scholars note that Ibrad (cooling down Dhuhr) is a collective Sunnah for the congregation's ease; if the mosque holds congregation early, a believer joins the congregation for its greater obligation and reward.

questionEn: According to the hadith of Uqbah ibn Amir (RA), how many strict short intervals during the day did the Prophet ﷺ forbid praying voluntary prayers or burying the dead?
optionsEn: Two times
Five times
Three times
Seven times
explanationEn: Uqbah ibn Amir (RA) reported three exact times when the Prophet ﷺ forbade praying or burying the dead: when the sun starts rising until it rises high, at exact zenith until it declines, and when the sun inclines to set until it sets.

questionEn: How high must the sun rise after sunrise before the strict morning prohibition on voluntary prayer ends?
optionsEn: Directly overhead at zenith
Forty-five degrees above the horizon
Halfway to solar noon
The height of a spear (qadr rumh), roughly 12 to 15 minutes after sunrise
explanationEn: In the hadith of Amr ibn Abasah (RA), the Prophet ﷺ told him to refrain from prayer at sunrise until the sun rises to the height of one or two spears above the horizon (roughly 12–15 minutes).

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ prohibit performing voluntary prayers precisely as the sun rises and sets?
optionsEn: Because the sun rises and sets between the two horns of Shaytan, and sun-worshippers prostrate to it at those moments
Because angels sleep at sunrise and sunset
Because Wudu cannot be performed during twilight
Because the Qiblah direction shifts during sunrise and sunset
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ explained to Amr ibn Abasah (RA) that at sunrise and sunset the sun is between the horns of Shaytan and disbelievers prostrate to it, so Muslims avoid resembling sun-worshippers.

questionEn: What is the second of the three strict forbidden times mentioned by Uqbah ibn Amir (RA), occurring around midday?
optionsEn: One hour after sunrise
When the sun stands directly at its zenith (istiwa / qaim al-zahira) just before declining westward
Immediately after Dhuhr Fard
When shadows equal twice an object's height
explanationEn: Right before Zawal, when the sun is at its zenith (lasting roughly 5–10 minutes), voluntary prayer is prohibited until the sun declines westward—because, as Amr ibn Abasah's hadith notes, Hellfire is stoked at that hour.

questionEn: In addition to the three short astronomical forbidden times, which two broader daily periods carry a prohibition on unrestricted voluntary (Nafl Mutlaq) prayers?
optionsEn: After Dhuhr until Asr, and after Isha until midnight
Between Maghrib and Isha, and before Fajr
After praying Fajr until sunrise, and after praying Asr until sunset
Between midnight and Fajr
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ forbade unrestricted voluntary prayers after Fajr until the sun rises high, and after Asr until the sun sets.

questionEn: In the morning prohibition after Fajr, what triggers the start of the prohibited period for an individual worshipper?
optionsEn: The moment the Fajr Adhan finishes
Midnight
An hour before dawn
Once the person has prayed the Fajr prayer (or from Fajr Sadiq itself for extra Nafl beyond Fajr's two Sunnahs)
explanationEn: Before praying Fajr Fard, the two Sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr (and Tahajjud/Witr if delayed before Fajr) are prayed; once a person performs the Fajr Fard prayer, general Nafl prayers are prohibited until after sunrise.

questionEn: Similarly, if a person has not yet prayed Asr during the afternoon, is he permitted to pray Tahiyyat al-Masjid or Sunnah before Asr?
optionsEn: Yes, because the afternoon restriction in 'no prayer after Asr' is tied to having prayed Asr (until the sun turns yellow/inclines to set)
No, no prayer is allowed after Dhuhr
Only on Mondays and Thursdays
Only while seated
explanationEn: The hadith states 'There is no prayer after the Asr prayer until the sun sets,' so a person who has not yet prayed Asr may pray voluntary prayers prior to praying Asr, provided it is not during the strict sunset prohibition.

questionEn: What is the ruling on making up a missed obligatory (Fard) prayer if a person wakes up or remembers it during one of the forbidden times?
optionsEn: He must wait until the forbidden time passes before praying it
He should pray it immediately even during a forbidden time, based on the command to pray whenever remembered
He is exempt from making up that prayer
He must pray only half of its rak'ahs
explanationEn: The Prophet's ﷺ command 'Whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, let him pray it when he remembers it' is general and overrides the restriction on voluntary prayers.

questionEn: If a person arrives at the mosque late for Fajr and joins the Fard prayer without having prayed the two Sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr beforehand, what did the Prophet ﷺ tacitly approve?
optionsEn: Praying the two Sunnah rak'ahs inside the Fard rows
Never making up the Sunnah of Fajr
Praying the two Sunnah rak'ahs immediately after the Fajr Fard prayer (or waiting until after sunrise)
Replacing them with two rak'ahs after Asr
explanationEn: When Qays ibn Amr (RA) prayed the two Sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr right after the Fajr Fard prayer, the Prophet ﷺ asked what they were and remained silent upon hearing they were the missed Fajr Sunnah, indicating permissibility.

questionEn: Which sacred act of worship in Makkah is explicitly exempted from all forbidden prayer times around the clock?
optionsEn: Salat al-Duha
Salat al-Istikharah
Salat al-Tasbih
The two rak'ahs after Tawaf around the Ka'bah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed Banu Abd Manaf: 'Do not prevent anyone from circumambulating this House and praying at any hour of the night or day he wishes,' making the two rak'ahs of Tawaf valid at any time.

questionEn: Upon entering a masjid after praying Asr (while the sun is still bright and high), how do the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools view praying the two rak'ahs of Tahiyyat al-Masjid?
optionsEn: Permissible and recommended because it is a prayer with an immediate cause (Dhat Sabab)
Strictly forbidden under all circumstances
Valid only if prayed in one rak'ah
Obligatory only on Tuesdays
explanationEn: Shafi'is and many Hanbalis (including Ibn Taymiyyah) hold that prayers with a specific immediate cause (Dhawat al-Asbab), such as Tahiyyat al-Masjid, Sunnah of Wudu, and Eclipse prayer, are allowed after Fajr and Asr, whereas Hanafis and Malikis restrict them.

questionEn: If a person has already prayed Fajr or Asr at home and then enters a mosque where the congregation is currently praying that same Fard prayer, what did the Prophet ﷺ instruct him to do?
optionsEn: Sit outside until they finish
Join and pray with them, and it will count as a voluntary prayer for him
Perform Tawaf around the courtyard instead
Wait until the sun sets before entering
explanationEn: At Masjid al-Khayf in Mina, the Prophet ﷺ saw two men who had prayed Fajr in their tents and did not join the congregation; he instructed them to pray with the congregation whenever they encounter one, counting it as Nafl.

questionEn: What special action did the Prophet ﷺ perform after Asr when a delegation kept him busy from praying the two Sunnah rak'ahs after Dhuhr?
optionsEn: He dropped the two Sunnah rak'ahs permanently
He prayed them at midnight instead
He prayed those two rak'ahs after Asr, and maintained them consistently thereafter
He gave charity in their place
explanationEn: When the Banu Tamim or Abd al-Qays delegation distracted the Prophet ﷺ from the two Sunnah rak'ahs after Dhuhr, he prayed them after Asr and—because he loved to keep up any righteous deed he began—continued praying them after Asr privately.

questionEn: Regarding the funeral prayer (Salat al-Janazah) during the three strict forbidden times (sunrise, zenith, sunset), what does the hadith of Uqbah ibn Amir (RA) state?
optionsEn: Janazah is encouraged specifically at exact zenith
Janazah is allowed at sunset only
Only women may pray Janazah at sunrise
The Prophet ﷺ forbade praying over or burying the dead during those three short intervals unless urgently necessary
explanationEn: Uqbah ibn Amir (RA) explicitly mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ forbade praying or burying the dead during those three brief times (sunrise, exact zenith, sunset), whereas outside those short moments—such as after Fajr or after Asr—Janazah is universally permitted.

questionEn: Is performing the Funeral Prayer (Salat al-Janazah) permissible immediately after the Asr prayer (before the sun turns yellow and inclines to set)?
optionsEn: Yes, scholars agree Janazah is permissible after Fajr and after Asr so long as it is not during the three strict short intervals
No, Janazah can never be prayed after Asr
Only if the deceased was a child
Only inside Makkah
explanationEn: Muslim jurists agree that Salat al-Janazah is valid after Fajr and after Asr because it is a communal obligation with a pressing cause; only the three brief astronomical moments (sunrise, zenith, sunset) are avoided.

questionEn: When the sun is at its zenith (istiwa) on Friday (Yawm al-Jumu'ah), what exception do many scholars (such as the Shafi'is) make for voluntary prayers?
optionsEn: No prayer of any kind is allowed at the mosque before Jumu'ah
Arriving early on Friday and praying voluntary prayers continuously until the Imam comes out is exempted from the zenith restriction
Only one rak'ah is permitted
Only fasting is permitted at zenith on Friday
explanationEn: Shafi'i jurists cite narrations encouraging whoever arrives early on Friday to pray whatever is decreed for him until the Imam ascends the minbar, making Friday midday an exception to the zenith prohibition.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing the Eclipse Prayer (Salat al-Kusuf) if a solar eclipse occurs after the Asr prayer?
optionsEn: It must be postponed until the next morning
It is performed silently without bowing
Many scholars (including Shafi'is and Hanbalis) hold it is prayed immediately because it has an urgent, specific cause
Only the Imam prays it alone
explanationEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ commanded: 'When you see [the eclipse], hasten to prayer,' scholars who permit prayers with an immediate cause (Dhawat al-Asbab) during restricted periods rule that Kusuf should be prayed right away.

questionEn: What happens in Makkah regarding the restriction on voluntary prayers after Fajr and after Asr according to the Prophet's ﷺ instruction to Banu Abd Manaf?
optionsEn: All prayers are strictly barred inside Masjid al-Haram after Asr
Only residents of Madinah are exempt
No one may perform Tawaf after Asr
Any pilgrim may perform Tawaf and its two rak'ahs at any hour of the day or night without restriction
explanationEn: Based on the hadith in Sunan Abi Dawud and at-Tirmidhi addressed to Banu Abd Manaf, the two rak'ahs following Tawaf are universally permitted in Makkah at any hour, even after Fajr or Asr.

questionEn: What is the difference in severity between the three brief astronomical forbidden times (sunrise, zenith, sunset) and the broader periods after Fajr and after Asr?
optionsEn: The three brief times are stricter prohibitions tied to sun-worshipping times, whereas after Fajr/Asr is more flexible regarding prayers with a cause
After Fajr is stricter than exact sunrise
Zenith is the only forbidden time for men, while sunset is only for women
There is no scholarly distinction between them
explanationEn: Even scholars who allow prayers with a cause (like Tahiyyat al-Masjid) after Fajr and Asr maintain greater caution during the three narrow astronomical moments—especially forbidding burying the dead or starting voluntary prayers at sunrise, zenith, and sunset.

questionEn: If someone begins a voluntary two-rak'ah prayer before Fajr Sadiq and the true dawn breaks while he is still praying, or begins Duha and zenith arrives mid-prayer, what is the ruling?
optionsEn: He should stop immediately and sit down
He completes the prayer cleanly without breaking it, as it was started in a lawful time
He must add two extra rak'ahs
He must repeat it after Dhuhr
explanationEn: Because the prayer was initiated during a permissible time, completing a short two-rak'ah prayer is valid according to jurists (though Hanafis distinguish sunrise specifically for Fajr, where sunrise interrupts unfinished prayer in their view).

questionEn: During the period between sunrise and the sun reaching a spear's height, how long does the prohibition typically last in minutes?
optionsEn: Only 10 seconds
Approximately two hours
Approximately 12 to 15 minutes after sunrise
Until solar noon
explanationEn: Astronomically, the sun rises about 15 degrees per hour (1 degree every 4 minutes); a spear's height above the horizon corresponds to roughly 3 to 4 degrees, or about 12–15 minutes after sunrise.

questionEn: When does the voluntary prayer of Salat al-Duha (the morning forenoon prayer) become permissible to begin?
optionsEn: Immediately after praying Fajr Fard
At the exact moment the sun's edge touches the horizon
Only after Zawal
Once the sun has risen to the height of a spear after sunrise (roughly 15 minutes after sunrise)
explanationEn: Duha begins once the morning prohibited time ends (about 12–15 minutes after sunrise, when the sun is a spear's height above the horizon) and continues until just before exact zenith.

questionEn: Which non-prayer acts of worship ARE completely permissible during all five forbidden/disliked prayer times?
optionsEn: Reciting Qur'an, making Dhikr, sending Salawat, and making Dua
Only sleeping
Only fasting
No verbal worship is permitted at sunrise or sunset
explanationEn: The prohibition during those times applies specifically to performing ritual prayers (Salah), whereas remembering Allah, reciting Qur'an, making Dua, and seeking forgiveness are blessed at all hours.

questionEn: If a Muslim makes Wudu during the forbidden time after Asr, is he allowed to pray the two Sunnah rak'ahs of Wudu?
optionsEn: All four schools forbid it strictly
Shafi'i and some Hanbali jurists allow it as a prayer with a specific cause, while Hanafi and Maliki jurists advise delaying general Nafl until Maghrib
It is obligatory after Asr
Only one rak'ah is allowed
explanationEn: This is a classic scholarly difference: Shafi'is allow Dhawat al-Asbab (like Sunnah of Wudu and Tahiyyat al-Masjid) after Fajr and Asr, while Hanafis and Malikis apply the general prohibition to them.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Sujud al-Tilawah (prostration of Qur'an recitation) during a disliked time such as after Asr?
optionsEn: Permissible only if one skips the Takbir
Strictly sinful under all schools
Permitted by the majority of scholars (Shafi'is, Hanbalis, and many Hanafis if the verse was recited then), though avoided at the three strict astronomical moments
Replaced by giving charity
explanationEn: Majority jurists permit Sujud al-Tilawah when reciting a verse of prostration after Fajr or Asr (since it is tied to an immediate cause, not a standalone Nafl prayer), while avoiding the three strict moments of sunrise, zenith, and sunset.

questionEn: What happens if someone arrives at the mosque before Fajr Fard and has already prayed the two Sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr at home? Should he pray Tahiyyat al-Masjid?
optionsEn: He must pray ten more rak'ahs
He must pray another two Sunnah of Fajr
He must leave the mosque until Iqamah

Under the Hanbali/majority view restricting extra Nafl between Fajr Adhan and Fajr Fard, opinions differ: Shafi'is permit Tahiyyat al-Masjid as Dhat Sabab, while others advise sitting with Dhikr if Fajr Sunnah was already prayed
explanationEn: Narrations state 'There is no prayer after dawn breaks except the two rak'ahs of Fajr,' so scholars who make an exception for Tahiyyat al-Masjid permit it upon entering, while Hanafis and Hanbalis generally advise engaging in Dhikr and Dua if one already prayed Fajr Sunnah at home.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ prohibit prayer specifically during the few minutes when the sun is at exact zenith (istiwa) in the narration of Amr ibn Abasah (RA)?
optionsEn: Because at that exact hour the gates of Hellfire are stoked (tusajjaru Jahannam)
Because the sun enters an eclipse daily
Because travelers rest at noon
Because shadows disappear across the entire earth
explanationEn: In Amr ibn Abasah's detailed narration in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ taught him to cease prayer at midday when a spear casts no east-west shadow, explaining: 'For at that time Hellfire is stoked (blazed).'

questionEn: In what order did the Prophet ﷺ describe the daily cycle of permissible and prohibited prayer times to Amr ibn Abasah (RA)?
optionsEn: Pray from sunrise to sunset without pause
Pray Fajr, abstain until sun rises a spear's height, pray until zenith, abstain until sun declines, pray until Asr, then abstain until sunset
Abstain only between Dhuhr and Asr
Pray only at sunrise and sunset
explanationEn: The long hadith of Amr ibn Abasah (RA) in Sahih Muslim 832 maps out the entire daytime schedule of worship and the exact moments when prayer is paused.

questionEn: If a person forgot his Witr prayer at night and remembers it after praying Fajr (before sunrise), when is it best to make it up according to the Prophet's ﷺ Sunnah?
optionsEn: Right before sunrise during the strict sunrise prohibition
He can never make up Witr
Wait until after sunrise (during Duha) and pray it in an even number of rak'ahs, as the Prophet ﷺ did
Pray one rak'ah during exact zenith
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) narrated that whenever sleep or pain prevented the Prophet ﷺ from his night prayer (including Witr), he would pray twelve rak'ahs during the day (Duha time), making it an even number.

questionEn: Is there any disliked or forbidden time for voluntary prayer during the night (between Maghrib and Fajr Sadiq)?
optionsEn: Yes, between Isha and midnight
Yes, between 1:00 AM and 3:00 AM
Yes, immediately after Maghrib
No; the entire night is free of forbidden prayer times until Fajr Sadiq (aside from praying while the Iqamah is being called)
explanationEn: None of the five forbidden prayer times fall at night; voluntary night prayers are blessed throughout the night from after Maghrib/Isha until dawn.

questionEn: What is the ruling on performing Salat al-Istikharah after the Asr prayer if a matter is urgent vs non-urgent?
optionsEn: If non-urgent, delay until after Maghrib; if genuinely urgent before sunset, scholars who allow Dhawat al-Asbab permit it after Asr (avoiding the final yellowing before sunset)
Istikharah may only be prayed at exact zenith
Istikharah requires four rak'ahs at sunset
Istikharah is forbidden at night
explanationEn: Istikharah for a non-urgent decision is best delayed outside the post-Asr window, while if urgent before Maghrib, jurists who permit prayers with an immediate cause allow it so long as it avoids the strict sunset prohibition.

questionEn: What did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) do when people attempted to pray voluntary prayers immediately after Asr?
optionsEn: He joined them and encouraged extra rak'ahs
He forbade them and struck their hands/warned them, enforcing the Prophetic prohibition after Asr
He ordered them to pray sitting down
He replaced Asr with Dhuhr
explanationEn: Reports in Sahih al-Bukhari show Umar (RA) strictly enforcing the Prophetic prohibition against voluntary prayers after Fajr and after Asr.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the moment the sun turns pale yellow (when its disk inclines toward setting) in the hadith of Uqbah ibn Amir (RA)?
optionsEn: It is the best time for Duha
It is when Jumu'ah begins
It is the third strict forbidden time to pray or bury the dead until the sun completely sets
It is when Fajr begins
explanationEn: The third strict time in Uqbah ibn Amir's (RA) narration is 'when the sun inclines to set until it sets completely,' i.e., roughly the final 10–15 minutes before Maghrib.

questionEn: If a person enters Masjid al-Haram in Makkah right after Fajr prayer to perform Umrah, when should he pray the two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim after completing Tawaf?
optionsEn: He must wait outside the Haram until sunrise plus 15 minutes
He must wait until Dhuhr
He skips the two rak'ahs of Tawaf completely
He prays the two rak'ahs of Tawaf immediately after finishing Tawaf, even though it is after Fajr
explanationEn: Because of the explicit Prophetic exception for Tawaf in Makkah ('Do not prevent anyone from circumambulating this House and praying at any hour of night or day'), the two rak'ahs of Tawaf are prayed right after Tawaf at any time.

questionEn: If someone enters a mosque while the Mu'adhdhin is calling the Iqamah for an obligatory prayer, why is starting a voluntary prayer forbidden at that moment?
optionsEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ stated: 'When the Iqamah for prayer is called, there is no prayer except the prescribed one'
Because the mosque doors close during Iqamah
Because Iqamah lasts thirty minutes
Because voluntary prayers require a separate Adhan
explanationEn: Once the Iqamah begins, starting any Sunnah or Nafl prayer is forbidden so that the worshipper joins the congregational Fard prayer right from the opening Takbir.

questionEn: In the Hanafi school, if a person is already in the middle of a voluntary prayer when the Iqamah for Fard begins, what is he advised to do?
optionsEn: Wait twenty minutes before joining
