Complete two rak'ahs quickly if he is close to finishing (or break it if necessary) so as not to miss the congregation, whereas Shafi'is/Hanbalis advise finishing lightly or breaking if congregation will be missed
Turn his voluntary prayer into a four-rak'ah Fard
Leave the mosque immediately
explanationEn: Scholars advise finishing quickly if one is near the end (e.g., already in the second rak'ah) or gently exiting if just started, to avoid missing the opening Takbir and congregation, adhering to Sahih Muslim 710.

questionEn: Why is the prohibition of prayer after Fajr and after Asr described as a preventative barrier (Sadd adh-Dhara'i)?
optionsEn: To prevent people from sleeping too long
To limit the number of mosques in a city
To keep worshippers away from approaching the exact moments of sunrise and sunset when sun-worshippers bow to the sun
To conserve water for Wudu
explanationEn: Scholars note that extending the restriction from Fajr to sunrise and from Asr to sunset acts as a protective buffer around the two critical moments of sunrise and sunset.

questionEn: Does the prohibition of praying after Asr apply to making up an obligatory prayer (Qada) that one genuinely forgot earlier in the day?
optionsEn: Yes, Qada is barred after Asr
Yes, unless it is Friday
Only if it is Fajr Qada
No; missed obligatory prayers must be prayed as soon as remembered, even after Fajr or after Asr
explanationEn: Obligatory prayers take absolute precedence; the Prophet ﷺ said 'Whoever forgets a prayer, let him pray it when he remembers it,' which applies at all times.

questionEn: What if a person enters a mosque on Friday just as the Imam has already begun delivering the Jumu'ah Khutbah—should he sit down or pray two brief rak'ahs?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ commanded one who enters during the Khutbah to pray two brief rak'ahs (Tahiyyat al-Masjid) before sitting
He must pray four long rak'ahs
He must wait in the courtyard until the Khutbah finishes
He must perform Sujud al-Shukr only
explanationEn: When Sulayk al-Ghatafani (RA) sat down while the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the Friday Khutbah, the Prophet ﷺ asked him if he had prayed two rak'ahs, then ordered him: 'Stand up and pray two brief rak'ahs.'

questionEn: Are the restrictions on praying after Fajr and after Asr applicable to praying inside one's home as well as inside the mosque?
optionsEn: Only inside the mosque
Yes, the time-based prohibition on unrestricted Nafl prayers applies everywhere, both at home and in the mosque
Only while traveling
Only in open fields
explanationEn: The prohibition is tied to the astronomical time and the state of having prayed Fajr or Asr, applying equally at home, at work, or in the masjid.

questionEn: Before the Adhan was revealed, what three methods were suggested by Companions in Madinah to gather Muslims for prayer?
optionsEn: Smoke signals, drums, and flags
Lanterns, whistles, and mirrors
A bell/clapper (Naqus), a horn (Buq), and lighting a fire
Carrier pigeons, trumpets, and bells
explanationEn: During consultation in Madinah, some suggested a wooden clapper/bell like the Christians, others a horn like the Jews, and others lighting a fire like the Magians—all disliked by the Prophet ﷺ before the Adhan was revealed via dream.

questionEn: Which Companion saw a dream of a man wearing green garments who taught him the exact words of the Adhan and Iqamah?
optionsEn: Bilal ibn Rabah (RA)
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA)
Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA)
Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA)
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Abd Rabbih (RA) came to the Prophet ﷺ in the morning and recounted his dream of a man in two green garments teaching him the Adhan and Iqamah; the Prophet ﷺ confirmed it was a true vision.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ instruct Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA) to teach the words of his dream to Bilal (RA) rather than calling the Adhan himself?
optionsEn: Because Bilal (RA) had a stronger, more resonant voice (anda sawtan)
Because Abdullah ibn Zayd had lost his voice permanently
Because only freed slaves could call the Adhan
Because Bilal lived closer to the well
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA): 'Teach it to Bilal, for he has a more resonant/far-reaching voice than you,' making Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) the first Mu'adhdhin of Islam.

questionEn: Which senior Companion rushed out of his house upon hearing Bilal's very first Adhan, saying he had seen the exact same dream?
optionsEn: Uthman ibn Affan (RA)
Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)
Talhah ibn Ubaydillah (RA)
explanationEn: When Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) heard Bilal's call, he emerged trailing his cloak and told the Prophet ﷺ that he had seen the very same dream, upon which the Prophet ﷺ praised Allah.

questionEn: Who was the second regular Mu'adhdhin appointed by the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah alongside Bilal (RA)?
optionsEn: Anas ibn Malik (RA)
Ammar ibn Yasir (RA)
Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (RA)
Salman al-Farisi (RA)
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (RA), who was blind, alternated with Bilal (RA) in calling the Adhan in Madinah—especially calling the second Adhan of Fajr once people informed him dawn had arrived.

questionEn: Which young Makkahn Companion had a beautiful voice and was personally taught the Adhan (including Tarji') by the Prophet ﷺ to serve as Mu'adhdhin in Makkah?
optionsEn: Ibn Abbas (RA)
Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA)
Zayd ibn Thabit (RA)
Abu Mahdhurah (RA)
explanationEn: After the Battle of Hunayn, the Prophet ﷺ gently called Abu Mahdhurah (RA), blessed his forelock, taught him the 19-phrase Adhan with Tarji', and appointed him Mu'adhdhin of Makkah.

questionEn: How many total phrases make up the standard Adhan taught to Bilal (RA)?
optionsEn: 15 phrases
11 phrases
19 phrases
7 phrases
explanationEn: Bilal's Adhan consists of 15 phrases: 4 Takbirs, 2 Shahadah of Tawhid, 2 Shahadah of Messengership, 2 Hayya 'alas-Salah, 2 Hayya 'alal-Falah, 2 closing Takbirs, and 1 La ilaha illallah.

questionEn: What is 'Tarji'' in the 19-phrase Adhan taught by the Prophet ﷺ to Abu Mahdhurah (RA)?
optionsEn: Repeating the final Takbir four times
Reciting the two Shahadahs first in a lower voice, then repeating both aloud in a raised voice
Adding 'Qad qamatis-salah' to the Adhan
Walking backward while calling the Adhan
explanationEn: In Abu Mahdhurah's narration, Tarji' means whispering the four testimonies (Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah x2, Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah x2) softly first, then proclaiming them aloud, bringing the total to 19 phrases.

questionEn: What is 'Tathwib' in the Fajr Adhan?
optionsEn: Saying 'Subhanallah' four times before Takbir
Adding 'Alhamdulillah' after Hayya 'alal-Falah
Saying 'As-salatu khayrun min an-nawm' (Prayer is better than sleep) twice after Hayya 'alal-Falah
Calling the Adhan twice in rapid succession
explanationEn: Tathwib is the addition of 'As-salatu khayrun min an-nawm' twice after 'Hayya 'alal-Falah' in the Fajr Adhan, reminding sleepers that prayer is better than sleep.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari 605, how did Anas ibn Malik (RA) summarize the structure of Bilal's Adhan compared to his Iqamah?
optionsEn: Both Adhan and Iqamah are always odd
Adhan is single and Iqamah is doubled
Both are identical except for Tathwib
Bilal was commanded to pronounce the Adhan in even phrases and the Iqamah in odd phrases, except 'Qad qamatis-salah'
explanationEn: Anas (RA) explained that Bilal was ordered to double the phrases of the Adhan (even) and say the phrases of the Iqamah once (odd)—except for 'Qad qamatis-salah' which is said twice (making 11 phrases in standard Iqamah).

questionEn: How many phrases are in the standard Iqamah (following Bilal's narration in Sahih al-Bukhari and Abu Dawud)?
optionsEn: 11 phrases
15 phrases
17 phrases
9 phrases
explanationEn: Standard Iqamah has 11 phrases: Allahu Akbar (2x), Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah (1x), Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah (1x), Hayya 'alas-Salah (1x), Hayya 'alal-Falah (1x), Qad qamatis-salah (2x), Allahu Akbar (2x), La ilaha illallah (1x).

questionEn: Why were two separate Adhans called for Fajr in Madinah during the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime?
optionsEn: Because there were two separate mosques next to each other
Bilal called the first before true dawn to wake sleepers and return those praying Tahajjud, while Ibn Umm Maktum called the second when true dawn entered
Because one was in Arabic and one in Syriac
To double the length of Fajr prayer
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ clarified: 'Bilal calls the Adhan at night, so eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktum calls the Adhan,' explaining the first call wakes the sleeping and alerts those praying Qiyam to prepare for Fajr and finish Suhoor.

questionEn: Who introduced the additional early Jumu'ah Adhan at the Az-Zawra marketplace in Madinah, and why?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr (RA), to honor Friday travellers
Umar (RA), during a famine
Uthman ibn Affan (RA), when the population of Madinah grew large and markets were far from the Prophet's Mosque
Ali (RA), in Kufah
explanationEn: During Uthman's (RA) caliphate, Madinah expanded greatly, so he added an earlier Adhan at Az-Zawra marketplace to alert merchants and residents well before the Khutbah, with the Companions' consensus.

questionEn: On a very cold, rainy, or fiercely windy night, what did Ibn Umar (RA) and the Prophet's ﷺ Mu'adhdhins announce in the Adhan?
optionsEn: 'All prayers are cancelled tonight'
'Wait until sunrise to pray Isha'
'Pray only one rak'ah at home'
'Ala sallu fi rihalikum' (Pray in your dwellings/lodgings)
explanationEn: On rainy or bitterly cold nights, the Prophet ﷺ commanded the Mu'adhdhin to announce 'Sallu fi rihalikum' (pray in your homes/tents), either right after Hayya 'alal-Falah or in place of it.

questionEn: What physical gesture did Bilal (RA) make while calling 'Hayya 'alas-Salah' and 'Hayya 'alal-Falah'?
optionsEn: He turned his face/head to the right for 'Hayya 'alas-Salah' and to the left for 'Hayya 'alal-Falah', while keeping his feet toward the Qiblah
He spun around in a full circle
He knelt on the ground
He raised both arms above his head
explanationEn: Abu Juhayfah (RA) watched Bilal calling the Adhan and turning his face to the right and left on the two Hay'alas (to project the call across directions) while his body remained facing the Qiblah.

questionEn: What unique honor will Mu'adhdhins (those who call the Adhan) receive on the Day of Resurrection according to Sahih Muslim?
optionsEn: They will carry green banners
They will have the longest necks of all people on the Day of Resurrection
They will speak only in poetry
They will enter before the prophets
explanationEn: Mu'awiyah (RA) heard the Prophet ﷺ say: 'The Mu'adhdhins will have the longest necks of all people on the Day of Resurrection'—interpreted as eminence, anticipation of Allah's mercy, or staying above the sweat of the gathering.

questionEn: Who or what will testify in favor of the Mu'adhdhin on the Day of Judgment according to Sahih al-Bukhari 609?
optionsEn: Only the people praying in the first row
Only the angels writing deeds
Every jinn, human, or anything (wet or dry, stone or tree) within the reach of his voice
Only his immediate family
explanationEn: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA) advised raising the voice in Adhan outdoors, reporting the Prophet ﷺ said: 'No jinn, human, or anything hears the extent of the Mu'adhdhin's voice except that it will bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection.'

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ contrast the roles of the Imam and the Mu'adhdhin in his supplication for both?
optionsEn: The Imam is wealthy and the Mu'adhdhin is poor
The Imam is optional and the Mu'adhdhin is solitary
Both carry identical responsibilities
'The Imam is a guarantor (damin) and the Mu'adhdhin is entrusted (mu'taman); O Allah, guide the Imams and forgive the Mu'adhdhins'
explanationEn: Because the Imam bears responsibility for the congregation's prayer and the Mu'adhdhin is entrusted with accurate prayer and fasting times, the Prophet ﷺ prayed for guidance for Imams and forgiveness for Mu'adhdhins.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say people would do if they truly knew the reward contained in calling the Adhan and praying in the first row?
optionsEn: They would draw lots (cast arrows) to compete for the honor
They would pay gold to avoid them
They would reserve them only for elders
They would alternate once a year
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'If people knew what reward lies in the call to prayer and the first row, and found no other way to settle it except drawing lots, they would surely draw lots for it.'

questionEn: What happens to Shaytan the moment the Adhan for prayer is proclaimed?
optionsEn: He stands in the back row
He turns his back and flees while breaking wind so he does not hear the Adhan
He whispers louder in the Imam's ear
He sleeps until after Taslim
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrated that when the Adhan is called, Shaytan runs away breaking wind so he cannot hear it; when the Adhan finishes he returns, flees again at Iqamah, and returns afterward to whisper distractions.

questionEn: When listening to the Mu'adhdhin, what should the listener say immediately upon hearing 'Hayya 'alas-Salah' and 'Hayya 'alal-Falah'?
optionsEn: Repeat 'Hayya 'alas-Salah' and 'Hayya 'alal-Falah' verbatim
Say 'Allahu Akbar Kabira'
Say 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' (There is no might nor power except through Allah)
Remain completely silent
explanationEn: While the listener repeats every other phrase of the Adhan verbatim after the Mu'adhdhin, upon hearing the two calls to prayer and success, the Sunnah is to say 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah,' expressing reliance on Allah to answer the call.

questionEn: Which supplication is narrated in Sahih Muslim 386 to be recited when the Mu'adhdhin pronounces the two testimonies of faith (Shahadatayn)?
optionsEn: Subhanallahi wa bihamdihi
Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah
Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal-wakil
'Wa ana ashhadu an la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah... Raditu billahi Rabban wa bi-Muhammadin Rasulan wa bil-Islami dina'
explanationEn: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) narrated that whoever says upon hearing the Mu'adhdhin's Shahadah: 'And I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah alone without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger; I am pleased with Allah as Lord, Muhammad as Messenger, and Islam as religion,' his sins are forgiven.

questionEn: After repeating the phrases of the Adhan, what two things did the Prophet ﷺ instruct believers to do immediately afterward to earn his intercession (Shafa'ah)?
optionsEn: Send Salawat (blessings) upon the Prophet ﷺ, then ask Allah to grant him Al-Wasilah using Dua al-Wasilah
Stand up and clap twice
Recite Surah Al-Fatihah three times
Wash the face and hands
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed: 'Say what the Mu'adhdhin says, then send blessings upon me... then ask Allah to grant me Al-Wasilah, which is a station in Paradise reserved for one servant of Allah... whoever asks Allah for Al-Wasilah for me will receive my intercession.'

questionEn: What is 'Al-Wasilah' mentioned in the Dua after the Adhan ('Allahumma Rabba hadhihi ad-da'wati at-tammah...')?
optionsEn: A well in Makkah
The highest rank/station in Paradise reserved for a single servant of Allah, which the Prophet ﷺ hoped to receive
A bridge over the Sea of Madinah
The staff carried during Friday Khutbah
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim 384, the Prophet ﷺ defined Al-Wasilah as the loftiest rank in Paradise suitable for only one of Allah's servants, adding: 'And I hope that I will be he.'

questionEn: What special virtue characterizes the period between the Adhan and the Iqamah?
optionsEn: Fasting during it equals a full year
Speaking to others is forbidden
Supplication (Dua) made between the Adhan and Iqamah is not rejected
Only the Imam is allowed to sit
explanationEn: Anas (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The supplication made between the Adhan and the Iqamah is not rejected,' making it one of the prime times for personal Dua.

questionEn: How did Abu Hurayrah (RA) react when he saw a man walk out of the masjid after the Adhan had already been called?
optionsEn: He congratulated him on arriving early
He asked him to bring water
He invited him to lead the prayer later
He remarked: 'As for this man, he has disobeyed Abul-Qasim (the Prophet ﷺ)'
explanationEn: Scholars rule it impermissible to leave the mosque after Adhan without a valid excuse (such as needing to renew Wudu and return, or having an urgent necessity/leading another mosque), based on Abu Hurayrah's stern rebuke.

questionEn: Under what condition is it permissible for someone inside a mosque to leave after the Adhan has been called?
optionsEn: When leaving for a genuine need intending to return (like renewing Wudu) or to pray in another mosque where one serves as Imam/attends another congregation
Whenever one feels slightly bored
Whenever one wants to shop at the market
It is never permissible even to renew Wudu
explanationEn: Jurists explain that Abu Hurayrah's warning applies to leaving without excuse intending not to pray in congregation; leaving to make Wudu and return, or for a genuine necessity or duty elsewhere, is permitted.

questionEn: What guideline did the Prophet ﷺ give to Mu'adhdhins (like Bilal) regarding how long to wait between calling the Adhan and calling the Iqamah?
optionsEn: Always wait exactly one hour
Allow enough time for a person eating to finish his meal unhurriedly and for one needing Wudu to relieve himself and prepare
Call Iqamah immediately within five seconds of finishing Adhan for all five prayers
Wait only if the sun is shining
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ advised Bilal (RA) to pause between Adhan and Iqamah long enough for someone eating to finish and one answering the call of nature to complete Wudu and reach the prayer peacefully (with Maghrib kept shorter).

questionEn: For which of the five daily prayers is the interval between Adhan and Iqamah kept noticeably briefest according to prophetic practice?
optionsEn: Fajr
Dhuhr
Maghrib
Isha
explanationEn: Because Maghrib's preferred window right after sunset is brief and the Prophet ﷺ emphasized hastening Maghrib, mosques traditionally allow only a short pause (e.g., enough for two light rak'ahs or brief preparation) before Iqamah.

questionEn: What is the key difference in pace and vocal delivery between the Adhan and the Iqamah?
optionsEn: Adhan is whispered and Iqamah is shouted
Both are recited at identical speed
Adhan is sung rapidly and Iqamah is drawn out slowly
Adhan is delivered slowly with pauses (Tarassul) to reach distant listeners, while Iqamah is delivered briskly (Hadr) for those already gathered
explanationEn: Jurists explain that Adhan uses measured, deliberate pacing (Tarassul) to summon people from afar, whereas Iqamah uses brisk, connected phrasing (Hadr) to alert those present that prayer is starting immediately.

questionEn: What is the primary functional distinction between the Adhan and the Iqamah?
optionsEn: Adhan announces that the prayer time has entered and calls people to the mosque; Iqamah announces that the congregation is standing to begin the prayer right now
Adhan is for travelers only; Iqamah is for residents only
Adhan is only for Friday; Iqamah is for weekdays
Adhan is recited silently; Iqamah is only for Fajr
explanationEn: Adhan notifies the community of the arrival of the prayer's time, whereas Iqamah signals the immediate commencement of the standing Fard prayer.

questionEn: Are women required or recommended to call the Adhan or Iqamah when praying alone or in an all-women congregation?
optionsEn: Both Adhan and Iqamah are strictly obligatory on women
Adhan and Iqamah are not obligatory upon women; they may pray without them (some scholars allow women to say Iqamah softly among themselves)
Women must call Adhan on rooftops
Women must call Adhan only during Ramadan
explanationEn: By scholarly consensus, Adhan and Iqamah are not obligatory upon women; Aisha (RA) and Ibn Umar (RA) are reported to have viewed women's prayer valid without Adhan or Iqamah, though softly saying Iqamah among women is permitted by some schools.

questionEn: What is the ruling on a Mu'adhdhin taking a regular salary specifically in exchange for calling the Adhan, vs receiving a stipend from the public treasury (Bayt al-Mal)?
optionsEn: He must charge attendees directly at the door
It is forbidden for a Mu'adhdhin to receive any state livelihood support
He should not stipulate a wage from worshippers for Adhan itself, though receiving a community/treasury stipend so he can devote himself to the duty is permitted by most jurists
He must pay the Imam to call Adhan
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ advised Uthman ibn Abil-As (RA): 'Appoint a Mu'adhdhin who does not take a wage for his Adhan,' which jurists distinguish from an institutional stipend/provision from Bayt al-Mal or waqf enabling full-time mosque service.

questionEn: When the Iqamah is heard, how did the Prophet ﷺ instruct worshippers to approach the mosque and join the prayer rows?
optionsEn: Run as fast as possible so as not to miss the first Takbir
Crawl quietly along the walls
Jump over seated people
Walk with tranquility and dignity (Sakinah and Waqar); pray what you catch and complete what you missed
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ commanded: 'When the Iqamah is pronounced, do not come to it running; walk with tranquility and dignity. Whatever you catch, pray it, and whatever you miss, complete it.'

questionEn: If a person enters a mosque after the Imam has already begun prayer or missed the congregation and prays alone, should he call the Adhan?
optionsEn: No, because the mosque's public Adhan has already been called; calling another Adhan aloud would confuse people
Yes, he must shout a full Adhan inside the hall
He must go outside and call Adhan from the street
He must wait until the next prayer's Adhan
explanationEn: Since the neighborhood mosque's Adhan already fulfilled the communal announcement for that prayer time, a latecomer praying alone or in a second group does not repeat a loud public Adhan (though he may quietly say Iqamah).

questionEn: What is the ruling on calling the Adhan and Iqamah when two or three Muslims are traveling together in the desert or countryside far from any mosque?
optionsEn: They are forbidden to call Adhan outdoors
Calling Adhan and Iqamah is strongly encouraged (Sunnah Mu'akkadah) for travelers, even for a lone shepherd in the wilderness
Only Iqamah is permitted outdoors
They must return to a city before praying
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told Malik ibn al-Huwayrith (RA) and his companion when traveling: 'When the prayer time arrives, let one of you call the Adhan and let the oldest among you lead,' and praised the shepherd calling Adhan alone in the mountains.

questionEn: According to the majority of jurists, what is the communal ruling (Hukm) of calling the Adhan for the five daily prayers in a Muslim town or neighborhood?
optionsEn: Disliked (Makruh)
Individual obligation on every single resident
Fard Kifayah (communal obligation)—if some fulfill it, the obligation is met; if everyone abandons it, the community sins
Permissible only during Hajj
explanationEn: Because Adhan is one of the foremost outward symbols (Sha'a'ir) of Islam—to the point the Prophet ﷺ waited to hear Adhan before judging whether a settlement was Muslim—jurists classify it as Fard Kifayah (or emphatic Sunnah) in every locality.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ approached a tribe at night during a campaign, what sound at dawn made him refrain from attacking them?
optionsEn: Seeing white flags on rooftops
Hearing bells ringing
Seeing lanterns in the tents
Hearing the Fajr Adhan called from among them
explanationEn: Anas (RA) reported that whenever the Prophet ﷺ reached a people by night, he would wait until morning: if he heard the Adhan, he withheld; if he did not hear it, he knew they had not accepted Islam.

questionEn: During the Adhan, what is the Sunnah practice regarding placing one's fingertips in the ears?
optionsEn: Placing the index fingers in the ears helps project the voice and signals the call clearly, as Bilal (RA) did
Covering both eyes with both palms
Holding a staff in both hands
Placing hands in one's pockets
explanationEn: Abu Juhayfah (RA) described seeing Bilal (RA) calling the Adhan with his fingers in his ears, which jurists recommend as it strengthens vocal resonance and lets onlookers see he is calling Adhan even from afar.

questionEn: Is it permissible for someone without Wudu (in a state of minor impurity) to call the Adhan?
optionsEn: No, it invalidates the congregation's prayer
Yes, the Adhan is valid without Wudu, though having Wudu is strongly recommended (Mustahabb)
Only if he wears gloves
Only for Asr prayer
explanationEn: Because Adhan is a form of Dhikr rather than Salah, being in a state of Wudu is recommended (Mustahabb) for honor and readiness to pray immediately, not a strict condition of validity; major impurity (Janabah), however, makes calling Adhan disliked.

questionEn: When combining Dhuhr and Asr (or Maghrib and Isha) while traveling, how many Adhans and Iqamahs are called?
optionsEn: Two Adhans and one Iqamah
No Adhan and no Iqamah
One Adhan for the pair, and a separate Iqamah before each of the two combined prayers
Two Adhans and two Iqamahs
explanationEn: During the Farewell Pilgrimage at Arafah and Muzdalifah, the Prophet ﷺ had one Adhan called followed by two separate Iqamahs—one before each of the two combined prayers.

questionEn: Which two prayers are NOT preceded by an Adhan or Iqamah in the Prophetic Sunnah?
optionsEn: Fajr and Jumu'ah
Dhuhr and Asr
Maghrib and Isha
The two Eid prayers (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha) and the Funeral prayer (Janazah)
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Samurah (RA) reported praying the two Eids with the Prophet ﷺ many times 'without Adhan and without Iqamah,' and the same applies to Janazah and eclipse prayers (where 'As-Salatu Jami'ah' is announced for eclipses).

questionEn: For the Eclipse Prayer (Salat al-Kusuf), what announcement replaces the Adhan to gather people?
optionsEn: 'As-Salatu Jami'ah' (Prayer is about to gather)
Tathwib ('As-salatu khayrun min an-nawm')
'Hayya 'alal-Falah' repeated seven times
Silent waving of a banner
explanationEn: When the sun eclipsed on the day Ibrahim (the Prophet's ﷺ son) died, the Prophet ﷺ ordered a caller to announce 'As-Salatu Jami'ah' rather than calling the standard Adhan.

questionEn: What does the phrase 'Qad qamatis-salah' in the Iqamah mean in English?
optionsEn: Prayer is better than sleep
Prayer has now been established (is about to begin)
Come to the mosque quickly
Peace be upon the worshippers
explanationEn: 'Qad qamatis-salah' means 'The prayer is now established / ready to commence,' signaling the congregation to straighten rows and begin.

questionEn: Before the Qiblah was commanded to face the Ka'bah in Makkah, toward which sacred direction did the Prophet ﷺ and Muslims pray after arriving in Madinah?
optionsEn: Directly east toward the rising sun
Toward Mount Sinai
Toward Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem)
Toward the Prophet's Mosque courtyard in every direction
explanationEn: After migrating to Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) for sixteen or seventeen months while longing for Allah to turn him toward the Ka'bah.

questionEn: Approximately how many months did the Prophet ﷺ pray facing Bayt al-Maqdis after arriving in Madinah before the revelation changing the Qiblah?
optionsEn: Three months
Six months
Thirty-six months
Sixteen or seventeen months
explanationEn: Al-Bara' ibn Azib (RA) narrated that when the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, he prayed facing Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months, and loved that he be turned toward the House (Ka'bah).

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ manage to face both the Ka'bah and Bayt al-Maqdis simultaneously while praying in Makkah before the Hijrah?
optionsEn: He stood between the Yemeni Corner (ar-Rukn al-Yamani) and the Black Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad), placing the Ka'bah directly in front of him toward Sham/Jerusalem
He prayed facing south only
He rotated midway through each rak'ah
He prayed atop Mount Abu Qubays
explanationEn: Because Jerusalem lies north of Makkah, standing at the southern wall of the Ka'bah (between the Yemeni Corner and Black Stone) allowed the Prophet ﷺ to face both the Ka'bah and Jerusalem at once.

questionEn: In which Surah and verses is the historic change of the Qiblah from Jerusalem to al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah recorded?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Imran 3:96-97
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:142-150
Surah Al-Anfal 8:1-5
Surah Al-Hajj 22:26-29
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:142–150 addresses the change of Qiblah, responds to critics, reassures believers about past prayers, and commands: 'Turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah 2:144, how does Allah describe the Prophet's ﷺ longing just before revealing the change of Qiblah?
optionsEn: He asked the Companions to vote on a direction
He sent a letter to the elders of Makkah
'We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, and We will surely turn you to a Qiblah with which you will be pleased'
He fasted forty days in Cave Hira
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ used to gaze frequently toward the sky hoping for revelation directing him to the Ka'bah (the Qiblah of Prophet Ibrahim AS), and Allah honored his heart's wish in Al-Baqarah 2:144.

questionEn: What worried some Companions immediately after the Qiblah was changed to Makkah, prompting the revelation of Surah Al-Baqarah 2:143?
optionsEn: Whether Makkah was too far to travel
Whether Wudu remained valid
Whether the Adhan words had to change
The fate of Companions who had died while praying toward Jerusalem before the change
explanationEn: Companions asked about brothers who passed away praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis (such as As'ad ibn Zurarah and al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur); Allah revealed: 'And never would Allah have caused your faith (i.e., your prayers) to be lost.'

questionEn: Why does Surah Al-Baqarah (2:142-143) explain that the change of Qiblah was also a test?
optionsEn: To make evident who genuinely follows the Messenger ﷺ versus who turns back on his heels
To test who could navigate using stars
To measure the height of the Ka'bah
To distinguish travelers from merchants
explanationEn: Allah states in Al-Baqarah 2:143: 'And We did not make the Qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels.'

questionEn: How did the worshippers at Masjid Quba (and Masjid Banu Salamah / Masjid al-Qiblatayn) respond when news of the Qiblah change reached them mid-prayer?
optionsEn: They broke their prayer and went home
They turned around mid-prayer (from facing north toward Jerusalem to facing south toward Makkah) without breaking their prayer
They waited until the next day to change direction
They faced east for the rest of the day
explanationEn: In Quba during Fajr and in Banu Salamah (Masjid al-Qiblatayn), a messenger announced the Quranic revelation changing the Qiblah; the congregation rotated 180 degrees mid-prayer from north (Jerusalem) to south (Makkah) and completed their prayer.

questionEn: Why is the historic mosque of Banu Salamah in Madinah famous by the name 'Masjid al-Qiblatayn'?
optionsEn: It has two identical minarets facing east and west
It was built by two prophets
Because in a single prayer there, the congregation prayed the early part toward Jerusalem and turned mid-prayer toward the Ka'bah in Makkah
Because it sits halfway between Makkah and Jerusalem
explanationEn: Masjid al-Qiblatayn ('Mosque of the Two Qiblahs') commemorates the congregational prayer where worshippers pivoted mid-prayer upon hearing that Allah had commanded turning toward al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: Which two geographical directions are opposite each other between Madinah and the two Qiblahs?
optionsEn: East (Jerusalem) and West (Makkah)
Northeast (Makkah) and Southwest (Jerusalem)
Southeast (Jerusalem) and Northwest (Makkah)
North (Jerusalem) and South (Makkah)
explanationEn: Madinah sits almost directly between Jerusalem to the north and Makkah to the south, so changing Qiblah in Madinah required turning approximately 180 degrees from due north to due south.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say to reassure the people of Madinah regarding the precision required when facing the Qiblah from afar?
optionsEn: 'Whatever is between the East and the West is Qiblah' (for Madinah, whose Qiblah is south)
'A one-degree error invalidates every prayer'
'Only astronomers may determine the Qiblah'
'Only those inside Makkah are required to face the Ka'bah'
explanationEn: For those who cannot see the Ka'bah directly, the Prophet ﷺ taught the people of Madinah (whose Qiblah lies south): 'Whatever is between the East and the West is Qiblah,' indicating that facing the general direction (Jihat al-Ka'bah) suffices.

questionEn: How do jurists distinguish between the Qiblah obligation of one who can physically see the Ka'bah versus one who is far away?
optionsEn: Both must hit the exact center millimeter of the Black Stone
One who sees the Ka'bah must face its physical structure ('Ayn al-Ka'bah), whereas one far away faces its general direction (Jihat al-Ka'bah)
One far away prays facing east
There is no Qiblah obligation outside Makkah
explanationEn: Inside Masjid al-Haram in view of the Ka'bah, worshippers align directly with the Ka'bah itself ('Ayn al-Ka'bah); outside Makkah, facing its direction (Jihat al-Ka'bah) satisfies the condition.

questionEn: If a worshipper prays inside the Ka'bah itself (or inside the Hijr Ismail), which direction is valid to face?
optionsEn: Only toward the door
Only toward Madinah
Any of the four walls of the Ka'bah, as the Prophet ﷺ prayed inside the Ka'bah facing its wall
Prayer is invalid inside the Ka'bah
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ entered the Ka'bah at the Conquest of Makkah, he prayed two rak'ahs facing the opposite interior wall; jurists agree any wall inside the Ka'bah serves as Qiblah (though for Fard, most advise outside or facing a wall).

questionEn: What was the Prophet's ﷺ practice regarding the Qiblah when performing voluntary (Nafl) prayers while riding his camel on a journey?
optionsEn: He only prayed Nafl when the camel faced south
He stopped and dismounted for every voluntary prayer
He prohibited voluntary prayers during travel
He prayed voluntary prayers on his mount in whichever direction the camel traveled, bowing and prostrating by nodding his head (leaning lower for Sujud)
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) and Ibn Umar (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ prayed voluntary prayers (including Witr) atop his mount regardless of where it turned, gesturing with his head for Ruku' and lower for Sujud—while always dismounting to face Qiblah for Fard prayers.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ prayed an obligatory (Fard) prayer while on a journey, did he remain seated on his camel facing the road, or did he face the Qiblah?
optionsEn: He dismounted from his mount, stood on the ground, and faced the Qiblah
He remained riding without facing Qiblah
He faced Qiblah only for Fajr Fard
He faced backward on the camel
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) clearly stated that the Prophet ﷺ prayed voluntary prayers on his mount wherever it faced, 'except for the obligatory prayers,' for which he always dismounted and faced the Qiblah.

questionEn: On a long-haul airplane flight when the time for an obligatory prayer is about to expire before landing, what should a Muslim passenger do regarding Qiblah and posture?
optionsEn: Skip the prayer until the next day
Pray on time in the plane: stand facing the Qiblah if space and safety permit, or pray seated facing the Qiblah (or as close to it as possible) if standing/turning is impossible
Wait until arrival even if three prayer times pass
Always face the cockpit regardless of flight direction
explanationEn: Obligatory prayers cannot be delayed past their time window (An-Nisa 4:103); based on 'Fear Allah as much as you are able' (64:16), one prays in the designated space facing Qiblah standing if safe and allowed, or seated in one's seat if not.

questionEn: When traveling on a ship at sea and praying an obligatory prayer, what should a worshipper do if the ship changes heading mid-prayer?
optionsEn: Continue facing the ship's stern regardless
Break the prayer and wait until reaching port
Turn one's body smoothly toward the Qiblah during the prayer to stay aligned as the ship turns
Sit down immediately without turning
explanationEn: On a ship where one can stand and move freely, jurists stipulate facing Qiblah and gently rotating with the ship if its course shifts mid-prayer so Qiblah alignment is maintained.

questionEn: If a traveler in a car, bus, or train fears an obligatory prayer's time will completely expire before stopping (e.g., Fajr before sunrise) and cannot stop or stand safely, how should he pray?
optionsEn: Let the prayer time expire and make it up next week
Only think about the prayer mentally without Takbir
Wait until the bus reaches the terminal even after sunrise
Pray in his seat on time facing Qiblah as best he can, nodding for Ruku' and lower for Sujud
explanationEn: When stopping is impossible or unsafe and the prayer time is about to run out, guarding the prayer within its time takes priority, so one prays as capable in the seat (At-Taghabun 64:16).

questionEn: If a group of travelers arrive in an unfamiliar place on a pitch-dark, overcast night with no compass or local guide, what must they do before praying?
optionsEn: Exert sincere effort (Ijtihad) using all available clues—wind, stars, terrain, phone/compass—then pray in the direction they judge most likely
Guess randomly without thinking
Refuse to pray until daylight
Pray four times—once toward each cardinal direction
explanationEn: Allah burdens no soul beyond its capacity (2:286). When Qiblah is hidden, a Muslim must exert diligent effort (Ijtihad) to estimate it rather than guessing carelessly, then pray toward the resulting direction.

questionEn: In a famous incident narrated by Jabir (RA) and Amir ibn Rabi'ah (RA), Companions prayed on a dark, cloudy night after exerting effort, only to discover at sunrise they had prayed away from the Qiblah. What did the Prophet ﷺ rule?
optionsEn: They had to repeat the entire prayer
Their prayer was completely valid and did not need to be repeated
They had to pay charity as expiation
Only the leader's prayer was valid
explanationEn: Amir ibn Rabi'ah (RA) reported that when they told the Prophet ﷺ they had mistakenly prayed off-Qiblah on a dark night after trying their best, Surah Al-Baqarah 2:115 ('Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah') was cited and he did not order them to repeat it.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a person prays in an unfamiliar hotel room WITHOUT making any inquiry or effort (Ijtihad) to check the Qiblah, and later learns he faced the opposite direction?
optionsEn: His prayer is automatically valid without effort
Only half the prayer counts
The majority of jurists rule he must repeat that prayer because he neglected the obligation to investigate the Qiblah first
He must pray Maghrib twice
explanationEn: Unlike one who performed genuine Ijtihad and missed, a person who negligently guessed without asking, checking a sign, or using a compass failed to fulfill a prerequisite of prayer and must repeat it if it was wrong.

questionEn: If a worshipper realizes *mid-prayer* that he is facing the wrong direction (e.g., someone reliable informs him or he spots the mihrab/sun), what should he do?
optionsEn: Stop praying and start over from Takbirat al-Ihram
Finish the prayer facing the wrong direction
Perform Sujud al-Sahw before turning
Turn smoothly toward the correct Qiblah immediately during the prayer and continue from where he is, just as the people of Quba did
explanationEn: Following the precedent of Masjid Quba (Sahih al-Bukhari 403), one who learns the true Qiblah mid-prayer pivots directly toward the Qiblah without restarting the prayer.

questionEn: If two travelers in the wilderness disagree after doing their own independent Ijtihad on where the Qiblah lies, how should they pray?
optionsEn: Each prays facing the direction his own Ijtihad concluded, and one should not follow the other as Imam if he believes the Imam's Qiblah is wrong
They must always follow the younger traveler's guess
They skip prayer until reaching a town
They pray facing each other
explanationEn: Because neither has certainty over the other, each acts upon his own honest Ijtihad; neither can follow an Imam whom he genuinely believes is facing away from the Qiblah.

questionEn: If a reliable Muslim local tells a traveler the exact Qiblah direction in a city, may the traveler ignore him and rely on an uncalibrated guess?
optionsEn: Yes, personal guessing overrides local knowledge
No; testimony of a trustworthy resident who knows the local Qiblah (or an established masjid mihrab) takes precedence over personal guesswork
Only if it is raining
Only during Dhuhr
explanationEn: Jurists establish a hierarchy of Qiblah evidence: seeing the Ka'bah first, then established mosque mihrabs and reliable local witnesses, then instruments/celestial signs (sun, Polaris), and finally personal estimation.

questionEn: Why must Muslims be careful when using a magnetic compass or smartphone app to find Qiblah indoors near steel beams or electronic equipment?
optionsEn: Compasses stop working at night
Apps only point toward Madinah
Ferrous metal structures and magnetic interference can deflect a compass needle, so verifying against maps or the sun/stars prevents error
Using electronic tools in prayer invalidates Wudu
explanationEn: Digital and magnetic compasses are easily skewed by steel rebar, elevators, or magnets; cross-checking with the sun's azimuth or a map ensures accurate Qiblah alignment.

questionEn: When calculating Qiblah on a globe, why do Muslims in North America face northeast rather than southeast toward Makkah?
optionsEn: Because North America is south of the equator
Because maps tilt north
Because the earth is flat
Because the shortest path on a sphere (great-circle route) from North America to Makkah curves northward across the Atlantic/Europe
explanationEn: Although Makkah (21.4° N) is at a lower latitude than most US/Canadian cities (30°–45° N), on a spherical earth the shortest line (great-circle bearing) from North America to Makkah heads northeast.

questionEn: On two specific days each year (May 27–28 and July 15–16), the sun passes directly overhead above the Ka'bah in Makkah at solar noon. How has this historically helped Muslims worldwide?
optionsEn: Anyone who sees the sun at that exact moment can verify the exact Qiblah by facing directly toward the sun (or opposite its shadow)
It marks the start of Ramadan
It turns all shadows purple
It waives the Qiblah requirement for that day
explanationEn: At Makkah solar zenith (~12:18 PM Makkah time on May 28 and ~12:27 PM on July 16), the sun stands vertically above the Ka'bah, allowing anyone on the sunlit side of Earth to calibrate the Qiblah directly from the sun's bearing.

questionEn: In which extreme circumstance mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:239) is the requirement to face the Qiblah waived even for obligatory prayers?
optionsEn: When feeling slightly drowsy
During severe fear/combat (Salat al-Khawf), when one may pray on foot or riding facing any direction
During Eid celebrations
When praying in a carpeted room
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:239 states: 'And if you fear [an enemy], then [pray] on foot or riding,' which Ibn Umar (RA) explained means facing the Qiblah or not facing it as survival demands.

questionEn: What is the ruling for a severely ill, bedridden patient whose bed faces away from the Qiblah and who has no one available to turn him toward it?
optionsEn: He is excused from praying until fully healed
His prayer is invalid unless someone moves the bed
He prays in the direction he is facing, because Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity
He waits until night to pray all prayers at once
explanationEn: Facing the Qiblah is waived when one is genuinely unable to turn and has no helper to turn him, per Surah At-Taghabun 64:16 ('Fear Allah as much as you are able') and Surah Al-Baqarah 2:286.

questionEn: In Masjid al-Haram, why are the prayer rows arranged in concentric circles around the Ka'bah rather than straight parallel lines?
optionsEn: For decorative symmetry only
Because the floor is sloped
To fit fewer people near the center
So that every worshipper on every side directly faces the Ka'bah ('Ayn al-Ka'bah) at the center
explanationEn: Because worshippers in Makkah can see the Ka'bah from all 360 degrees, circular rows ensure every person in every direction directly faces the Ka'bah.

questionEn: What distinguishes a condition (Shart) of Salah from a pillar (Rukn) of Salah?
optionsEn: A Shart is optional for voluntary prayers, whereas a Rukn applies only to obligatory prayers
A Shart can be compensated with Sujud al-Sahw if forgotten, whereas a Rukn cannot
A Shart precedes the prayer and must remain valid throughout it, whereas a Rukn is an integral part performed inside the prayer
A Shart is performed only after Takbirat al-Ihram, whereas a Rukn is fulfilled before it
explanationEn: In Islamic jurisprudence, a Shart (condition) lies outside the essence of the prayer—it must be met before starting and maintained until the end—while a Rukn (pillar) is an internal component of the prayer itself.
reference: Al-Fiqh al-Islami / Principles of Fiqh (Shurut vs Arkan al-Salah)

questionEn: Which foundational condition must be true of a person for their Salah to be accepted by Allah?
optionsEn: Being a Muslim, as worship is invalid without Iman
Having memorized at least one juz' of the Qur'an
Being a permanent resident rather than a traveler
Having reached forty years of age
explanationEn: Islam is the primary prerequisite for the validity of Salah and all acts of worship; Allah states that the deeds of those who disbelieve are not accepted.

questionEn: At what age did the Prophet (peace be upon him) instruct parents to command their children to pray?
optionsEn: Twelve years old
Ten years old
Seven years old
Five years old
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) instructed: 'Command your children to pray when they are seven years old, and discipline them over it when they are ten.' Seven is commonly linked with the age of discernment (tamyiz).

questionEn: Why is sanity ('Aql) a prerequisite for the obligation and validity of Salah?
optionsEn: Moral and legal accountability (Taklif) is lifted from someone who lacks reason
Because an unconscious person can only perform silent prayers
Because sanity is required only to recite Surah Al-Fatihah from memory
Because one must be able to calculate prayer times astronomically
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) taught that the pen of accountability is lifted from three people, including the insane person until he regains his sanity.

questionEn: What does the condition of 'Tamyiz' (discernment) signify regarding a young child's prayer?
optionsEn: The child is permitted to lead adult congregational prayers in all obligatory prayers
The child understands basic speech, intention, and the general meaning of prayer, making their prayer valid though not yet obligatory
The child must repeat every prayer performed before turning fifteen
The child has reached puberty and is now sinful if they miss a prayer
explanationEn: A discerning (mumayyiz) child understands the basic meaning of prayer and intention; their Salah is valid and rewarded, even though prayer only becomes strictly obligatory upon puberty.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse establishes that Salah is prescribed at fixed, appointed times?
optionsEn: Surah An-Nisa 4:103: 'Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times'
Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:6: 'When you rise to prayer, wash your faces...'
Surah Al-Kawthar 108:2: 'So pray to your Lord and sacrifice'
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:238: 'Maintain with care the prayers and the middle prayer'
explanationEn: Surah An-Nisa 4:103 explicitly states that Salah is a timed obligation (kitaban mawquta), meaning each prayer has a defined start and end window.

questionEn: Which prayer's time begins immediately after the sun passes its zenith (Zawal) and shadows start lengthening eastward?
optionsEn: Maghrib
Asr
Fajr
Dhuhr
explanationEn: The time of Dhuhr enters as soon as the sun declines past its meridian (zenith), as explained by the Prophet (peace be upon him) in the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr.

questionEn: According to the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, when does the time of Maghrib end?
optionsEn: When the evening twilight (red afterglow, al-shafaq) disappears from the horizon
When the crescent moon sets
Ten minutes after sunset
At astronomical midnight
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) stated that the time of Maghrib lasts as long as the twilight (al-shafaq) has not vanished, at which point Isha begins.

questionEn: What marks the beginning of Fajr prayer time?
optionsEn: Two hours after the disappearance of the western twilight
The appearance of the true dawn (Fajr Sadiq), a horizontal white light spreading across the eastern horizon
The vertical column of light known as the false dawn (Fajr Kadhib)
The exact moment the upper limb of the sun appears
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) distinguished between the false dawn (vertical light) and the true dawn (horizontal light spreading along the horizon), stating that Fajr time begins with the true dawn.

questionEn: Which type of purification removes minor ritual impurity (al-Hadath al-Asghar) as a condition for Salah?
optionsEn: Ghusl only, as Wudu is merely recommended
Sprinkling rosewater over the chest
Removing dust from one's shoes
Wudu (or Tayammum when water is unavailable or harmful)
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah does not accept the prayer of any one of you if he nullifies his state of purity until he performs Wudu.' Tayammum substitutes when water cannot be used.

questionEn: What is required before praying if a person is in a state of major ritual impurity (Janabah)?
optionsEn: Waiting until the next prayer time enters
Reciting Ayatul Kursi three times before Takbir
Performing Ghusl (full-body ritual bath), or Tayammum if legitimately unable to use water
Performing Wudu twice without washing the body
explanationEn: Major ritual impurity (Janabah) requires Ghusl before prayer, as commanded in Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:6 ('And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves').

questionEn: Which three things must be free from physical filth (Najasah) as a condition of Salah?
optionsEn: The worshipper's body, their clothing, and the specific spot where they pray
Only the prayer mat and the shoes left outside
The entire building, all furniture inside, and the worshipper's pockets
Only the worshipper's hands, face, and forehead
explanationEn: Purification from physical impurity (Najasah) encompasses the worshipper's body, garments, and place of prostration/standing, supported by the command to purify garments and remove filth from the masjid.

questionEn: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) realized mid-prayer that his sandals had filth on them after Jibril informed him, what did he do?
optionsEn: He completed the prayer with the sandals on and repeated it afterward
He broke the prayer immediately and repeated Wudu
He took his sandals off during the prayer and continued praying without restarting
He performed Sujud al-Sahw before the Salam
explanationEn: When Jibril informed him of impurity on his sandals, the Prophet (peace be upon him) removed them while continuing his prayer, teaching that removing Najasah immediately preserves the validity of the prayer if done without delay.

questionEn: What happens to a person's Salah if they genuinely forgot or were unaware of Najasah on their garment and only discovered it after finishing?
optionsEn: They must perform two prostrations of Sahw without repeating the prayer
They must perform Ghusl and repeat all prayers of that day
They must pay expiation (Kaffarah) to the poor
According to the narration of the Prophet removing his sandals, many scholars hold the prayer remains valid and need not be repeated
explanationEn: Because the Prophet (peace be upon him) did not restart the part of the prayer already performed before Jibril alerted him of impurity on his sandals, many jurists hold that praying with unnoticed Najasah out of ignorance or forgetfulness does not invalidate the prayer.

questionEn: What is the minimal Awrah that a man must cover during Salah according to the majority of jurists?
optionsEn: Only the private parts themselves
From the navel to the knees
From the neck to the wrists
From the chest to the ankles
explanationEn: Jurists agree that a man's Awrah in prayer encompasses the region from the navel to the knees, while also noting the Sunnah and Prophetic prohibition against praying in a single garment with bare shoulders.

questionEn: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him) forbid regarding a man's shoulders when praying in a single garment?
optionsEn: Praying while wearing a turban over the head
Praying with sleeves reaching the wrists
Praying in a single garment with nothing covering any part of his shoulders
Praying in a white garment during midday
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'None of you should pray in a single garment with no part of it over his shoulders.'

questionEn: What parts of a free adult woman's body may remain uncovered during Salah when no non-mahram men are present?
optionsEn: Her face and hands (up to the wrists), according to the majority of scholars
Her face, hands, and feet below the ankles according to all scholars
Only her eyes and fingertips
Her face, hair, and forearms
explanationEn: According to the majority of jurists, a woman's entire body is Awrah in prayer except her face and hands, while the Hanafi school also permits uncovering the feet; the Prophet noted that the prayer of a woman who has reached menstruation is not accepted without a head-covering (khimar).

questionEn: Why is wearing sheer or transparent clothing that reveals skin tone insufficient for covering the Awrah in Salah?
optionsEn: Because the Prophet forbade all dyed garments in prayer
Because only wool and cotton are valid materials for prayer clothes
Because transparent fabric always holds static electricity
Covering the Awrah requires a fabric that conceals the color of the skin beneath it
explanationEn: To fulfill the condition of satr al-awrah, the garment must prevent the skin color from showing through; transparent cloth fails to conceal the Awrah.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic command established facing Al-Masjid al-Haram (the Ka'bah) as the Qiblah for Muslims everywhere?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Hajj 22:26: 'Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf'
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:115: 'To Allah belong the east and the west'
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:144: 'So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you [believers] are, turn your faces toward it'
Surah Al-Anfal 8:45: 'O you who have believed, when you encounter a company, stand firm'
explanationEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah 2:144, Allah commanded the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the believers to shift the Qiblah from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Sacred Mosque in Makkah.

questionEn: When Muslims in Madinah were first commanded to face the Ka'bah, which mosque became famous because its congregation turned mid-prayer?
optionsEn: Masjid al-Qiblatayn
Masjid al-Khaif
Masjid al-Ghamamah
Masjid Quba
explanationEn: During an afternoon or Fajr prayer in Madinah, news of the revelation shifting the Qiblah reached a congregation, and they turned around mid-prayer toward Makkah; the mosque became known as Masjid al-Qiblatayn (Mosque of the Two Qiblahs).

questionEn: What is the ruling for a person inside Makkah who can directly see the Ka'bah versus someone praying far away from Makkah?
optionsEn: Both must face the exact millimeter of the Black Stone corner
Facing the Qiblah applies only inside the Arabian Peninsula
One who sees the Ka'bah must face its exact structure ('Ayn al-Ka'bah), while one far away must face its general direction (Jihah)
Someone far away may face any cardinal direction they prefer
explanationEn: Jurists explain that someone directly viewing the Ka'bah must face the building itself, whereas someone at a distance is obligated to face the direction (Jihah) of the Ka'bah, supported by the hadith: 'What is between the East and the West is Qiblah' (for Madinah).

questionEn: In which situation is a Muslim permitted to pray voluntary (Nafl) prayers without facing the Qiblah?
optionsEn: Whenever one feels too tired to turn around
While traveling on a riding mount or vehicle, facing whichever direction it travels
When praying Sunnah Rawatib inside the masjid
When praying inside a dark room at home
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to pray voluntary prayers on his mount while traveling, regardless of the direction it faced, though he would face the Qiblah for obligatory prayers by dismounting.

questionEn: What should a traveler do if they are uncertain of the Qiblah direction and have no one to ask and no compass?
optionsEn: Face due north by default in all regions
Strive to determine the direction using available signs (sun, stars, landmarks) and pray in that direction
Skip the prayer and make it up the next day
Delay the prayer indefinitely until returning home
explanationEn: Based on the Qur'anic principle 'Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity' and the example of Companions who exercised ijtihad on a cloudy night, a person investigates to the best of their ability and prays.

questionEn: If someone exercised sincere effort (Ijtihad) to find the Qiblah in an unfamiliar place, prayed, and later discovered they were facing slightly or completely the wrong way, what is the stronger ruling?
optionsEn: They must repeat the prayer and also fast three days
They must perform Sujud al-Sahw an hour later
Their prayer is automatically converted into a voluntary prayer
Their prayer is valid and does not need to be repeated
explanationEn: In a report narrated by Jabir and others, Companions prayed toward what they thought was the Qiblah on a dark night, discovered the mistake at dawn, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) told them their prayer was valid.

questionEn: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed while ill, injured, or in extreme fear (Salat al-Khawf) unable to turn to the Qiblah, how is the Qiblah condition handled?
optionsEn: The person recites Al-Fatihah without bowing or prostrating
One faces the Qiblah if able, and if genuinely unable due to fear or immobility, one prays in whichever direction they are able
A friend must physically carry and turn the person toward Makkah during every rak'ah
The prayer is postponed until danger passes or full mobility returns
explanationEn: Allah says in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:239: 'And if you fear [an enemy], then [pray] on foot or riding,' which scholars cite to show that facing the Qiblah is waived in cases of inability or active danger.

questionEn: Where is the Niyyah (intention) for Salah formed according to the Sunnah?
optionsEn: By reciting a specific Arabic formula aloud before Takbir
By writing the prayer name on a card
In the heart, without uttering it aloud
By raising the index finger while facing the Imam
explanationEn: Intention (Niyyah) is an act of the heart; neither the Prophet (peace be upon him) nor his Companions ever pronounced a verbal intention formula before starting Salah.

questionEn: Why is specifying the exact prayer (e.g., Dhuhr vs. Asr, or Fard vs. Sunnah) part of the Niyyah for obligatory prayers?
optionsEn: Because the Angel on the left side records only spoken specifications
Because without saying the Imam's name aloud, congregational prayer fails
Because Dhuhr and Asr have different verses in Al-Fatihah
Because multiple prayers share the same external actions and rak'ah count, so intention distinguishes one from another
explanationEn: Since Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha all consist of four rak'ahs with identical postures, the heart's intention distinguishes which specific obligatory prayer is being fulfilled, per 'Actions are judged by intentions.'

questionEn: What happens if a person is praying four rak'ahs of Dhuhr Sunnah and suddenly decides midway to change the intention into the Fard Dhuhr prayer?
optionsEn: It becomes valid as Fard if they perform Sujud al-Sahw
It counts as both Sunnah and Fard simultaneously
The Fard prayer is invalid because its specific intention did not exist from the beginning of the prayer
The prayer seamlessly converts into Fard Dhuhr
explanationEn: An obligatory prayer requires its specific Niyyah from Takbirat al-Ihram; switching from a general or voluntary prayer to a specific Fard midway does not fulfill the Fard.

questionEn: What if someone begins an obligatory prayer alone and then decides mid-prayer to switch their intention to a voluntary (Nafl) prayer in order to join an arriving congregation?
optionsEn: One must immediately utter 'I break my prayer' aloud
One must finish all four rak'ahs as Fard and is forbidden to join the congregation
Switching from Fard to Nafl is strictly impossible under all circumstances
Most jurists permit switching from a single Fard prayer to a general Nafl prayer so one can shorten it to two rak'ahs and join the congregation
explanationEn: Many jurists allow converting an individual Fard prayer into a two-rak'ah Nafl prayer so the worshipper can finish quickly and catch the congregational prayer (Jama'ah) without wasting the rak'ahs already prayed.

questionEn: What does maintaining 'continuity of intention' (Istishab hukm an-niyyah) mean during Salah?
optionsEn: Not forming a firm decision to break or abandon the prayer while inside it
Repeating the intention mentally before every single Takbir
Keeping one's eyes closed so no worldly thoughts enter
Never pausing to breathe between verses of Al-Fatihah
explanationEn: Continuity of Niyyah means the worshipper does not resolve to exit or nullify the prayer; brief distraction or wondering thoughts do not break the intention, whereas firmly deciding to quit the prayer invalidates it.

questionEn: What is the ruling on praying in a place where camels habitually kneel (Ma'atin al-Ibil)?
optionsEn: Camel pens are preferred because camels are gentle animals
The Prophet (peace be upon him) prohibited praying in camel pens, while permitting prayer in sheep pens
Both camel pens and sheep pens are equally prohibited
Only Fajr prayer is prohibited near animals
explanationEn: When asked about praying in sheep pens, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said 'Yes,' and when asked about camel pens, he said 'No, for they were created from devils' (or due to their restless, startling nature).

questionEn: Which two places did the Prophet (peace be upon him) explicitly declare unfit as a place of prayer in his statement: 'All of the earth is a masjid except...'?
optionsEn: Graveyards and bathrooms (hammam/toilets)
Markets and rooftops
Deserts and mountain caves
Ships and wooden bridges
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The entire earth is a place of prayer except graveyards and bathrooms (al-maqbarah wal-hammam).'

questionEn: Why did the Prophet (peace be upon him) forbid praying toward graves?
optionsEn: Because recitation cannot be heard near a graveyard
Because graves block the view of the moon
To prevent any resemblance to grave worship and to protect pure monotheism (Tawhid)
Because the earth around graves cannot hold a prayer mat
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) warned: 'Do not sit on graves and do not pray facing them,' guarding the Ummah against taking graves as places of worship.

questionEn: How did the Prophet (peace be upon him) handle a small spot of impurity (urine) poured in the masjid by a Bedouin?
optionsEn: He prohibited anyone from praying in the masjid for seven days
He covered the spot with a prayer rug without washing it
He ordered a bucket of water to be poured over it, purifying the spot immediately
He ordered the entire floor of the masjid to be dug up and replaced
explanationEn: Pouring a large bucket of water over urine on earthen ground diluted and removed the impurity, demonstrating the ease of purifying the place of prayer.

questionEn: If someone prays while wearing a garment that was acquired unlawfully (stolen/usurped), what is the view of the majority of jurists regarding the legal validity of the prayer?
optionsEn: All four schools agree the person must pay twice the garment's value to make the prayer valid
All four schools agree the prayer automatically brings double reward
The prayer is valid only if performed silently
The person is sinful for the theft, yet the prayer itself fulfills the outward obligation according to the majority (with the Hanbali view holding it invalid)
explanationEn: While wearing stolen clothing is a major sin, the majority (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i) separate the sin of usurpation from the validity of covering the Awrah, whereas the Hanbali school considers covering with a usurped garment invalid.

questionEn: What should a person do if they have no clean clothes at all and no way to wash or borrow a garment before the prayer time expires?
optionsEn: Pray as they are (even sitting to better conceal themselves) rather than missing the prayer time
Wait until midnight and combine all five prayers
Skip all prayers until new clothing is purchased
Perform Tayammum instead of praying
explanationEn: Conditions like covering the Awrah and wearing pure clothes are required according to ability ('Fear Allah as much as you are able'); one never abandons Salah completely due to lack of garments.

questionEn: When does the condition of 'Taharah' require repeating Wudu during Salah?
optionsEn: Whenever a dog barks outside the masjid
Only when one is certain of breaking Wudu—such as hearing a sound or smelling an odor—not based on mere doubt
Every time a person shifts their foot in Ruku'
Whenever a person feels any muscle twitch in their stomach
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) advised a man who felt something in his abdomen during prayer: 'He should not leave his prayer unless he hears a sound or smells an odor,' establishing the principle that certainty is not removed by doubt.

questionEn: What is the legal consequence of omitting a pillar (Rukn) of Salah, even out of forgetfulness?
optionsEn: Sujud al-Sahw alone completely erases the omission without performing the missed pillar
It invalidates the prayer only if it occurred in Fajr or Maghrib
It only reduces the reward by half while keeping the prayer valid
The prayer is incomplete until that pillar (or its replacement rak'ah) is performed; Sujud al-Sahw alone cannot substitute for it
explanationEn: Unlike a Sunnah or Wajib, a Rukn is part of the essence of the prayer; if missed unintentionally, it must be made up (or the entire rak'ah repeated) alongside Sujud al-Sahw, and if missed deliberately, the prayer is void.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse commands standing devoutly in obligatory prayer when physically able?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:238: '...and stand before Allah, devoutly obedient'
Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:1: 'O you who have believed, fulfill [all] contracts'
Surah Al-Muzzammil 73:20: 'Recite what is easy of the Qur'an'
Surah Al-Isra 17:78: 'Establish prayer at the decline of the sun'
explanationEn: Allah commands 'Wa qumu lillahi qanitin' ('And stand before Allah, devoutly obedient') in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:238, establishing Qiyam (standing) as a pillar of obligatory prayers.

questionEn: How did the Prophet (peace be upon him) instruct Imran ibn Husayn when Imran suffered from hemorrhoids and could not stand comfortably?
optionsEn: 'Skip the prayer until you recover completely'
'Pray standing for Fajr only and sit for the remaining four prayers'
'Delegate someone else to pray on your behalf'
'Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; and if you cannot, then lying on your side'
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) established the tiered rule of Qiyam based on capacity: stand if able, sit if unable to stand, and pray on one's side if unable to sit.

questionEn: What is the reward of a healthy person who chooses to pray a voluntary (Nafl) prayer sitting down when they are fully able to stand?
optionsEn: They receive half the reward of one who prays standing
They receive one-tenth of the reward
They receive the exact same reward as one standing
The voluntary prayer is completely invalid
explanationEn: Imran ibn Husayn narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever prays standing, that is best; whoever prays sitting gets half the reward of the one who stands.' (Those unable due to illness receive full reward.)

questionEn: If someone can stand for Takbirat al-Ihram and Al-Fatihah, or leans slightly on a wall/staff due to weakness, what is required in an obligatory prayer?
optionsEn: They may choose freely between sitting and standing in Fard prayers
They must sit for the entire prayer if they cannot stand without any support
They must stand as much as they are able (even with a cane or support) before sitting when unable to continue
They must pray lying down so as not to lean on anything
explanationEn: Because Qiyam is a pillar of obligatory Salah, a worshipper must fulfill whatever portion of standing they are capable of, using a staff or support if needed, rather than abandoning standing altogether.

questionEn: Which phrase constitutes Takbirat al-Ihram, the opening pillar that enters a person into the sacred state of Salah?
optionsEn: 'Allahu Akbar' (Allah is the Greatest)
'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim'
'Al-Hamdu lillahi Rabbil-Alamin'
'SubhanAllah wal-Hamdu lillah'
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The key to prayer is purification, its sacred opening (tahrim) is the Takbir, and its closing (tahlil) is the Taslim,' and specifically taught saying 'Allahu Akbar' to enter Salah.

questionEn: Why is the opening Takbir called 'Takbirat al-Ihram'?
optionsEn: Because upon pronouncing it, everyday actions like speaking, eating, and drinking become forbidden (haram) until the prayer ends
Because it makes movement of the eyes mandatory
Because it may only be uttered while wearing white Ihram garments
Because it is whispered only inside Masjid al-Haram
explanationEn: Takbirat al-Ihram ('Takbir of sacred prohibition') marks the threshold where worldly speech and actions become prohibited during the prayer, as described in 'its tahrim is the Takbir.'

questionEn: What posture must a capable person be in when uttering Takbirat al-Ihram in an obligatory prayer?
optionsEn: Standing fully upright; uttering it while still bending into Ruku' invalidates the obligatory Takbirat al-Ihram
Sitting in Tashahhud posture
Prostrating on the forehead
Already bowed in Ruku' to catch up with the Imam
explanationEn: A latecomer joining the Imam in Ruku' must pronounce Takbirat al-Ihram while standing completely upright before bowing; if pronounced while already stooping, Takbirat al-Ihram is not fulfilled.

questionEn: Is silently thinking 'Allahu Akbar' in one's mind without moving the tongue or lips sufficient for Takbirat al-Ihram?
optionsEn: Yes; mental thought replaces all verbal pillars of Salah
No; one must actually pronounce the words quietly enough to hear oneself (unless mute)
No, unless one shouts it as loudly as the Adhan
Yes, provided one raises both hands above the head
explanationEn: Verbal pillars like Takbirat al-Ihram, Al-Fatihah, and Taslim require articulation with the tongue and lips, not mere internal thought, except for someone physically unable to speak.

questionEn: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him) state regarding a prayer in which Surah Al-Fatihah is not recited?
optionsEn: 'The prayer is valid if one recites Surah Al-Ikhlas three times instead'
'Al-Fatihah is required only in the first rak'ah of Fajr'
'The prayer only lacks extra reward, though it remains valid'
'There is no prayer for the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatihah)'
explanationEn: Ubadah ibn as-Samit narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) declared: 'La salata liman lam yaqra bi-Fatihatil-Kitab' ('There is no prayer for whoever does not recite the Opening of the Book').

questionEn: In which rak'ahs of a four-rak'ah prayer is reciting Surah Al-Fatihah a pillar according to the majority (Shafi'i, Maliki, Hanbali) and the hadith of the man who prayed badly?
optionsEn: Only the first two rak'ahs
Every single rak'ah
Only the first rak'ah
Only the last two rak'ahs
explanationEn: After teaching the man who prayed poorly to recite what he knew (Al-Fatihah), the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Then do that throughout your entire prayer,' and Abu Hurayrah affirmed it is recited in every rak'ah.

questionEn: What should a new Muslim who has not yet memorized Surah Al-Fatihah recite in Salah while learning it?
optionsEn: Glorifications of Allah such as 'SubhanAllah, wal-Hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illallah, wallahu Akbar, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah'
They must remain completely silent and skip praying until memorized
They should repeat 'Allahu Akbar' fifty times instead
They should read a translation of Al-Fatihah in English during prayer
explanationEn: When a man told the Prophet (peace be upon him) he could not memorize the Qur'an, the Prophet taught him to say: 'SubhanAllah, wal-Hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illallah, wallahu Akbar, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.'

questionEn: In the Hadith Qudsi about Surah Al-Fatihah, how does Allah describe the dialogue during its recitation?
optionsEn: 'I have divided the prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves, and My servant shall have what he asks'
'The angels write down Al-Fatihah only on Fridays'
'Whoever recites Al-Fatihah fast finishes the prayer early'
'Half of Al-Fatihah belongs to Jibril and half to the Imam'
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim, Allah responds verse by verse as the servant recites Al-Fatihah: 'My servant has praised Me... glorified Me... entrusted himself to Me... This is between Me and My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks.'

questionEn: What is the primary criterion that defines a valid Ruku' (bowing)?
optionsEn: Bending the torso forward until the palms can comfortably reach the knees, with the back flat and steady
Bending the knees sharply while keeping the back upright
Dropping all the way until the chest touches the shins
Tilting the head slightly downward while keeping the spine vertical
explanationEn: In the Prophetic description of Ruku', the Prophet (peace be upon him) placed his hands firmly on his knees as if grasping them, and kept his back level—neither raising his head high nor letting it droop low.

questionEn: How did Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) describe the position of the Prophet's head during Ruku'?
optionsEn: He pressed his chin tightly against his chest
When he bowed, he neither raised his head upward nor lowered it sharply, keeping it level between the two
He turned his head slightly to the right
He tilted his head up to watch the Imam
explanationEn: Aishah reported: 'When he bowed, he neither raised his head nor let it drop, but kept it between those two (level with his back).'

questionEn: What happens if a worshipper drops straight from Ruku' into Sujud without pausing upright in I'tidal?
optionsEn: The prayer is invalid because rising completely from Ruku' and attaining stillness (I'tidal and Tuma'ninah) is a pillar
It is valid as long as they say 'Sami'Allahu liman hamidah' while falling
It is valid in Fajr and Asr but invalid in Maghrib
It is merely a minor disliked act with no effect on validity
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) told the man who prayed poorly: 'Then raise your head until you stand up straight (completely upright),' making full rising and tranquility after Ruku' a pillar of Salah.

questionEn: How did the Prophet (peace be upon him) describe the standing posture after rising from Ruku' (I'tidal)?
optionsEn: Rising halfway and immediately bending back down
Leaning forward at a 45-degree angle
Standing until every vertebra (bone of the spine) returns to its natural place
Standing on one's toes for three seconds
explanationEn: Abu Humayd as-Sa'idi described the Prophet's prayer: 'When he raised his head (from Ruku'), he stood upright until every vertebra returned to its place.'

questionEn: Which seven bones did the Prophet (peace be upon him) state a person is commanded to prostrate upon?
optionsEn: The crown of the head, two elbows, two knees, and two heels
The forehead (including the nose), the two hands, the two knees, and the tips of the toes of both feet
The forehead, two shoulders, two knees, and two heels
The chin, two wrists, two thighs, and two ankles
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'I have been commanded to prostrate on seven bones: the forehead—and he pointed with his hand to his nose—the two hands, the two knees, and the ends of the feet.'

questionEn: What happens to Sujud if a person intentionally lifts both feet completely off the floor throughout the entire prostration?
optionsEn: It only invalidates the prostration if done on Fridays
It is recommended because it makes the body lighter
The prostration is defective/invalid because resting the toes of both feet on the ground is required as part of the seven bones
It has no effect because only the forehead matters
explanationEn: Prostrating on all seven bones—including the toes of both feet—is commanded; deliberately keeping a required limb lifted throughout the entire Sujud violates the pillar of Sujud.

questionEn: In Sujud, how are the forehead and nose treated in the count of the seven bones?
optionsEn: They count as two separate bones, omitting the toes
Together they count as one bone; both should touch the ground
Neither needs to touch if one wears a cap over the forehead
Only the nose needs to touch the floor
explanationEn: When naming the seven bones, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said 'the forehead' and gestured to his nose as well, showing they function together as one unit on the ground.

questionEn: What if a worshipper wears a turban or cap whose thick edge covers the forehead so that the forehead itself does not touch the floor?
optionsEn: The turban alone counts as the forehead even if suspended inches above the ground
The forehead should make direct contact with the prayer surface (or through a thin normal cloth in extreme heat/cold per dispensation), rather than resting on a raised object carried on the head
One must remove all clothing above the waist
One should replace Sujud with a nod of the chin
explanationEn: Jurists stipulate that the forehead must firmly press against the place of prostration; Anas reported that in extreme heat the Companions would spread part of their garment under their foreheads, whereas a thick barrier attached to the head that prevents contact is avoided.

questionEn: How many prostrations (Sajdahs) are obligatory in every single rak'ah of Salah?
optionsEn: Two continuous prostrations without lifting the forehead in between
Two prostrations separated by a brief calm sitting
One prostration in odd rak'ahs and two in even rak'ahs
Three prostrations in Fajr and two in other prayers
