explanationEn: Every rak'ah contains two distinct prostrations with a calm sitting posture (Jalsah) between them, as taught explicitly in the hadith of the man who prayed poorly.

questionEn: What is the ruling on the sitting posture between the two prostrations (Jalsah bayn as-Sajdatayn)?
optionsEn: One should remain hovering slightly above the heels without sitting upright
It is an essential pillar (Rukn) in which the worshipper must sit upright calmly before making the second Sujud
It is required only in the second and fourth rak'ahs
It is an optional Sunnah that may be skipped to finish faster
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) instructed: 'Then raise your head until you are sitting calmly and at ease, then prostrate again,' establishing both the sitting and its tranquility as pillars.

questionEn: What is the Sunnah leg posture (Iftirash) while sitting between the two prostrations and in the first Tashahhud?
optionsEn: Sitting cross-legged with both ankles tucked under the thighs
Flattening the left foot to sit on it while keeping the right foot upright with its toes pointing toward the Qiblah
Flattening the right foot to sit on it and raising the left foot
Keeping both knees pulled up to the chest
explanationEn: Abu Humayd as-Sa'idi and Aishah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to spread out his left foot and keep his right foot upright (Iftirash) between the two prostrations and in the two-rak'ah Tashahhud.

questionEn: Which sitting posture (Tawarruk) is Sunnah during the final Tashahhud of a three- or four-rak'ah prayer?
optionsEn: Sitting on both heels with knees apart
Stretching both legs forward toward the Qiblah
Placing the left foot out under the right shin and resting the left hip directly on the ground, with the right foot upright
Resting on the right hip while folding the left knee upward
explanationEn: Abu Humayd as-Sa'idi described that in the final sitting (of a three- or four-rak'ah prayer), the Prophet (peace be upon him) brought his left foot forward under his right leg and sat directly on his left hip/buttock (Tawarruk).

questionEn: Which Tashahhud is a pillar (Rukn) of Salah according to the majority/Hanbali school, as opposed to the first Tashahhud?
optionsEn: The Tashahhud recited after Taslim
Neither Tashahhud is a pillar
The final Tashahhud (before the Taslim) and sitting for it
Only the first Tashahhud after two rak'ahs
explanationEn: The final Tashahhud and sitting for it are pillars (Arkan) without which the prayer cannot conclude properly, whereas the Prophet (peace be upon him) compensated for omitting the first Tashahhud with Sujud al-Sahw, showing it is a Wajib/Sunnah rather than a Rukn.

questionEn: Before the Tashahhud ('At-Tahiyyatu lillah...') was revealed, what mistake were the Companions making at the end of prayer that the Prophet corrected?
optionsEn: They were saying 'As-salamu ala Allah' (Peace be upon Allah), so the Prophet taught them that Allah Himself is As-Salam and taught them 'At-Tahiyyatu lillah...'
They were standing up to leave without sitting at all
They were clapping their hands to signal the end of prayer
They were reciting Surah Al-Fatihah a second time while sitting
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud reported that before Tashahhud was taught, they used to say 'Peace be upon Allah from His servants.' The Prophet (peace be upon him) corrected them: 'Do not say peace be upon Allah, for Allah is As-Salam; rather say: At-Tahiyyatu lillahi was-salawatu wat-tayyibat...'

questionEn: Why did Abdullah ibn Mas'ud say the Companions changed 'As-salamu alayka ayyuhan-Nabiyyu' to 'As-salamu alan-Nabiyyi' in some reports, while most scholars keep the original taught wording?
optionsEn: Because Ibn Mas'ud felt 'alayka' (upon you) addressed the Prophet directly while alive, though the majority retained the exact Prophetic wording taught as a greeting in absentia as well
Because Tashahhud was originally revealed in Persian
Because only the Imam says 'ayyuhan-Nabiyyu'
Because the Prophet forbade sending Salam upon prophets after Hijrah
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud narrated that they said 'As-salamu alayka ayyuhan-Nabiyyu' while the Prophet was among them and 'As-salamu alan-Nabiyyi' after his passing, while Umar and the majority preserved the exact wording taught by the Prophet.

questionEn: What does the opening word 'At-Tahiyyat' in the Tashahhud mean?
optionsEn: All prayers end at sunset
All physical prostrations belong to the angels
All charitable wealth belongs to the masjid
All greetings, tributes, sovereignty, and expressions of reverence belong solely to Allah
explanationEn: 'At-Tahiyyat' encompasses all forms of verbal homage, glorification, and sovereignty, affirming that ultimate honor and dominion belong exclusively to Allah.

questionEn: Which action officially exits the worshipper from the sacred state of Salah (Tahlil)?
optionsEn: The Taslim ('As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah')
Saying 'Amin' after the final dua
Raising the index finger at the end of Tashahhud
Wiping the face with both hands
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) stated: 'Its sacred opening is the Takbir, and its closing (tahlil) is the Taslim.'

questionEn: How did the Prophet (peace be upon him) perform the Taslim at the end of prayer?
optionsEn: Turning his head to the right saying 'As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah' until the whiteness of his right cheek was visible, then to the left saying 'As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah'
Shaking hands with the person on the right before turning left
Turning the entire torso 90 degrees to the right and left
Looking straight down and whispering 'Salam' once
explanationEn: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Ibn Mas'ud narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) gave Salam to his right and left so that the whiteness of his cheek could be seen from behind.

questionEn: Between the first Salam (to the right) and the second Salam (to the left), which does the majority of jurists (Maliki, Shafi'i, and one view of Hanbali) consider the minimal obligatory pillar?
optionsEn: Only the second Salam to the left
Three Salams including one straight ahead
The first Salam (while the Hanbali school's relied-upon position requires both Salams in Fard prayers)
Neither Salam is required if one stands up politely
explanationEn: Jurists agree the first Salam is essential to exit prayer, with the Hanbali school requiring both Salams in obligatory prayers and the Shafi'i/Maliki schools treating the first as the pillar and the second as Sunnah.

questionEn: In the famous hadith of the man who prayed badly ('Al-Musi'u Salatihi'), why did the Prophet (peace be upon him) repeatedly tell him 'Go back and pray, for you have not prayed'?
optionsEn: Because he prayed too slowly and kept the congregation waiting
Because he wore colorful garments during the prayer
Because he rushed through his postures without achieving tranquility and stillness (Tuma'ninah)
Because he forgot to perform Wudu beforehand
explanationEn: The man prayed swiftly in the mosque, and three times the Prophet (peace be upon him) told him he had not prayed, then taught him to pause in every posture—standing, bowing, rising, prostrating, and sitting—until fully at ease (tuma'ninah).

questionEn: What severe label did the Prophet (peace be upon him) apply to the person who does not complete their Ruku' and Sujud properly due to rushing?
optionsEn: 'The most forgetful traveler'
'The silent reciter'
'The one who speaks before the Imam'
'The worst thief among people is the one who steals from his own prayer'
explanationEn: When asked how a person steals from their prayer, the Prophet (peace be upon him) replied: 'He does not perfect its Ruku' and its Sujud' (or does not keep his back straight in them).

questionEn: What did Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman say to a man he saw rushing through Ruku' and Sujud without pausing?
optionsEn: 'Your prayer is valid, though you missed extra Sunnah reward'
'You should sit down for the rest of the day in the masjid'
'You have not prayed, and if you died in this state, you would die upon other than the natural way (Fitrah) upon which Allah created Muhammad'
'You must add two extra rak'ahs to make up for the speed'
explanationEn: Hudhayfah sternly warned the man that praying without proper stillness and completion in Ruku' and Sujud invalidates the prayer altogether.

questionEn: What does the pillar of 'Tuma'ninah' require in practical terms during each movement of Salah?
optionsEn: Rocking gently back and forth to stay alert
Remaining frozen in every posture for at least three full minutes
Closing one's eyes and holding one's breath during Ruku'
Every limb settles completely still for at least a brief moment (long enough to utter the obligatory dhikr calmly) before moving to the next posture
explanationEn: Tuma'ninah means complete physical stillness in each posture so that bones settle in their joints and the body is not in continuous motion between pillars.

questionEn: To what bird's rapid motion did the Prophet (peace be upon him) negatively compare a worshipper who rushes through Sujud without pausing?
optionsEn: The swimming of a duck
The soaring of an eagle
The singing of a nightingale
The pecking of a crow (naqr al-ghurab)
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) forbade three things in prayer, including 'pecking like a crow' (rapid, fleeting prostration without stillness).

questionEn: What does the pillar of 'Tartib' (proper sequence) require in Salah?
optionsEn: Reciting the Qur'an in reverse surah order
Performing the pillars in their prescribed Prophetic order—standing, recitation, bowing, rising, prostrating, sitting, prostrating—without reversing them
Arranging worshippers strictly by height
Praying Dhuhr before Fajr every morning
explanationEn: Tartib means maintaining the sequence taught by the Prophet (peace be upon him) when he said, 'Pray as you have seen me praying,' and demonstrated step-by-step in the hadith of the man who prayed poorly.

questionEn: What happens if a person deliberately performs Sujud before Ruku' in a rak'ah?
optionsEn: The prayer is invalidated because deliberately violating the prescribed sequence (Tartib) of pillars breaks Salah
It counts as two voluntary prayers
It is valid as long as they perform Ruku' afterward
It requires only saying Astaghfirullah after Salam
explanationEn: Deliberately altering the order of pillars violates Tartib, which is itself a pillar of Salah; if done forgetfully, one returns to the missed pillar in order and compensates with Sujud al-Sahw.

questionEn: If a worshipper prays behind an Imam and joins while the Imam is already bowing in Ruku', which pillars must the latecomer still perform before bowing to count that rak'ah?
optionsEn: Pronouncing Takbirat al-Ihram while sitting on the floor
Reciting the entire Surah Al-Fatihah while the Imam is in Ruku'
Performing two prostrations first and skipping Ruku'
Standing upright to pronounce Takbirat al-Ihram, then bowing into Ruku' with Tuma'ninah before the Imam rises
explanationEn: The latecomer must utter Takbirat al-Ihram while standing upright, then bow into Ruku' while the Imam is still in Ruku' (with stillness); the Prophet taught Abu Bakrah that catching Ruku' catches the rak'ah (meaning Al-Fatihah is borne by the Imam for that case).

questionEn: Why did the Prophet (peace be upon him) say to Abu Bakrah, 'May Allah increase your eagerness, but do not do it again,' when Abu Bakrah rushed into Ruku' before reaching the row?
optionsEn: Because Abu Bakrah prayed in the first row instead of the last
Because Abu Bakrah made Takbir and bowed before walking into the row instead of walking calmly to join the row first
Because Abu Bakrah recited Al-Fatihah too loudly
Because Abu Bakrah raised his hands during Ruku'
explanationEn: Abu Bakrah bowed outside the row and walked while bowed to reach the row; the Prophet (peace be upon him) appreciated his eagerness to catch the rak'ah (and did not tell him to repeat it) while instructing him not to bow outside the row again.

questionEn: What is the ruling on moving the tongue and lips when reciting Al-Fatihah in a silent prayer like Dhuhr or Asr?
optionsEn: Only the first verse needs to be pronounced
One must keep the mouth sealed and read silently with the eyes only
One should recite as loudly as in Fajr so the whole row hears
It is necessary to whisper/articulate the words with the tongue and lips so one can hear oneself, rather than merely reading mentally with closed lips
explanationEn: Khabbab confirmed the Prophet (peace be upon him) recited in Dhuhr and Asr by noticing the movement of his beard, showing silent prayer still involves quiet articulation rather than pure mental thought.

questionEn: If someone forgets to sit between the two prostrations and goes straight from the first Sujud into the second Sujud without sitting upright, what is required if remembered immediately?
optionsEn: Nothing is needed because one prostration covers both
They simply skip the second Sujud altogether
They must return to sitting between the two prostrations, perform the second Sujud properly, and make Sujud al-Sahw
They must recite Surah Al-Ikhlas while prostrating
explanationEn: Since the sitting between the two prostrations is a pillar, two consecutive prostrations without a separating sitting do not count as a valid rak'ah; one must sit and perform the second Sujud properly.

questionEn: What is the minimum requirement of the final sitting (Jalsah al-Akhirah) as a pillar of Salah?
optionsEn: Sitting on a chair even when able to sit on the floor
Sitting before the first prostration
Sitting for the duration required to recite the obligatory portion of the final Tashahhud (and Salawat according to Shafi'is/Hanbalis) and utter the Taslim
Sitting for at least five minutes after Taslim
explanationEn: The final sitting is a pillar specifically because it is the posture in which the final Tashahhud and Taslim are performed.

questionEn: Which prophetic statement summarizes the overarching duty of learning and performing the pillars of Salah accurately?
optionsEn: 'Pray as you have seen me praying'
'Only scholars need to learn the pillars of Salah'
'Pray whichever way feels quickest in your heart'
'Every tribe may design its own order of postures'
explanationEn: Malik ibn al-Huwayrith narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Sallu kama ra'aytumuni usalli' ('Pray as you have seen me praying'), making his demonstrated sequence and pillars the binding model for the Ummah.

questionEn: When a worshipper rises from Sujud to stand for the next rak'ah, how should they perform the transition according to the Sunnah?
optionsEn: By remaining kneeling for two minutes before standing
By omitting the Takbir completely when rising from Sujud
By jumping up rapidly before the Imam finishes Sujud
By resting briefly in a sitting position (Jalsat al-Istirahah) or rising smoothly on the balls of the feet while saying the Takbir, without rushing
explanationEn: Malik ibn al-Huwayrith reported that when the Prophet (peace be upon him) was in an odd-numbered rak'ah, he would sit upright briefly before rising to stand (Jalsat al-Istirahah), while other narrations describe rising smoothly while pronouncing Takbir.

questionEn: In the Hanbali classification of prayer acts, how does a Wajib (obligatory act) differ from a Sunnah?
optionsEn: A Wajib is performed only in voluntary prayers, whereas a Sunnah is only for Fard prayers
Omitting a Wajib deliberately invalidates the prayer and omitting it forgetfully requires Sujud al-Sahw, whereas omitting a Sunnah does not invalidate the prayer or require Sujud al-Sahw
There is no practical difference between a Wajib, a Rukn, and a Sunnah
A Sunnah invalidates the prayer if omitted forgetfully, whereas a Wajib never requires Sujud al-Sahw
explanationEn: Jurists who distinguish between Rukn, Wajib, and Sunnah explain that a Wajib is excused by forgetfulness (compensated with Sujud al-Sahw) unlike a Rukn which must be performed, while omitting a Sunnah does not affect validity at all.

questionEn: Which opening supplication (Dua al-Istiftah) begins with 'Allahumma ba'id bayni wa bayna khatayaya kama ba'adta baynal-mashriqi wal-maghrib'?
optionsEn: The supplication recited after exiting the masjid
The Dua al-Istiftah narrated by Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (peace be upon him) recited silently between Takbirat al-Ihram and Al-Fatihah
The Qunut supplication of Witr prayer
The supplication recited exclusively between the two prostrations
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) what he said during his silent pause between Takbir and recitation, and he replied with 'Allahumma ba'id bayni wa bayna khatayaya...' (O Allah, distance me from my sins as You distanced the East from the West).

questionEn: Which shorter Dua al-Istiftah did Umar ibn al-Khattab recite aloud to teach the congregation?
optionsEn: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, wa tabarakasmuka, wa ta'ala jadduka, wa la ilaha ghayruk'
'Rabbana lakal-hamdu hamdan kathiran tayyiban mubarakan fih'
'Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ala ali Muhammad'
'Sajada wajhi lilladhi khalaqahu wa sawwarahu'
explanationEn: Umar ibn al-Khattab used to recite 'Subhanakallahumma wa bihamdika...' at the start of prayer so the people would learn this authentic Sunnah opening supplication.

questionEn: At what exact moment in the prayer is Dua al-Istiftah recited?
optionsEn: Immediately after Taslim at the end of prayer
Immediately after Takbirat al-Ihram and before seeking refuge (Ta'awwudh) and reciting Al-Fatihah in the first rak'ah only
Before saying Takbirat al-Ihram
At the beginning of every single rak'ah
explanationEn: Dua al-Istiftah is an opening Sunnah placed exclusively between Takbirat al-Ihram and the Ta'awwudh/recitation in the first rak'ah.

questionEn: Why is seeking refuge with Allah (Ta'awwudh: 'A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim') recited before Al-Fatihah?
optionsEn: Only to alert the congregation that recitation is starting
Because it replaces Ruku' in the first rak'ah
Because it counts as the first verse of Surah Al-Fatihah
In obedience to the Qur'anic command: 'So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the expelled [from His mercy]'
explanationEn: Surah An-Nahl 16:98 commands seeking refuge in Allah before reciting the Qur'an; in Salah, this is done silently in the first rak'ah (or before recitation) prior to Basmalah and Al-Fatihah.

questionEn: According to the narration of Anas ibn Malik regarding the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar, how did they recite 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim' in loud congregational prayers?
optionsEn: Silently (inaudibly) before starting 'Al-Hamdu lillahi Rabbil-Alamin' aloud
As loudly as the rest of Surah Al-Fatihah in every prayer
They recited Bismillah only after finishing Al-Fatihah
They omitted Bismillah entirely even silently
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik reported: 'I prayed behind the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman, and they used to begin (aloud) with Al-Hamdu lillahi Rabbil-Alamin,' meaning they recited Bismillah silently (while Shafi'i jurists cite other reports to recite it aloud).

questionEn: According to the narration of Abdullah ibn Umar, at which four places in Salah did the Prophet (peace be upon him) raise his hands (Raf' al-Yadayn)?
optionsEn: When saying Amin and when making Taslim
At Takbirat al-Ihram, when bowing for Ruku', when rising from Ruku', and when standing up from the second rak'ah (first Tashahhud)
Before and after every single prostration (Sujud)
Only at Takbirat al-Ihram and never again during prayer
explanationEn: Ibn Umar reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him) raised his hands to shoulder level upon opening the prayer, when saying Takbir for Ruku', when raising his head from Ruku', and when standing up after two rak'ahs—and did not do so in Sujud.

questionEn: To what height did the Prophet (peace be upon him) raise his hands during Raf' al-Yadayn according to authentic narrations?
optionsEn: Tapping the sides of his knees
Only up to waist level
Level with his shoulders or level with his earlobes
Fully extended straight above the crown of his head
explanationEn: Narrations from Ibn Umar describe raising the hands parallel to the shoulders (hadhwa mankibayh), while Malik ibn al-Huwayrith described raising them parallel to the earlobes/ears; both are authentic Sunnah forms.

questionEn: What is the Sunnah position of the hands during Qiyam (standing in Salah) while reciting?
optionsEn: Placing the right hand over the left hand/forearm (Qabd) over the chest or upper torso
Placing the left hand over the right hand on the knees
Interlacing the fingers behind the back
Holding the hands outward like in Dua
explanationEn: Sahl ibn Sa'd stated: 'The people were commanded that a man should place his right hand over his left forearm during prayer,' and Wa'il ibn Hujr described the Prophet placing his right hand over the back of his left hand, wrist, and forearm.

questionEn: When the Imam finishes reciting 'Ghayril-maghdubi alayhim wa lad-dallin' in a loud prayer, what is the Sunnah for both the Imam and the followers?
optionsEn: To say 'SubhanAllah' loudly
To say 'Amin' aloud (in loud prayers) and together
To remain completely silent so only the Imam says Amin
To bow immediately without saying Amin
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'When the Imam says Amin, then say Amin, for whoever's Amin coincides with the Amin of the angels will have his past sins forgiven.'

questionEn: What does the word 'Amin' mean at the conclusion of Surah Al-Fatihah?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, forgive our parents only'
'Praise be to the angels'
'The prayer has concluded'
'O Allah, answer/accept [our supplication]'
explanationEn: Because the second half of Al-Fatihah is a supplication for guidance to the straight path, saying 'Amin' means 'O Allah, respond and accept.'
reference: Fath al-Bari (Ibn Hajar); Tafsir Ibn Kathir

questionEn: In which rak'ahs of a four-rak'ah prayer is it Sunnah to recite another Surah or verses from the Qur'an after Al-Fatihah?
optionsEn: Only the first rak'ah
Only the third and fourth rak'ahs
All four rak'ahs equally in every prayer
The first two rak'ahs
explanationEn: Abu Qatadah narrated that in Dhuhr and Asr, the Prophet (peace be upon him) recited Al-Fatihah and a Surah in the first two rak'ahs, and only Al-Fatihah in the last two rak'ahs (with occasional exceptions reported by Abu Sa'id).

questionEn: Which length of Surahs (from the Mufassal section of the Qur'an) is it generally Sunnah to recite in Fajr prayer?
optionsEn: Tiwal al-Mufassal (the longer Mufassal surahs, roughly from Surah Qaf to An-Naba')
Qisar al-Mufassal (only the shortest surahs like Al-Kawthar)
Exclusively Surah Al-Fatihah with nothing after it
Only single-line verses from Surah Al-Baqarah
explanationEn: Narrations from Sulayman ibn Yasar and others describe the Prophet (peace be upon him) lengthening Fajr with longer Mufassal surahs (e.g., 60 to 100 verses), shortening Maghrib with shorter ones, and reciting medium Mufassal surahs in Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha.

questionEn: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) heard a baby crying during congregational prayer, what did he do regarding his Surah recitation?
optionsEn: He skipped Ruku' in that rak'ah
He shortened his recitation out of mercy for the mother
He stopped the prayer and sent the mother home
He lengthened the recitation to test the congregation's patience
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'I stand in prayer intending to lengthen it, then I hear the crying of a child, so I shorten my prayer, disliking to cause distress to his mother.'

questionEn: What is the ruling on the transition Takbirs ('Allahu Akbar' when bowing, prostrating, sitting, and standing) in the Hanbali school versus the majority?
optionsEn: All four schools agree they should be omitted when praying alone
The Hanbali school classifies them as Wajib (obligatory), while the majority (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i) classify them as emphasized Sunnah
All four schools agree they are Pillars (Arkan) whose omission voids the prayer even if forgotten
Only the Imam is allowed to say transition Takbirs
explanationEn: Based on the hadith 'Pray as you have seen me praying' and Ibn Mas'ud's report that the Prophet pronounced Takbir at every lowering and rising, Hanbalis classify Takbirat al-Intiqal as Wajib while the majority treat them as Sunnah.

questionEn: Which transition in Salah does NOT use 'Allahu Akbar', and what is said instead?
optionsEn: Sitting between the two prostrations; one says 'Astaghfirullah'
Rising from Ruku' to standing; one says 'Sami'Allahu liman hamidah' (followed by 'Rabbana wa lakal-hamd')
Standing up for the third rak'ah; one says 'Al-Hamdu lillah'
Going down into the first Sujud; one says 'SubhanAllah'
explanationEn: Every transition in prayer uses 'Allahu Akbar' except rising from Ruku', where 'Sami'Allahu liman hamidah' (Allah hears whoever praises Him) is said.

questionEn: When praying behind an Imam, what should the follower say when the Imam rises from Ruku' and says 'Sami'Allahu liman hamidah'?
optionsEn: 'Allahu Akbar' loudly
'Subhana Rabbiyal-Azim'
'Sami'Allahu liman hamidah' only, without adding praise
'Rabbana wa lakal-hamd' (or 'Allahumma Rabbana lakal-hamd')
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) instructed: 'When the Imam says Sami'Allahu liman hamidah, say Allahumma Rabbana lakal-hamd; for whoever's words coincide with the words of the angels will have his past sins forgiven.'

questionEn: What additional words did a Companion add after 'Rabbana wa lakal-hamd' that caused the Prophet (peace be upon him) to see thirty-something angels racing to record them?
optionsEn: 'Hamdan kathiran tayyiban mubarakan fih'
'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah'
'Allahummaghfir li warhamni'
'Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la wa bihamdih'
explanationEn: Rifa'ah ibn Rafi' narrated that a man behind the Prophet said 'Rabbana wa lakal-hamd, hamdan kathiran tayyiban mubarakan fih,' and the Prophet said he saw over thirty angels competing to write it down first.

questionEn: Which dhikr is recited in Ruku' (bowing), and how does it reflect the Qur'anic command in Surah Al-Waqi'ah 56:74?
optionsEn: 'Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la', fulfilling Surah Al-A'la
'Astaghfirullah al-Azim', fulfilling Surah Nuh
'Subhana Rabbiyal-Azim' ('Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty'), fulfilling 'So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great'
'Allahu Akbar Kabira', fulfilling Surah Al-Muddathir
explanationEn: When 'Fasabbih bismi Rabbikal-Azim' was revealed, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Put it in your Ruku',' establishing 'Subhana Rabbiyal-Azim' as the standard dhikr of bowing.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet (peace be upon him) forbid reciting the Qur'an while in Ruku' or Sujud?
optionsEn: Because Ruku' is a posture for glorifying the Lord (Ta'zim) and Sujud is a posture for diligent supplication (Dua), not Qur'an recitation
Because recitation in Ruku' takes too much breath
Because angels cannot hear recitation near the floor
Because the Qur'an may only be recited while sitting
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed I have been forbidden to recite the Qur'an while bowing or prostrating. As for bowing, glorify the Lord in it; and as for prostrating, strive hard in supplication, for it is worthy of being answered.'

questionEn: Which dhikr did Aishah report the Prophet (peace be upon him) frequently said in his Ruku' and Sujud after Surah An-Nasr was revealed?
optionsEn: 'La ilaha illa Anta subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimin'
'Subhanakallahumma Rabbana wa bihamdika, Allahummaghfir li'
'HasbunAllahu wa ni'mal-Wakil'
'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un'
explanationEn: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said that after Surah An-Nasr ('Fasabbih bihamdi Rabbika wastaghfirh') was revealed, the Prophet (peace be upon him) frequently recited 'Subhanakallahumma Rabbana wa bihamdika, Allahummaghfir li' in Ruku' and Sujud, acting upon the Qur'an.

questionEn: Which dhikr is prescribed in Sujud (prostration), fulfilling Surah Al-A'la 87:1?
optionsEn: 'Subhana Rabbiyal-Azim'
'Al-Hamdu lillahi Rabbil-Alamin'
'Sami'Allahu liman hamidah'
'Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la' ('Glory be to my Lord, the Most High')
explanationEn: When 'Sabbihisma Rabbikal-A'la' was revealed, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Put it in your Sujud,' and Hudhayfah narrated that he repeated 'Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la' in prostration.

questionEn: Why is increasing personal Dua (supplication) especially encouraged during Sujud?
optionsEn: Because Dua is forbidden after the Tashahhud
Because the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is in prostration, so increase supplication'
Because speaking in Sujud replaces Al-Fatihah
Because Sujud is the longest posture in every prayer automatically
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) highlighted Sujud as the moment of greatest spiritual closeness to Allah, making it prime for sincere Dua.

questionEn: What is the Sunnah placement of the elbows and arms during Sujud?
optionsEn: Stretching both arms straight behind the back
Resting the elbows and forearms flat on the prayer mat
Keeping the forearms raised off the floor and holding the upper arms away from the sides of the torso (without crowding neighbors in congregation)
Tucking the elbows tightly against the ribs and thighs
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Be balanced in Sujud, and let none of you spread his forearms out like a dog.' He used to keep his upper arms away from his sides unless cramped in a row.

questionEn: Which supplication is Sunnah/Wajib to recite while sitting between the two prostrations (Jalsah bayn as-Sajdatayn)?
optionsEn: 'Subhana Rabbiyal-Azim' three times
'Sami'Allahu liman hamidah'
'Rabbighfir li, Rabbighfir li' (or 'Allahummaghfir li, warhamni, wahdini, wajburni, wa 'afini, warzuqni')
'At-Tahiyyatu lillahi was-salawatu wat-tayyibat'
explanationEn: Hudhayfah narrated that between the two prostrations the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to say 'Rabbighfir li, Rabbighfir li,' and Ibn Abbas narrated the fuller supplication asking for forgiveness, mercy, guidance, healing/sufficiency, and provision.

questionEn: How long did the Prophet (peace be upon him) make the sitting between the two prostrations and the standing after Ruku' compared to his Ruku' and Sujud?
optionsEn: Nearly equal in duration, avoiding hasty rising or sitting
Less than half a second, just touching the heels
Ten times longer than Ruku'
Only long enough to inhale once
explanationEn: Al-Bara' ibn Azib reported that the Prophet's Ruku', Sujud, standing after Ruku', and sitting between the two prostrations were nearly equal in length.

questionEn: How is the first Tashahhud (after the second rak'ah of a 3- or 4-rak'ah prayer) meant to be performed in terms of length?
optionsEn: Relatively brief—like sitting on heated stones—reciting At-Tahiyyat and then rising promptly without adding lengthy personal duas
Followed immediately by the Taslim to the right
Longer than the final Tashahhud
Recited while standing upright
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud narrated that when the Prophet (peace be upon him) sat after the first two rak'ahs, it was as if he were sitting on heated stones (meaning he kept it brief and rose right after At-Tahiyyat).

questionEn: In the Sunnah, what is done with the right index finger during Tashahhud?
optionsEn: Both hands are raised to shoulder height throughout Tashahhud
All five fingers are spread wide on the thigh without moving
The left index finger is pointed toward the ceiling
The fingers are curled or the thumb and middle finger form a ring, and the right index finger is raised pointing toward the Qiblah while looking toward it
explanationEn: Ibn Umar and Wa'il ibn Hujr described the Prophet (peace be upon him) curling his fingers or making a circle with the thumb and middle finger and pointing with his right index finger in Tashahhud while keeping his gaze on it.

questionEn: What is the Salawat Ibrahimiyyah recited in the final Tashahhud?
optionsEn: A special dua recited only inside Masjid Ibrahim in Makkah
Sending blessings and peace upon Prophet Muhammad and his family just as Allah sent blessings upon Prophet Ibrahim and his family
The opening Takbir of Eid prayer
A supplication recited when entering a graveyard
explanationEn: When the Companions asked how to send Salah (blessings) upon him after Surah Al-Ahzab 33:56 was revealed, the Prophet (peace be upon him) taught 'Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ala ali Muhammad kama sallayta ala Ibrahim...'

questionEn: From which four things did the Prophet (peace be upon him) instruct Muslims to seek refuge at the end of the final Tashahhud before making Salam?
optionsEn: The punishment of Hellfire, the punishment of the grave, the trials of life and death, and the evil trial of the False Messiah (Masih ad-Dajjal)
Wild beasts, storms at sea, eclipses, and earthquakes
Illness, old age, sleeplessness, and hunger
Poverty, travel delays, forgetting surahs, and rain
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) instructed: 'When one of you finishes the final Tashahhud, let him seek refuge in Allah from four things: from the torment of Hell, the torment of the grave, the trials of life and death, and the evil of the trial of al-Masih ad-Dajjal.'

questionEn: What short supplication for forgiveness did Abu Bakr as-Siddiq ask the Prophet (peace be upon him) to teach him for inside his prayer (at the end before Salam)?
optionsEn: 'Allahumma ahsin aqibatana fil-umuri kulliha'
'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanah'
'SubhanAllah wal-Hamdu lillah wa la ilaha illallah'
'Allahumma inni zalamtu nafsi zulman kathiran, wa la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa Anta, faghfir li maghfiratan min 'indika warhamni, innaka Antal-Ghafurur-Rahim'
explanationEn: Abu Bakr asked for a dua to say in his prayer, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) taught him this heartfelt confession of sin and plea for Allah's forgiveness and mercy.

questionEn: What is a 'Sutrah' in Salah, and why is placing one in front of a person praying alone or as an Imam Sunnah?
optionsEn: A thin curtain wrapped around the worshipper's waist
A small stone placed on the forehead during Sujud
A special prayer mat reserved only for the Imam
A physical barrier (like a wall, pillar, chair, or object about a saddle-back's height) placed in front to demarcate the prayer space and prevent passersby from crossing directly in front
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you prays, let him pray facing a Sutrah and draw close to it,' establishing a boundary so people do not walk right in front of his place of prostration.

questionEn: How tall should a Sutrah ideally be according to the Prophet's description?
optionsEn: At least taller than a standing adult
Exactly three meters high
At least about the height of the back of a camel saddle (roughly two-thirds of a cubit / around 30–45 cm)
Flat like a thin piece of paper on the floor
explanationEn: Talhah ibn Ubaydillah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said when someone sets something like the back of a saddle (mu'akhkhirat ar-rahl) in front of them, they need not worry about who passes beyond it.

questionEn: How close should the worshipper stand to their Sutrah?
optionsEn: At least ten meters away from the wall
With their forehead touching the Sutrah while standing
Halfway across the prayer hall
Close enough that there is only about enough space for a sheep to pass between the place of prostration/feet and the Sutrah (roughly three cubits from feet to wall)
explanationEn: Sahl ibn Sa'd reported that between the Prophet's place of prayer and the wall there was space enough for a sheep to pass, and Ibn Umar noted about three cubits between the Ka'bah wall and the Prophet's standing spot.

questionEn: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him) say about the gravity of passing directly in front of someone who is praying?
optionsEn: 'If the one who passes in front of a praying person knew what [sin] is upon him, it would be better for him to stand waiting for forty rather than pass in front of him'
'Only passing during Fajr carries any blame'
'Walking in front of someone praying invalidates the passerby's Wudu'
'Passing in front of a praying person carries no sin if one walks swiftly'
explanationEn: Abu Juhaym narrated this stern warning, with the narrator remarking he did not know whether the Prophet meant forty days, months, or years—emphasizing how serious it is to cross in front of someone praying.

questionEn: What should a praying person do if someone tries to walk right in front of them between them and their Sutrah?
optionsEn: Turn 90 degrees to let them walk past
Break the prayer immediately and chase them
Shout loudly at them to leave the masjid
Gently block or push them back with a hand signal; and if they insist, block them more firmly
explanationEn: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'If anyone tries to pass in front of you while you are praying, repel him; if he refuses, repel him again; and if he still refuses, fight/push him back, for he is but a devil (or driven by Shaytan).'

questionEn: In a congregational prayer, does every follower in the rows need to place a personal Sutrah in front of themselves?
optionsEn: Yes; every worshipper must carry a stick into the row
Only the first row is covered by the Imam's Sutrah
Yes, unless the masjid has carpets
No; the Imam's Sutrah serves as a Sutrah for all those praying behind him
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas narrated that he rode a donkey across part of the row while the Prophet (peace be upon him) was leading prayer at Mina, and nobody objected—demonstrating that the Imam's Sutrah suffices for the congregation.

questionEn: Where should a worshipper direct their gaze while standing, bowing, and sitting in Salah (according to the majority of scholars)?
optionsEn: Around the room to watch who enters the masjid
Toward the place of prostration (sujud) on the ground while standing (and toward the raised index finger in Tashahhud)
Strictly closed throughout every prayer
Upward toward the ceiling or sky to show humility
explanationEn: Aishah reported that when the Prophet (peace be upon him) entered the Ka'bah to pray, his gaze never wandered from the place of his prostration until he came out, and Ibn Umar noted looking toward the pointing finger in Tashahhud.

questionEn: What is the Sunnah Qunut supplication in Witr prayer that the Prophet (peace be upon him) taught his grandson al-Hasan ibn Ali?
optionsEn: 'Allahummahdini fiman hadayt, wa 'afini fiman 'afayt, wa tawallani fiman tawallayt...'
'Subhanakallahumma wa bihamdika wa tabarakasmuka'
'Rabbana wa lakal-hamd hamdan kathiran'
'Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik'
explanationEn: Al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) taught him these exact words to recite in the Qunut of Witr, asking Allah for guidance, well-being, protection, and blessing.

questionEn: At what point in the final rak'ah of Witr is Qunut normally recited according to the authentic narrations?
optionsEn: Either after rising from Ruku' (before Sujud) or right before bowing into Ruku' after finishing Qur'anic recitation—both have precedent, with after Ruku' well-established in Nawazil and Witr
While lying in Sujud
Before Takbirat al-Ihram
After completing the Taslim
explanationEn: Narrations from Anas and others show Qunut was practiced both before Ruku' (reported by Ubayy ibn Ka'b in Witr) and after rising from Ruku' (reported by Abu Hurayrah and Anas in Nawazil and Witr).

questionEn: What is 'Qunut al-Nawazil', and when did the Prophet (peace be upon him) practice it?
optionsEn: Standing silently for ten minutes after Witr every night
Reciting Surah Al-Kahf after Ruku' on Fridays
Skipping the third rak'ah of Maghrib during heavy rain
Supplicating aloud in the final rak'ah after rising from Ruku' during obligatory prayers when a severe calamity or oppression befalls the Muslim community
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) practiced Qunut al-Nawazil for about a month in obligatory prayers (such as Fajr and others) after rising from Ruku', praying for oppressed believers or against active oppressors (such as after the tragedy of Bi'r Ma'unah).

questionEn: Should one wipe their face with their hands immediately after finishing Qunut or supplicating inside Salah?
optionsEn: According to many scholars (including Ahmad, Ibn Taymiyyah, and others), wiping the face after Qunut in Salah has no authentically established Prophetic basis, so one simply lowers the hands or goes into Sujud
One must clap before lowering the hands
Yes, one must wipe the chest and shoulders after every Dua
Yes, wiping the face three times is an obligatory pillar of Qunut
explanationEn: Al-Bayhaqi and later scholars noted that the narrations about wiping the face after Dua are weak and none establish it inside Salah after Qunut; thus many scholars advise simply lowering the hands without wiping the face.

questionEn: When moving into Sujud from standing after Ruku', what did the Companions report regarding whether the hands or knees touch the ground first?
optionsEn: One must jump forward onto both elbows first
Only one knee touches the floor
Both methods are reported in scholarly discussion: Wa'il ibn Hujr reported knees before hands, while Abu Hurayrah reported hands before knees (avoiding kneeling like a camel)
Only the forehead may touch before the hands and knees
explanationEn: Jurists discuss both authentic approaches: Wa'il ibn Hujr's report of placing knees then hands (followed by Hanafis, Shafi'is, and Hanbalis), and Abu Hurayrah's hadith 'Let none of you kneel as a camel kneels—let him place his hands before his knees' (followed by Malikis and Ibn Baz/Al-Albani).

questionEn: What is the Sunnah position of the hands during Sujud?
optionsEn: Fingers spread wide behind the hips
Clenched in tight fists under the chin
Palms flat on the ground beside the shoulders or ears, fingers together and pointing toward the Qiblah
Palms facing upward beside the knees
explanationEn: Wa'il ibn Hujr and Abu Humayd narrated that when the Prophet (peace be upon him) prostrated, he placed his palms flat parallel to his shoulders/ears with fingers closed together pointing toward the Qiblah.

questionEn: In a loud prayer like Fajr, Maghrib, or Isha, what is the Sunnah for the person praying alone regarding loudness of recitation?
optionsEn: Shouting at maximum volume in all five prayers
Using a microphone even when alone in a bedroom
Reciting moderately aloud (so they hear themselves clearly without disturbing others), though silent recitation is also valid
Whispering silently is strictly required when praying alone at Fajr
explanationEn: Reciting aloud in the first two rak'ahs of Fajr, Maghrib, and Isha is Sunnah for the Imam and permitted/recommended moderately for one praying alone, whereas Dhuhr and Asr are recited quietly.

questionEn: When did the Prophet (peace be upon him) pause slightly in prayer—a practice Abu Hurayrah asked him about—and what did he say during that pause?
optionsEn: Between every verse of Surah Al-Ikhlas
Right after Takbirat al-Ihram before beginning Al-Fatihah, during which he recited Dua al-Istiftah
Before saying Takbirat al-Ihram
Right after Taslim before standing up, during which he recited Surah Yasin
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah noticed a brief silence between Takbir and recitation and asked what the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, leading to the narration of 'Allahumma ba'id bayni wa bayna khatayaya...'

questionEn: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him) teach Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam as-Sulami when Mu'awiyah spoke aloud during prayer to bless a sneezing companion?
optionsEn: 'Speaking is permitted in prayer as long as it is good manners'
'Indeed, this prayer does not allow anything of human speech; it is only Tasbih, Takbir, and recitation of the Qur'an'
'Only whispering in a low voice is allowed during prayer'
'You must repeat your prayer and fast one day'
explanationEn: When Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam spoke during prayer out of ignorance of the prohibition, the Prophet (peace be upon him) gently explained after Salah that no ordinary human conversation is fitting inside prayer.

questionEn: Which companion narrated that the early Muslims used to speak to one another during Salah until the verse 'And stand before Allah, devoutly obedient (qanitin)' was revealed?
optionsEn: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari
Zayd ibn Arqam
Bilal ibn Rabah
Sa'd ibn Mu'adh
explanationEn: Zayd ibn Arqam reported: 'We used to speak during prayer—a man would speak to his companion beside him—until "Wa qumu lillahi qanitin" was revealed; then we were commanded to remain silent and forbidden to speak.'

questionEn: If someone speaks intentionally during Salah with knowledge that it is forbidden and not for a life-saving emergency, what happens to their prayer?
optionsEn: It only invalidates voluntary prayers, not obligatory ones
The prayer is invalidated immediately and must be restarted
Only the current rak'ah is cancelled
The prayer remains valid if they perform Sujud al-Sahw
explanationEn: Jurists agree by consensus that deliberate human speech unrelated to prayer (outside rare emergencies like warning a blind person of imminent danger) invalidates Salah.

questionEn: What is the ruling if someone accidentally speaks a few words in Salah forgetting they are praying, or out of genuine ignorance of the prohibition (like Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam)?
optionsEn: Their prayer becomes a Sunnah automatically
They must perform Ghusl before restarting
According to the Shafi'i, Hanbali (in one narration), and many contemporary scholars, the prayer is not invalidated; the Prophet did not order Mu'awiyah to repeat his prayer
They must repeat all five prayers of that day
explanationEn: Because the Prophet (peace be upon him) taught Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam after the prayer without ordering him to repeat it, many jurists hold that speaking out of ignorance or forgetfulness does not void the prayer (while Hanafis hold it does).

questionEn: What happens to a person's Salah if they intentionally eat or drink anything during the prayer?
optionsEn: It is merely disliked (Makruh) if swallowed quickly
Drinking water is allowed in long Tarawih prayers
The prayer is invalidated by consensus of the scholars
Only eating solid food invalidates Salah, not drinking
explanationEn: Ibn al-Mundhir recorded scholarly consensus that intentional eating or drinking during Salah nullifies it, as it contradicts the sacred state and reverence of prayer.

questionEn: What if a tiny particle of food stuck between the teeth dissolves in saliva and is swallowed unintentionally without chewing?
optionsEn: One must spit out all saliva continuously during prayer
It requires repeating the prayer with two extra rak'ahs
Any swallowing of saliva invalidates Salah
It does not invalidate the prayer, whereas intentionally chewing or swallowing food placed in the mouth invalidates it
explanationEn: Jurists distinguish between swallowing residual saliva or tiny dissolved traces unintentionally (which does not break prayer) versus intentionally chewing or consuming food.

questionEn: What is the difference between smiling (Tabassum) and laughing aloud (Qahqahah) during Salah?
optionsEn: Smiling breaks the prayer immediately
Laughing aloud only breaks prayer if heard by the Imam
Laughing aloud (Qahqahah) invalidates the prayer, whereas a silent smile does not invalidate the prayer (though it reduces focus)
Both smiling and laughing equally require repeating Wudu and Salah
explanationEn: Scholars agree that audible laughter (Qahqahah) invalidates Salah because it resembles speech/play and destroys reverence, whereas silent smiling without sound does not break the prayer.

questionEn: What kind of physical movement during Salah invalidates the prayer?
optionsEn: Any single movement of a finger or eyelid
Excessive, continuous, unrelated movement (al-'amal al-kathir) without necessity, which makes an onlooker think the person is not praying
Killing a dangerous scorpion or snake nearby
Adjusting a slipping garment once with one hand
explanationEn: Minor or necessary movements do not break Salah, whereas sustained, purposeless, excessive movement unrelated to prayer invalidates it.

questionEn: Which Prophetic action demonstrates that minor, purposeful movement during Salah does not invalidate it?
optionsEn: The Prophet wrote letters during the second rak'ah
The Prophet climbed a tree during Witr prayer
The Prophet walked to the marketplace and back during Dhuhr
The Prophet (peace be upon him) carried his granddaughter Umamah bint Zaynab during prayer—putting her down when he prostrated and picking her up when he stood
explanationEn: Abu Qatadah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) led people in prayer carrying Umamah on his shoulder; when he bowed or prostrated he set her down, and when he stood he picked her up again.

questionEn: Which two dangerous creatures did the Prophet (peace be upon him) explicitly permit killing even while praying?
optionsEn: Stray dogs and cats
Houseflies and ants
The snake and the scorpion (al-aswadayn)
Birds and lizards
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Kill the two black ones during prayer: the snake and the scorpion.'

questionEn: What happened when Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) knocked on the locked door while the Prophet (peace be upon him) was praying inside the house?
optionsEn: He broke his prayer and started over after greeting her
He walked a few steps toward the door (facing the Qiblah direction), opened it for her, and returned to his prayer spot
He waited twenty minutes until finishing 11 rak'ahs
He called out to her from across the room
explanationEn: Aishah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) was praying near the door, walked to open it when she arrived, and returned to his place of prayer—showing brief, purposeful movement does not invalidate prayer.

questionEn: What happens if a worshipper's Awrah becomes significantly uncovered during Salah and they leave it uncovered deliberately instead of immediately covering it?
optionsEn: The prayer remains valid if they close their eyes
The prayer is invalidated because maintaining the Awrah covered is a continuing condition throughout Salah
It only matters before Takbirat al-Ihram, not during prayer
It only invalidates congregational prayers
explanationEn: Covering the Awrah is an ongoing condition; if wind blows a garment aside and the person covers it right away, the prayer stays valid, but leaving a substantial portion uncovered deliberately invalidates it.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a worshipper deliberately turns their chest completely away from the Qiblah during an obligatory prayer without an excuse?
optionsEn: It is only disliked if done during Tashahhud
It is valid as long as their eyes remain toward the Qiblah
It only requires saying Astaghfirullah three times
The prayer becomes invalid immediately
explanationEn: Facing the Qiblah with the torso/chest is an ongoing condition throughout Salah; turning the head briefly is Makruh, whereas deliberately turning the chest away from the Qiblah invalidates the prayer.

questionEn: What happens if someone intentionally or unintentionally breaks their Wudu (e.g., passes wind) while praying?
optionsEn: The prayer is invalidated immediately; they should quietly exit, renew Wudu, and restart the prayer
Only passing urine breaks prayer, not passing wind
They can simply perform Sujud al-Sahw to fix it
They should finish the prayer anyway out of politeness to the row
explanationEn: Ritual purity is an unbroken condition of Salah; the Prophet (peace be upon him) instructed leaving the prayer if one hears a sound or smells an odor (certainty of breaking Wudu), holding one's nose out of modesty if in congregation.

questionEn: If someone in congregation loses Wudu mid-prayer, what polite practice did the Prophet (peace be upon him) suggest when exiting the row?
optionsEn: Climbing over people's shoulders
Announcing aloud to the Imam why they are leaving
Holding one's nose as if having a nosebleed and walking out calmly
Sitting in place until everyone else finishes
explanationEn: Aishah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said when someone experiences Hadath (or feels sick) in prayer, he should hold his nose and leave, preserving modesty and avoiding embarrassment.

questionEn: What stern warning did the Prophet (peace be upon him) give to people who raise their eyes toward the sky during Salah?
optionsEn: 'Let people desist from raising their eyes to the sky during prayer, or their sight will not return to them (it may be snatched away)'
'Looking upward is recommended during Qunut'
'Whoever looks at the sky must donate a sheep'
'Looking at the sky only reduces the prayer's reward by a quarter'
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik and Abu Hurayrah narrated this severe warning against lifting one's gaze upward during Salah, as true humility entails lowering one's gaze.

questionEn: How did the Prophet (peace be upon him) describe turning one's head/glancing around during Salah (al-iltifat) when Aishah asked him about it?
optionsEn: 'It invalidates Wudu immediately'
'It is a harmless habit if done slowly'
'It is a snatching (ikhtilas) by which Satan steals from a servant's prayer'
'It is encouraged to stay aware of friends arriving'
explanationEn: Aishah asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) about looking right and left in prayer, and he described it as Shaytan snatching away a portion of the servant's concentration and reward.

questionEn: If someone glances briefly with their head during prayer out of genuine need (without turning the chest away from Qiblah), such as checking on a child or danger, is the prayer invalidated?
optionsEn: Yes, even blinking rapidly breaks the prayer
Yes, any eye movement invalidates the prayer
No, unless it happens during Fajr
No; glancing without need is Makruh, whereas glancing briefly for a valid need is permissible and does not invalidate the prayer
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) himself once looked toward the mountain pass while leading prayer because he had sent a scout out; thus turning the head/eyes for a real need is allowed, while idle glancing is Makruh.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 916; Fath al-Bari (Ibn Hajar)

questionEn: What should a Muslim do if they feel a yawn coming on during Salah?
optionsEn: Yawn loudly and stretch both arms upward
Turn away from the Qiblah while yawning
Suppress it as much as possible—and if unable, cover the mouth with the hand—because Shaytan laughs or enters when one yawns openly
Sit down immediately until the yawn passes
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Yawning in prayer is from Shaytan, so when one of you feels the urge to yawn, let him suppress it as much as he can,' and in another narration, place his hand over his mouth.

questionEn: What is the ruling on interlacing or crossing one's fingers (Tashbik al-Asabi') while walking to prayer or inside prayer?
optionsEn: It is the Sunnah position during Qiyam
It is recommended during the first Tashahhud
It is required while listening to the Imam's recitation
It is disliked (Makruh) while waiting for prayer, walking to it after Wudu, and inside the prayer
explanationEn: Ka'b ibn Ujrah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you performs Wudu well and heads to the masjid, let him not interlace his fingers, for he is already in prayer.'

questionEn: What posture is called 'Al-Ikhtisar' that Abu Hurayrah reported the Prophet (peace be upon him) forbade in Salah?
optionsEn: Placing one's hands on one's hips/waist while praying
Crossing the ankles while sitting
Shortening Surah Al-Fatihah
Praying in a short cloak
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) forbade praying with hands on the hips (al-ikhtisar); Aishah added that it is the posture of the People of the Book (or arrogance/the inhabitants of Hellfire).

questionEn: What sitting posture did the Prophet (peace be upon him) forbid, comparing it to the way a dog or predator sits?
optionsEn: Sitting on a prayer mat made of wool
Sitting briefly before standing up from Sujud
Sitting on the buttocks with knees drawn up and hands resting flat on the floor (Iq'a' of the dog), as well as spreading forearms flat on the floor in Sujud
Sitting on the left foot with the right foot upright
explanationEn: Aishah reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him) forbade 'uqbat ash-shaytan' (sitting like a devil/dog) and spreading forearms like a beast of prey, while Ibn Abbas distinguished the permissible Sunnah iq'a' (resting on heels between two prostrations).

questionEn: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him) forbid regarding clothing and hair when he said 'I was commanded not to tuck up garments or hair' (Kaff al-thawb wash-sha'r)?
optionsEn: Rolling up sleeves/garments or tying up flowing hair specifically to keep them from touching the floor during prayer, because hair and clothes should prostrate with the worshipper
Washing garments before Friday prayer
Wearing a stitched shirt in Salah
Combing one's hair before Wudu
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'I was commanded to prostrate on seven bones and not to tuck up my hair or my garment'—meaning rolling sleeves/hem or gathering hair solely for prayer rather than letting them fall naturally.

questionEn: Why did Ibn Abbas rebuke Abdullah ibn al-Harith when he saw him praying with his hair tied up in a bun behind his head?
optionsEn: He untied it and told him, 'You are praying like one whose hands are tied behind his back,' citing the prohibition of tucking hair in prayer
He told him men are forbidden to grow hair past the ears
He said tied hair blocks the angels from descending
He ordered him to shave his head before Dhuhr
explanationEn: When Ibn Abbas saw Abdullah ibn al-Harith praying with his hair braided/tied back, he got up and undid it, explaining that the Prophet (peace be upon him) compared praying with tied-back hair to praying with hands bound.

questionEn: What is the ruling on praying while desperately holding back urine, feces, or trapped wind (Mudafa'at al-Akhbathayn)?
optionsEn: It is meritorious because resisting physical discomfort doubles the reward

It is strongly disliked (Makruh) and the Prophet said 'There is no [complete] prayer... while holding back the two impurities,' so one should relieve oneself first even if one misses the start of congregation
One should always hold it until after Sunnah prayers too
It is only disliked during Asr prayer
explanationEn: Aishah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no [proper/complete] prayer in the presence of food, nor while resisting the two impurities (urine and feces),' because it destroys Khushu' (humility and focus).

questionEn: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him) instruct when dinner is served right as the Iqamah for Maghrib (or another prayer) is called?
optionsEn: 'Leave the food untouched until after Isha'
'When supper is served and the prayer is commenced, begin with supper first' (if the person desires it and will be distracted by it)
'Throw the food away so it does not tempt you'
'Eat quickly while reciting Al-Fatihah'
explanationEn: Anas and Ibn Umar narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) commanded starting with served food when one is hungry so the worshipper's heart is not preoccupied with the meal during Salah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him) do when a man named Mu'ayqib kept smoothing the pebbles at his place of prostration during Salah?
optionsEn: He made smoothing pebbles an obligatory pillar
He ordered him to sweep the entire masjid before every rak'ah
He told him: 'If you must do it, then only once' (disliking repeated fidgeting with the ground)
He told him to stop praying altogether
explanationEn: Mu'ayqib narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) forbade repeatedly leveling pebbles/sand during prayer, permitting at most a single quick wipe if truly needed so focus is not broken.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet (peace be upon him) return a patterned garment (Khamisah) with markings to Abu Jahm and ask for a plain woolen garment (Anbijaniyyah) instead?
optionsEn: Because it did not cover his shoulders
Because wool is heavier and warmer
Because its patterns and markings distracted him from his prayer
Because patterned garments are completely haram to own
explanationEn: Aishah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed in a Khamisah with designs, looked briefly at its markings, and after finishing asked for a plain Anbijaniyyah, saying: 'Its markings distracted me just now.'

questionEn: Similarly, why did the Prophet (peace be upon him) tell Aishah to remove a figured curtain (Qiram) from the front of the prayer room?
optionsEn: Because curtains block airflow in Madinah
Because its images kept appearing before him and distracting his focus during prayer
Because curtains invalidate Wudu
Because the curtain was green
explanationEn: Anas narrated that Aishah had a curtain with pictures covering a wall; the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Remove this curtain of yours from us, for its images keep appearing to me in my prayer.'

questionEn: Which direction did the Prophet (peace be upon him) forbid spitting toward during Salah?
optionsEn: Directly in front (toward the Qiblah) or to one's right side
Nowhere—spitting anywhere in the masjid was encouraged
Toward the left side even outside the masjid
Into a tissue or fold of one's own garment
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) explained that when one stands in prayer, Allah is before him (toward the Qiblah) and an angel is on his right, so one must never spit in front or to the right, but rather into one's garment/handkerchief (or to the left outside carpeted masjids).

questionEn: Is closing one's eyes throughout the entire Salah considered Sunnah or Makruh by the majority of jurists?
optionsEn: Disliked (Makruh) if done without need, unless there is an unavoidable visual distraction nearby that harms Khushu'
Strictly forbidden to the point of invalidating every rak'ah
Recommended in all prayers regardless of surroundings
An obligatory pillar of Salah
explanationEn: Ibn al-Qayyim noted it was not the Prophet's guidance to close his eyes in prayer (since he pointed and looked at his finger in Tashahhud and looked at his place of prostration); thus jurists deem closing eyes without need Makruh, though permitted if opening them causes severe distraction.

questionEn: What is the ruling on cracking one's knuckles or joints (Farqa'at al-Asabi') during Salah?
optionsEn: It is disliked (Makruh) because it is idle, distracting movement lacking reverence
It is Sunnah before Ruku' to loosen the fingers
It is encouraged in Fajr prayer
It is equivalent to breaking Wudu
explanationEn: Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ibn Abbas strongly disapproved of cracking fingers during prayer, and jurists classify it as Makruh because it constitutes purposeless fidgeting contrary to Khushu'.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet (peace be upon him) instruct worshippers to avoid praying directly behind someone who is sleeping or talking?
optionsEn: Because sleeping people nullify the Qiblah
Because talking nearby invalidates Wudu
Because their movements or chatter may distract the worshipper and impair Khushu' (note: Aishah lying silently across his prayer space at night was due to cramped quarters and did not disturb him)
Because prayer behind a sleeper is strictly void by consensus
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas narrated a warning against praying behind a sleeper or someone conversing (due to distraction), while Aishah explained that in her small room she lay crosswise before the Prophet and drew her legs in when he prostrated.

questionEn: What is the ruling on praying while wearing clothing with pictures of animate beings or distracting slogans on the back?
optionsEn: Invalidates the prayer of the entire row behind them
Disliked (Makruh) for the wearer and harmful to the congregation behind them, as images and text distract worshippers
Only disallowed for the Imam, not followers
Recommended on Eid days
explanationEn: Based on the hadith prohibiting distracting markings/images in prayer and the dislike of animate images in worship spaces, wearing garments with distracting prints or faces is Makruh.

questionEn: What happens if a worshipper deliberately adds an extra pillar—such as intentionally bowing twice (two Ruku's) or prostrating three times in a single rak'ah of a regular prayer?
optionsEn: It is completely harmless if done slowly
It turns the prayer into Salat al-Kusuf (Eclipse Prayer)
It doubles the reward of that rak'ah
It invalidates the prayer because it deliberately alters the legislated form of Salah
explanationEn: Adding a physical pillar intentionally violates the Prophetic form ('Pray as you have seen me praying') and voids the prayer; only Eclipse Prayer (Kusuf) uniquely has two Ruku's per rak'ah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him) warn regarding the worshipper who consistently lifts his head before the Imam in Ruku' or Sujud?
optionsEn: 'He becomes the assistant Imam automatically'
'His prayer counts as two congregational prayers'
'He only needs to say SubhanAllah once'
'Does not the one who raises his head before the Imam fear that Allah may turn his head into the head of a donkey, or his form into the form of a donkey?'
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah narrated this stern warning against preceding the Imam; jurists state that deliberately preceding the Imam in Takbirat al-Ihram prevents the prayer from starting, and deliberately racing ahead in pillars can invalidate prayer.

questionEn: Why is praying directly facing an open fire, burning hearth, or idolatrous symbol disliked (Makruh)?
optionsEn: Because fire extinguishes the light of Al-Fatihah
Because smoke breaks Wudu automatically
Because lamps are forbidden inside masjids
To avoid any outward resemblance to fire-worshippers (Magians) or distraction of the heart
explanationEn: Classical jurists such as Ibn Qudamah and An-Nawawi state it is Makruh to pray directly facing an open fire or furnace because it resembles Majusi fire-worship (whereas an ordinary ceiling lamp or candle off to the side is harmless).

questionEn: What is the ruling on clearing one's throat (Tanahnuh) needlessly during Salah until two distinct letters are uttered aloud?
optionsEn: It converts the prayer into a silent prayer
Clearing the throat loudly is Sunnah before every Surah

If done unnecessarily and producing clear audible letters, some jurists treat it like speech that breaks prayer; if done out of genuine physical need (e.g., to clear phlegm or recite Al-Fatihah), it does not invalidate the prayer
Any cough automatically nullifies the prayer even when sick
explanationEn: Jurists distinguish between involuntary coughing/necessary throat-clearing (excused) and deliberate, unnecessary vocalization resembling speech.

questionEn: What is the ruling on resting one's body lazily against a wall or pillar while praying an obligatory prayer when one is healthy and able to stand upright independently?
optionsEn: Completely identical to standing independently regardless of weight
Disliked (Makruh) if slight, and invalidates Qiyam if the person leans so heavily that they would collapse if the support were removed
Recommended in all four-rak'ah prayers to save energy
Obligatory for anyone praying in the first row
explanationEn: Standing independently (Qiyam) is a pillar of obligatory prayer for the able; leaning lightly out of minor fatigue is Makruh, while transferring one's entire weight onto a wall without medical excuse violates independent standing.

questionEn: When is leaving the prayer mid-way NOT sinful—and even obligatory—despite the general rule against breaking an obligatory prayer?
optionsEn: To rescue someone from drowning, fire, fatal danger, or to stop a severe imminent harm
Whenever one's phone rings with a casual call
When one remembers a minor errand at the grocery store
Whenever the Imam recites a slightly longer Surah
explanationEn: Preserving human life takes precedence over continuing a current prayer; one exits immediately to save the person in danger and restarts the prayer afterward.

questionEn: What are the three main causes that necessitate Sujud al-Sahw (the prostration of forgetfulness) in Salah?
optionsEn: Unintended addition (Ziyadah), unintended omission (Naqs), or genuine doubt (Shakk) regarding the number of rak'ahs or acts performed
Deliberate talking, eating, and laughing aloud
Praying in a mosque with carpets, praying on travel, and praying behind an Imam
Missing Takbirat al-Ihram, breaking Wudu, and praying before time enters
explanationEn: Sujud al-Sahw compensates for forgetfulness in three categories: adding an extra act/rak'ah unintentionally, omitting a Wajib/non-pillar act unintentionally, or experiencing doubt during prayer.

questionEn: How many prostrations comprise Sujud al-Sahw, and what dhikr is recited inside them?
optionsEn: Two prostrations where only silence is allowed
Four prostrations reciting At-Tahiyyat in each
Two prostrations with a brief sitting between them, reciting 'Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la' as in regular Sujud
One single prostration reciting Surah Al-Fatihah
explanationEn: Every authentic narration describes Sujud al-Sahw as two prostrations just like the two prostrations of a normal rak'ah, saying 'Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la' and seeking forgiveness/supplicating as usual (no special invented 'Subhana man la yanam' dhikr is authentically established).

questionEn: In the hadith of Abdullah ibn Buhaynah, what did the Prophet (peace be upon him) do when he stood up after the second rak'ah of Dhuhr without sitting for the first Tashahhud?
optionsEn: He continued standing and finished the prayer, then performed two prostrations of forgetfulness (Sujud al-Sahw) before making Salam
He omitted Sujud al-Sahw completely because Tashahhud is optional
He sat back down immediately after already standing upright
He restarted the entire four-rak'ah prayer from the beginning
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Buhaynah reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him) stood up after two rak'ahs without sitting, continued when the people said SubhanAllah, and at the end performed two prostrations while sitting before the Taslim.

questionEn: If a worshipper forgets the first Tashahhud and starts rising, when may they still return to sit for it versus when must they keep standing?
optionsEn: They must always drop back down even if they already started Ruku' of the third rak'ah
They should sit down only if praying Fajr
They may never return even if their knees have barely lifted a centimeter
If they have not yet stood completely upright, they return to sit; once they have stood completely upright, they do not return and instead perform Sujud al-Sahw at the end
explanationEn: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) instructed: if someone rises after two rak'ahs and has not stood fully upright, let him sit; once fully upright, let him not sit back down, and let him perform two prostrations of forgetfulness.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1036; Sunan Ibn Majah 1208

questionEn: In the famous incident of Dhul-Yadayn, the Prophet (peace be upon him) mistakenly made Salam after only two rak'ahs of Dhuhr or Asr. When reminded, what did he do?
optionsEn: He made Sujud al-Sahw immediately without praying the missing two rak'ahs
He told the congregation two rak'ahs suffice whenever the Imam forgets
He stood up, prayed the remaining two rak'ahs, made Salam, and then performed two prostrations of Sahw after Salam
He started the entire four-rak'ah prayer all over again
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah narrated that after Dhul-Yadayn asked whether the prayer had been shortened or forgotten and the Companions confirmed two rak'ahs were prayed, the Prophet (peace be upon him) completed the remaining two rak'ahs, made Salam, and then performed Sujud al-Sahw.

questionEn: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him) do when he mistakenly prayed five rak'ahs in Dhuhr (as narrated by Abdullah ibn Mas'ud) and was informed after making Salam?
optionsEn: He added a sixth rak'ah to make it an even number
He told them extra rak'ahs require no Sujud al-Sahw
He repeated all four rak'ahs of Dhuhr from scratch
He turned to face the Qiblah, performed two prostrations of forgetfulness (after Salam), and then made Salam again
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud narrated that when told he had prayed five rak'ahs, the Prophet (peace be upon him) folded his legs toward the Qiblah, performed two prostrations, and gave Salam, adding: 'I am only a human being like you; I forget as you forget, so when I forget, remind me.'

questionEn: Suppose a worshipper realizes in the middle of a fifth rak'ah (during a 4-rak'ah prayer) that they accidentally stood up for an extra rak'ah. What must they do immediately?
optionsEn: Turn the prayer into six rak'ahs of voluntary prayer
Stand quietly until the next prayer time
Finish the fifth rak'ah so it doesn't get cut off mid-way
Sit down right away, recite Tashahhud (if not yet recited), make Salam, and perform Sujud al-Sahw after Salam
explanationEn: Because the fifth rak'ah is an unintended addition (Ziyadah), continuing it deliberately once realized is forbidden; one sits immediately, completes Tashahhud and Salam, and performs Sujud al-Sahw after Salam.

questionEn: According to Abu Sa'id al-Khudri's hadith, what should a person do when they doubt during prayer whether they prayed three or four rak'ahs and neither number feels more likely?
optionsEn: Break the prayer immediately and start over
Assume the larger number (four) so the prayer finishes sooner
Cast aside doubt and build upon what is certain (the lesser number, i.e., three), pray the fourth rak'ah, and perform two prostrations before Salam
Ask the person next to them aloud during prayer
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'If one of you doubts in his prayer and does not know how much he has prayed—three or four—let him cast away doubt and build upon what he is certain of (the lesser), then perform two prostrations before giving Salam.'

questionEn: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him) explain as the spiritual effect of performing the two prostrations of Sahw when experiencing doubt?
optionsEn: 'They erase all future sins of the entire week'
'If he had actually prayed five, they make his prayer even-numbered; and if he had prayed four completely, they are a humiliation (targhim) for Satan'
'They turn an obligatory prayer into a Sunnah prayer'
'They automatically double the length of his prayer'
explanationEn: In Abu Sa'id al-Khudri's narration in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet (peace be upon him) gave this comforting wisdom showing that Sujud al-Sahw either rectifies the count or humiliates Shaytan who caused the confusion.

questionEn: How does the rule of doubt differ when one possibility clearly outweighs the other (Ghalabat az-Zann / Taharri as-Sawab) according to Ibn Mas'ud's hadith?
optionsEn: One investigates what seems most likely/accurate, completes the prayer based on that predominant conviction, makes Salam, and performs Sujud al-Sahw after Salam
One must skip Sujud al-Sahw whenever one feels fairly sure
One must ignore strong conviction and always restart from Takbirat al-Ihram
One must always pray two extra rak'ahs just in case
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you doubts in his prayer, let him seek what is most likely right (falyataharra as-sawab), complete it accordingly, then make Salam, and then make two prostrations.'

questionEn: According to the synthesis of Prophetic narrations adopted by scholars like Imam Malik and Ibn Taymiyyah, when is Sujud al-Sahw generally placed BEFORE Salam versus AFTER Salam?
optionsEn: Always after Salam in every single school without exception
Before Salam only in Fajr and Maghrib; after Salam only in Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha
Before Salam only for the Imam; after Salam only for women
Before Salam for omissions (like missing the first Tashahhud) and doubt without preponderance; after Salam for additions (like an extra rak'ah or early Salam) and doubt with preponderance
explanationEn: Comparing Ibn Buhaynah (omission -> before Salam) and Abu Sa'id (certainty doubt -> before Salam) with Dhul-Yadayn and Ibn Mas'ud (addition -> after Salam) gives this clear, harmonious principle (while both placements remain valid).

questionEn: Does Sujud al-Sahw compensate for forgetting an essential pillar (Rukn), such as skipping Ruku' or one of the two Sujuds in a rak'ah?
optionsEn: Yes; Sujud al-Sahw replaces any missed Ruku' or Sujud without needing to repeat it

No; if remembered before reaching that same pillar in the next rak'ah, one goes back to perform it and completes from there; if reached/passed it, the incomplete rak'ah is discarded and the next rak'ah takes its place, followed by Sujud al-Sahw
Yes, as long as one says SubhanAllah three times after Salam
No; forgetting a pillar means the person may never pray that prayer again
explanationEn: A pillar cannot be dropped by Sujud al-Sahw; it must be performed (or its defective rak'ah replaced by an added rak'ah) before concluding with Sujud al-Sahw.

questionEn: What if a worshipper realizes after finishing Salah that they forgot a sunnah act, such as Dua al-Istiftah or raising hands (Raf' al-Yadayn)?
optionsEn: They must make up two extra rak'ahs after Isha
They must repeat the entire prayer
No Sujud al-Sahw is required (and one should not do it for mere Sunnah acts), though the prayer is completely valid
They must perform Sujud al-Sahw twice
explanationEn: Sujud al-Sahw is prescribed for forgetting a Wajib, adding an unintended pillar/rak'ah, or doubt—not for missing recommended Sunnahs like Dua al-Istiftah or Raf' al-Yadayn.

questionEn: If someone prays behind an Imam from the very beginning of the prayer and the follower alone makes an accidental mistake (e.g., forgets to say 'Subhana Rabbiyal-Azim' in Ruku'), does that follower perform Sujud al-Sahw on their own?
optionsEn: Yes; the follower must pull the Imam back to repeat Ruku'
No; the Imam bears the follower's minor forgetfulness so the follower stays synchronized with the Imam and does not do Sahw alone
Yes; the follower must stay seated after the Imam leaves to do Sahw
The follower must break away from the congregation immediately
explanationEn: Based on the hadith 'The Imam is appointed to be followed' and reports from the Companions, a follower who prayed the entire prayer behind the Imam does not perform independent Sujud al-Sahw for their own omission of a Wajib; the Imam carries it.

questionEn: What must a follower (Ma'mum) do if the Imam performs Sujud al-Sahw—either before Salam or after Salam?
optionsEn: Remain seated and watch the Imam prostrate alone
Stand up and leave as soon as the Imam begins Sahw
Follow the Imam in Sujud al-Sahw, even if the follower joined late or did not personally make the mistake
Prostrate only once instead of twice
explanationEn: The Prophet (peace be upon him) commanded: 'The Imam is only appointed to be followed... when he prostrates, then prostrate.'
