While a follower present from the start follows the Imam in both pre-Salam and post-Salam Sahw, a latecomer (Masbuq) follows the Imam in pre-Salam Sahw and—if the Imam's Sahw is after Salam—either joins then or completes their missed rak'ahs first and performs Sahw at their own end.

questionEn: If a latecomer (Masbuq) caught part of the prayer with the Imam, and then made a mistake during the missed rak'ahs they are completing alone after the Imam's Salam, what should they do?
optionsEn: Restart the entire prayer from the first rak'ah
Skip Sujud al-Sahw because they started behind an Imam
Perform Sujud al-Sahw at the end of their own prayer for the mistake they made while praying alone
Call the Imam back to prostrate with them
explanationEn: Once the Imam finishes with Salam and the Masbuq stands to complete missed rak'ahs, the Masbuq is effectively praying alone for that portion and performs Sujud al-Sahw if they commit a mistake during it.

questionEn: What if a worshipper keeps having obsessive, chronic doubts (Waswas) in every single prayer about how many rak'ahs they prayed or whether they missed something?
optionsEn: They should repeat every prayer ten times until completely calm
They should perform ten prostrations of Sahw after every prayer
They should stop praying altogether for a month
They should ignore the obsessive whispers completely and not act on them or perform Sujud al-Sahw for mere Waswas
explanationEn: Scholars unanimously advise ignoring obsessive doubts (Waswas) so as not to indulge Shaytan's disturbance; Sujud al-Sahw is for genuine, occasional uncertainty, not chronic compulsions.

questionEn: When Sujud al-Sahw is performed AFTER the Taslim, should one utter a final Taslim again after completing the two prostrations?
optionsEn: One must repeat Surah Al-Fatihah before leaving
One must make Taslim four times
Yes; one makes Takbir for each prostration, sits between them, and concludes with Taslim again (without needing to repeat the full Tashahhud according to the stronger view)
No; one simply stands up and walks away silently after the second prostration
explanationEn: In both the hadith of Dhul-Yadayn and Ibn Mas'ud, the Prophet (peace be upon him) performed the two prostrations after Salam and then concluded with Taslim again.

questionEn: What is the ruling on Sujud al-Tilawah (prostration upon reciting or attentively listening to a Qur'anic verse of prostration) according to the majority of scholars?
optionsEn: It is only permissible inside Ramadan
It is an emphasized Sunnah (Sunnah Mu'akkadah), not strictly obligatory (Wajib)
It is an obligatory pillar without which reading the Qur'an is haram
It is disliked outside of Fajr prayer
explanationEn: Umar ibn al-Khattab recited Surah An-Nahl on the pulpit one Friday and prostrated, and the next Friday recited it and did not prostrate, declaring: 'Indeed, Allah has not made prostration obligatory upon us unless we wish.' (The Hanafi school considers it Wajib.)

questionEn: Why did Zayd ibn Thabit not prostrate when he recited Surah An-Najm to the Prophet (peace be upon him), and what did that demonstrate?
optionsEn: Because Sujud al-Tilawah was abrogated in Madinah
Because Zayd was sitting on a mat
Because Surah An-Najm does not contain a verse of prostration
The Prophet (peace be upon him) did not prostrate nor rebuke him, proving that Sujud al-Tilawah is Sunnah rather than strictly obligatory
explanationEn: Zayd ibn Thabit reported: 'I recited An-Najm before the Prophet (peace be upon him) and he did not prostrate during it,' which jurists cite alongside Umar's report to show it is recommended rather than strictly obligatory.

questionEn: Which Surah was the very first Surah revealed to contain a verse of prostration (Sajdah), where both Muslims and polytheists prostrated when the Prophet (peace be upon him) recited it in Makkah?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Kahf (Surah 18)
Surah An-Najm (Surah 53)
Surah Al-Baqarah (Surah 2)
Surah Yasin (Surah 36)
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud reported: 'The first Surah in which a prostration was revealed was An-Najm. The Prophet (peace be upon him) prostrated, and everyone behind him prostrated'—overwhelmed by the majesty of the recitation.

questionEn: Which Surah in the Qur'an uniquely contains TWO verses of prostration (according to the Shafi'i and Hanbali counts)?
optionsEn: Surah Maryam (Surah 19)
Surah Al-A'raf (Surah 7)
Surah Al-Baqarah (Surah 2)
Surah Al-Hajj (Surah 22)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hajj has two prostration verses (verses 18 and 77); Uqbah ibn Amir asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) whether Surah Al-Hajj was favored with two prostrations, and the Prophet affirmed that it has two prostrations.

questionEn: How do scholars view the prostration in Surah Sad (38:24) when Prophet Dawud fell down in repentance?
optionsEn: Every scholar forbids prostrating in Surah Sad
One must prostrate three times in Surah Sad
Surah Sad must be skipped during Salah

Ibn Abbas noted it is a prostration of gratitude/repentance (not among the strict required prostrations in one view, though he saw the Prophet prostrate in it), so many schools still prostrate in Surah Sad
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas explained that Sad is not among the 'aza'im (mandated prostrations) yet he personally witnessed the Prophet (peace be upon him) prostrate in it; thus Hanafis and Hanbalis count it as a prostration of recitation (making 14 or 15 total), while Shafi'is treat it as a prostration of gratitude outside prayer.

questionEn: How is Sujud al-Tilawah performed when reciting the Qur'an outside of Salah?
optionsEn: One prays two full rak'ahs before prostrating
One prostrates twice and finishes with Tashahhud and two Salams
One makes Takbir ('Allahu Akbar') when going down, performs a single prostration, praises Allah and recites its Dua, and rises (without needing Tashahhud or Taslim according to the stronger view)
One must stand for ten minutes after rising
explanationEn: Sujud al-Tilawah outside Salah consists of a single prostration preceded by Takbir; Tashahhud and Taslim are not established for it in the Sunnah (though some Hanbalis/Shafi'is add a closing Takbir or Salam by analogy).

questionEn: Which authentic supplication did Aishah narrate that the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to say during Sujud al-Tilawah at night?
optionsEn: 'Subhanakallahumma innaka Antal-Wahhab'
'Sami'Allahu liman hamidah Rabbana lakal-hamd'

'Sajada wajhi lilladhi khalaqahu, wa shaqqas-sam'ahu wa basarahu bi-hawlihi wa quwwatihi' ('My face has prostrated to the One Who created it and fashioned its hearing and sight by His might and power')
'Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab wa Sha'ban'
explanationEn: Aishah reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him) recited this profound acknowledgment of Allah's creation of the senses during his prostration of Qur'an recitation.

questionEn: Which other Dua for Sujud al-Tilawah was narrated by Ibn Abbas, asking Allah to record a reward, remove a sin, and accept it as He accepted from Dawud?
optionsEn: 'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah'
'At-Tahiyyatu lillahi was-salawatu wat-tayyibat'
'Allahummahdini fiman hadayt wa 'afini fiman 'afayt'
'Allahummaktub li biha 'indaka ajran, wa da' 'anni biha wizran, waj'alha li 'indaka dhukhran, wa taqabbalha minni kama taqabbalta min 'abdika Dawud'
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas narrated that a man dreamed of a tree prostrating and reciting this dua, and when he told the Prophet (peace be upon him), the Prophet recited the verse of prostration, prostrated, and recited the exact same words.

questionEn: When an Imam recites a verse of prostration during congregational prayer and prostrates, what must the followers do?
optionsEn: Prostrate immediately with the Imam and rise with the Imam
Break the prayer because Sujud al-Tilawah cannot be done inside Salah
Remain standing and wait for the Imam to come back up
Wait until after Taslim to perform Sujud al-Tilawah
explanationEn: Following the Imam applies to Sujud al-Tilawah inside prayer; Abu Hurayrah and others narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) prostrated when reciting Idhas-sama'un-shaqqat and Al-Alaq in prayer, and the congregation prostrated with him.

questionEn: If someone is listening attentively to a reciter (Mustami') outside prayer, when should the listener perform Sujud al-Tilawah?
optionsEn: Only if the listener is holding a physical Mushaf
Never—only the reciter is permitted to prostrate
Even if the reciter does not prostrate, the listener must prostrate twice
Only if the reciter himself prostrates; if the reciter chooses not to prostrate, the listener does not prostrate
explanationEn: Zayd ibn Thabit recited An-Najm before the Prophet (peace be upon him), who did not prostrate, and Zayd did not prostrate either—establishing that the listener follows the reciter (and a casual passerby who isn't sitting to listen isn't asked to prostrate).

questionEn: If someone is reciting a verse of prostration in a silent prayer (like Dhuhr or Asr), is it best to skip prostrating or prostrate?
optionsEn: Many scholars say it is permissible to prostrate, while some (like Imam Malik and Abu Hanifah in silent prayer) advise avoiding it if it might confuse followers who cannot hear why the Imam suddenly prostrated
Reciting verses with Sajdah in Dhuhr is strictly forbidden
The Imam must shout the verse aloud right before prostrating
The followers should go into Ruku' instead of Sujud
explanationEn: Jurists note that if an Imam wants to avoid confusing followers who think he skipped Ruku', it is wise to avoid Sajdah verses in silent congregational prayers, though reciting and prostrating remains valid in itself.

questionEn: Does Sujud al-Tilawah strictly require Wudu and facing the Qiblah according to all scholars, or is there a well-known scholarly distinction?
optionsEn: One must face away from the Qiblah during Sujud al-Tilawah
No scholar ever recommended Wudu for Sujud al-Tilawah
All scholars agree one must perform Ghusl before Sujud al-Tilawah

The majority of jurists require Wudu, covering Awrah, and facing Qiblah by analogy to Salah, whereas Ibn Umar and scholars like Ibn Taymiyyah held that Wudu is recommended rather than strictly required since it is not a full Salah
explanationEn: Ibn Umar used to perform Sujud al-Tilawah even without Wudu (as recorded by Al-Bukhari in a chapter heading), while the majority of the four schools treat it like Salah regarding purity and Qiblah—making having Wudu and facing Qiblah best whenever possible.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Chapter: Prostration of the Muslims with the Polytheists); Majmu' al-Fatawa

questionEn: If someone hears a pre-recorded audio recording of the Qur'an (e.g., on radio or phone) playing a verse of prostration, is Sujud al-Tilawah prescribed?
optionsEn: Most contemporary jurists hold it is NOT prescribed for a recording because there is no live human reciter, though prostrating is permissible if one wishes
It becomes strictly obligatory to prostrate every time the recording replays
Listening to Qur'an recordings is forbidden during daytime
One must perform Sujud al-Sahw instead
explanationEn: Scholars distinguish between a live reciter (whom the Sunnah links with the listener) and a mechanical replay/recording, noting that Sujud al-Tilawah is tied to live recitation.
reference: Fatawa al-Lajnah al-Da'imah; Majmu' Fatawa Ibn Baz

questionEn: By how many degrees does praying in congregation surpass praying alone, according to the narration of Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari?
optionsEn: 10 degrees
70 degrees
27 degrees
12 degrees
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ stated that prayer in congregation is superior to prayer offered alone by twenty-seven degrees.

questionEn: In the narration of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA), by how many degrees is congregational prayer reported to excel praying individually?
optionsEn: 25 degrees
15 degrees
7 degrees
40 degrees
explanationEn: Authentic narrations mention both twenty-five and twenty-seven degrees, showing the immense multiplied blessing of Salah al-Jama'ah.

questionEn: When hearing the Iqamah while walking toward the masjid, what manner of walking did the Prophet ﷺ command?
optionsEn: Stop outside until the second rak'ah begins
Jog lightly until reaching the mosque courtyard
Walk calmly with serenity and dignity without running
Sprint quickly so as not to miss the opening Takbir
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ forbade running to prayer, instructing believers to walk with sakinah (tranquility) and waqar (dignity), pray what they catch, and complete what they missed.

questionEn: If a person performs Wudu thoroughly at home and walks to the masjid solely for obligatory prayer, what happens with every pair of steps they take?
optionsEn: One step erases a sin and the other raises a degree
Every ten steps forgive a major sin automatically
Every step equals one full rak'ah of voluntary prayer
Each step counts as giving a dirham in charity
explanationEn: Each step taken toward the masjid after purifying at home carries a dual blessing: one step removes a sin and the next elevates the believer's rank.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ advise the tribe of Banu Salamah not to relocate closer to Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Because they were commanded to build a separate mosque
Because their footprints from walking farther were recorded in their deeds
Because walking in heat was discouraged in Madinah
Because there was no available land near the mosque
explanationEn: He ﷺ told Banu Salamah, 'Keep to your homes, for your footprints are recorded,' reassuring them that their longer walk earned greater reward.

questionEn: Which worshipper receives the greatest reward for attending congregational prayer according to Sahih Muslim?
optionsEn: The one who walks from the farthest distance
The one who lives next door to the masjid
The one who arrives immediately after the prayer ends
The one who rides the fastest mount to the masjid
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that the person greatest in reward for Salah is the one who comes from the farthest away, then the next farthest.

questionEn: Praying Isha in congregation is likened in reward to standing in night prayer for what duration?
optionsEn: One-quarter of the night
Two complete nights
One full hour of Qiyam
Half of the night
explanationEn: Uthman ibn Affan (RA) narrated that whoever prays Isha in congregation is as if he stood in prayer for half the night.

questionEn: Praying both Isha and Fajr in congregation carries the spiritual equivalent of praying for how long?
optionsEn: Half of a week
Only the last third of the night
Three consecutive days
The entire night
explanationEn: In the same narration from Uthman (RA), adding Fajr in congregation to Isha in congregation equals standing in prayer the whole night through.

questionEn: What happens in a village or desert where three people reside and do not establish prayer in congregation?
optionsEn: They must travel to the nearest city daily
Shaytan gains mastery over them
Their prayers automatically double in reward
They are excused from praying Dhuhr and Asr
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ warned that if three are together and do not pray in congregation, Shaytan overtakes them, comparing a lone sheep to the wolf's prey.

questionEn: What glad tidings did the Prophet ﷺ give to those who walk to the mosques in the darkness of night?
optionsEn: Guaranteed leadership in their community
Exemption from fasting in Ramadan
A palace of silver in Madinah
Complete light on the Day of Resurrection
explanationEn: He ﷺ said: 'Give glad tidings to those who walk to the masajid in darkness of complete light (nur tamm) on the Day of Judgment.'

questionEn: Among the seven categories shaded under Allah's Throne on the Day of Judgment, how is the mosque-goer described?
optionsEn: A person who recites poetry inside the masjid
A person who only visits the masjid on Eid
A person whose heart is attached to the masajid
A person who owns the largest house near a masjid
explanationEn: One of the seven shaded by Allah when there is no shade except His is a man whose heart remains attached to the mosques from the time he leaves until he returns.

questionEn: At which two congregational prayers do the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather together?
optionsEn: Fajr and Asr
Fajr and Dhuhr
Maghrib and Isha
Dhuhr and Maghrib
explanationEn: The angels take turns watching over believers, assembling together at Fajr and Asr and reporting how they left the believers praying.

questionEn: Sitting in the masjid waiting for the next obligatory prayer after finishing one prayer is described in Sahih Muslim as what?
optionsEn: Al-I'tikaf al-Wajib
At-Tashahhud
Ar-Ribat (guarding the spiritual frontier)
Al-Qasr
explanationEn: Along with perfecting Wudu in hardship and taking many steps to the mosque, waiting from prayer to prayer is called 'Ribat'—the spiritual station of steadfastness.

questionEn: What physical hand gesture did the Prophet ﷺ forbid while walking to the mosque or sitting in the mosque waiting for prayer?
optionsEn: Raising the hands in quiet dua
Placing the right hand on the chest
Holding a miswak in the right hand
Interlacing one's fingers (Tashbik)
explanationEn: When a person has performed Wudu and sets out for prayer, he is already considered in a state of prayer, so interlacing fingers (tashbik) is forbidden.

questionEn: According to the Hadith of Abu Qatadah (RA), what should a Muslim pray upon entering a mosque before sitting down?
optionsEn: Four rak'ahs of Dhuhr Sunnah
Two rak'ahs (Tahiyyat al-Masjid)
Three rak'ahs of Maghrib
One single rak'ah of Witr
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed: 'When any one of you enters the masjid, let him not sit down until he prays two rak'ahs.'

questionEn: What should a worshipper do upon entering the masjid if the Iqamah for the obligatory prayer has already begun?
optionsEn: Quickly pray two voluntary rak'ahs in the back first
Sit down immediately and make intention for Sunnah
Join the obligatory congregation directly without starting Tahiyyat al-Masjid
Wait outside the door until the first rak'ah finishes
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'When the Iqamah for prayer is called, there is no prayer except the prescribed obligatory prayer.'

questionEn: What supplication do the angels continuously make for a worshipper who remains seated in his prayer spot in Wudu waiting for Salah?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, have mercy on him'
'O Allah, record a full Hajj for every minute'
'O Allah, exempt him from the next prayer'
'O Allah, grant him wealth and long travel'
explanationEn: As long as the worshipper stays in his spot without breaking Wudu or harming anyone, the angels continually supplicate for his forgiveness and mercy.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ describe the importance of straightening the rows (Taswiyat al-Sufuf) in congregational prayer?
optionsEn: It applies only to the very last row
It is required only when praying outdoors
It is an optional cultural custom only for Eid
It is part of the perfection and establishment of Salah
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik (RA) narrated the Prophet's ﷺ command: 'Straighten your rows, for straightening the rows is part of establishing the prayer.'

questionEn: What serious spiritual consequence did the Prophet ﷺ warn of if worshippers fail to straighten their prayer rows?
optionsEn: The prayer time expires immediately
Their Wudu becomes automatically invalidated
Allah will cause discord and division among their hearts and faces
They must repeat the Adhan three times
explanationEn: He ﷺ warned: 'Either you straighten your rows or Allah will cause your faces (or hearts) to differ from one another.'

questionEn: In what order did the Prophet ﷺ instruct congregations to fill the rows inside the masjid?
optionsEn: Complete the first row fully, then the next, leaving any incompleteness in the last row
Leave the center of the first row empty for latecomers
Fill the back row first and move forward
Spread evenly across all rows simultaneously
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ commanded: 'Complete the front row, then the one after it; if there is any shortage, let it be in the very last row.'

questionEn: What reward is promised to the believer who connects a row by stepping forward to fill an empty gap?
optionsEn: He is excused from praying the following Sunnah
He is permitted to speak during the rest of the prayer
Allah raises him a degree and builds a house for him in Paradise
He receives half the reward of the Imam
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) narrated that Allah and His angels send blessings upon those who connect rows, and whoever fills a gap, Allah elevates him in rank.

questionEn: To what did the Prophet ﷺ compare the small gaps left open between worshippers in a prayer row?
optionsEn: Windows for light to enter the prayer hall
Spaces through which Shaytan slips like a small black lamb (Hadhaf)
Paths reserved for the Muezzin to walk through
Gates leading out of the mosque courtyard
explanationEn: He ﷺ urged standing shoulder to shoulder and closing gaps, warning that Shaytan enters through openings like a small lamb.

questionEn: How did the Companions physically align themselves to ensure straight rows according to Anas ibn Malik (RA)?
optionsEn: By holding each other's hands throughout Qiyam
By joining shoulder to shoulder and foot to foot with their neighbors
By standing strictly on alternating tiles
By leaving an arm's length of empty space on each side
explanationEn: Anas (RA) reported that each Companion would align his shoulder with his companion's shoulder and his foot with his companion's foot.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ instruct a man whom he saw praying completely alone behind a full row when there was space to join or another option?
optionsEn: 'Continue your prayer, for solitude increases focus'
'Perform two extra Sujoods at the end'
'Stand directly to the right of the last person in the row'
'Repeat your prayer, for there is no valid prayer for one praying alone behind a row'
explanationEn: In the narration of Wabisah ibn Ma'bad (RA), the Prophet ﷺ ordered the man who prayed alone behind the row to repeat his prayer.

questionEn: When men and women pray together in the same open hall without a dividing partition, which rows are best for men and which for women?
optionsEn: Best for both men and women is the middle row
All rows carry identical virtue regardless of position
Best for men is the first row; best for women is the last row
Best for men is the last row; best for women is the first row
explanationEn: In an open shared hall, men's front row is furthest from mixing and closest to the Imam, while women's back row offers greater modesty and separation.

questionEn: Which side of the congregational rows receives special mention in a Hadith stating Allah and His angels send blessings upon it?
optionsEn: The far-left corner only
The side nearest the exit doors
Only the space directly behind the Muezzin
The right side of the rows
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) narrated: 'Indeed Allah and His angels send blessings upon the right sides of the rows (mayamin as-sufuf),' though completing the center near the Imam remains priority.

questionEn: Whom did the Prophet ﷺ advise to stand directly behind the Imam in the front row?
optionsEn: Those who wish to leave first after Salam
Travelers who arrived latest to the masjid
Those of maturity, knowledge, and sound understanding
Young children learning how to pray for the first time
explanationEn: He ﷺ said: 'Let those of wisdom and understanding among you stand near me, then those next to them,' so they can prompt or replace the Imam if needed.

questionEn: When a single male follower prays in congregation with a male Imam, where should the follower stand?
optionsEn: One pace diagonally in front of the Imam
Two paces directly behind the Imam's heels
Aligned directly to the left side of the Imam
Aligned directly to the right side of the Imam
explanationEn: When Ibn Abbas (RA) stood on the Prophet's ﷺ left during night prayer, the Prophet ﷺ moved him around to stand on his right side.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ do when Jabir (RA) stood on his right and Jabbar ibn Sakhr (RA) stood on his left during prayer?
optionsEn: He took both of their hands and pushed them to stand in a row behind him
He stepped backward to align between the two of them
He asked Jabbar to pray separately in another room
He continued the prayer with one on each side
explanationEn: With two or more male followers, the Sunnah is for the followers to form a row behind the Imam while the Imam stands alone in front.

questionEn: In the narration of Anas ibn Malik (RA) when the Prophet ﷺ led Anas, an orphan boy, and Umm Sulaym (RA) in prayer, how were the rows arranged?
optionsEn: All three stood side by side in one single row behind the Prophet ﷺ
Anas and the orphan stood in a row behind the Prophet ﷺ, and Umm Sulaym stood in a row behind them
Umm Sulaym stood beside the Prophet ﷺ while the two boys stood behind
The orphan stood to the Prophet's ﷺ right while Anas stood behind
explanationEn: A lone woman stands in a separate row behind the male row(s), even if she is the only woman present.

questionEn: When a woman leads an all-female congregation in prayer, where does she stand according to the practice of Aishah and Umm Salamah (RA)?
optionsEn: In the middle of the first row alongside the other women
Two paces ahead of the front row like a male Imam
On an elevated platform facing the women
In the back row behind all the other women
explanationEn: Both Aishah and Umm Salamah (RA) led women in prayer by standing in the center of the front row rather than stepping ahead.

questionEn: What is the minimum number of people required to form a valid congregational prayer (Jama'ah)?
optionsEn: Twelve residents of the city
Three people (an Imam and two followers)
Two people (an Imam and one follower)
Four adult men from the neighborhood
explanationEn: Two people constitute a congregation, as seen when the Prophet ﷺ prayed with Ibn Abbas (RA) and told Malik ibn al-Huwayrith and his single companion to establish prayer together.

questionEn: What strict principle governs the follower's movements relative to the Imam during congregational prayer?
optionsEn: Complete Ruku' independently at one's own preferred pace
Skip the Imam's movements if one finishes reciting early
Follow each movement strictly after the Imam transitions, never preceding him
Move into Ruku' and Sujood simultaneously before the Imam finishes his Takbir
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ declared: 'The Imam is appointed only to be followed; when he says Allahu Akbar, say Allahu Akbar, and when he bows, bow.'

questionEn: What severe warning did the Prophet ﷺ issue to a follower who raises his head from Ruku' or Sujood before the Imam?
optionsEn: He cannot attend the masjid for three days
He must pay a fine of dates to the mosque
His clothing becomes ritually impure
Does he not fear that Allah may turn his head into a donkey's head?
explanationEn: Abu Hurairah (RA) narrated this stark warning to instill reverence and discipline against racing ahead of the Imam.

questionEn: Whose 'Ameen' must a believer's 'Ameen' coincide with after the Imam recites Al-Fatihah for past sins to be forgiven?
optionsEn: The 'Ameen' of the angels
Only the 'Ameen' of the person on the left
The 'Ameen' of the Muezzin outside
The 'Ameen' spoken after the final Taslim
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught: 'When the Imam says Ameen, say Ameen, for whoever's Ameen coincides with the Ameen of the angels, his previous sins will be forgiven.'

questionEn: In congregational prayer, who is responsible for placing a Sutrah (barrier) in front of the worshippers?
optionsEn: Every single follower must place a separate object in front of himself
No Sutrah is ever used during congregational prayer
Only the last row needs a Sutrah behind them
The Imam's Sutrah suffices as a Sutrah for all followers behind him
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) rode a she-ass in front of the rows in Mina while the Prophet ﷺ led prayer, demonstrating that the Imam's Sutrah covers the congregation.

questionEn: What should a worshipper do if he enters the mosque and finds the Imam already in Sujood or Tashahhud?
optionsEn: Say Takbirat al-Ihram standing and immediately join the Imam in whatever posture he is in
Stand waiting upright until the Imam rises for the next rak'ah
Perform two quick Ruku's on his own to catch up
Wait until the Imam says Salam and then begin alone
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed: 'When one of you comes to prayer while the Imam is in a state, let him do as the Imam is doing.'

questionEn: Why is praying behind an Imam sitting when the Imam himself is injured and praying seated sometimes narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari?
optionsEn: Because sitting is always superior to standing in congregation
Because worshippers are forbidden from standing indoors
Because standing is reserved only for Jumu'ah prayer
Because the Imam is appointed to be followed, so when he prays sitting due to disability from the start, followers also sit (with nuance from the final illness)
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ fell from a horse and led seated from the start, he told Companions to sit; scholars also discuss the later incident in his final illness where Abu Bakr stood.

questionEn: Why should a follower wait until the Imam completes his opening 'Allahu Akbar' before saying Takbirat al-Ihram?
optionsEn: Because saying Takbirat al-Ihram before the Imam finishes invalidates entering the congregation behind him
Because the follower must finish Al-Fatihah before saying Takbir
Because the Muezzin must repeat the Iqamah first
Because the follower's Takbir must be louder than the Imam's
explanationEn: The Hadith 'When he says Allahu Akbar, then say Allahu Akbar' teaches that a follower cannot legally enter the Imam's prayer before the Imam himself has entered it.

questionEn: If a person normally prays in congregation regularly, what reward does Allah write for him when sickness or travel prevents him from attending the masjid?
optionsEn: He must pay expiation for every missed congregation
Only half the reward of praying alone
The full reward of what he used to pray while healthy and resident
Zero reward until he physically returns to the masjid
explanationEn: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA) narrated that when a servant falls ill or travels, Allah records for him the like of the righteous deeds he used to perform when healthy and at home.

questionEn: What did Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) say about the practice of the Companions regarding attending congregational prayers?
optionsEn: No one stayed behind from it except a known hypocrite or a sick person who had to be carried between two men
They attended congregation only on Fridays and Mondays
Travelers inside Madinah were forbidden from joining
Only the Muezzin and Imam attended daily prayers
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud (RA) described how even ill Companions would walk supported between two men just to stand in the congregational row.

questionEn: What excuse did the Prophet ﷺ reject when the blind Companion Ibn Umm Maktum (RA) asked permission to pray at home?
optionsEn: When he confirmed he could hear the call to prayer (Adhan), the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Then answer it'
He instructed him to listen to the Adhan from his rooftop only
He told him to pray at home every single day
He exempted him because he lived across the street
explanationEn: Though Ibn Umm Maktum had no guide to lead him, the Prophet ﷺ asked 'Do you hear the call to prayer?' and upon his 'Yes,' told him to respond to it.

questionEn: When two people are in a desert or open wilderness without a masjid nearby and establish congregational prayer together after Adhan and Iqamah, who joins them according to Hadith?
optionsEn: Hosts of angels stretching farther than the eye can see
Only the birds overhead
Their prayer counts as half a single prayer
No spiritual blessing occurs outside a roofed building
explanationEn: Salman al-Farisi (RA) narrated that if a man in a desolate land makes Adhan, Iqamah, and prays, angels pray behind him in rows whose ends cannot be seen.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, why did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) and Companions maintain the reward of congregation even when someone set out for it with sincere intention and found it already finished?
optionsEn: Because they repeated the Adhan loudly a second time
Because whoever performs Wudu well and walks out intending congregation earns the reward of those who attended it
Because walking in the streets automatically cancels Salah
Because they waited until the next day's Fajr
explanationEn: Abu Hurairah (RA) narrated: 'Whoever performs Wudu properly and comes to the masjid, finding the people have already prayed, Allah gives him the same reward as those who prayed and attended.'

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about how long a worshipper remains legally 'in prayer'?
optionsEn: Only during the moments he is in Sujood
Until he finishes eating dinner afterward
Only from the second Takbir until the first Taslim
As long as he is waiting for the prayer inside the masjid
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught: 'One of you continues to be in prayer as long as the prayer detains him, and nothing keeps him from returning to his family except the prayer.'

questionEn: If a person is already praying a voluntary prayer alone and the obligatory Iqamah begins, what happens if he continues his long voluntary prayer?
optionsEn: The Imam must pause the congregation until he finishes
He misses the opening Takbir and contradicts the Hadith forbidding other prayers once Iqamah starts
His voluntary prayer converts automatically into the obligatory prayer
He gains double the reward of the first row
explanationEn: Once the Iqamah is called, starting or unnecessarily prolonging voluntary prayers is prohibited so one does not miss joining the obligatory congregation.

questionEn: What virtuous habit did the Prophet ﷺ praise regarding catching the opening Takbir (Takbirat al-Ihram) with the Imam for forty consecutive days?
optionsEn: Two decrees of freedom are written for him: freedom from the Hellfire and freedom from hypocrisy
He is exempted from Zakah for one year
He is guaranteed to see Laylat al-Qadr immediately
He becomes the permanent Imam of his city
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik (RA) narrated that whoever prays forty days in congregation catching the first Takbir receives immunity from the Fire and from hypocrisy.

questionEn: How should worshippers align themselves relative to the Kaaba when praying inside Al-Masjid al-Haram's Mataf?
optionsEn: In concentric circles surrounding the Kaaba from all sides
Only behind Maqam Ibrahim in straight rows
Facing strictly south regardless of which side of the Kaaba they stand on
Standing exclusively between Safa and Marwah
explanationEn: Because the Kaaba is at the center, rows in Al-Masjid al-Haram form rings around it so every worshipper faces directly toward the Sacred House.

questionEn: What is the ruling on eating a heavy meal immediately before prayer when dinner is already served and the Iqamah is called?
optionsEn: Eat dinner first calmly so the heart is not distracted during Salah
Fast the rest of the evening instead
Bring the dinner tray into the prayer row
Leave the food untouched even if intensely hungry
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed: 'When dinner is served and the prayer is called, start with dinner first,' so hunger does not rob the heart of Khushu'.

questionEn: If a person is praying alone and a second Muslim arrives wanting to pray in congregation with him, what may the second person do?
optionsEn: Stand directly in front of him facing the Qibla
Stand to the right side of the first person and follow him as Imam
Stand two rows behind him without informing him
Tap him on the head to stop his prayer and restart together
explanationEn: As established in the Hadith of Ibn Abbas (RA) joining the Prophet ﷺ at night, a second person stands on the Imam's right side to establish Jama'ah.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ explain why Allah looks favorably upon a shepherd or lone caller who prays in the wilderness as compared to people in towns?
optionsEn: Allah is amazed at a shepherd on a mountain peak who calls Adhan and establishes Salah solely out of awe of Him
Because mountains amplify the sound of Adhan better than minarets
Because wilderness prayer requires no Qibla direction
Because shepherds pray only two prayers a day
explanationEn: Uqbah ibn Amir (RA) narrated that Allah marvels at a shepherd on a mountain top calling Adhan and praying alone, saying: 'Look at My servant; he fears Me—I have forgiven him.'

questionEn: When leaving the prayer hall or waiting after congregation ends, why did the Prophet ﷺ advise men in Masjid an-Nabawi to pause briefly after Salam?
optionsEn: To count every tile in the mosque floor
To let the Muezzin lock the doors from inside
To allow the women to exit the mosque peacefully before the men stood up
To wait until the sun set completely
explanationEn: Umm Salamah (RA) narrated that when the Prophet ﷺ concluded prayer with Salam, the women would rise immediately while he and the men remained seated briefly so women could depart unhindered.

questionEn: According to the Hadith of Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari (RA) in Sahih Muslim, who has the very first priority to lead the congregation as Imam?
optionsEn: The wealthiest donor in the neighborhood
The one most proficient in reciting and knowing the Book of Allah
The youngest unmarried man in attendance
The tallest man standing in the front row
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ established a clear hierarchy: 'The one who is best versed in the Book of Allah leads the people.'

questionEn: If multiple men present are equal in their mastery of the Qur'an, what is the second criterion for selecting the Imam?
optionsEn: The one with the deepest voice
The one who arrived wearing the most expensive garment
The one most knowledgeable in the Sunnah
The one who lives farthest from the masjid
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim 673, after Qur'an proficiency comes knowledge of the Sunnah, then earliness in Hijrah, then seniority in Islam or age.

questionEn: In the same Hadith on Imamah priority, what rule protects the rights of a homeowner or resident authority?
optionsEn: A guest must always force the host to step back and follow
No man may lead another in his own domain/home or sit in his place of honor without his permission
Whoever enters the house last automatically becomes Imam
The Muezzin always overrides the homeowner inside a private home
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ forbade leading a host in his own sphere of authority (sultanihi) or taking his seat of honor unless he grants permission.

questionEn: What instruction did the Prophet ﷺ give to Malik ibn al-Huwayrith (RA) and his young companions when they were equal in Qur'anic knowledge?
optionsEn: 'Draw straws before every single prayer'
'Let one of you call the Adhan, and let the eldest of you lead the prayer'
'Pray separately in different corners of the room'
'Let the youngest lead Fajr and the eldest lead Isha'
explanationEn: When two or more travelers are close in learning, seniority in age and Islam takes precedence to honor the elders.

questionEn: How old was Amr ibn Salamah (RA) when his tribe appointed him to lead them in prayer because he had memorized the most Qur'an?
optionsEn: Eighteen years old
Six or seven years old
Twenty-five years old
Forty years old
explanationEn: Amr ibn Salamah learned the surahs from travelers passing his tribe; being six or seven and knowing the most Qur'an, his elders placed him forward to lead.

questionEn: Which blind Companion did the Prophet ﷺ repeatedly appoint to lead the Muslims of Madinah in prayer during his journeys?
optionsEn: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA)
Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (RA)
Salman al-Farisi (RA)
Bilal ibn Rabah (RA)
explanationEn: Ibn Umm Maktum (RA) frequently led prayer in Madinah, establishing the permissibility of a blind Imam leading sighted worshippers.

questionEn: If a traveling Imam leads local residents in Dhuhr prayer and shortens it to two rak'ahs (Qasr), what must the resident followers do when he concludes with Salam?
optionsEn: Say Salam with the Imam and stop at two rak'ahs
Stand up and complete the remaining two rak'ahs to make four
Repeat all four rak'ahs from the beginning alone
Add two Sujoods of forgetfulness instead of standing
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ led Makkans in two rak'ahs during the Conquest, he instructed: 'Complete your prayer, O people of Makkah, for we are travelers.'

questionEn: What happens if an Imam realizes during prayer that he has lost his Wudu (or was stabbed/incapacitated), as occurred with Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)?
optionsEn: Everyone in the mosque must immediately abandon prayer and restart an hour later
He continues leading the congregation without Wudu until Salam
He steps aside and pulls a capable follower from behind him forward to complete leading the prayer
The Muezzin finishes leading from the minaret
explanationEn: When Umar (RA) was struck during Fajr, he took Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf (RA) by the hand and brought him forward to finish leading the congregation.

questionEn: If an Imam sincerely forgets he lacked Wudu and leads a congregation, then remembers after the prayer ends, whose prayer must be repeated?
optionsEn: Only the front row must repeat the prayer
Neither the Imam nor the followers repeat anything
Only the Imam repeats his prayer; the followers' prayer remains valid
Both the Imam and all followers must repeat the prayer
explanationEn: Because the followers prayed in purity unaware of the Imam's state, their prayer is valid (as reflected in Umar and Uthman's rulings and Bukhari's chapter).

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ command Imams to keep congregational prayers reasonably brief and measured?
optionsEn: Because behind the Imam stand the weak, the elderly, and people with urgent needs
Because reciting more than one verse in prayer is disliked
Because the masjid lamps only stayed lit for ten minutes
Because longer prayers are forbidden in Islam
explanationEn: He ﷺ said: 'When one of you leads people in prayer, let him keep it light, for among them are the weak, the sick, and the elderly; when he prays alone, let him lengthen as he wills.'

questionEn: Which Companion did the Prophet ﷺ gently rebuke with 'Are you putting people to trial?' after he recited Surah Al-Baqarah while leading Isha?
optionsEn: Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA)
Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA)
Zayd ibn Thabit (RA)
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA)
explanationEn: When a tired laborer left Mu'adh's long Isha prayer to pray alone, the Prophet ﷺ advised Mu'adh to recite moderate surahs like Al-A'la, Ash-Shams, and Al-Layl.

questionEn: What caused the Prophet ﷺ to shorten a congregational prayer even after intending to lengthen it?
optionsEn: A sudden gust of wind blowing through the courtyard
Hearing merchants arriving outside the mosque
Forgetting which Surah came next
Hearing a young child crying, out of compassion for the mother's distress
explanationEn: Anas (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said he would begin prayer intending to prolong it, then hear a baby cry and shorten it knowing how deeply the mother feels for her child.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ lengthen his recitation in the first rak'ah of Dhuhr compared to the second rak'ah according to Abu Qatadah (RA)?
optionsEn: So that latecomers would have time to catch the first rak'ah before Ruku' ended
To test whether the followers had memorized Surah Al-Kahf
Because the second rak'ah of Dhuhr requires no recitation
Because Dhuhr is always shorter in the second half
explanationEn: Abu Qatadah (RA) observed that lengthening the first rak'ah helped people arrive and join the congregation smoothly.

questionEn: What did Al-Bara' ibn Azib (RA) observe the Prophet ﷺ do after concluding congregational prayer with Salam?
optionsEn: He turned around to face the congregation (either to his right or left) rather than remaining facing the Qibla
He walked backward out of the Mihrab
He lay down immediately on the mosque floor
He remained rigidly facing the Qibla wall until everyone left
explanationEn: Turning toward the congregation after post-Salam adhkar was the Prophet's ﷺ consistent Sunnah, marking the clear end of the Imam's prayer.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ define the distinct responsibilities of the Imam and the Muezzin?
optionsEn: 'The Imam calls the time, and the Muezzin leads the rows'
'Only the Muezzin is responsible for the number of rak'ahs'
'The Imam is a guarantor (Damin), and the Muezzin is entrusted (Mu'taman)'
'Both share equal blame if any follower loses Wudu'
explanationEn: The Imam bears responsibility for guarding the pillars and pace of the congregation's prayer, while the Muezzin is trusted with accurately announcing prayer times.

questionEn: What reassuring principle did the Prophet ﷺ state if an Imam errs in a way that affects the prayer while the followers prayed sincerely behind him?
optionsEn: 'None of the congregation's good deeds are recorded that day'
'Everyone must fast three days to expiate the Imam's error'
'If they pray correctly, it counts for you and them; if they err, the reward is for you and the error is upon them'
'The followers receive double punishment for choosing that Imam'
explanationEn: Abu Hurairah (RA) narrated this great comfort for congregations, reminding Imams of the weighty trust upon their shoulders.

questionEn: If an Imam makes an unexpected mistake in action during prayer (such as standing for an extra rak'ah), how should male and female followers alert him?
optionsEn: Both men and women shout 'Mistake!' loudly
Everyone remains completely silent and follows the error
Men tap their shoulders and women stand up immediately
Men say 'SubhanAllah' and women clap (tap one hand on the back of the other)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught: 'If something occurs to you in prayer, let the men say SubhanAllah and let the women clap (tasfiq).'

questionEn: What should a knowledgeable follower do if the Imam pauses, hesitates, or confuses a verse during aloud Qur'anic recitation?
optionsEn: Walk up to the front and hand him a physical Mushaf
Remain quiet even if the Imam stops reciting completely
Prompt the Imam gently by reciting the correct word or verse aloud
Say 'SubhanAllah' repeatedly until the Imam skips to Ruku'
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ once omitted part of a recitation and asked why Ubayy ibn Ka'b didn't remind him, he approved prompting the Imam in Qur'an.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ accidentally stood up directly into the third rak'ah of Dhuhr without sitting for the middle Tashahhud, what did the congregation do?
optionsEn: They added an extra Ruku' in the fourth rak'ah
They stayed seated until he finished the fourth rak'ah alone
They broke their prayer and restarted from the first rak'ah
They stood up with him, and he performed two prostrations of forgetfulness (Sujood al-Sahw) before Salam
explanationEn: Once the Imam rises fully into a standing pillar, the congregation follows him and rectifies the missed middle Tashahhud via Sujood al-Sahw together.

questionEn: If the Imam stands up for a fifth rak'ah in a four-rak'ah prayer and refuses to sit despite hearing 'SubhanAllah,' what should a follower who is certain it is a fifth rak'ah do?
optionsEn: Walk out of the mosque immediately without Salam
Stand up and pray the fifth rak'ah anyway
Begin praying Asr right away
Remain seated in Tashahhud and wait to conclude with the Imam (or conclude after waiting), rather than knowingly adding a fifth rak'ah
explanationEn: A follower who knows with certainty that the prayer is complete does not knowingly perform an invalid extra rak'ah, waiting seated until the Imam finishes.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ disapprove of a man leading a community in prayer when the congregation genuinely dislikes him for valid religious or moral reasons?
optionsEn: Because the Muezzin is required to resign
Because a Hadith warns that such an Imam's prayer does not rise a handspan above his head
Because the Imam would be forced to pray facing west
Because the masjid roof would collapse
explanationEn: Scholars clarify this warning targets an Imam disliked for legitimate religious shortcomings or oppression, not one opposed out of personal whim while upright.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach regarding praying behind any Muslim leader or Imam, whether righteous or flawed, so long as they establish prayer?
optionsEn: Pray behind them to preserve unity and community worship, without fracturing the congregation
Pray at home alone whenever you disagree with an Imam's lineage
Refuse to pray behind anyone unless he is proven infallible
Demand to examine every Imam's private sins first
explanationEn: Companions like Ibn Umar (RA) prayed behind governors of varying character, preserving the unity of congregational and Jumu'ah prayers.

questionEn: Why did Abu Bakr (RA) step backward to stand in the row when the Prophet ﷺ came out during his final illness, even after Abu Bakr had begun leading?
optionsEn: Because the Qibla direction shifted mid-prayer
Because Abu Bakr forgot how to recite Al-Fatihah
Because Abu Bakr had to leave to fetch water
Out of deep respect, knowing no one should step ahead of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he is present
explanationEn: Abu Bakr (RA) remarked that it was not fitting for Ibn Abi Quhafah to lead while Allah's Messenger ﷺ was present, so the Prophet ﷺ sat beside him and led.

questionEn: What physical act did the Prophet ﷺ prohibit for an Imam standing higher than the congregation without a teaching purpose?
optionsEn: Wearing a white turban while leading
Standing on an elevated platform noticeably higher than the followers
Standing on a woven prayer mat
Using a walking staff before starting prayer
explanationEn: Hudhayfah (RA) forbade an Imam from standing higher than the congregation unless teaching (as the Prophet ﷺ once stood on the minbar then stepped down for Sujood).

questionEn: What determines whether a latecomer (Masbuq) has validly caught a rak'ah with the Imam?
optionsEn: Catching at least the second Sujood of that rak'ah
Entering the front door of the masjid before the Imam begins Tashahhud
Hearing the Imam's 'Allahu Akbar' from the parking area
Reaching Ruku' and settling in it with the Imam before the Imam rises from Ruku'
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ declared: 'Whoever catches the Ruku' of a rak'ah has caught the rak'ah.'

questionEn: When Abu Bakrah (RA) hurriedly bowed into Ruku' before reaching the row and then shuffled into the row, what did the Prophet ﷺ tell him afterward?
optionsEn: 'Your entire prayer is invalid; repeat four rak'ahs'
'Stand outside the mosque until the next prayer'
'May Allah increase your eagerness, but do not do it again'
'You must always bow at the doorway from now on'
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ acknowledged his zeal (and counted his rak'ah according to the majority), while instructing him not to rush and bow before joining the row.

questionEn: If a Masbuq enters the mosque and joins the Imam after the Imam has already risen upright from Ruku' into I'tidal or Sujood, does that rak'ah count for him?
optionsEn: Yes, if he catches the final Tashahhud it counts as two rak'ahs
No, and he must wait standing without joining until the next rak'ah
No, he does not count that rak'ah, though he joins immediately to gain the blessing of congregation
Yes, catching Sujood counts as catching the full rak'ah
explanationEn: Missing the Ruku' means that rak'ah is missed, yet the Masbuq still joins the Imam immediately rather than standing idle.

questionEn: In what posture MUST a latecomer say Takbirat al-Ihram when trying to catch an Imam who is currently in Ruku'?
optionsEn: Standing completely upright before bending down into Ruku'
After already touching his knees in Ruku'
Already bent halfway into Ruku' to save time
While walking rapidly across the carpet
explanationEn: Standing (Qiyam) for Takbirat al-Ihram is an essential pillar of prayer; saying the opening Takbir while bent over invalidates the entry into Salah.

questionEn: When a Masbuq joins the Imam while the Imam is already in Ruku', what happens to the obligation of reciting Al-Fatihah in that rak'ah?
optionsEn: He must stay standing to finish Al-Fatihah even after the Imam goes to Sujood
He recites Al-Fatihah twice during the final Tashahhud
The Masbuq must recite Al-Fatihah quickly while bent in Ruku'
The obligation of Al-Fatihah is waived/carried by the Imam for that caught rak'ah
explanationEn: Catching the Imam in Ruku' secures that rak'ah without requiring the Masbuq to stand and recite Al-Fatihah separately, as seen in Abu Bakrah's incident.

questionEn: At what exact moment should a Masbuq rise to make up the rak'ahs he missed behind the Imam?
optionsEn: Immediately when the Imam begins reciting 'At-Tahiyyat'
After the Imam completes both Taslims concluding the prayer
Before the Imam completes the final Sujood
Right after the Imam says only the first Taslim to the right
explanationEn: Because the follower must remain with the Imam until the Imam fully concludes his prayer, the Masbuq stands only after the Imam finishes the Salam.

questionEn: If a Masbuq arrives and catches only the fourth (final) rak'ah of Dhuhr with the Imam, how many rak'ahs must he pray after the Imam says Salam?
optionsEn: Two rak'ahs
Three rak'ahs
Four rak'ahs
One rak'ah
explanationEn: Dhuhr has four rak'ahs; having caught one valid rak'ah with the Imam, the Masbuq stands after Salam to complete the remaining three.

questionEn: If a Masbuq catches only the third (final) rak'ah of Maghrib with the Imam, how does he perform the sitting of Tashahhud while making up his remaining two rak'ahs?
optionsEn: He prays 1st missed rak'ah, sits for middle Tashahhud (his 2nd total rak'ah), then prays his final rak'ah and ends with Tashahhud and Salam
He stands and prays two rak'ahs straight through without any middle Tashahhud
He says Salam immediately after finishing just one additional rak'ah
He sits after his very last rak'ah only and skips middle Tashahhud
explanationEn: Catching 1 rak'ah with the Imam means his next rak'ah is the 2nd of his prayer, so he sits for the first Tashahhud after it, then rises for his 3rd rak'ah.

questionEn: If a Masbuq catches the second and third rak'ahs of Maghrib with the Imam, how many rak'ahs does he stand up to complete after the Imam's Salam?
optionsEn: Three rak'ahs from the beginning
One rak'ah (with Al-Fatihah and a Surah), followed by final Tashahhud and Salam
Two rak'ahs without reciting a Surah
Zero rak'ahs; he finishes with the Imam
explanationEn: He has already prayed two rak'ahs with the Imam and sat for his own middle Tashahhud with the Imam's final Tashahhud, so only one rak'ah remains.

questionEn: If a Masbuq joins the congregation during the Imam's final Tashahhud before Salam, what must he do after the Imam finishes Salam?
optionsEn: Pray only one rak'ah to make it even
Wait for the next congregation to start
Say Salam with the Imam because catching Tashahhud counts as a rak'ah
Stand up and pray all the rak'ahs of that prayer completely (e.g., all 4 of Isha)
explanationEn: Joining in the final Tashahhud earns the blessing of entering the congregation, but zero rak'ahs were caught, so all rak'ahs are performed after Salam.

questionEn: What happens if a Masbuq catches the second rak'ah of Fajr with the Imam—how does he complete his prayer after the Imam says Salam?
optionsEn: He stands and prays one remaining rak'ah, then sits for Tashahhud and says Salam
He says Salam with the Imam since Fajr has only two rak'ahs
He sits silently for five minutes then leaves
He prays two additional rak'ahs
explanationEn: Having caught one rak'ah of Fajr, he rises after the Imam's Salam to complete his single missed rak'ah and concludes.

questionEn: If a latecomer joins Jumu'ah prayer after the Imam has already risen from Ruku' in the second rak'ah, what must he pray after the Imam says Salam?
optionsEn: Nothing, as catching Sujood catches Jumu'ah
Four rak'ahs of Dhuhr prayer
One single rak'ah of Jumu'ah
Two rak'ahs of Jumu'ah prayer
explanationEn: A person catches Jumu'ah only by catching at least one full rak'ah (i.e., Ruku' of the second rak'ah); missing both Ruku's means he completes four rak'ahs of Dhuhr.

questionEn: If a latecomer catches the Ruku' of the second rak'ah of Jumu'ah with the Imam, how does he complete his prayer after the Imam's Salam?
optionsEn: He stands and prays two full rak'ahs from scratch
He says Salam immediately with the Imam
He stands and completes just one more rak'ah to complete two rak'ahs of Jumu'ah
He must pray four rak'ahs of Dhuhr
explanationEn: Whoever catches one rak'ah of Jumu'ah (by catching Ruku' of the second rak'ah) has caught Jumu'ah and adds only one rak'ah after the Imam's Salam.

questionEn: If the Imam performs Sujood al-Sahw (prostration of forgetfulness) at the end of prayer before Salam, what should a Masbuq do?
optionsEn: Perform Sujood al-Sahw together with the Imam, then stand to complete his missed rak'ahs after the Imam's Salam
Wait until the end of his own missed rak'ahs and skip joining the Imam
Stand up immediately while the Imam goes into Sujood al-Sahw
Remain sitting upright and refuse to prostrate with the Imam
explanationEn: Because a Masbuq is bound to follow the Imam until the Imam concludes his prayer, he joins the Imam in Sujood al-Sahw before making up missed units.

questionEn: What if an Imam performs Sujood al-Sahw AFTER his Taslim (Salam) because of an error, and a Masbuq had already stood up to make up missed rak'ahs?
optionsEn: Stop mid-recitation and leave the mosque
Wait if aware, or if already standing, finish his own missed rak'ahs and then perform his own Sujood al-Sahw at the end (depending on juristic school)
Start over with a new congregation
Skip all missed rak'ahs and sit down
explanationEn: Scholars note that if the Imam prostrates after Salam before the Masbuq stands, the Masbuq follows him (or completes his own and prostrates at the end if he already rose).

questionEn: What should a Masbuq do if he accidentally forgets and says Salam together with the Imam instead of standing up to complete his missed rak'ahs?
optionsEn: His prayer is forever ruined and cannot be fixed
Do nothing and leave the mosque
Recite Surah Al-Ikhlas three times while seated
Immediately stand up upon remembering, complete the missed rak'ahs, and perform Sujood al-Sahw at the end
explanationEn: An accidental Salam out of forgetfulness does not break the prayer if rectified promptly; the Masbuq rises, finishes his remaining rak'ahs, and performs Sujood al-Sahw.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ taught 'Pray what you catch and complete (fa-atimmu) what you missed,' what does 'what you catch is the beginning of your prayer' practically mean in schools like Shafi'i/Hanbali?
optionsEn: You must say Salam before every missed rak'ah
You always repeat Al-Fatihah three times in every rak'ah
You pray the missed rak'ahs silently even in Maghrib
The rak'ahs prayed with the Imam count as your first rak'ahs, and those made up after Salam are the end of your prayer (so no extra Surah after Fatihah in the 3rd/4th rak'ahs)
explanationEn: Under the wording 'fa-atimmu' (complete), what you caught with the Imam is treated as the start of your Salah, while Hanafi/Maliki scholars distinguish actions vs recitation using the wording 'fa-qdu' (make up).

questionEn: According to the Maliki and Hanafi perspective on 'what you catch is the end of your prayer' (for recitation) vs actions, how do they instruct a Masbuq who caught only the 4th rak'ah of Isha?
optionsEn: Recite Al-Fatihah and a Surah in his first two made-up rak'ahs, while sitting for Tashahhud at his proper 2nd total rak'ah
Skip Al-Fatihah completely in every made-up rak'ah
Pray only two rak'ahs instead of three
Recite Surah Al-Baqarah in the final rak'ah
explanationEn: Both scholarly approaches rely on authentic prophetic wording ('complete' vs 'make up'), differing gently on whether an extra Surah is read in the made-up units.

questionEn: If a Masbuq joins the Imam during Qiyam (standing) before Ruku' and begins reciting Al-Fatihah, what should he do if the Imam bows into Ruku' before he finishes Al-Fatihah?
optionsEn: Skip Ruku' and go straight to Sujood
Stop reciting and bow into Ruku' immediately with the Imam so as not to lag behind
Stay standing to finish Al-Fatihah even if the Imam rises from Ruku'
Leave the congregation and start praying alone
explanationEn: Following the Imam takes priority over completing Al-Fatihah when one joined late; catching Ruku' with the Imam preserves the rak'ah.

questionEn: What if a follower makes a minor mistake of forgetfulness (like forgetting Subhana Rabbiyal-Azim in Ruku') while praying behind an Imam?
optionsEn: He interrupts the Imam loudly to ask for Sujood al-Sahw
He does not perform Sujood al-Sahw separately; the Imam bears/covers the minor slip of the follower
He must stay behind and do Sujood al-Sahw after the Imam leaves
His entire prayer becomes invalid
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) and early jurists stated there is no individual Sujood al-Sahw upon a follower for his own minor slip while following the Imam.

questionEn: If a person is praying alone and an obligatory congregation starts nearby in the same masjid, what did the Prophet ﷺ advise if he has not yet completed his prayer?
optionsEn: Shout at the Imam to wait for him
Break or finish lightly so he can join the congregation, as no prayer should compete once Iqamah is called
Pray twice as slowly to avoid joining
Ignore the congregation and stay praying alone in the corner
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ forbade starting or maintaining separate prayers when the Iqamah for the communal prayer is established.

questionEn: If a man who has already prayed an obligatory prayer alone enters a masjid and sees a congregation just beginning that same prayer, what did the Prophet ﷺ instruct at Mina?
optionsEn: Walk out of the masjid immediately
Only join for the final Tashahhud without standing
Sit back and refuse to pray with the congregation
Pray with them anyway; it will be counted for him as a blessed voluntary (Nafl) prayer
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told two men who had prayed in their tents: 'When you pray at home and then come to a congregational masjid, pray with them, for it is Nafl for you.'

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when asked about a man who entered late and prayed behind the Imam, then someone else arrived after the Imam finished and wanted to pray with the Masbuq?
optionsEn: A person finishing his missed rak'ahs may serve as Imam for a newly arriving worshipper (or another person may give him charity by praying with him)
They must wait until the next day's Fajr
Only the original Imam can ever lead in that building
It is strictly prohibited for two latecomers to pray together
explanationEn: When a lone latecomer arrived after congregation ended, the Prophet ﷺ asked: 'Who will give charity to this man by praying with him?' so a Companion stood and prayed with him.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a Masbuq who joined late makes an error of his own during the rak'ahs he makes up AFTER the Imam's Salam?
optionsEn: The original Imam still covers any error he makes after Salam
He must repeat the whole congregation with the next Imam
He performs Sujood al-Sahw at the end of his prayer, because he is now praying independently after the Imam's Salam
He cannot perform Sujood al-Sahw under any circumstance
explanationEn: Once the Imam says Salam, the Masbuq stands in the status of a solo worshipper for the remaining rak'ahs, so he rectifies his own errors with Sujood al-Sahw.

questionEn: What should a Masbuq do if he intends to join a congregation and sees the Imam sitting in Tashahhud—should he say Takbirat al-Ihram and sit immediately, or say an extra Takbir to sit?
optionsEn: Say Takbirat al-Ihram while standing upright, then sit down directly into Tashahhud (a transition Takbir may also be said)
Skip Takbirat al-Ihram altogether
Stand upright silently until the Imam turns his head
Sit down first and then say Takbirat al-Ihram while seated
explanationEn: Entering prayer always requires Takbirat al-Ihram while standing upright (for those able to stand), after which the Masbuq sits with the Imam.

questionEn: Why should the person standing directly behind the Imam be capable of stepping forward smoothly if needed?
optionsEn: So that he can distribute water cups during Ruku'
So that if the Imam loses Wudu, falls ill, or forgets a verse, someone qualified right behind him can prompt or take over seamlessly
So that he can call the second Adhan from the Mihrab
So that he can exit first through the Imam's private door
explanationEn: This practical wisdom is why the Prophet ﷺ urged people of knowledge and sound judgment to stand closest behind him.

questionEn: Which foot should a Muslim step forward with first when entering a masjid, and which dua is Sunnah to recite?
optionsEn: Left foot first, saying 'Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik'
Left foot first, saying 'Bismillahi tawakkaltu alallah'
Right foot first, saying 'SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik'
Right foot first, saying 'Allahummaftah li abwaba rahmatik' (O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ loved to begin honorable acts with the right side, and taught entering the masjid with Salawat and asking Allah to open the gates of His mercy.

questionEn: When exiting the masjid, which foot should step out first and what supplication is Sunnah to recite?
optionsEn: Right foot first, saying 'Allahummaftah li abwaba rahmatik'
Left foot first, saying 'Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik' (O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty)
Right foot first, saying 'HasbunAllahu wa ni'mal-wakil'
Left foot first, saying 'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah'
explanationEn: Upon leaving the house of worship to return to daily provision and worldly duties, a Muslim asks Allah of His bounty (fadl).

questionEn: What happens when a believer recites 'A'udhu billahil-'Azim wa bi-wajhihil-karim wa sultanihil-qadim minash-shaytanir-rajim' upon entering the masjid?
optionsEn: Every angel in the city stops praying to listen
All past major sins are erased without repentance
Shaytan declares that the believer is protected from him for the rest of the day
The believer is excused from Tahiyyat al-Masjid
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) narrated that when a person says this refuge-seeking supplication upon entering the masjid, Shaytan says: 'He is protected from me all day.'

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ prohibit anyone who has recently eaten raw garlic, onions, or leeks from approaching the masjid?
optionsEn: Because onions and garlic are permanently haram to eat at home
Because raw garlic causes drowsiness during Ruku'
Because the angels are offended by foul odors just as the children of Adam are offended by them
Because eating vegetables breaks Wudu immediately
explanationEn: Raw pungent foods linger on the breath and disturb fellow worshippers and the angels; cooking them thoroughly removes the offensive odor.

questionEn: What does Allah command believers regarding clothing and appearance whenever attending a masjid in Surah Al-A'raf (7:31)?
optionsEn: 'O children of Adam, take your adornment (clean, modest, dignified attire) at every masjid'
'Wear only black garments inside every masjid'
'Remove all footwear before reaching the street outside'
'Wear silk and gold rings exclusively during Dhuhr'
explanationEn: Standing before Allah in His house calls for cleanliness, covering the awrah properly, and neat, respectful dress rather than unkempt clothing.

questionEn: If you witness someone buying or selling goods inside the prayer hall of a masjid, what did the Prophet ﷺ instruct you to say?
optionsEn: 'May Allah not make your trade profitable'
'Offer half of your merchandise to the Muezzin'
'May Allah double your earnings in this hall'
'Move your stall closer to the Mihrab'
explanationEn: Mosques are sanctuaries dedicated to worship and remembrance of Allah, never marketplaces for commercial buying and selling.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ instruct Muslims to say to anyone loudly announcing a lost item inside the masjid?
optionsEn: 'Offer a reward of dates inside the first row'
'Speak louder so the Imam can pause and help search'
'Wait until the middle of Sujood to call out again'
'May Allah not return it to you, for the masajid were not built for this'
explanationEn: This firm response protects the tranquility and spiritual purpose of the mosque from turning into a lost-and-found shouting hall.

questionEn: After a desert Bedouin mistakenly urinated in a corner of the Prophet's ﷺ masjid, how did the Prophet ﷺ handle the situation and explain the mosque's purpose?
optionsEn: He ordered the Bedouin barred from Madinah permanently
He stopped Companions from scolding him mid-act, had water poured over it, and gently taught that masajid are for remembrance of Allah, Salah, and Qur'an
He tore down that entire wall of the mosque and rebuilt it
He asked the Bedouin to fast for sixty consecutive days
explanationEn: The Prophet's ﷺ gentleness prevented impurity from spreading and won the Bedouin's heart while clearly teaching the sanctity of the masjid.

questionEn: How severe is the warning against walking directly in front of someone who is praying (within their Sutrah space)?
optionsEn: If the passerby knew the sin upon him, standing and waiting forty (days, months, or years) would be better than crossing in front of him
It is harmless as long as the passerby walks rapidly
It invalidates the passerby's fast
It only matters during Jumu'ah prayer
explanationEn: Respecting a worshipper's concentration and Sutrah boundary is a vital mosque etiquette emphasized strongly by the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: What should a worshipper praying behind a Sutrah do if someone attempts to walk directly between him and his Sutrah?
optionsEn: Step backward five rows to let them pass
Stop praying completely and shout at them
Ignore them and bow immediately regardless
Prevent them with a gentle gesture of the hand, and if they insist, push them back firmly
explanationEn: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ instructed repelling anyone who tries to cross in front of a praying person.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ forbid worshippers in the masjid from raising their voices loudly over one another while reciting the Qur'an?
optionsEn: Because Qur'an should never be recited inside a masjid outside Jumu'ah
Because only the Muezzin is permitted to read aloud
Because loud recitation wears out the mosque roof
Because every worshipper is conversing privately with his Lord, so they must not disturb or distract one another
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ heard Companions competing in volume while praying in the masjid, he reminded them to lower their voices out of mutual respect.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach regarding spitting inside the masjid (or toward the Qibla), and what is its expiation?
optionsEn: Spitting toward the Qibla is encouraged during hot weather
Its only expiation is sacrificing a camel
Spitting in the masjid is a sin, and burying or cleaning it up is its expiation
It carries no blame if done near the back pillars
explanationEn: He ﷺ personally scraped phlegm off the mosque wall and perfumed the spot, teaching believers to honor the cleanliness of Allah's houses.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ honor the humble woman (known as Umm Mihjan) who used to sweep and keep Masjid an-Nabawi clean after she passed away at night?
optionsEn: He named a new gate after her wealth
He forbade anyone else from sweeping the mosque
He ordered a marble dome built over her home
He asked why he wasn't informed, went to her grave, and led the funeral prayer over her
explanationEn: Her quiet, sincere service of cleaning the mosque earned such immense honor with Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.

questionEn: What instruction did the Prophet ﷺ give regarding neighborhood mosques in the narration of Aishah (RA)?
optionsEn: That masajid be built among neighborhoods and kept clean and perfumed
That masajid never be scented with incense
That neighborhood masajid remain locked except on Fridays
That only one single masjid exist per country
explanationEn: Building local houses of worship and maintaining their cleanliness and pleasant fragrance brings comfort and dignity to congregational worship.

questionEn: If someone carries arrows or sharp objects while passing through a masjid or gathering, what safety etiquette did the Prophet ﷺ command?
optionsEn: Test their sharpness against the wooden pillars
Leave them pointed outward along the carpet
Carry them unsheathed over the shoulder
Hold onto the sharp tips with one's hand so no Muslim is accidentally injured
explanationEn: Protecting fellow worshippers from physical harm inside the sanctuary reflects Islam's holistic care for life and safety.

questionEn: What practice of earlier nations did the Prophet ﷺ strictly forbid in his final days regarding graves and mosques?
optionsEn: Planting date palms outside a mosque courtyard
Praying Janazah outside the graveyard
Facing Makkah when praying inside any city
Taking the graves of prophets and righteous people as places of worship (masajid)
explanationEn: To safeguard pure Tawhid (monotheism), the Prophet ﷺ warned against building mosques over graves or praying toward them.

questionEn: Was sleeping or resting inside the masjid permissible during the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime when needed?
optionsEn: Only the Muezzin was permitted to sit or rest inside
Yes, for travelers, guests, or needy residents like the People of the Suffah and young single Companions
Only during the month of Muharram
No, anyone who fell asleep in the masjid had to leave Madinah
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) slept in the masjid in his youth, Ali (RA) rested there once, and the People of the Suffah resided in the shaded portico.

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, what did the Prophet ﷺ approve of Hassan ibn Thabit (RA) doing inside Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Reciting righteous poetry defending Islam and the Prophet ﷺ
Selling silk garments near the pulpit
Holding livestock auctions after Asr
Arguing loudly over tribal genealogy
explanationEn: Beneficial speech, learning, and defense of truth are welcome in the masjid, unlike idle chatter or worldly commerce.

questionEn: How does the reward of a single prayer in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi compare to a prayer in ordinary mosques around the world?
optionsEn: It is better than 1,000 prayers offered in other mosques, except Al-Masjid al-Haram
It is equal to 500 prayers, the exact same as Al-Masjid al-Haram
It is equal to 100 prayers everywhere
It is better than 10,000 prayers in Makkah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ declared: 'One prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque, except Al-Masjid al-Haram.'

questionEn: How does the reward of one prayer in Al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah compare to praying in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in Madinah?
optionsEn: 50 times greater than Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
Equal in numerical reward to Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
10 times greater than Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
100,000 times better than ordinary mosques, making it 100 times greater than Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated that one prayer in Al-Masjid al-Haram is superior to 100,000 prayers elsewhere, whereas Masjid an-Nabawi equals 1,000.

questionEn: What two authentic figures are reported in Hadith collections for the multiplied reward of one prayer in Al-Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem compared to ordinary mosques?
optionsEn: 500 times (in Ibn Majah/al-Bazzar) and 250 times (in Ahmad/al-Hakim, i.e., one-fourth of Masjid an-Nabawi)
1,000 times and 100,000 times
50 times and 10 times
10,000 times and 50,000 times
explanationEn: Abu Dharr (RA) narrated that prayer in the Prophet's ﷺ Mosque equals four prayers in Bayt al-Maqdis (250x), while another narration states 500x.

questionEn: What does the prophetic phrase 'La tushaddu ar-rihal' (Do not set out on a journey/saddle mounts) specifically prohibit?
optionsEn: Attending Islamic schools or conferences in other cities
Going to any local neighborhood masjid by car
Undertaking a special journey seeking the inherent sanctity of a place of worship except to the Three Sacred Masajid
Traveling by airplane or camel to visit relatives
explanationEn: Shadd al-Rihal means packing baggage for religious pilgrimage; Islam restricts sacred-site pilgrimage solely to Al-Masjid al-Haram, Masjid an-Nabawi, and Masjid al-Aqsa.

questionEn: Which mosque in Madinah offers the reward of performing an Umrah to anyone who purifies at home, goes there, and prays two rak'ahs?
optionsEn: Masjid Bilal
Masjid al-Qiblatayn
Masjid Quba
Masjid al-Ghamamah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ promised: 'Whoever purifies himself in his house, then comes to Masjid Quba and prays a prayer in it, will have a reward like that of an Umrah.'

questionEn: On which day of every week did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ regularly visit Masjid Quba, whether riding or walking?
optionsEn: Every Tuesday
Only on the first Sunday of Ramadan
Every Saturday
Every Wednesday
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ used to visit Masjid Quba every Saturday, riding or walking, and pray two rak'ahs there.

questionEn: In Surah At-Tawbah (9:108), which mosque is described as 'a masjid founded on righteousness (Taqwa) from the very first day'?
optionsEn: Masjid Dirar in Madinah
Masjid Quba (and the Prophet ﷺ affirmed Masjid an-Nabawi shares this attribute)
Masjid al-Khayf in Mina
Masjid al-Aqsa exclusively
explanationEn: While Surah 9:108 was revealed contrasting Masjid Quba with Masjid Dirar, the Prophet ﷺ also pointed to his own mosque in Madinah when asked about it.

questionEn: According to Abu Dharr (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari, which were the first and second mosques established on earth for the worship of Allah, and how many years separated them?
optionsEn: Al-Masjid an-Nabawi first, followed by Masjid Quba ten years later
Al-Masjid al-Haram first, followed by Al-Masjid al-Aqsa forty years later
Masjid Quba first, followed by Al-Masjid al-Haram forty years later
Al-Masjid al-Aqsa first, followed by Al-Masjid al-Haram seventy years later
explanationEn: When Abu Dharr (RA) asked which mosque was built first on earth, the Prophet ﷺ replied Al-Masjid al-Haram, then Al-Masjid al-Aqsa forty years later.

questionEn: What blessed area inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi did the Prophet ﷺ call 'a garden from the gardens of Paradise (Rawdah min Riyad al-Jannah)'?
optionsEn: The entire city wall surrounding Madinah
The space between his house (Aishah's chamber) and his pulpit (Minbar)
The roof of the northern courtyard
The outer steps of Bab al-Baqi
explanationEn: Praying and supplicating in Ar-Rawdah ash-Sharifah is deeply cherished by pilgrims visiting Madinah.

questionEn: What reward did the Prophet ﷺ promise to anyone who builds a masjid solely seeking the Face of Allah—even if it is as small as a sandgrouse's nest?
optionsEn: He is automatically made governor of that town
Allah will build for him a house like it in Paradise
He receives ten thousand gold dinars in this world
He is exempted from all future prayers
explanationEn: Whether one builds an entire mosque or contributes sincerely toward its construction, Allah builds a corresponding abode for them in Jannah.
