questionEn: According to Surah At-Tawbah (9:18), what four spiritual qualities characterize those worthy of maintaining and inhabiting Allah's mosques?
optionsEn: Being born in Makkah, speaking Arabic only, and building tall towers
Traveling constantly, trading spices, fasting daily, and writing poetry
Believing in Allah and the Last Day, establishing Salah, giving Zakah, and fearing none except Allah
Possessing vast palaces, high lineages, sharp swords, and silver coins
explanationEn: Surah At-Tawbah teaches that true stewardship of mosques is rooted in sincere faith, worship, charity, and awe of Allah alone.

questionEn: Who does Allah describe in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:114) as among the greatest of wrongdoers?
optionsEn: Those who wear simple sandals to the mosque courtyard
Those who arrive five minutes early to the masjid
Those who prevent Allah's name from being mentioned in His mosques and strive toward their ruin
Those who bring children quietly to pray
explanationEn: Barricading mosques or driving believers out from remembering Allah inside them is condemned severely in the Qur'an.

questionEn: What clear command did the Prophet ﷺ give to men regarding women requesting permission to attend the masjid?
optionsEn: 'Refuse them permission unless they bring a written permit'
'Allow them only at Dhuhr and forbid Fajr and Isha'
'Only allow women to attend once every Ramadan'
'Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from attending the mosques of Allah'
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) narrated this explicit Prophetic instruction safeguarding women's access to the houses of Allah.

questionEn: What etiquette condition did the Prophet ﷺ set when women go out to attend congregational prayers at the masjid?
optionsEn: They must bring incense burners into the street
They must pray ahead of the men's first row
They must go out without wearing perfume or alluring adornment
They must wear strong musk so others notice their arrival
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed: 'When any of you (women) witnesses Isha (or attends the masjid), let her not touch perfume that night,' preserving modesty and focus.

questionEn: Why did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) designate a specific entrance of Masjid an-Nabawi as 'Bab an-Nisa'' (The Women's Gate)?
optionsEn: Because women were barred from using the rest of the mosque roof
Implementing the Prophet's ﷺ wish that one door be reserved exclusively for women so men and women wouldn't crowd together at the exits
To store charity dates inside that archway
Because it was the only door facing south
explanationEn: After the Prophet ﷺ remarked 'How good it would be if we left this door for the women,' Ibn Umar narrated that he never entered through it again.

questionEn: How does the Prophet's ﷺ statement that 'a woman's prayer in her innermost room is better for her' harmonize with allowing women to attend the masjid?
optionsEn: It means women may only pray Jumu'ah at home
It applies solely to Makkah and nowhere else
It means women's prayers at the masjid are completely invalid
Praying at home offers greater reward and ease for women, yet if they wish to attend the masjid for congregation, learning, or spiritual uplift, husbands must not forbid them
explanationEn: Balancing both authentic Hadiths preserves both the ease of home worship and women's prophetic right to benefit from the masjid.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the best place to build and preserve one's connection with the masjid in any town?
optionsEn: Marketplaces and mosques carry identical spiritual status
The best place in town is wherever trade is loudest
The most beloved places to Allah in any land are its masajid, and the most disliked places are its marketplaces
Only mosques built of gold are beloved to Allah
explanationEn: Masajid are hubs of remembrance, sincerity, and brotherhood, whereas marketplaces often foster heedlessness and disputes.

questionEn: Which two prayers in Masjid al-Haram vs ordinary mosques highlight that multiplied reward in Makkah encompasses the entire sacred Haram boundary according to many scholars?
optionsEn: Only the Roof of Safa receives any reward
Many scholars (including Ibn Abbas, Ata', and Ahmad) hold the 100,000x reward covers all mosques within Makkah's Haram sanctuary, while Al-Masjid al-Haram itself remains supreme
Prayers outside the Kaaba wall get zero reward
The 100,000x reward applies only to Friday Fajr
explanationEn: The Qur'an often uses 'Al-Masjid al-Haram' for the entire sacred precinct of Makkah (e.g., 17:1), though praying directly around the Kaaba holds unmatched honor.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ command believers not to treat the masjid as merely a pedestrian walkway or shortcut without worshipping?
optionsEn: Because only Imams may cross from north to south
Because one should honor the house of Allah by at least praying two rak'ahs or remembering Allah if passing through regularly
Because walking through a masjid ruins the carpets
Because passing through cancels fasting
explanationEn: Treating a masjid merely as a thoroughfare strips it of reverence; greeting it with Tahiyyat al-Masjid or dhikr maintains its sanctity.

questionEn: Which mosque in Madinah is famously associated with the revelation changing the Qibla direction from Jerusalem to Makkah mid-prayer?
optionsEn: Masjid Quba
Masjid al-Jumu'ah
Masjid al-Ijabah
Masjid al-Qiblatayn (Mosque of the Two Qiblas)
explanationEn: Historically located in the Banu Salamah quarter, it commemorates the congregation turning mid-Salah toward the Kaaba upon receiving news of Surah 2:144.

questionEn: When entering a masjid carrying a bag or wearing dusty shoes in the Prophetic era, what hygiene check did the Prophet ﷺ teach?
optionsEn: Check the soles of one's shoes for impurity and wipe them clean before entering (or remove dirty footwear outside)
Throw one's shoes onto the courtyard roof
Always walk barefoot even on scorching rocks
Never wash sandals for an entire month
explanationEn: When Jibril (AS) informed the Prophet ﷺ of filth on his sandals during prayer, he removed them quietly—teaching utmost care for masjid purity.

questionEn: Is it permissible to eat simple, clean food (like dates or bread) or drink water inside a masjid without dirtying it, such as during I'tikaf or iftar?
optionsEn: Eating is forbidden in every mosque on Earth
No, drinking water inside a masjid invalidates prayer
Yes, provided one maintains cleanliness and avoids spilling crumbs or strong odors
Only dates from Madinah may ever be eaten indoors
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn al-Harith (RA) narrated: 'We used to eat bread and meat in the masjid during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,' while keeping it spotless.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when someone entered the masjid and immediately engaged in worldly idle talk or unsanctioned commotion, contrasting with what mosques are for?
optionsEn: That mosques are built for the remembrance of Allah, Salah, and recitation of Qur'an
That mosques exist mainly for sleeping through Dhuhr
That mosques are meant for debating politics daily
That mosques are built primarily for storing weapons
explanationEn: Keeping one's tongue engaged in dhikr, Qur'an, and quiet courtesy preserves the serene atmosphere of Allah's house.

questionEn: How should parents or elders respond when young children come to the masjid, following the example of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: Force children to stand outside in the heat
Ban all children under age twelve from ever entering
Welcome them gently and teach them mosque etiquette with kindness, just as the Prophet ﷺ carried Umamah and let Hasan and Husayn climb on him
Shout harshly at any child who whispers
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ held his granddaughter Umamah while leading prayer and shortened prayer when a baby cried, fostering love for the masjid in young hearts.

questionEn: What was the Masjid al-Jumu'ah in Madinah historically known for during the Prophet's ﷺ Hijrah?
optionsEn: It was built solely by Abu Bakr (RA) in Makkah
It was the mosque where Eid al-Adha was first prayed after Conquest of Makkah
It is located inside Cave Hira
It marks the site in Wadi Ranuna where the Prophet ﷺ led his very first Jumu'ah prayer upon arriving in Madinah
explanationEn: After staying in Quba, the Prophet ﷺ departed on Friday and led the first Madinan Jumu'ah in the valley of Banu Salim ibn Awf (Wadi Ranuna).

questionEn: Why does the Prophet ﷺ warn against sitting in circles inside the masjid before Jumu'ah prayer solely for idle chatter?
optionsEn: Because sitting in circles breaks Wudu automatically
Because talking before Jumu'ah cancels the Khutbah
Because the time before Jumu'ah is meant for quiet prayer, Qur'an, and dhikr rather than forming distracting social circles
Because only standing is allowed before Jumu'ah
explanationEn: Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrated that the Prophet ﷺ forbade sitting in Hilaq (study/chatter circles) inside the masjid on Friday before the prayer.

questionEn: What should a worshipper do when entering Al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah with the intention of performing Tawaf, instead of praying Tahiyyat al-Masjid first?
optionsEn: Refuse to perform Tawaf until praying four rak'ahs at Safa
Wait until midnight before entering the Mataf
Leave Al-Masjid al-Haram and pray at Masjid Quba first
Begin Tawaf directly, as Tawaf itself serves as the greeting of Al-Masjid al-Haram
explanationEn: Scholars agree that for one arriving to do Tawaf, Tawaf (followed by two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim) is the greeting of the Sacred Mosque; if not doing Tawaf, one prays two rak'ahs.

questionEn: What special etiquette applies when placing a Mushaf (copy of the Qur'an) down inside a masjid?
optionsEn: Place it on an elevated clean shelf or holder with care and reverence, never directly on the floor where feet pass
Lay it face-down open on the carpet walkway
Stack heavy shoes beside it
Leave it outside in the rain
explanationEn: Honoring the Mushaf as Allah's Speech is part of magnifying the sacred symbols of Allah (Surah Al-Hajj 22:32).

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach about a person who visits the masjid solely to learn good or teach good?
optionsEn: He is forbidden from listening unless he is over forty
He must pay a fee to the masjid caretaker
He receives a reward like that of a pilgrim who completed his Hajj
He receives half the reward of praying alone at home
explanationEn: Abu Umamah (RA) narrated that going to the masjid with no desire except to learn or teach goodness earns the reward of a complete Hajj.

questionEn: What is the etiquette when two people are already seated side-by-side in a masjid and a third person enters?
optionsEn: Do not squeeze between two seated companions without their permission, and do not force someone to give up their seat
Push between them immediately to claim the middle spot
Step over their shoulders to reach the front wall
Ask the younger one to stand outside
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught courtesy in gatherings: neither separate two people without consent nor displace anyone already seated.

questionEn: How does Surah An-Nur (24:36-37) describe the houses (masajid) that Allah has permitted to be raised and His name remembered therein?
optionsEn: Men glorify Him in them morning and evening—men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah and establishing Salah
They are built exclusively of red granite without windows
Only kings and poets may enter them after sunset
Commerce and bartering occur inside them every morning
explanationEn: Allah praises those whose hearts remain anchored in worship and charity inside His houses despite worldly responsibilities.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about how Allah welcomes the believer who regularly frequents the masjid?
optionsEn: Allah reduces his daily prayers from five to three
Allah prepares a feast of welcome (Nuzul) for him in Paradise every time he goes in the morning or evening
Allah gives him a physical gold coin under his mat
Allah excuses him from fasting in Shawwal
explanationEn: Abu Hurairah (RA) narrated: 'Whoever goes to the masjid in the morning or evening, Allah prepares for him an honorable welcome in Paradise every time he goes.'

questionEn: Which four momentous events in creation and cosmic history did the Prophet ﷺ mention as occurring on Friday (Yawm al-Jumu'ah)?
optionsEn: Nuh built the Ark, Ibrahim built Makkah, Musa crossed the sea, and Ramadan ended on it
Adam was created on it, entered Paradise on it, was sent down from it, and the Hour will be established on it
Only rain falls on it and markets open on it
The Qibla changed, Badr occurred, Uhud occurred, and Laylat al-Qadr fell on it
explanationEn: Calling Friday 'the best day on which the sun has risen,' the Prophet ﷺ highlighted these four pivotal events tied to Adam (AS) and the Last Day.

questionEn: What special blessing is hidden within Friday known as Sa'at al-Istijabah?
optionsEn: An hour when sleeping replaces Jumu'ah prayer
An hour when obligatory prayers become optional
A blessed hour during which no Muslim stands praying and asking Allah for good except Allah grants it to him
An hour when fasting is obligatory upon travelers
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ gestured with his hand to show this moment is brief and precious, encouraging constant dua throughout Friday.

questionEn: Which two specific time windows on Friday are identified by authentic Hadiths as the strongest candidates for the Hour of Response (Sa'at al-Istijabah)?
optionsEn: During the two hours immediately following sunrise
Between Fajr and sunrise only, and immediately after Isha
From when the Imam sits on the Minbar until the prayer concludes, and the final hour after Asr before sunset
Only at exact midnight on Thursday night
explanationEn: Sahih Muslim 853 specifies the time from the Imam sitting on the pulpit to the end of Salah, while Sunan Abi Dawud 1048 points to the last hour after Asr.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ urge Muslims to send abundant Salawat (blessings) upon him specifically on Friday?
optionsEn: Because Salawat cannot be recited on any other day
Because our Salawat are presented directly to him ﷺ on Friday
Because it exempts a person from paying Zakah
Because sending Salawat replaces reciting Al-Fatihah in Jumu'ah
explanationEn: When a Companion asked how his blessings would reach him after his passing, the Prophet ﷺ replied that Allah forbade the earth from consuming the bodies of prophets.

questionEn: What spiritual illumination is promised to the Muslim who recites Surah Al-Kahf on Friday?
optionsEn: A light (Nur) will shine for him from one Friday to the next Friday
He will automatically memorize the entire Qur'an overnight
Every tree in his yard turns green immediately
He does not need to pray Dhuhr on Saturday
explanationEn: Reciting Surah Al-Kahf every Friday nurtures faith against trials (fitan) and illuminates the believer's heart and path between Fridays.

questionEn: What special protection is mentioned in Jami' at-Tirmidhi for a believer who passes away on the day or night of Friday?
optionsEn: Allah protects him from the trial (Fitnah) of the grave
He is buried without a shroud
His family cannot inherit his property
No Janazah prayer is ever prayed for him
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) narrated that dying on Friday or Thursday night is a sign of good end, bringing protection from the questioning/trial of the grave.

questionEn: What spiritual cleansing occurs from one Jumu'ah prayer to the next according to Sahih Muslim?
optionsEn: They serve as expiation for the minor sins committed between them, so long as major sins are avoided
They erase all unpaid debts owed to people without repayment
They excuse missing Fajr for six days
They replace the obligation of Ramadan fasting
explanationEn: The five daily prayers, Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan continually purify the believer who stays away from major sins.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ describe the weekly spiritual status of Friday for the Muslim community?
optionsEn: 'It is a day of mourning on which joy is forbidden'
'It is an ordinary workday with no special rank'
'Indeed this day is a day of Eid (festival) that Allah has appointed for the Muslims'
'It is reserved only for scholars and governors'
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated this Hadith encouraging Muslims to bathe, wear clean garments, and celebrate Friday in gratitude and worship.

questionEn: What is the prophetic ruling on singling out Friday alone for voluntary fasting, or Thursday night (into Friday) alone for night prayer?
optionsEn: Staying awake all Friday night while sleeping through Fajr is recommended
Prohibited to single out Friday alone for fasting unless paired with Thursday or Saturday, and discouraged to single out Friday night alone for Qiyam
Voluntary fasting is allowed ONLY on Friday and forbidden on Mondays
Fasting every Friday alone is an obligatory pillar of Islam
explanationEn: Because Friday is a weekly day of Eid and communal worship, singling it out individually for fasting or night vigil is forbidden unless part of an existing routine.

questionEn: How strongly did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize taking a ritual bath (Ghusl) on Friday before attending Jumu'ah?
optionsEn: 'Ghusl on Friday is discouraged to conserve water'
'Only the Khatib is asked to perform Ghusl'
'Ghusl on Friday is only for travelers returning from Hajj'
'Ghusl on Friday is obligatory/incumbent (Wajib) upon every adult (Muhtalim)'
explanationEn: Taking Ghusl on Friday ensures physical purity and freshness in crowded congregations; scholars differ only on whether Wajib means strictly obligatory or deeply emphasized Sunnah.

questionEn: Alongside taking Ghusl on Friday, what two personal grooming Sunnahs did the Prophet ﷺ specifically encourage?
optionsEn: Shaving one's eyebrows and wearing wet clothes
Applying strong garlic paste and skipping shoes
Wearing unwashed work garments directly from the field
Using the Siwak (toothstick) and applying perfume/fragrance if available
explanationEn: Cleanliness of body, breath (Siwak), and pleasant fragrance (for men) honor the gathering of angels and believers at Jumu'ah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ advise regarding clothing for Jumu'ah if a Muslim can afford more than everyday work clothes?
optionsEn: To wear only animal hides
To wear torn garments to show poverty
To avoid washing garments on Thursday
To keep two special clean garments reserved specifically for Friday, separate from daily work clothes
explanationEn: When he saw people arriving dusty and sweaty from orchard work, he encouraged wearing clean, dignified attire dedicated to Jumu'ah.

questionEn: In the Hadith of early arrival on Friday, what sacrifice is the reward equal to for the person who arrives in the VERY FIRST hour?
optionsEn: Offering an egg
Sacrificing a horned ram
Sacrificing a camel (Badanah)
Sacrificing a cow (Baqarah)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ ranked the five early hours sequentially from greatest to smallest: camel, cow, horned ram, chicken, and egg.

questionEn: In the descending scale of Friday early arrival rewards, what corresponds to arriving in the second, third, fourth, and fifth hours respectively?
optionsEn: Ten dinars (2nd), five dinars (3rd), one dinar (4th), and a dirham (5th)
A cow (2nd), a horned ram (3rd), a chicken (4th), and an egg (5th)
A horse (2nd), a goat (3rd), a pigeon (4th), and a date (5th)
A horned ram (2nd), a cow (3rd), an egg (4th), and a chicken (5th)
explanationEn: Each earlier hour carries dramatically higher spiritual reward, motivating Muslims to leave worldly tasks early and hasten to the masjid.

questionEn: What do the angels stationed at the doors of the masjid recording arrivals do the moment the Imam comes out and mounts the Minbar on Friday?
optionsEn: They fold up their scrolls and sit down to listen to the Khutbah reminder
They lock the doors so latecomers cannot enter
They keep writing names until Maghrib
They depart immediately to another city
explanationEn: Arriving after the Imam ascends the pulpit still allows praying Jumu'ah validly, yet one misses the special early-arrival registry kept by the angels.

questionEn: What extraordinary reward is promised in Sunan Abi Dawud and Tirmidhi for every single step taken to Jumu'ah by one who washes properly, goes early, walks without riding, sits close to the Imam, and listens without idle talk?
optionsEn: The reward of a full year of fasting and standing in night prayer (Qiyam) for every step
Ten days of fasting for every hundred steps
One single Umrah regardless of distance
Exemption from praying Asr that afternoon
explanationEn: Aws ibn Aws (RA) narrated this astonishing Prophetic promise highlighting the unmatched value of preparing thoroughly and walking early to Jumu'ah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say while delivering the Khutbah to a man whom he saw stepping over people's necks and shoulders to push toward the front?
optionsEn: 'Stand outside in the sun for ten minutes'
'Keep stepping forward until you reach the Mihrab'
'Sit down, for you have harmed people (and come late)'
'Come up onto the Minbar beside me'
explanationEn: Arriving late does not justify inconveniencing seated worshippers; one should sit wherever space is respectfully available.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ forbid a latecomer from doing to obtain a spot during Jumu'ah prayer?
optionsEn: Making another Muslim stand up from his seat in order to sit in his place
Asking neighbors to gently make room
Sitting peacefully in an empty space in the back row
Spreading a clean prayer mat in the courtyard
explanationEn: He ﷺ commanded: 'None of you should make his brother get up from his seat on Friday and then sit in it; rather say: Make room and spread out.'

questionEn: What practical remedy did the Prophet ﷺ advise if a worshipper begins feeling drowsy in his seat while waiting or listening in the masjid on Friday?
optionsEn: Lie flat across the row and sleep through the Khutbah
Walk out of the masjid and skip Jumu'ah
Talk loudly with his neighbor to wake up
Change his seat and move to another spot
explanationEn: Standing up briefly to shift to a different place refreshes alertness and restores focus for the sermon and prayer.

questionEn: Which sitting posture—clasping one's hands or arms around drawn-up knees (Ihtiba')—did the Prophet ﷺ discourage while listening to the Friday Khutbah?
optionsEn: Kneeling gently on both knees
Sitting politely in the Tashahhud posture
Drawing the knees up to the chest and wrapping the arms around them (Ihtiba')
Sitting cross-legged attentively facing the Khatib
explanationEn: Ihtiba' during the Khutbah was discouraged because it easily induces sleepiness, risks uncovering the awrah in loose garments, or may lead to breaking Wudu.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Jumu'ah (62:9), what worldly activity must believers immediately pause when the call to Friday prayer is proclaimed?
optionsEn: Eating breakfast with one's family at dawn
Traveling between cities on Thursday
Sleeping after Fajr
Buying, selling, and commercial trade, hastening to the remembrance of Allah
explanationEn: Allah commands: 'When the call is proclaimed for prayer on Friday, hasten earnestly to the remembrance of Allah and leave off business.'

questionEn: After Jumu'ah prayer concludes, what balanced instruction does the very next verse (Surah Al-Jumu'ah 62:10) give?
optionsEn: 'Fast immediately without eating or drinking'
'Avoid all lawful work for the rest of the day'
'Remain locked inside the masjid until Monday morning'
'Disperse through the land, seek of the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah much that you may succeed'
explanationEn: Unlike religions that turn a sacred day into total idleness, Islam balances dedicated Friday worship with resuming lawful work afterward.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ structure the Friday Khutbah according to Abdullah ibn Umar (RA)?
optionsEn: He delivered three Khutbahs after the two rak'ahs of prayer
He delivered one single Khutbah while lying down
He delivered two Khutbahs standing, with a brief pause sitting down between them
He preached only while seated without ever standing
explanationEn: Standing for two sermons separated by a short seated pause remains the universal Sunnah of Jumu'ah.

questionEn: What miraculous event occurred in Masjid an-Nabawi when the Prophet ﷺ transitioned from leaning against a palm-tree trunk to preaching on a three-step wooden Minbar?
optionsEn: The Minbar walked on its own to Quba
The palm trunk wept and groaned like a pregnant she-camel until the Prophet ﷺ stepped down and embraced it to calm it
The roof of the mosque lifted into the sky
The palm trunk instantly sprouted fresh dates in winter
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated that the entire congregation heard the trunk crying out of longing for the remembrance of Allah it used to hear beside it.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say happens if a worshipper merely tells his talking neighbor 'Sah!' ('Be quiet!') while the Imam is delivering the Friday Khutbah?
optionsEn: He has engaged in idle speech (Laghw), which diminishes the full reward of his Jumu'ah
He becomes the deputy Imam for the rest of the day
He earns double reward for enforcing silence
He must restart his Wudu before the prayer
explanationEn: Silence during the Khutbah is so sacred that even shushing another person verbally counts as Laghw; one should signal silently with a gesture if needed.

questionEn: What seemingly harmless distraction during the Friday Khutbah did the Prophet ﷺ warn is 'Laghw' (idle distraction that spoils one's Jumu'ah perfection)?
optionsEn: Taking a deep breath silently
Looking directly toward the Khatib
Sitting upright against a pillar
Fiddling with pebbles (or small objects) on the floor
explanationEn: In the days when the mosque floor was gravel, playing with pebbles distracted the mind from the sermon; today, checking phones carries the same distraction.

questionEn: When Sulayk al-Ghatafani (RA) entered Masjid an-Nabawi while the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the Friday Khutbah and sat straight down, what did the Prophet ﷺ instruct him to do?
optionsEn: 'Remain seated immediately and do not stand'
'Stand up and pray two brief rak'ahs' (Tahiyyat al-Masjid)
'Pray four long rak'ahs of Dhuhr right there'
'Wait outside until the prayer starts'
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ paused to ask if Sulayk had prayed, then instructed him—and everyone entering during the Khutbah—to offer two quick rak'ahs before sitting.

questionEn: According to Ammar ibn Yasir (RA) in Sahih Muslim, what is a clear sign of a speaker's sound understanding (Fiqh) in leading Jumu'ah?
optionsEn: Skipping the second Khutbah entirely
Speaking in cryptic riddles no one understands
Lengthening the prayer (Salah) and keeping the sermon (Khutbah) concise and impactful
Delivering a two-hour Khutbah followed by a two-minute prayer
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ praised clear, focused sermons that touch the heart without exhausting the congregation before prayer.

questionEn: When making Dua during the regular Friday Khutbah on the Minbar, what hand gesture was the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: Covering his face with both palms
Pointing with the index finger of his right hand (rather than raising both hands high, which was reserved for Istisqa' rain prayers)
Clapping both hands together loudly
Raising both arms until his armpits showed every Friday
explanationEn: Umarah ibn Ru'aybah (RA) noticed the Prophet ﷺ did not raise both hands in normal Friday Khutbahs, only pointing with his forefinger, except during Istisqa'.

questionEn: Which Rightly Guided Caliph introduced the earlier first Adhan for Jumu'ah at Az-Zawra' in the Madinah marketplace as the city expanded?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)
Uthman ibn Affan (RA)
Umar ibn Abdil-Aziz
explanationEn: During the Prophet's ﷺ time and the caliphates of Abu Bakr and Umar, there was one Adhan when the Imam sat on the Minbar; Uthman (RA) added the earlier call to alert distant merchants.

questionEn: Toward whom does the Khatib face while delivering the Friday Khutbah?
optionsEn: Walking down the center aisle
Facing the Qibla wall with his back to the people
Directly toward the congregation sitting in front of the Minbar
Facing strictly west regardless of where the people sit
explanationEn: Unlike Salah where everyone faces the Qibla, the Khatib faces the worshippers during the Khutbah and they turn their attention toward him.

questionEn: Which pair of Surahs did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ consistently recite in the Fajr prayer on Friday morning?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Jumu'ah (62) and Surah Al-Munafiqun (63)
Surah Al-Kahf (18) and Surah Maryam (19)
Surah Al-Kawthar (108) and Surah Al-Ikhlas (112)
Surah As-Sajdah (32) in the first rak'ah and Surah Al-Insan / Ad-Dahr (76) in the second rak'ah
explanationEn: Both Abu Hurairah and Ibn Abbas (RA) reported this consistent Sunnah for Friday Fajr, as these surahs recount creation, human purpose, and the Resurrection.

questionEn: What spiritual reason do scholars like Ibn al-Qayyim highlight for why the Prophet ﷺ recited Surah As-Sajdah and Surah Al-Insan specifically in Friday Fajr?
optionsEn: Because neither Surah contains a prostration of recitation
Because they forbid praying in congregation
Both Surahs mention the creation of Adam (AS) and the events of the Resurrection—which both belong to Friday
Because they are the shortest two Surahs in the Qur'an
explanationEn: Reciting these two Surahs every Friday dawn reminds believers of their origin in Adam, their accountability, and the Final Day that will begin on a Friday.

questionEn: Which two pairs of Surahs did the Prophet ﷺ most frequently recite aloud in the two rak'ahs of the Jumu'ah prayer itself?
optionsEn: As-Sajdah (32) & Al-Insan (76)
Al-Jumu'ah (62) & Al-Munafiqun (63), OR Al-A'la (87) & Al-Ghashiyah (88)
Al-Baqarah (2) & Aal-Imran (3)
An-Nas (114) & Al-Falaq (113)
explanationEn: Authentic narrations in Sahih Muslim preserve both pairs—sometimes reciting Al-Jumu'ah and Al-Munafiqun, and other times Al-A'la and Al-Ghashiyah (often also recited in Eid).

questionEn: How many obligatory (Fard) rak'ahs are prayed in Salat al-Jumu'ah, and how is the Qur'an recited in them?
optionsEn: Three rak'ahs, just like Maghrib
Two rak'ahs, recited silently in the first and aloud in the second
Four rak'ahs, recited silently like Dhuhr
Two rak'ahs, recited aloud by the Imam
explanationEn: Jumu'ah replaces the four silent rak'ahs of Dhuhr with two Khutbahs followed by two aloud congregational rak'ahs.

questionEn: What Sunnah prayers did the Prophet ﷺ teach and practice AFTER completing the Jumu'ah prayer?
optionsEn: Six rak'ahs strictly in the middle of the street
Four rak'ahs if praying the Sunnah in the masjid, or two rak'ahs if praying at home
Zero voluntary prayers are permitted after Jumu'ah
Twelve rak'ahs standing on one foot
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed: 'When any of you finishes Jumu'ah, let him pray four after it' (Sahih Muslim 881), while Ibn Umar narrated the Prophet ﷺ prayed two at home (Bukhari 937).

questionEn: What should a worshipper do after finishing the two Fard rak'ahs of Jumu'ah before beginning the post-Jumu'ah Sunnah prayer in the masjid?
optionsEn: Wait until after Maghrib before praying Sunnah
Leave the mosque without ever praying Sunnah
Start the Sunnah immediately without saying Salam
Separate the Fard from the Sunnah by speaking briefly or shifting places slightly
explanationEn: Mu'awiyah (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ commanded not to join a Sunnah prayer directly to the obligatory prayer without speaking or moving aside.

questionEn: Is there a fixed number of Sunnah Mu'akkadah rak'ahs specifically prescribed BEFORE Jumu'ah, or what did the Prophet ﷺ encourage upon arriving early?
optionsEn: Exactly ten rak'ahs during the Khutbah itself
Only one single rak'ah of Witr
Nothing at all may be prayed before Jumu'ah under any condition
Open voluntary prayers (two by two) as much as Allah wills until the Imam ascends the Minbar
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever bathes and comes early 'prays whatever is decreed for him, then listens silently when the Imam speaks,' without fixing a specific Qabliyyah number.

questionEn: According to the Hadith in Sunan Abi Dawud (1067), which four categories of Muslims are excused from the obligation of attending Jumu'ah?
optionsEn: Every merchant, every student, every soldier, and every farmer
All men over forty years old
An enslaved person, a woman, a young child, and a sick person
Anyone who prayed Fajr in congregation
explanationEn: Jumu'ah is obligatory in congregation upon every free, adult, sane, resident, healthy Muslim man; those excused pray Dhuhr instead (or attend Jumu'ah voluntarily).

questionEn: Is attending Jumu'ah obligatory upon a traveler (Musafir) who is on the road?
optionsEn: Yes, every traveler must halt flights and trains to pray Jumu'ah
A traveler is forbidden from entering any mosque on Friday
No, Jumu'ah is not obligatory upon a traveler (the Prophet ﷺ prayed Dhuhr and Asr at Arafah on a Friday), though if he attends it with residents it is valid
A traveler must pray eight rak'ahs instead of four
explanationEn: During the Farewell Pilgrimage, Arafah fell on a Friday, and the Prophet ﷺ combined Dhuhr and Asr rather than holding Jumu'ah—proving travelers are excused.

questionEn: What frightening spiritual consequence did the Prophet ﷺ warn awaits a man who misses three consecutive Jumu'ah prayers out of negligence without a valid excuse?
optionsEn: He must perform Hajj three times in a row
He is forbidden from ever praying Fajr again
His wealth immediately disappears
Allah places a seal (Tab') over his heart
explanationEn: Deliberately abandoning three Fridays out of carelessness hardens the heart and blocks spiritual light, underscoring Jumu'ah's vital weekly obligation.

questionEn: If someone misses Jumu'ah prayer entirely due to oversleeping, illness, or arriving after the prayer ended, how must he make it up?
optionsEn: By praying four rak'ahs of Dhuhr (cannot pray Jumu'ah alone)
By giving a Khutbah to himself in his living room
By praying two aloud rak'ahs of Jumu'ah alone at home
By skipping Dhuhr and waiting until Asr
explanationEn: Jumu'ah requires a congregation and Khutbah; anyone excused or who misses it prays the regular four rak'ahs of Dhuhr.

questionEn: When did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ usually pray the Jumu'ah prayer according to Anas ibn Malik (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari?
optionsEn: Half an hour before Maghrib
At midnight before Saturday
Immediately at sunrise
When the sun passed its midday zenith (Zawal), matching the entry of Dhuhr time
explanationEn: The majority of scholars require Zawal to begin Jumu'ah, though the Hanbali school permits it slightly earlier in the morning before noon based on certain Companion reports.

questionEn: What concession (Rukhsah) did the Prophet ﷺ grant when an Eid day coincided with a Friday?
optionsEn: Whoever attended the Eid prayer was permitted a concession not to attend Jumu'ah (praying Dhuhr instead), though the Imam still established Jumu'ah for those who wished to attend
Eid prayer was permanently canceled that year
Both Eid and Dhuhr were skipped entirely
Only women were required to attend Jumu'ah
explanationEn: This mercy eased travel for rural worshippers who had already come into town in the morning for Eid, while keeping Jumu'ah open for residents.

questionEn: What physical act is recommended upon coming back home or leaving after Jumu'ah if someone previously could not afford perfume—and what did the Prophet ﷺ say about borrowing or applying fragrance on Friday?
optionsEn: Fragrance is allowed only on Wednesdays
One must bathe in olive oil before stepping out
Using any scent on Friday is strictly haram
Even applying a touch of one's family's perfume (excluding women's scented products with distracting color/effect) is part of honoring Friday cleanliness
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged every adult man attending Jumu'ah to bathe, use Siwak, and apply fragrance from whatever is available at home.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ advise regarding the Khatib's voice and delivery style during the Friday Khutbah according to Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA)?
optionsEn: His eyes would redden, his voice would rise, and his earnestness intensified as if warning an army of an approaching danger
He whispered softly so only the first two individuals could hear
He read strictly from a book without looking at the people
He sang rhythmic songs before starting
explanationEn: The Prophet's ﷺ Khutbahs were deeply heartfelt, stirring Taqwa and reminding believers of Allah, the Qur'an, and the Hereafter.

questionEn: Which opening praise and reminder did the Prophet ﷺ regularly begin his Friday Khutbahs with?
optionsEn: Asking every attendee to stand and introduce himself
Reciting Surah Al-Fatihah silently three times
Khutbat al-Hajah ('Innal-hamda lillahi nahmaduhu wa nasta'inuhu...'), followed by 'Amma ba'du: the best speech is the Book of Allah and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad ﷺ'
Counting the number of rows before speaking
explanationEn: Beginning sermons by praising Allah, bearing witness to Tawhid and Risalah, and warning against religious innovations sets the spiritual anchor for Jumu'ah.

questionEn: When a Muslim enters the masjid on Friday during the Khutbah and wishes to pray the two brief rak'ahs of Tahiyyat al-Masjid, what should he ensure about their length?
optionsEn: Skip Al-Fatihah to finish in five seconds
Keep them brief and concise so he can quickly sit down and listen to the Khutbah
Recite Surah Al-Baqarah in full before sitting
Pray four long rak'ahs slowly
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ explicitly told Sulayk al-Ghatafani: 'Pray two rak'ahs, and make them brief (tajawaz fihima),' balancing greeting the mosque with listening to the sermon.

questionEn: Which Surah of the Qur'an explicitly grants travelers permission to shorten their prayers when journeying through the earth?
optionsEn: Surah An-Nisa (4:101)
Surah Al-Maidah (5:6)
Surah Al-Anfal (8:41)
Surah Al-Hajj (22:27)
explanationEn: In Surah An-Nisa (4:101), Allah states that when you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer.

questionEn: How did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ describe the concession of shortening prayer (Qasr) during travel when asked why Muslims still shorten it in times of safety?
optionsEn: It is an optional penalty for leaving home
It is a charity (Sadaqah) that Allah has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity
It is restricted strictly to wartime expeditions
It is only permitted for journeys longer than one month
explanationEn: When Umar ibn al-Khattab asked about shortening prayers in peacetime, the Prophet ﷺ replied that Qasr is a charity from Allah that believers should gratefully accept.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Ya'la ibn Umayyah)

questionEn: Which daily obligatory prayers are shortened from four rak'ahs to two during travel (Qasr)?
optionsEn: Fajr, Dhuhr, and Maghrib
All five daily obligatory prayers
Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha
Only Dhuhr and Asr
explanationEn: Only the four-rak'ah obligatory prayers—Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha—are shortened to two rak'ahs during travel, while Fajr remains two and Maghrib remains three.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Book of Travelers' Prayer)

questionEn: What is the minimum travel distance (roughly four burud) cited by early Companions like Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas for shortening prayers?
optionsEn: Approximately 12 kilometers (about 7.5 miles)
Approximately 25 kilometers (about 15 miles)
Approximately 160 kilometers (about 100 miles)
Approximately 80–85 kilometers (about 48–50 miles)
explanationEn: Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas would shorten prayers and break fasts on journeys of four burud, equal to 16 farsakhs or roughly 80–85 kilometers according to the majority of jurists.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Mu'allaq report in Book of Shortening Prayer)

questionEn: At what point in a journey does a traveler begin shortening four-rak'ah prayers according to the Sunnah?
optionsEn: After leaving the built-up limits of their city or town
While still packing bags inside their home
Only after arriving at the destination city
After passing three different towns along the road
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik reported that the Prophet ﷺ prayed Dhuhr as four rak'ahs in Madinah and then prayed Asr as two rak'ahs after reaching Dhul-Hulayfah outside the city.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Anas ibn Malik)

questionEn: When the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ stayed in Makkah during the Conquest without intending permanent residence, for how many days did he continue shortening his prayers?
optionsEn: 3 days
19 days
7 days
40 days
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ stayed in Makkah for nineteen days during the Conquest, praying two rak'ahs throughout because he had not settled as a resident.

questionEn: During the Farewell Pilgrimage, how did the Prophet ﷺ lead the four-rak'ah prayers while camped in Mina?
optionsEn: He prayed them in full four rak'ahs and combined them all
He prayed them individually in each tent
He shortened Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha to two rak'ahs at their respective times
He omitted Dhuhr and prayed only Asr
explanationEn: In Mina during Hajj, the Prophet ﷺ—and after him Abu Bakr and Umar—prayed Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha as two rak'ahs each, shortened without combining them.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Ibn Umar)

questionEn: If a traveler joins a congregation led by a resident Imam praying Dhuhr in full (four rak'ahs), what must the traveler do?
optionsEn: Leave the congregation after two rak'ahs with Taslim
Sit quietly during the third and fourth rak'ahs without standing
Wait until the Imam finishes and pray only two rak'ahs alone
Complete all four rak'ahs behind the resident Imam
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas stated that it is the Sunnah for a traveler praying behind a resident Imam to pray four rak'ahs in full, following the Imam.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Musa ibn Salamah from Ibn Abbas)

questionEn: When a resident Imam or congregant prays behind a traveling Imam who finishes Qasr after two rak'ahs, what should the resident do?
optionsEn: Stand up after the Imam's Taslim and complete the remaining two rak'ahs
End the prayer with the Imam at two rak'ahs
Repeat the entire four-rak'ah prayer from the beginning
Join only from the Imam's second rak'ah
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ led the people of Makkah in two rak'ahs, he instructed the residents to complete their prayer because his group were travelers.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Narrated by Imran ibn Husayn)

questionEn: What is the term for combining Asr forward into the time of Dhuhr, or Isha forward into the time of Maghrib?
optionsEn: Jam' Ta'khir
Jam' Taqdim
Qasr al-Wajib
Talfiq as-Salah
explanationEn: Jam' Taqdim means advancing the second prayer (Asr or Isha) to offer it together with the first prayer (Dhuhr or Maghrib) during the first prayer's time.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Book of Travelers' Prayer)

questionEn: What is the term for delaying Dhuhr to pray it with Asr during Asr time, or delaying Maghrib to pray it with Isha during Isha time?
optionsEn: Jam' Taqdim
Qasr al-Mutlaq
Jam' Ta'khir
Jam' as-Suri
explanationEn: Jam' Ta'khir means delaying the earlier prayer of a pair (Dhuhr or Maghrib) until the time of the later prayer (Asr or Isha) enters, then praying both together.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Anas ibn Malik)

questionEn: Which two pairs of daily obligatory prayers are permissible to combine during travel?
optionsEn: Fajr with Dhuhr, and Asr with Maghrib
Only Maghrib with Isha, never Dhuhr with Asr
All five prayers into a single midday gathering
Dhuhr with Asr, and Maghrib with Isha
explanationEn: The Sunnah permits combining Dhuhr with Asr and Maghrib with Isha; Fajr cannot be combined with Dhuhr, nor can Asr be combined with Maghrib.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Ibn Umar & Mu'adh)

questionEn: When combining Dhuhr and Asr at Arafah during Hajj, how did the Prophet ﷺ arrange the Adhan and Iqamah?
optionsEn: One Adhan and two separate Iqamahs (one for Dhuhr, one for Asr)
Two Adhans and one Iqamah
One Adhan and one combined Iqamah for both
Neither Adhan nor Iqamah was called
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated that at Arafah, Bilal called one Adhan and then an Iqamah for Dhuhr, followed by a second Iqamah for Asr without praying anything between them.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Hadith of Jabir on the Farewell Pilgrimage)

questionEn: At Muzdalifah on the night after leaving Arafah, which combination of prayers did the Prophet ﷺ perform?
optionsEn: Jam' Taqdim of Maghrib and Isha before sunset
Jam' Ta'khir of Maghrib (3 rak'ahs) and Isha (2 rak'ahs) upon arrival at Isha time
Maghrib alone followed by Fajr before dawn
Shortening Maghrib to two rak'ahs and praying Isha in full
explanationEn: Upon reaching Muzdalifah during Isha time, the Prophet ﷺ prayed Maghrib (3 rak'ahs) and Isha (2 rak'ahs) together with one Adhan and two Iqamahs.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Usamah ibn Zayd & Jabir)

questionEn: When praying Jam' Ta'khir of Maghrib and Isha in Muzdalifah, how many rak'ahs is Maghrib prayed?
optionsEn: Two rak'ahs, because it is shortened during travel
One rak'ah joined with Witr
Three rak'ahs in full, as Maghrib is never shortened
Four rak'ahs to match Isha
explanationEn: Maghrib is always three rak'ahs whether at home or traveling; only four-rak'ah prayers (Dhuhr, Asr, Isha) are shortened to two.

questionEn: According to the practice of the Prophet ﷺ reported by Anas ibn Malik, how did he decide between Jam' Taqdim and Jam' Ta'khir while actively traveling?
optionsEn: He always prayed Jam' Taqdim regardless of departure time
He never combined prayers unless it rained
He waited until the next morning to make up missed prayers
If the sun passed midday before departing, he prayed Dhuhr (or combined Taqdim) before riding; if departing before midday, he delayed Dhuhr to Asr time
explanationEn: Anas narrated that when the Prophet ﷺ set out before the sun passed its zenith, he delayed Dhuhr until Asr time and combined them; if the sun had already passed its zenith, he prayed before mounting.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Anas ibn Malik)

questionEn: Which regular Sunnah (Rawatib) prayers did the Prophet ﷺ consistently maintain even while traveling and shortening his obligatory prayers?
optionsEn: The two Sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr and the Witr prayer
The four Sunnah rak'ahs before and after Dhuhr
The two Sunnah rak'ahs after Maghrib and Isha
All twelve daily Rawatib without exception
explanationEn: Ibn al-Qayyim and Aisha/Ibn Umar's reports clarify that the Prophet ﷺ dropped the regular Rawatib of Dhuhr, Maghrib, and Isha on journeys while faithfully keeping the Fajr Sunnah and Witr.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Ibn Umar & Aisha)

questionEn: What did Abdullah ibn Umar reply when someone asked why he did not pray voluntary Sunnah rak'ahs right after shortened obligatory prayers on a journey?
optionsEn: "Voluntary prayers are forbidden outside Madinah"
"Had I wanted to pray voluntary rak'ahs after them, I would have completed the obligatory prayer in full"
"Only the Imam is allowed to pray Sunnah while traveling"
"Sunnah prayers require standing on stationary ground for an hour"
explanationEn: Ibn Umar explained that he accompanied the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman on travels and none of them added Rawatib before or after shortened obligatory prayers (aside from Fajr Sunnah, Witr, and general nafl on a mount).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Hafs ibn Asim from Ibn Umar)

questionEn: When offering voluntary (nafl) prayers while riding a mount or traveling in a vehicle, how did the Prophet ﷺ handle the Qibla direction?
optionsEn: He stopped the mount for every single voluntary rak'ah
He forbade any voluntary prayer while riding
He prayed facing whichever direction his mount was heading, nodding for ruku' and sujud
He only prayed while facing backward on the saddle
explanationEn: Amir ibn Rabi'ah and Ibn Umar narrated that the Prophet ﷺ used to pray voluntary prayers (including Witr) on his mount in whatever direction it traveled, though he dismounted for obligatory prayers.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Ibn Umar)

questionEn: How does a person praying a voluntary prayer on a moving mount or airplane seat perform bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujud) when unable to descend?
optionsEn: By reciting the words without any physical movement
By standing up in the aisle for sujud only
By making the ruku' nod deeper than the sujud nod
By inclining the head/torso (ima'), making the nod for sujud lower than that for ruku'
explanationEn: When praying seated on a mount or while physically unable to prostrate on the floor, one gestures with the head/upper body, lowering more deeply for sujud than for ruku'.
reference: Jami' at-Tirmidhi & Sunan Abi Dawud (Narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah)

questionEn: What is the general rule for an obligatory (Fard) prayer on a journey regarding facing the Qibla and standing?
optionsEn: One must face the Qibla and stand if able—stopping the vehicle if possible, or facing Qibla aboard a ship or plane
One may face any random direction for obligatory prayers whenever riding
Obligatory prayers are postponed until the traveler arrives home days later
One only needs to face the Qibla during the final Taslim
explanationEn: Unlike voluntary prayers on a mount, obligatory prayers require facing the Qibla and standing if one has the ability; aboard ships, trains, or planes where stopping is impossible, one faces the Qibla as best as possible and stands if safe.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Narrated by Jabir) & Al-Hakim (Ship Prayer Hadith)

questionEn: If a resident in town joins a mosque during heavy rain or mud, what concession did Ibn Abbas narrate the Prophet ﷺ practiced in Madinah?
optionsEn: Shortening Dhuhr to one rak'ah at home
Combining Dhuhr with Asr, or Maghrib with Isha, to spare the community hardship
Praying silently in place of Jumu'ah
Delaying all five prayers until the rain stopped the next day
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ once combined Dhuhr and Asr, and Maghrib and Isha, in Madinah without fear or travel, explaining he wanted not to put his Ummah to undue hardship.

questionEn: Does combining prayers (Jam') due to rain or hardship in one's hometown also allow shortening (Qasr) four-rak'ah prayers to two?
optionsEn: Yes, combining always requires shortening to two rak'ahs
Yes, but only for Maghrib and Fajr
No, shortening (Qasr) is strictly for travel, so prayers combined at home are prayed in full
Only if the Imam is a traveler
explanationEn: Scholars agree that Qasr (shortening 4 rak'ahs to 2) is linked specifically to travel, whereas combining without travel (such as for severe rain or illness) keeps Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha at four rak'ahs each.

questionEn: What sequence of postures did the Prophet ﷺ prescribe to Imran ibn Husayn when praying while ill?
optionsEn: Pray sitting first, then standing if feeling better, then omit prayer if lying down
Pray only by heart without movement until fully healed
Delay all prayers until recovery and make them up together
Pray standing; if unable, then sitting; if unable, then lying on your side
explanationEn: When Imran ibn Husayn suffered from hemorrhoids and asked about praying, the Prophet ﷺ taught the golden rule: 'Pray standing; if you are not able, then sitting; and if you are not able, then upon your side.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Narrated by Imran ibn Husayn)

questionEn: If an ill person is able to stand for the opening Takbir and recitation, yet cannot bow or prostrate on the floor, how should they pray?
optionsEn: Stand for recitation as able, then sit and gesture for ruku' and sujud
Remain seated from the very start even though standing is easy
Skip the recitation and only say Takbir
Face away from the Qibla while leaning on a wall
explanationEn: In Salah, each pillar that a believer is physically able to perform remains obligatory, so one stands if able and only transitions to sitting or gesturing for the movements one cannot perform.
reference: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:286 & Sahih al-Bukhari (Imran ibn Husayn Hadith)

questionEn: When an ill person must pray lying on their side, which side and orientation are preferred according to the Sunnah and jurists?
optionsEn: Lying flat on the stomach facing downward
Lying on the right side with the body and face turned toward the Qibla
Lying on the left side facing away from the Qibla
Sitting upright against a door regardless of direction
explanationEn: Just as the deceased is placed in the grave on the right side facing the Qibla, praying on the right side facing the Qibla is preferred; if that is difficult, lying on the left side or on the back with feet toward the Qibla is permitted.
reference: An-Nasa'i & Fiqh Consensus based on Imran ibn Husayn Hadith

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ instruct when visiting a sick Companion who had placed a pillow in front of him to prostrate upon?
optionsEn: He praised using a high pillow for every prayer
He told him to raise a wooden board to his forehead instead
He removed the pillow and told him to pray by nodding on the ground or lowering his head without lifting an object to his face
He ordered him to stop praying until he recovered
explanationEn: Jabir narrated that the Prophet ﷺ saw a sick man praying on a pillow, threw it aside, and instructed him to pray on the earth if able, or otherwise gesture with his head, making sujud lower than ruku'.
reference: Sunan al-Bayhaqi & At-Tabarani (Authenticated from Jabir ibn Abdullah)

questionEn: If a sick person is completely paralyzed and cannot even move their head to nod for ruku' and sujud, how do they pray as long as their mind is conscious?
optionsEn: They are completely excused from prayer until cured
Someone else prays the rak'ahs on their behalf
They pay Fidyah charity instead of praying
They pray with their heart and intention, reciting verbally or mentally and moving eyes if able
explanationEn: Prayer is never waived as long as a Muslim retains consciousness and reason; one unable to move limbs or head prays by heart, tongue, and intention.
reference: Surah At-Taghabun 64:16 ('Fear Allah as much as you are able')

questionEn: Why does Islam allow a chronically or severely ill person to combine Dhuhr with Asr and Maghrib with Isha?
optionsEn: To remove hardship when making Wudu and preparing for five separate prayer times causes significant difficulty
Because illness automatically turns the five prayers into three
To allow shortening every prayer to one rak'ah
Only if the sick person is traveling outside their city
explanationEn: Based on the Hadith of Ibn Abbas—that the Prophet ﷺ combined prayers to remove hardship from his Ummah—and the case of women with chronic bleeding (istihadah), scholars permit the ill to combine prayers when separating them is burdensome.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Ibn Abbas) & Sunan Abi Dawud (Hamnah bint Jahsh)

questionEn: When a traveler begins a journey AFTER the time of Dhuhr has entered while still at home, and has not yet prayed Dhuhr, how should they pray Dhuhr once outside the city?
optionsEn: They cannot pray Dhuhr at all until returning home
Many scholars permit praying it as two rak'ahs (Qasr) once they are an active traveler, as the time is still active
They must pray Dhuhr as six rak'ahs
They must combine it with Fajr instead
explanationEn: According to the majority of jurists (Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanafi), what determines Qasr is the person's state at the moment of performing the prayer; once validly traveling outside city limits, they may shorten Dhuhr.
reference: Al-Mughni & Al-Majmu' (Classical Fiqh on Entering Travel)

questionEn: If a traveler remembers on the journey a four-rak'ah prayer they forgot to pray while still a resident at home, how do many jurists advise making it up?
optionsEn: Make it up as one rak'ah
Skip it entirely because travel erases missed resident prayers
Pray it in full (four rak'ahs), since it became due while at home
Pray it as two rak'ahs and give charity
explanationEn: Because the prayer became an obligation upon the person while residing at home in full, the majority of jurists hold it should be made up in full (four rak'ahs).
reference: Al-Mughni of Ibn Qudamah (Qada of Resident Prayer on Journey)

questionEn: If a traveler forgets a prayer while traveling and only remembers it after returning home as a resident, how should they make it up?
optionsEn: Wait until their next journey to pray it
Pray two rak'ahs because it was missed while traveling
Add it to Witr at night
According to Hanbali and Shafi'i jurists, pray four rak'ahs in full because the concession of travel has ended upon returning home
explanationEn: Once a traveler returns home, the status of residency returns; thus many jurists require making up the missed four-rak'ah prayer in full (while Hanafis look to the state when it became due).
reference: Al-Mughni & Al-Majmu' (Qada of Traveler's Prayer at Home)

questionEn: When offering Jam' Taqdim (combining Dhuhr and Asr during Dhuhr time), what condition helps ensure valid combination according to the majority of scholars?
optionsEn: Intending to combine, praying Dhuhr before Asr in order, and praying them consecutively without a long worldly break
Waiting two full hours between Dhuhr and Asr
Praying Asr first and Dhuhr second
Offering four Sunnah rak'ahs between Dhuhr and Asr
explanationEn: In Jam' Taqdim, the traveler observes the sequence (Dhuhr then Asr), intends the combination, and joins them consecutively without separating them with Sunnah prayers or unrelated activity.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Jabir's Hadith at Arafah) & Fiqh of Jam'

questionEn: When a traveler stops in a city with the intention of staying for an indefinite period (not knowing when their business will finish, such as waiting for weather or paperwork), what is their ruling regarding Qasr?
optionsEn: They become a permanent resident after exactly 24 hours
They remain a traveler and may shorten prayers until they resolve to stay beyond the residency threshold or depart
They must stop praying until they return home
They are forbidden from praying in local mosques
explanationEn: Ibn Umar stayed in Azerbaijan for six months waiting out snow while shortening his prayers, because he did not have a settled intention to reside permanently.
reference: Sunan al-Bayhaqi (Authentic report of Ibn Umar in Azerbaijan)

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ do regarding prayer when traveling on a camel during the night toward Khaybar or other expeditions, if he wanted to pray voluntary night prayers (Witr/Tahajjud)?
optionsEn: He stopped the entire caravan for every two rak'ahs
He omitted Witr completely while traveling
He prayed voluntary night prayers and Witr atop his camel facing whichever way it walked
He prayed Witr only after sunrise
explanationEn: Ibn Umar narrated that the Prophet ﷺ prayed Witr and voluntary prayers on his camel regardless of the direction it faced, though he never prayed obligatory prayers upon it.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Ibn Umar)

questionEn: If a sick person praying in a seated position is physically capable of sitting cross-legged (tarabbu') vs sitting in iftirash, what did the Sunnah report regarding how the Prophet ﷺ sat when praying seated?
optionsEn: He forbade sitting on the floor and required a tall chair
He required standing on one foot
He required lying down immediately
Aisha reported seeing him pray seated cross-legged (mutarabbi'an)
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) narrated that she saw the Prophet ﷺ praying seated cross-legged (mutarabbi'an), though any comfortable seated posture—including on a chair if floor-sitting is painful—is permissible.

questionEn: When an ill person prays seated on a chair because they cannot bend their knees to sit on the floor, where should the chair be placed in a congregational row?
optionsEn: Aligned so that their body (or the back legs) matches the row cleanly without blocking the person behind them
Always three meters ahead of the Imam
Outside the mosque doors in the street
Directly in front of the Mihrab
explanationEn: Aligning the chair thoughtfully with the row—especially aligning the shoulders when standing or back legs when seated throughout—preserves straight rows and avoids crowding others' prostration space.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Book of Adhan: Straightening Rows)

questionEn: What special reward does a believer receive when illness prevents them from performing the full standing prayers or voluntary worship they used to do when healthy?
optionsEn: Only half the reward of their normal worship
Allah writes for them the full reward of the good deeds they habitually performed when healthy and at home
They must make up the difference with extra fasting
No reward is recorded until they stand again
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ gave the comforting glad tiding: 'When a servant falls ill or travels, Allah writes for him the like of what he used to do when healthy and resident.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Narrated by Abu Musa al-Ash'ari)

questionEn: If a person begins an obligatory prayer standing, then suddenly feels faint or weak mid-prayer, what should they do?
optionsEn: Stop praying entirely and abandon the Salah
Force themselves to collapse rather than sit
Sit down smoothly and complete the rest of the prayer seated
Switch to making Tasbih without finishing the rak'ah
explanationEn: One continues the prayer in whatever posture one becomes limited to—transitioning from standing to sitting without breaking the prayer.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Imran ibn Husayn Hadith & Aisha on Prophet's late-life seated prayer)

questionEn: During the Prophet's ﷺ final illness when he led Abu Bakr and the companions while seated, what did he gesture to the congregation who were standing?
optionsEn: To leave the mosque and pray at home
To stand only on their toes
To lie down on their sides
To sit down when their Imam was praying seated due to illness
explanationEn: In the narration of Aisha and Anas, the Prophet ﷺ led prayer seated during illness and signaled the companions to sit, teaching that the Imam is appointed to be followed.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Aisha & Anas)

questionEn: If a traveler is praying voluntary Salah on a camel or vehicle and can face the Qibla at the opening Takbir before the mount turns along the road, what is recommended?
optionsEn: Facing the Qibla for the opening Takbir if feasible, then continuing in the direction of travel
Always refusing to say the opening Takbir
Facing away from the Qibla deliberately at the start
Stopping the airplane before every Takbir
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik reported that when the Prophet ﷺ wanted to pray voluntary Salah while traveling, he turned his camel toward the Qibla, said Allahu Akbar, and then prayed whichever direction the camel walked.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Narrated by Anas ibn Malik)

questionEn: What is the ruling on a person praying Qasr (two rak'ahs) while traveling if they doubt whether they will stay at their destination four days or less vs more than four days (according to the majority of scholars)?
optionsEn: They must always shorten for up to 10 years regardless of residency plans
If they intend a settled stay exceeding four days (per Shafi'i/Maliki/Hanbali; 15 days per Hanafi), they pray in full from arrival
They must never pray Qasr even during the trip itself
They pray three rak'ahs as a compromise
explanationEn: The majority of scholars (Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali) set a planned stay of more than four days as the threshold to resume full prayers upon arrival, whereas the Hanafi school sets fifteen days.
reference: Classical Four-Madhhab Fiqh on Travel Residency Threshold

questionEn: While traveling, what happens to the reward of a traveler who takes the concession of shortening prayers rather than insisting on praying four rak'ahs?
optionsEn: Their reward is cut in half because the rak'ahs were halved
They are blamed for taking an easier path
Their reward is complete and even beloved to Allah, who loves His concessions to be accepted
They must make up the remaining two rak'ahs upon returning home
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Indeed, Allah loves that His concessions be accepted just as He dislikes His prohibitions to be committed.'
reference: Musnad Ahmad & Sahih Ibn Hibban (Narrated by Ibn Umar)

questionEn: When a Muslim travels for an Umrah or Hajj journey and arrives at Miqat or Makkah before settling long-term, how should they pray obligatory prayers when praying alone in their hotel?
optionsEn: Always pray 4 rak'ahs because Makkah is a sacred city
Skip Dhuhr and Asr while doing Tawaf
Combine all five prayers into one evening prayer
Shorten four-rak'ah prayers to two if they meet travel criteria, though behind the Haram Imam they pray four in full
explanationEn: When praying behind the resident Imam of Al-Masjid al-Haram, a pilgrim prays four rak'ahs in full; if praying alone while still under traveler rulings, they may shorten four-rak'ah prayers to two.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Musa ibn Salamah from Ibn Abbas)

questionEn: If an ill person has an ongoing medical condition causing continual bleeding, urinary incontinence, or chronic flatulence that invalidates Wudu, how do they maintain their five daily prayers?
optionsEn: Make fresh Wudu after each prayer's time enters and pray normally without being hindered by involuntary discharge during that prayer window
Abandon prayer permanently until cured
Take a full Ghusl every five minutes
Pray only once a week on Friday
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed women experiencing chronic non-menstrual bleeding (istihadah) to perform Wudu for each prayer time and pray even if drops continue, a mercy extended to all excused chronic conditions (ma'dhur).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sunan Abi Dawud (Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh)

questionEn: According to the Hadith of Umm Habibah (RA), how many daily Sunnah Rawatib rak'ahs earn the believer a house built in Paradise?
optionsEn: 8 rak'ahs every day
12 rak'ahs every day
20 rak'ahs every day
6 rak'ahs every day
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ promised: 'Whoever prays twelve rak'ahs in a day and night, a house will be built for him in Paradise.'

questionEn: What is the exact breakdown of the twelve daily Sunnah Rawatib rak'ahs described in Jami' at-Tirmidhi and Sahih Muslim's narration from Umm Habibah?
optionsEn: 2 before Fajr, 2 before Dhuhr, 2 after Dhuhr, 4 after Asr, 2 after Isha
4 before Fajr, 2 after Dhuhr, 2 before Asr, 2 after Maghrib, 2 after Isha
4 before Dhuhr, 2 after Dhuhr, 2 after Maghrib, 2 after Isha, and 2 before Fajr
2 before Fajr, 2 before Dhuhr, 2 after Dhuhr, 2 after Maghrib, and 4 after Isha
explanationEn: At-Tirmidhi explicitly details the twelve rak'ahs from Umm Habibah: four before Dhuhr, two after Dhuhr, two after Maghrib, two after Isha, and two before Fajr.
reference: Jami' at-Tirmidhi & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Umm Habibah)

questionEn: Which pair of Surahs did the Prophet ﷺ frequently recite in the two Sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Kafirun in the first rak'ah and Surah Al-Ikhlas in the second
Surah Yasin in the first rak'ah and Surah Al-Mulk in the second
Surah Al-A'la in the first rak'ah and Surah Al-Ghashiyah in the second
Surah Al-Falaq in the first rak'ah and Surah An-Nas in the second
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ recited 'Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun' (Al-Kafirun) and 'Qul huwallahu ahad' (Al-Ikhlas) in the two Sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr.

questionEn: Besides Surah Al-Kafirun and Surah Al-Ikhlas, which two Qur'anic verses did Ibn Abbas report the Prophet ﷺ sometimes reciting in the two Sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr?
optionsEn: Al-Fatihah alone without any extra verse
Al-Baqarah 2:136 in the first rak'ah and Al Imran 3:64 in the second
Ayatul Kursi in the first rak'ah and Al-Asr in the second
The opening of Surah Al-Kahf and the end of Surah Al-Hashr
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ would recite 'Qulu amanna billahi...' (Al-Baqarah 2:136) in the first rak'ah and 'Qul ya ahlal-kitabi ta'alaw...' (Al Imran 3:64) in the second.

questionEn: How did Aisha (RA) describe the length of the Prophet's ﷺ two Sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr?
optionsEn: So long that dawn nearly turned into midday
Lasting over forty minutes each
So light and brief that she wondered whether he had even recited Surah Al-Fatihah
Always accompanied by Qunut for ten minutes
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) remarked that the Prophet ﷺ made the two rak'ahs before Fajr so concise that she would ask herself whether he had recited the Mother of the Book (Al-Fatihah).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Aisha RA)

questionEn: What special promise did the Prophet ﷺ mention in Sunan Abi Dawud and At-Tirmidhi for one who consistently guards four rak'ahs before Dhuhr and four rak'ahs after Dhuhr?
optionsEn: Automatic exemption from Hajj
A palace made of pearls in Madinah
Doubled wealth within a single year
Allah will forbid his flesh from the Hellfire
explanationEn: Umm Habibah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever maintains four rak'ahs before Dhuhr and four after it, Allah will forbid him from the Fire.'
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Jami' at-Tirmidhi (Narrated by Umm Habibah)

questionEn: If a Muslim arrives at the mosque late and misses the two Sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr because the obligatory congregation has begun, what does the Sunnah allow afterward?
optionsEn: Praying them right after the Fajr obligatory prayer or after sunrise
Never making them up under any circumstance
Combining them into Dhuhr later that afternoon
Breaking off from the Imam in the middle of Fajr to pray them first
explanationEn: Qays ibn Amr prayed the two Sunnah rak'ahs immediately after Fajr and explained to the Prophet ﷺ that he had missed them before Fajr; the Prophet ﷺ remained silent in approval, and another narration recommends waiting until after sunrise if preferred.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Jami' at-Tirmidhi (Narrated by Qays ibn Amr & Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: Where did the Prophet ﷺ say is the best place to offer voluntary and Sunnah Rawatib prayers?
optionsEn: Exclusively in the courtyard of the marketplace
In one's home, reserving the mosque primarily for obligatory prayers
Always on the rooftop of a neighbor's house
Strictly in the back corner of the mosque
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught: 'Pray in your homes, O people, for the best prayer of a person is in his house, except for the prescribed (obligatory) prayer.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Zayd ibn Thabit)

questionEn: What supplication of mercy did the Prophet ﷺ make for those who pray four voluntary rak'ahs before Asr?
optionsEn: "May Allah double their charity tenfold"
"May Allah grant them leadership over cities"
"May Allah have mercy on a person who prays four (rak'ahs) before Asr"
"May Allah excuse them from Witr that night"
explanationEn: Ibn Umar narrated that the Prophet ﷺ explicitly invoked mercy: 'May Allah have mercy on a person who prays four rak'ahs before Asr.'
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Jami' at-Tirmidhi (Narrated by Ibn Umar)

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ tell the Companions regarding praying two light voluntary rak'ahs between the Adhan and Iqamah of Maghrib?
optionsEn: "It is strictly prohibited in Madinah"
"It is an obligatory pillar of Islam"
"Only travelers may pray before Maghrib"
"Pray before Maghrib, pray before Maghrib," adding on the third time, "for whoever wishes"
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik reported that the Prophet ﷺ encouraged praying before Maghrib twice and added 'for whoever wishes' the third time so people would not treat it as an obligatory Sunnah.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Narrated by Abdullah al-Muzani & Anas)

questionEn: What is the minimum number of rak'ahs required to fulfill Salat al-Witr?
optionsEn: 1 rak'ah
2 rak'ahs
4 rak'ahs
6 rak'ahs
explanationEn: While 3 or more odd rak'ahs are common, the Prophet ﷺ taught that night prayer is two by two, and when one fears dawn is near, he prays one rak'ah to make odd (Witr) what he has prayed.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Ibn Umar)

questionEn: When does the valid time window for offering Salat al-Witr begin and end?
optionsEn: From Maghrib until midnight
After praying Isha (even if combined at Maghrib time) until the break of true dawn (Fajr)
Only during the last ten minutes before sunrise
From Dhuhr until Asr
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ explained that Allah added Witr for the believers and appointed its time between Isha prayer and the rising of Fajr.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Jami' at-Tirmidhi (Narrated by Kharijah ibn Hudhafah)

questionEn: What guidance did the Prophet ﷺ give regarding whether to pray Witr before sleeping or at the end of the night?
optionsEn: Everyone must stay awake all night to pray Witr
Witr is invalid if prayed before midnight
Whoever fears not waking at the end of the night should pray Witr before sleeping; whoever is confident of waking should pray it at the end of the night
Only scholars may delay Witr until the last third of the night
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ advised praying Witr before sleeping for those who fear missing Qiyam, while noting that prayer at the end of the night is witnessed (by angels) and better.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah)

questionEn: Which three Surahs did the Prophet ﷺ customarily recite across the three rak'ahs of Witr?
optionsEn: Al-Mulk, Al-Qalam, and Al-Haqqah
Al-Qadr, Al-Zalzalah, and Al-Adiyat
Al-Falaq, An-Nas, and Al-Masad
Al-A'la in the first, Al-Kafirun in the second, and Al-Ikhlas in the third
explanationEn: Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn Abbas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ recited Surah Al-A'la in the first rak'ah of Witr, Surah Al-Kafirun in the second, and Surah Al-Ikhlas in the third.
reference: Sunan an-Nasa'i & Sunan Abi Dawud (Narrated by Ubayy ibn Ka'b)

questionEn: When praying three rak'ahs of Witr continuously without separating them by Taslim after the second rak'ah, why did the Prophet ﷺ forbid sitting for Tashahhud after the second rak'ah?
optionsEn: So that Witr does not resemble the three-rak'ah Maghrib prayer
Because sitting in Tashahhud is forbidden in all night prayers
Because Witr has no Tashahhud even at the end
To shorten the prayer to under thirty seconds
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Do not pray Witr as three [like Maghrib], rather make Witr five or seven or do not make it resemble Maghrib'—so one either prays 2+1 with Taslim or 3 continuous with only one Tashahhud at the end (though Hanafis have a distinct view).
reference: Al-Mustadrak & Sunan ad-Daraqutni (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: What opening phrase begins the famous Du'a al-Qunut that the Prophet ﷺ taught Al-Hasan ibn Ali (RA) to recite in Witr?
optionsEn: "Allahumma antas-Salam wa minkas-Salam..."
"Allahumma ihdini fiman hadayt, wa 'afini fiman 'afayt..."
"Subhana zil-malakuti wal-jabarut..."
"Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan..."
explanationEn: Al-Hasan ibn Ali reported that the Prophet ﷺ taught him words to say in the Qunut of Witr: 'Allahumma ihdini fiman hadayt, wa 'afini fiman 'afayt, wa tawallani fiman tawallayt...'
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Jami' at-Tirmidhi (Narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Ali)

questionEn: What rule did the Prophet ﷺ state if someone already prayed Witr before sleeping and then wakes up later in the night wanting to pray more Tahajjud?
optionsEn: They must pray Witr a second time at the very end
They cannot pray any night prayer after Witr
They pray two by two without repeating Witr, for 'there are no two Witrs in one night'
They must repeat Isha before praying Tahajjud
explanationEn: Talq ibn Ali narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'There are not two Witrs in one night.' So one simply prays pairs of two rak'ahs without making it odd again.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Jami' at-Tirmidhi (Narrated by Talq ibn Ali)

questionEn: According to Aisha (RA), what did the Prophet ﷺ do if illness or heavy sleep caused him to miss his night prayer (which was usually 11 rak'ahs including Witr)?
optionsEn: He prayed 11 rak'ahs right before Maghrib
He skipped it permanently and fasted instead
He prayed 3 rak'ahs silently at midnight the next week
He prayed twelve rak'ahs (an even number) during the daytime
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) narrated that whenever sleep or pain overcame the Prophet ﷺ at night, he would pray twelve rak'ahs during the day (making up his 11-rak'ah routine in an even number).

questionEn: Which short dhikr did the Prophet ﷺ habitually recite three times aloud after concluding the Taslim of Salat al-Witr?
optionsEn: "Subhana Al-Malik Al-Quddus" (raising his voice on the third)
"Alhamdulillahi Rabbil-Alamin" ten times
"Allahu Akbar Kabira" seven times
"Astaghfirullahal-Azim" seventy times
explanationEn: Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Abdur-Rahman ibn Abza reported that after saying Salam in Witr, the Prophet ﷺ would say 'Subhanal-Malikil-Quddus' three times, extending/raising his voice on the third.
reference: Sunan an-Nasa'i & Sunan Abi Dawud (Narrated by Ubayy ibn Ka'b)

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:79), what elevated station does Allah promise the Prophet ﷺ when commanding him to pray Tahajjud at night?
optionsEn: Sidrat al-Muntaha
Maqaman Mahmuda (a Praiseworthy Station)
Al-Kawthar
Jannat al-Firdaws
explanationEn: Allah says in Surah Al-Isra (17:79): 'And from [part of] the night, pray with it as additional [worship] for you; it is expected that your Lord will resurrect you to a praised station (Maqaman Mahmuda).'

questionEn: How does Surah As-Sajdah (32:16) poetically describe the believers who rise for night prayer (Qiyam al-Layl)?
optionsEn: Their footsteps echo through marketplaces at dawn
They sleep through the entire night in peace
Their sides forsake their beds as they call upon their Lord in fear and hope
They gather at mountain peaks once a year
explanationEn: Surah As-Sajdah (32:16) praises the believers: 'Their sides part from [their] beds; they supplicate their Lord in fear and aspiration, and from what We have provided them, they spend.'

questionEn: What pattern of rak'ah groupings did the Prophet ﷺ specify for night prayer (Salat al-Layl)?
optionsEn: Four by four with one sitting at the end
Three by three without Taslim
Six continuous rak'ahs
Two by two (Mathna mathna), ending with one rak'ah of Witr
explanationEn: When asked about the night prayer, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The night prayer is two by two; and when one of you fears the approach of dawn, let him pray one rak'ah to make odd what he has prayed.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Ibn Umar)

questionEn: According to Aisha (RA), how many total rak'ahs did the Prophet ﷺ regularly pray at night (both inside and outside Ramadan)?
optionsEn: Eleven rak'ahs (or thirteen in some narrations including two light opening rak'ahs or Fajr Sunnah)
Always forty rak'ahs every night
Strictly two rak'ahs only
Twenty-five rak'ahs without rest
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ did not exceed eleven rak'ahs in Ramadan or outside it, praying four, then four, then three (or two-by-two up to eleven/thirteen per Ibn Abbas).
