reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Aisha RA)

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ advise beginning one's Tahajjud / Qiyam al-Layl when waking up from sleep?
optionsEn: By standing immediately for an hour-long Surah
By opening with two light, brief rak'ahs
By eating a heavy meal first
By reciting all of Surah Al-Baqarah silently
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed: 'When one of you stands to pray at night, let him begin his prayer with two light rak'ahs'—to refresh body and mind before longer standing.

questionEn: According to the famous Hadith Qudsi on the last third of the night, what does Allah declare as He descends to the lowest heaven?
optionsEn: "Sleep well until sunrise"
"Bring your sacrifices to the mosque now"
"Who is calling upon Me that I may answer him? Who is asking of Me that I may give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness that I may forgive him?"
"Today all deeds are paused until Dhuhr"
explanationEn: Every night in its final third, Allah descends to the lowest heaven in a manner befitting His Majesty and asks who is supplicating, asking, and seeking forgiveness so He may respond.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: After the five daily obligatory prayers, which prayer did the Prophet ﷺ declare to be the most virtuous prayer?
optionsEn: Salat al-Istikharah
Salat al-Eid
Salat al-Duha
The prayer offered in the depths of the night (Salat al-Layl)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The best fasting after Ramadan is Allah's month of Muharram, and the best prayer after the obligatory prayer is the night prayer.'

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ describe the balanced night-prayer routine of Prophet Dawud (AS), calling it the most beloved prayer to Allah?
optionsEn: He slept half the night, stood in prayer for a third of the night, and slept the final sixth
He stayed awake all night every single night of his life
He prayed only ten minutes right after sunset
He slept three-quarters of the night and prayed the first quarter
explanationEn: Prophet Dawud (AS) slept the first half of the night, rose to pray during the third (next two-sixths), and rested for the final sixth so he woke refreshed for Fajr.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abdullah ibn Amr)

questionEn: What practical advice did the Prophet ﷺ give if a believer feels overwhelmed by drowsiness while standing in night prayer?
optionsEn: Force oneself to keep standing even while mumbling errors
Go back to sleep until drowsiness passes, lest one intend to seek forgiveness and mistakenly curse oneself
Splash boiling water on one's feet
Skip Fajr the next morning
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ compassionately advised: 'If one of you feels drowsy while praying, let him sleep until sleepiness leaves him, for if he prays while drowsy he does not know—perhaps he intends to seek forgiveness yet ends up reviling himself.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Aisha RA)

questionEn: What reward is written for a Muslim who goes to bed intending to wake up for Tahajjud, yet sleeps soundly until Fajr?
optionsEn: They are penalized with extra fasting
Nothing is recorded unless they wake up
The reward of their intended night prayer is written for them, and their sleep is a charity from Allah
They must pray double the next night to avoid sin
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ gave this glad tiding: 'Whoever goes to his bed intending to get up and pray at night, and sleep overcomes him until morning, what he intended is written for him, and his sleep is a charity from his Lord upon him.'
reference: Sunan an-Nasa'i & Sunan Ibn Majah (Narrated by Abu ad-Darda / Aisha)

questionEn: What tender encouragement did the Prophet ﷺ give about spouses helping each other wake up for night prayer?
optionsEn: Never wake a sleeping spouse under any condition
Divorce anyone who misses Tahajjud once
Compete silently without speaking to one another
May Allah have mercy on a husband or wife who rises at night, prays, and wakes their spouse—gently sprinkling water on their face if they hesitate
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ invoked mercy upon both the man and the woman who get up at night to pray and lovingly wake their spouse, even gently sprinkling water on their face.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Sunan an-Nasa'i (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: What dhikr did the Prophet ﷺ teach for a person who wakes up suddenly in the night, promising that any dua made right after it will be answered?
optionsEn: "La ilaha illallah wahdahu la sharika lah... SubhanAllah, walhamdulillah, wa la ilaha illallah, wallahu Akbar, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah"
Reciting Surah At-Tawbah silently
Counting backwards from one hundred
Saying Ameen fifty times
explanationEn: Ubadah ibn as-Samit reported that whoever wakes at night and says this Tawhid and Tasbih formula, then says 'Allahummaghfir li' or supplicates, will have their prayer answered—and if they make Wudu and pray, their prayer will be accepted.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Narrated by Ubadah ibn as-Samit)

questionEn: Which Surah's final verses did Ibn Abbas witness the Prophet ﷺ reciting while wiping sleep from his face upon waking up in the night?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Kahf
Surah Al Imran (3:190–200)
Surah Al-Maidah
Surah Al-Anfal
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas slept at the house of his aunt Maymunah and saw the Prophet ﷺ wake at midnight, wipe sleep from his eyes, look toward the sky, and recite the final verses of Surah Al Imran ('Inna fi khalqis-samawati wal-ard...').
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Ibn Abbas)

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ stop coming out to lead Tarawih (Qiyam Ramadan) in congregation after the third or fourth night in Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Because nobody attended the mosque on the fourth night
Because he traveled out of Madinah for the rest of Ramadan
Out of compassion, fearing it would be made obligatory upon his Ummah and they would not be able to bear it
Because congregational night prayer was permanently forbidden
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ explained to the waiting companions: 'Nothing prevented me from coming out to you except that I feared it would be prescribed as obligatory upon you, and you would be unable to keep it up.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Aisha RA)

questionEn: What immense promise did the Prophet ﷺ make for standing in prayer during the nights of Ramadan (Tarawih/Qiyam) out of faith and hope for reward?
optionsEn: Exemption from all future fasting
A guaranteed trip to Makkah every year
Double the wealth of one's household
Forgiveness of all previous sins
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever stands in prayer during Ramadan out of sincere faith (iman) and hoping for reward from Allah (ihtisab), his past sins will be forgiven.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: Which Companion did Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) appoint to lead the united Tarawih congregation in Masjid an-Nabawi, remarking 'What an excellent revival this is!'?
optionsEn: Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA)
Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA)
Bilal ibn Rabah (RA)
Salman al-Farisi (RA)
explanationEn: Seeing worshippers praying in scattered small groups, Umar ibn al-Khattab united them behind Ubayy ibn Ka'b (and Tamim ad-Dari), calling it 'ni'matil-bid'ah hadhihi' (what an excellent practice!).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Narrated by Abdur-Rahman ibn Abd al-Qari)

questionEn: According to the Hadith of Abu Dharr (RA), what reward does a believer earn if they stay and pray Tarawih behind the Imam until the Imam finishes and departs?
optionsEn: The reward of two hours of prayer
The reward of spending the entire night in prayer (Qiyam al-Layl)
Half the reward of a Friday prayer
The reward of one voluntary fast
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ promised: 'Whoever prays Qiyam with the Imam until he finishes, it is recorded for him as if he spent the entire night in prayer.'
reference: Jami' at-Tirmidhi & Sunan Abi Dawud (Narrated by Abu Dharr)

questionEn: What did Aisha (RA) say the Prophet ﷺ used to do during the last ten nights of Ramadan that distinguished them from the rest of the year?
optionsEn: He slept longer and avoided the mosque
He traveled away from Madinah every Ramadan
He tightened his waist-wrapper (worked hard in worship), stayed awake at night, and woke his family
He stopped praying Witr during those ten nights
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) reported that when the last ten nights of Ramadan began, the Prophet ﷺ tightened his lower garment (exerting himself in devotion), enlivened his nights, and awakened his family.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Aisha RA)

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim, praying two rak'ahs of Salat al-Duha fulfills the daily charity owed on behalf of how many joints (sulama) in the human body?
optionsEn: 100 joints
206 joints
700 joints
360 joints
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ taught that every person wakes up owing charity for each of their 360 joints, and two rak'ahs offered in the Duha (forenoon) suffice for all of them.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Dharr) & Sahih Muslim (Aisha RA)

questionEn: By what alternative name did the Prophet ﷺ call Salat al-Duha when offered at its prime time—when the desert sand grows hot under young camels' feet?
optionsEn: Salat al-Awwabin (Prayer of the Oft-Repentant)
Salat al-Fath
Salat al-Ghurub
Salat al-Khawf
explanationEn: Zayd ibn Arqam heard the Prophet ﷺ declare: 'The prayer of the oft-repentant (Salat al-Awwabin) is when the young camels feel the heat of the sun [mid-to-late morning].'
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Zayd ibn Arqam)

questionEn: How many rak'ahs of Salat al-Duha did Umm Hani (RA) witness the Prophet ﷺ praying in her house on the day of the Conquest of Makkah?
optionsEn: Two rak'ahs
Eight rak'ahs
Twenty rak'ahs
One single rak'ah
explanationEn: Umm Hani (RA) narrated that on the Day of the Conquest of Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ bathed and prayed eight rak'ahs of Duha, resting briefly after every two rak'ahs.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Umm Hani)

questionEn: Which three lifelong habits did the Prophet ﷺ counsel Abu Hurayrah (RA) never to abandon until death?
optionsEn: Fasting every day, praying 100 rak'ahs, and living in Makkah
Giving half his wealth daily, traveling monthly, and reciting Surah Yasin nightly
Fasting three days every month, praying two rak'ahs of Duha, and praying Witr before sleeping
Praying only on Fridays, fasting Mondays only, and visiting Quba daily
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah (RA) testified: 'My close friend (the Prophet ﷺ) advised me with three things that I will never leave until I die: fasting three days of every month, the two rak'ahs of Duha, and sleeping after praying Witr.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: What is the minimum and the commonly cited upper count of rak'ahs for Salat al-Duha according to authentic narrations?
optionsEn: Minimum 1, maximum 3
Minimum 4, maximum 40
Minimum 6, maximum 24
Minimum 2 rak'ahs, up to 8 (and up to 12 in some narrations)
explanationEn: Two rak'ahs is the established minimum of Duha, the Prophet ﷺ prayed four and sometimes more (as Allah willed), and eight on the Conquest of Makkah (with Anas narrating up to twelve in At-Tirmidhi).
reference: Sahih Muslim (Aisha RA) & Sahih al-Bukhari (Umm Hani)

questionEn: When does the valid time for Salat al-Duha end each day?
optionsEn: Shortly before the sun reaches its midday zenith (about 10–15 minutes before Dhuhr)
Right at Asr time
Just after Maghrib
At midnight
explanationEn: Salat al-Duha begins once the sun has risen the height of a spear (~15–20 minutes after sunrise) and ends just before the zenith (Zawal), when prayer is briefly prohibited before Dhuhr.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Amr ibn Abasah & Zayd ibn Arqam)

questionEn: How strongly did the Prophet ﷺ emphasize teaching Salat al-Istikharah (the prayer for seeking Allah's guidance) to his Companions?
optionsEn: He mentioned it only once in private
He used to teach it to them in all matters just as he taught them a Surah of the Qur'an
He restricted it solely to choosing military commanders
He permitted it only during Ramadan
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) reported: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us Al-Istikharah in all matters just as he would teach us a Surah from the Qur'an.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah)

questionEn: How many rak'ahs does a Muslim pray before reciting the supplication of Salat al-Istikharah?
optionsEn: Four obligatory rak'ahs
Three odd rak'ahs
Two non-obligatory (nafl) rak'ahs
One silent rak'ah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ instructed: 'When any of you intends to undertake a matter, let him pray two rak'ahs other than the obligatory prayer, and then say: Allahumma inni astakhiruka bi'ilmika...'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah)

questionEn: In Du'a al-Istikharah, what does the supplicant ask Allah to do if the matter is bad for their religion, livelihood, and ultimate outcome?
optionsEn: Send a visible dream within three nights
Force the matter to succeed anyway
Reveal the future in a vision
Turn the matter away from them, turn them away from it, and decree good for them wherever it may be, then make them pleased with it
explanationEn: In Istikharah, the believer asks Allah—by His infinite knowledge and power—to facilitate the matter if good, or turn it away and ordain good elsewhere if bad, and grant contentment with His decree.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah)

questionEn: For which kinds of decisions should a Muslim perform Salat al-Istikharah?
optionsEn: Permissible (mubah) or recommended decisions where one seeks what is best, such as marriage, work, or travel—never for obligatory duties or sinful acts
Deciding whether to pray the five daily prayers
Choosing whether to engage in something clearly forbidden (haram)
Replacing the need to seek sound advice from trustworthy people
explanationEn: Istikharah is not done over whether to perform an obligation or commit a sin; it is performed in permissible choices (or choosing between two good options) alongside wise consultation (Istisharah).

questionEn: Must a person wait for a vivid dream after praying Salat al-Istikharah before taking action?
optionsEn: Yes, Istikharah is invalid without a dream
No; a dream is not required—rather one proceeds toward the good option with trust in Allah, who eases what is best or closes the path if harmful
Yes, and the dream must feature the color green
Only if prayed seven nights in a row
explanationEn: Scholars clarify that expecting a dream after Istikharah has no basis in the Hadith; instead, a believer consults wise advisors, prays Istikharah, and moves forward trusting Allah's facilitation.

questionEn: What is Salat al-Tawbah, as taught by the Prophet ﷺ through Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA)?
optionsEn: A group prayer offered only on Arafah
Standing all night in silence without reciting Qur'an
Purifying oneself with Wudu after committing a sin, praying two rak'ahs, and seeking Allah's forgiveness
Repeating Fajr four times after oversleeping
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'There is no servant who commits a sin, then purifies himself well, stands and prays two rak'ahs, and seeks Allah's forgiveness, except that Allah will forgive him,' then he recited Al Imran 3:135.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Jami' at-Tirmidhi (Narrated by Abu Bakr as-Siddiq)

questionEn: When a solar eclipse coincided with the death of the Prophet's ﷺ young son Ibrahim, what misconception did the Prophet ﷺ immediately correct?
optionsEn: That eclipses only happen in winter
That eclipses require sacrificing a camel
That eclipses signal the end of the world that evening
That the sun and moon eclipse for anyone's death or life—rather they are two signs of Allah urging people to pray and remember Him
explanationEn: When people whispered that the sun eclipsed for Ibrahim's death, the Prophet ﷺ stood in the sermon and declared: 'The sun and the moon are two of Allah's signs; they do not eclipse for the death or life of anyone. When you see them, supplicate to Allah, proclaim His greatness, pray, and give charity.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Al-Mughirah & Aisha)

questionEn: What special structural feature makes Salat al-Kusuf (the Eclipse Prayer) distinct from all regular two-rak'ah prayers?
optionsEn: Each of the two rak'ahs contains two standing recitations and two bowings (ruku') along with two prostrations
It has four prostrations in a row before bowing
It has no Al-Fatihah and no bowing
It consists of six rak'ahs without any sitting
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) described the Prophet's ﷺ eclipse prayer: in each of the two rak'ahs he stood long, bowed long, rose to stand again for a second recitation (shorter than the first), bowed a second time, and then made two prostrations—making four bowings and four prostrations across two rak'ahs.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Aisha RA & Ibn Abbas)

questionEn: How are Muslims summoned to gather for the Eclipse Prayer (Salat al-Kusuf), since there is neither Adhan nor Iqamah for it?
optionsEn: By ringing a bell outside the mosque
By announcing 'As-salatu jami'ah' (The prayer is about to gather)
By reciting the full Fajr Adhan twice
By firing arrows into the air
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Amr narrated that when the sun eclipsed in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, the caller announced: 'Innas-salata jami'ah' (The prayer is gathering in congregation).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abdullah ibn Amr)

questionEn: Besides praying Salat al-Kusuf, what other pious deeds did the Prophet ﷺ specifically urge believers to perform during an eclipse?
optionsEn: Closing all doors and sleeping silently
Staring directly at the sun without blinking
Making Takbir, supplicating (Dua), seeking forgiveness, giving charity, and freeing slaves
Completing seven circuits around the mosque
explanationEn: In his eclipse sermons, the Prophet ﷺ commanded: 'When you see that, hasten to the remembrance of Allah, supplicate to Him, seek His forgiveness, and give charity.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Aisha & Abu Musa)

questionEn: During the sermon after the Eclipse Prayer, what awesome visions did the Prophet ﷺ tell the Companions he had just been shown while praying?
optionsEn: Future cities across oceans
The names of every star in the sky
Treasures buried beneath Madinah
Paradise (whose cluster of grapes he nearly plucked) and Hellfire, warning them against the trial of the grave
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ saw Paradise and reached toward a bunch of its fruit, and saw Hellfire, and warned the community to seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Ibn Abbas & Aisha)

questionEn: How should Muslims respond if a lunar eclipse (Khusuf) occurs during the night?
optionsEn: Pray Salat al-Khusuf just like the solar eclipse prayer—two rak'ahs with two bowings each—along with dua, dhikr, and charity
Ignore lunar eclipses because the Sunnah applies only to the sun
Pray three rak'ahs without bowing
Wait until the next noon to pray
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ explicitly coupled both signs together: 'The sun and the moon are two of Allah's signs... when you see them, pray and supplicate until what you are experiencing clears.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Mas'ud & Al-Mughirah)

questionEn: What is Salat al-Istisqa'?
optionsEn: A prayer offered exclusively before boarding a ship
A communal prayer and supplication performed during drought to humbly ask Allah for beneficial rain
A midnight prayer for healing broken bones
A prayer offered after harvesting dates
explanationEn: Salat al-Istisqa' (seeking rain) is the Sunnah prayer in which the community goes out humbly to seek beneficial, merciful rain from Allah during times of drought.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Book of Istisqa')

questionEn: In what attire and demeanor did Ibn Abbas describe the Prophet ﷺ going out to the open prayer ground (Musalla) for Salat al-Istisqa'?
optionsEn: Wearing his finest royal silk and riding swiftly
Carrying swords and banners of victory
Walking out in everyday humble clothing, with deep humility, submission, and earnest supplication
Wearing perfumed holiday garments as for Eid
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ went out for Istisqa' wearing ordinary, humble clothes (mutabadhdhilan), exhibiting humility (mutawadi'an) and earnest submission (mutadarri'an).
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Jami' at-Tirmidhi (Narrated by Ibn Abbas)

questionEn: What symbolic gesture did the Prophet ﷺ perform with his outer cloak (Rida') while facing the Qibla and supplicating in Salat al-Istisqa'?
optionsEn: He folded it neatly and placed it on the ground
He gave it away before starting the prayer
He waved it three times above his head
He turned his cloak inside out / switched its right side to his left shoulder as a sign of optimism that Allah would reverse the drought
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Zayd narrated that the Prophet ﷺ faced the Qibla, turned his cloak around (switching right to left), and prayed two rak'ahs reciting aloud; scholars note this expresses hope that Allah will transform hardship into relief.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abdullah ibn Zayd)

questionEn: How did Anas ibn Malik describe the way the Prophet ﷺ raised his hands during the supplication for rain (Istisqa'), unlike his usual posture in dua?
optionsEn: He raised his hands so high that the whiteness of his underarms was visible, with the backs of his hands toward the sky
He kept his hands clasped behind his back
He raised only one finger to chest level
He placed his hands flat on his knees
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik reported that the Prophet ﷺ did not raise his hands so high in any supplication except in Istisqa', raising them until the whiteness of his underarms could be seen, turning the backs of his palms upward.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Anas ibn Malik)

questionEn: After rain fell following the Prophet's ﷺ supplication at Hudaybiyyah, what statement did he warn turns a person into a disbeliever in Allah's blessing?
optionsEn: "Thank Allah for this rain"
"We have been given rain by the rising/setting of such-and-such star (Naw')"
"This rain brings mercy to the crops"
"O Allah, make it a beneficial downpour"
explanationEn: In the Hadith Qudsi narrated by Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, Allah states: 'Whoever says, "We were given rain by the grace of Allah and His mercy," is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the stars; whoever says, "We were given rain by such-and-such star," is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the stars.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani)

questionEn: What concise two-word dua did the Prophet ﷺ ask Allah for when people requested rain during a Friday Khutbah, and what did he say when heavy rain continued the next week?
optionsEn: "Allahumma amsirna" then "Allahumma akhrijna"
"Allahumma arzilna" then "Allahumma amhilna"
"Allahumma aghithna" (O Allah, send us relief/rain), then "Allahumma hawalayna wa la 'alayna" (Around us, not upon us)
"Allahumma ihdina" then "Allahumma barik lana"
explanationEn: When a man entered during the Friday sermon asking for rain, the Prophet ﷺ prayed 'Allahumma aghithna' until clouds gathered and poured for a week; the next Friday he prayed 'Allahumma hawalayna wa la 'alayna' so the clouds parted over Madinah onto the hills and valleys.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Anas ibn Malik)

questionEn: What is the Sunnah practice regarding the 2-rak'ah Fajr Sunnah if one prays it at home before walking to the mosque, according to Aisha (RA)?
optionsEn: Running immediately to the mosque without pausing
Staying seated cross-legged for one hour
Drinking milk before standing for Fajr
Lying down briefly on one's right side between the Sunnah and going out for the obligatory prayer
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) reported that after praying the two light rak'ahs of Fajr, the Prophet ﷺ would lie down briefly on his right side (resting from night prayer before rising for the Fajr congregation).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Aisha RA)

questionEn: According to the Prophet ﷺ, how many rak'ahs is a believer encouraged to pray in pairs before concluding with Witr if they want to perform Qiyam al-Layl, and what is the virtue of praying Tahiyyat al-Wudu?
optionsEn: Two rak'ahs after making Wudu with full presence of heart makes Paradise guaranteed for the believer
Ten rak'ahs after Wudu removes the need for Fajr
Four rak'ahs after Wudu replaces Jumu'ah
One rak'ah after Wudu cancels fasting
explanationEn: Uqbah ibn Amir narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'There is no Muslim who performs Wudu well, then stands and prays two rak'ahs focusing upon them with his heart and face, except that Paradise becomes guaranteed for him.'
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Uqbah ibn Amir)

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Muzzammil (73:20), why did Allah lighten the earlier command of standing nearly the entire night in prayer?
optionsEn: Because night prayer was completely abrogated for all Muslims
Because Allah knew that among the believers would be the sick, travelers seeking Allah's bounty, and those fighting in Allah's path
Because the nights in Madinah were too short
Because daytime prayers were abolished
explanationEn: Surah Al-Muzzammil (73:20) warmly explains that Allah eased the obligation of standing most of the night out of mercy for the ill, travelers, and defenders—commanding instead: 'Recite what is easy from the Qur'an.'

questionEn: How does the sequence of the prayer and the sermon (Khutbah) in Eid prayers differ from the Friday Jumu'ah prayer?
optionsEn: In Eid, the two-rak'ah prayer is offered BEFORE the Khutbah, whereas in Jumu'ah the Khutbah precedes the prayer
In Eid, there are two Khutbahs before the prayer and none afterward
Eid has no Khutbah at all
Eid is prayed after Asr instead of the morning
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri confirmed that the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, and Umar always offered the Eid prayer first and then delivered the sermon afterward.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Ibn Umar & Abu Sa'id)

questionEn: What is the Prophetic Sunnah regarding the Adhan and Iqamah for Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha prayers?
optionsEn: Both Adhan and Iqamah are called twice
Neither an Adhan nor an Iqamah is called for the Eid prayers
Only the Adhan is called without an Iqamah
Only the Iqamah is called ten minutes before sunrise
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Samurah narrated: 'I prayed the two Eids with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ more than once or twice without an Adhan and without an Iqamah.'
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Jabir ibn Samurah)

questionEn: Where did the Prophet ﷺ customarily lead the Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha prayers in Madinah?
optionsEn: Always inside the closed courtyard of his home
On top of Mount Uhud
Outdoors in the open prayer ground (Musalla) outside the city's built area
Inside Masjid Quba every single year
explanationEn: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to go out on the days of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha to the open Musalla, unless excused by weather such as heavy rain.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri)

questionEn: How many extra Takbirs (Takbirat az-Zawa'id) are pronounced in the first and second rak'ahs of the Eid prayer according to the well-known Sunnah report from Aisha (RA) and Amr ibn Shu'ayb?
optionsEn: 3 in the first rak'ah and 3 in the second rak'ah
5 in the first rak'ah and 7 in the second rak'ah
10 in the first rak'ah and 10 in the second rak'ah
7 extra Takbirs in the first rak'ah (after Takbirat al-Ihram) and 5 in the second rak'ah (after standing up)
explanationEn: Amr ibn Awf, Aisha, and Abdullah ibn Amr reported that the Prophet ﷺ pronounced seven extra Takbirs in the first rak'ah before Qur'an recitation and five in the second rak'ah before recitation.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Jami' at-Tirmidhi (Narrated by Aisha RA)

questionEn: Which pairs of Surahs did the Prophet ﷺ frequently recite aloud during the two rak'ahs of the Eid prayers?
optionsEn: Surah Al-A'la & Surah Al-Ghashiyah, OR Surah Qaf & Surah Al-Qamar
Surah Al-Kafirun & Surah Al-Ikhlas exclusively
Surah Al-Baqarah & Surah Al Imran
Surah Yasin & Surah Al-Mulk
explanationEn: An-Nu'man ibn Bashir reported he recited Al-A'la and Al-Ghashiyah in Eid and Jumu'ah, while Abu Waqid al-Laythi reported the Prophet ﷺ reciting Surah Qaf and Surah Al-Qamar in Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by An-Nu'man ibn Bashir & Abu Waqid al-Laythi)

questionEn: What did Anas ibn Malik (RA) report regarding the Prophet's ﷺ breakfast before heading out to the Eid al-Fitr prayer?
optionsEn: He fasted until sunset on Eid al-Fitr
He would not go out on the morning of Eid al-Fitr until he had eaten an odd number of dates
He drank only saltwater before Eid al-Fitr
He ate meat from a sacrifice before Eid al-Fitr
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik narrated: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not go out on the morning of Eid al-Fitr until he had eaten some dates, and he used to eat an odd number of them.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Narrated by Anas ibn Malik)

questionEn: How did the Prophet's ﷺ eating habit on the morning of Eid al-Adha differ from Eid al-Fitr?
optionsEn: He ate seven dates before going to Eid al-Adha as well
He fasted for three consecutive days starting on Eid al-Adha
He delayed eating on Eid al-Adha until returning from prayer so he could eat from his sacrificed animal (Udhiyah)
He forbade eating any meat on the day of Eid al-Adha
explanationEn: Buraydah (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ did not go out on Eid al-Fitr without eating first, and did not eat on Eid al-Adha until he returned from the prayer (to eat from his sacrifice).
reference: Jami' at-Tirmidhi & Sunan Ibn Majah (Narrated by Buraydah)

questionEn: What Sunnah practice did Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) observe regarding the walking routes the Prophet ﷺ took on the day of Eid?
optionsEn: He always rode the fastest horse down the exact same alley
He refused to walk on public roads on Eid
He took three detours around the market before arriving
He took one route going to the Eid prayer ground and returned by a different route
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: 'On the day of Eid, the Prophet ﷺ used to vary his route'—going one way and returning another, so both streets and people could witness the joy and greetings of Eid.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah)

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ instruct Umm Atiyyah (RA) regarding women—including young women and even menstruating women—attending the Eid gathering?
optionsEn: Bring all women out to the Musalla to witness the goodness and Muslims' supplication, while menstruating women keep apart from the prayer area itself
Forbid all women from leaving their homes on Eid day
Require menstruating women to stand in the front prayer row
Allow only elderly women over seventy to attend
explanationEn: Umm Atiyyah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ commanded bringing out mature girls, secluded women, and menstruating women to witness the blessings and supplications of Eid, while menstruating women stayed clear of the prayer mat area.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Umm Atiyyah)

questionEn: According to Ibn Abbas (RA), what did the Prophet ﷺ do regarding voluntary prayers right before or right after the Eid prayer at the Musalla?
optionsEn: He prayed four rak'ahs before and four after at the Musalla
He prayed two rak'ahs of Eid alone, praying neither before nor after it at the prayer ground
He always prayed Tahiyyat al-Masjid in the open desert field
He prayed two rak'ahs of Witr right after Eid
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ came out on the day of Fitr, prayed two rak'ahs of Eid, and did not pray before it or after it (though upon returning home one may offer Duha/nafl).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Ibn Abbas)

questionEn: When Eid al-Fitr or Eid al-Adha falls on a Friday, what concession did the Prophet ﷺ grant to those who attend the morning Eid prayer in congregation?
optionsEn: Jumu'ah is completely abolished for everyone including the Imam
They are excused from Asr and Maghrib as well
Attending Jumu'ah becomes optional for those who prayed Eid (they may pray Dhuhr at home), though the Imam still holds Jumu'ah for whoever wishes
Both Eid and Jumu'ah are merged into a single four-rak'ah prayer
explanationEn: Zayd ibn Arqam and Abu Hurayrah narrated that when Eid coincided with Friday, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Two Eids have come together on this day of yours; whoever wishes, it suffices him for Jumu'ah, though we will hold Jumu'ah.'
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Sunan Ibn Majah (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah & Zayd ibn Arqam)

questionEn: When does the Takbir for Eid al-Fitr begin and end according to the Qur'anic command in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:185) and the practice of the Companions?
optionsEn: From the 1st of Ramadan until the 10th of Shawwal
Only during the five minutes after the Eid Khutbah
From Fajr of the 9th of Ramadan until sunset
From sunset on the eve of Eid (confirming the end of Ramadan) until the Imam comes out to lead the Eid prayer
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:185) links completing the fast to magnifying Allah ('wa litukabbirullaha 'ala ma hadakum'), so Takbir starts when the Shawwal crescent confirms Ramadan's completion and continues until the Eid prayer begins.
reference: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:185 & Sunan ad-Daraqutni (Practice of Ibn Umar)

questionEn: What is the well-known period for the restricted Takbir (Takbir Muqayyad) recited immediately after every obligatory prayer during Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: From Fajr on the Day of Arafah (9th Dhul-Hijjah) until Asr on the last Day of Tashreeq (13th Dhul-Hijjah)
Only on the morning of the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah
From the 1st of Dhul-Hijjah until the 5th of Dhul-Hijjah
Strictly between Maghrib and Isha on the 12th of Dhul-Hijjah
explanationEn: According to the authentic reports from Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Mas'ud, the restricted Takbir after obligatory prayers runs from Fajr of the Day of Arafah (9th) through Asr of the 13th of Dhul-Hijjah.
reference: Al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah & Al-Bayhaqi (Reports of Ali & Ibn Abbas)

questionEn: Which authentic wording of the Eid and Tashreeq Takbir was famously narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA)?
optionsEn: "SubhanAllah wa bihamdihi" repeated ten times
"Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illallah, wallahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, wa lillahil-hamd"
"Allahu Akbar" once followed by silence
"Astaghfirullah, Allahu Akbar, SubhanAllah"
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud used to proclaim: 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illallah, wallahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, wa lillahil-hamd' (some narrations repeat Allahu Akbar thrice at the beginning as well).
reference: Al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah (Authenticated from Ibn Mas'ud)

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ describe the Days of Tashreeq (the 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah) in Sahih Muslim?
optionsEn: Days of strict fasting and silence
Days when voluntary charity is forbidden
Days of eating, drinking, and the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah
Days reserved solely for staying indoors
explanationEn: Nubayshah al-Hudhali narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The Days of Tashreeq are days of eating, drinking, and remembering Allah.'

questionEn: Why is it Sunnah to pray Eid al-Adha slightly earlier in the morning than Eid al-Fitr?
optionsEn: Because Eid al-Adha has no Khutbah
Because the sun sets earlier in Dhul-Hijjah
So travelers can leave before noon
To give Muslims ample time after Eid al-Adha to perform their sacrifices, while delaying Eid al-Fitr slightly gives time to distribute Zakat al-Fitr
explanationEn: Jundub and Ibn Qudamah explain that Eid al-Adha is prayed early once the sun rises a spear's height so people can begin their Udhiyah sacrifices promptly, whereas Eid al-Fitr is delayed slightly so everyone can fulfill Zakat al-Fitr before prayer.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Yazid ibn Khumayr) & Al-Mughni

questionEn: What warm greeting did the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ commonly exchange with one another on the day of Eid?
optionsEn: "Taqabbalallahu minna wa minkum" (May Allah accept from us and from you)
"Ramadan Kareem" on Eid al-Adha
"La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah"
"As-salatu khayrun min an-nawm"
explanationEn: Jubayr ibn Nufayr reported that when the Companions met on the day of Eid, they would say to each other: 'Taqabbalallahu minna wa minka' (May Allah accept from us and from you).
reference: Fath al-Bari (Authenticated by Ibn Hajar from Jubayr ibn Nufayr)

questionEn: What is the Islamic legal classification of Salat al-Janazah (the funeral prayer over a deceased Muslim)?
optionsEn: Fard Ayn upon every Muslim worldwide individually
Fard Kifayah (a communal obligation—if enough Muslims perform it, the duty is lifted from the rest)
Strictly forbidden inside cities
Optional only for family members and never for neighbors
explanationEn: Washing, shrouding, praying Janazah over, and burying a deceased Muslim are communal obligations (Fard Kifayah): if a group fulfills them, the community is absolved; if all neglect them, all share sin.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Fiqh Consensus (Book of Funerals)

questionEn: How many Takbirs make up the standard structure of Salat al-Janazah, and does it contain bowing (ruku') or prostration (sujud)?
optionsEn: Two Takbirs with two prostrations
Five Takbirs with one bowing
Four Takbirs performed entirely standing, with neither bowing (ruku') nor prostration (sujud)
Seven Takbirs with three sittings
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ announced the death of An-Najashi (Negus), he lined up the companions and pronounced four Takbirs while standing—Salat al-Janazah has no ruku' and no sujud.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: What is recited immediately after the FIRST Takbir in Salat al-Janazah?
optionsEn: Durood Ibrahim (Salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ)
Surah Yasin in full
Only the final Taslim
Surah Al-Fatihah (after the opening Ta'awwudh/Bismillah)
explanationEn: Talhah ibn Abdullah ibn Awf narrated that he prayed Janazah behind Ibn Abbas, who recited Al-Fatihah aloud and then explained: 'I did so that you know it is the Sunnah.'

questionEn: What is recited after the SECOND Takbir in Salat al-Janazah?
optionsEn: Sending blessings (Salawat / Durood Ibrahim) upon the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
Ayatul Kursi three times
Du'a al-Qunut
Surah Al-Mulk
explanationEn: Abu Umamah ibn Sahl narrated from a Companion that the Sunnah in Janazah is to recite Al-Fatihah silently after the first Takbir, then send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ after the second Takbir.
reference: Sunan an-Nasa'i & Ash-Shafi'i's Al-Umm (Authenticated by Al-Albani)

questionEn: What is the central supplication recited after the THIRD Takbir in Salat al-Janazah?
optionsEn: Asking for rain and abundant crops
Sincere, heartfelt dua seeking Allah's forgiveness, mercy, and Paradise for the deceased (and all Muslims)
Reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas one hundred times
Standing in complete silence without making any dua
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ commanded: 'When you pray over the deceased, make sincere supplication for him,' teaching beautiful prayers like 'Allahummaghfir lahu warhamhu wa 'afihi wa'fu 'anhu...'
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Abu Hurayrah) & Sahih Muslim (Awf ibn Malik)

questionEn: In the famous Janazah dua narrated by Awf ibn Malik (RA), what purifying metaphors did the Prophet ﷺ use when asking Allah to cleanse the deceased's sins?
optionsEn: Wash them with river stones and desert sand
Melt their sins like wax under noon sunlight
Wash them with water, snow, and hail, and purify them from sins as a white garment is purified from filth
Hide their sins beneath deep ocean waves
explanationEn: Awf ibn Malik said the Prophet's ﷺ supplication ('Allahummaghfir lahu warhamhu... waghsilhu bil-ma'i wath-thalji wal-barad, wa naqqihi minal-khataya kama naqqaytath-thawbal-abyada minad-danas...') was so moving he wished he himself were that deceased person.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Awf ibn Malik)

questionEn: What happens after the FOURTH Takbir in Salat al-Janazah?
optionsEn: Everyone performs two prostrations on the ground
The Imam delivers a thirty-minute Khutbah
Everyone recites Surah Al-Baqarah
A brief pause or short general dua (such as 'Rabbana atina...' or 'Allahumma la tahrimna ajrahu...'), followed by the Taslim
explanationEn: After the fourth Takbir, one pauses briefly (and may offer a short dua such as 'Allahumma la tahrimna ajrahu wa la taftinna ba'dahu') and then concludes with the Taslim.
reference: Sunan an-Nasa'i & Sunan Abi Dawud (Narrated by Abu Umamah & Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: Where does the Imam stand in relation to the body during Salat al-Janazah according to the Prophetic Sunnah?
optionsEn: In line with the head of a male deceased, and in line with the middle (waist) of a female deceased
Always at the feet for both men and women
Behind the congregation facing away from the bier
At the middle for a man and at the head for a woman
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik and Samurah ibn Jundub narrated that the Prophet ﷺ stood aligned with the head of a male deceased and aligned with the middle of a female deceased.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Samurah ibn Jundub)

questionEn: According to Abu Hurayrah (RA), what massive reward equal to Mount Uhud awaits a believer who attends a funeral prayer (Janazah)?
optionsEn: One grain of silver
One Qirat (like Mount Uhud) for praying the Janazah, and two Qirats for staying until the burial is completed
Exemption from praying Isha that night
Three Qirats only for carrying the coffin
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ promised: 'Whoever attends a funeral until the prayer is offered over it has one Qirat, and whoever stays until it is buried has two Qirats.' Asked what two Qirats are, he replied: 'Like two great mountains (like Uhud).'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: How many rows of worshippers did the Prophet ﷺ specifically encourage forming in Salat al-Janazah, promising forgiveness/Paradise for the deceased?
optionsEn: Only one single long row
Seven rows facing opposite directions
Three rows (at least), for whoever has three rows of Muslims pray over him will be forgiven / granted Paradise
Twelve rows strictly
explanationEn: Malik ibn Hubayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'No Muslim dies and three rows of Muslims pray over him except that Paradise becomes assured for him (or he is forgiven),' so Malik would divide small gatherings into three rows.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Jami' at-Tirmidhi (Narrated by Malik ibn Hubayrah)

questionEn: What is Salat al-Gha'ib, exemplified when the Prophet ﷺ led the funeral prayer in Madinah for An-Najashi (Negus), the righteous king of Abyssinia?
optionsEn: A funeral prayer offered silently by a single person at midnight
A prayer offered before someone dies
A prayer offered over an empty grave dug a year later
A funeral prayer performed in absentia when the deceased died in another land (especially when no funeral prayer was prayed over them there)
explanationEn: When An-Najashi died in Abyssinia, the Prophet ﷺ informed the Companions on the very day he passed away, took them to the Musalla, lined them in rows, and led four Takbirs in absentia (Salat al-Gha'ib).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ learned that the humble Black woman (or man) who used to sweep Masjid an-Nabawi had passed away and been buried at night without informing him, what did he do?
optionsEn: He asked to be shown the grave, stood before it, and led Salat al-Janazah over the grave
He said it was too late to pray once someone is buried
He ordered the body to be dug up and washed again
He only made private dua inside his house without visiting the grave
explanationEn: Deeply caring for the mosque caretaker, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Show me her grave,' then went to it and prayed Salat al-Janazah over her grave—establishing the permissibility of praying Janazah at the grave for one who missed it.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: Is it permissible to perform Salat al-Janazah inside a mosque, or must it only be done outdoors?
optionsEn: It is strictly invalid if performed inside any mosque
It is permissible inside a mosque—Aisha (RA) reminded critics that the Prophet ﷺ prayed over Suhayl ibn Bayda inside the mosque
It may only be done inside a cemetery
It is only permitted on mosque rooftops
explanationEn: When some hesitated over praying for Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas in the mosque, Aisha (RA) corrected them: 'By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over the two sons of Bayda inside the mosque.'

questionEn: When praying Salat al-Janazah over a young child who died before puberty, what special meaning should the dua after the third Takbir express?
optionsEn: Asking Allah to forgive their major adult sins
Omitting the third Takbir completely
Asking Allah to make the child a precursor (faratan), a stored reward, and an accepted intercessor for their parents
Reciting Surah Al-Masad
explanationEn: Since young children are sinless, the Sunnah/salaf dua asks Allah to make the child a forerunner of reward and intercession for the parents ('Allahummaj'alhu lana faratan wa salafan wa ajran').
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Chapter Title citing Al-Hasan al-Basri) & Fiqh of Janazah

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ command believers to walk briskly (hurry without running recklessly) when carrying a funeral bier to the grave?
optionsEn: To avoid getting tired in the heat
Because slow walking invalidates the Janazah
To compete with other processions
If the deceased was righteous, it hastens them to the good awaiting them; if otherwise, it relieves the bearers of a heavy burden
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ explained: 'Hurry with the funeral bier; if it was righteous, it is good to which you are speeding it, and if it was otherwise, it is an evil you are putting off your necks.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse in Surah At-Tawbah (9:84) was revealed prohibiting the Prophet ﷺ from ever standing in funeral prayer over known disbelievers or exposed hypocrites?
optionsEn: "And do not pray [the funeral prayer] over any of them who has died—ever—and do not stand at his grave"
"Pray for them seventy times and they will be forgiven"
"Stand at every grave in Madinah every Friday"
"Only pray over those who paid the charity tax"
explanationEn: After the Prophet ﷺ prayed over Abdullah ibn Ubayy, Allah revealed Surah At-Tawbah (9:84): 'And do not pray over any of them who has died—ever—nor stand at his grave. Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger.'

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ deal with the martyrs slain on the battlefield of Uhud regarding washing, shrouding, and funeral rites?
optionsEn: He ordered every martyr to be bathed three times in musk
He ordered them buried in their blood-stained garments without washing them, noting their wounds will testify on the Day of Resurrection
He shipped their bodies back to Makkah
He cremated their armor and left them unburied
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ commanded regarding the martyrs of Uhud: 'Do not wash them, for every wound or drop of blood will smell of musk on the Day of Resurrection,' and he did not perform the standard Janazah over them (though some scholars allow praying over martyrs).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Musnad Ahmad (Narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah)

questionEn: If a Muslim joins Salat al-Janazah late after the Imam has already pronounced one or two Takbirs, how should they proceed?
optionsEn: Wait until the Imam finishes and walk away without praying
Join the Imam on the current Takbir, follow through to his Salam, and then quickly pronounce the missed Takbirs (with brief dua) before the bier is lifted
Stand quietly without ever saying Allahu Akbar
Perform two prostrations to make up the missed Takbirs
explanationEn: According to the majority of jurists, the latecomer joins the Imam immediately, follows whatever the Imam is reciting, and after the Imam's Taslim swiftly completes the missed Takbirs (or follows them consecutively if the body is about to be carried away).
reference: Al-Mughni & Majmu' Fatawa (Fiqh of Joining Janazah Late)

questionEn: Which Companion narrated that he used to raise his hands with every single one of the four Takbirs in Salat al-Janazah, a practice followed by several major jurists?
optionsEn: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA)
Salman al-Farisi (RA)
Abdullah ibn Umar (RA)
Bilal ibn Rabah (RA)
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) raised his hands with all four Takbirs of Salat al-Janazah (and Ibn Abbas is also reported to have raised his hands on the first and subsequent Takbirs), which is Sunnah in the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools (while Hanafis and Malikis raise only on the first).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Mu'allaq report from Ibn Umar) & Sunan al-Bayhaqi

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when someone commits suicide—did he personally lead the prayer as a deterrent while still allowing other Muslims to pray Janazah over them?
optionsEn: He declared them completely outside Islam forever and forbade anyone to bury them
He led the prayer himself with extra celebrations
He refused to bury the person in any ground
He declined to lead it himself as a stern warning against suicide, while letting the Companions pray Janazah over the person
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Samurah narrated that a man killed himself with broad arrowheads and the Prophet ﷺ did not personally pray over him (as a warning to the community), while allowing the Muslims to offer the Janazah since suicide is a major sin, not disbelief.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Jabir ibn Samurah)

questionEn: What special question did the Prophet ﷺ used to ask before praying Salat al-Janazah over a deceased person in early Madinah, until Allah later granted the Muslim treasury wealth?
optionsEn: "Did he leave behind any unpaid debt?" (And once Allah enriched the treasury, the Prophet ﷺ paid off the deceased's debts himself)
"How many camels did he own?"
"Was he born in Makkah?"
"Did he memorize five Juz of Qur'an?"
explanationEn: Initially, the Prophet ﷺ asked whether a deceased person left unpaid debts—telling the companions to pray over him if debts remained unpaid—until Allah opened conquests and wealth, whereupon he declared himself closer to every believer and paid their debts before praying over them.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Kawthar (108:2)—'So pray to your Lord and sacrifice'—connect directly to Eid al-Adha according to many Qur'an commentators?
optionsEn: It refers only to fasting in Rajab
It instructs believers to offer the Eid al-Adha prayer first and then offer the sacrificial animal (Udhiyah/Nahr) solely for Allah
It commands sacrificing before sunrise prior to Eid prayer
It applies only to the Tahajjud prayer
explanationEn: Many early exegetes (including Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Qatadah) explained 'Fasalli li-Rabbika wanhar' as offering the Eid prayer for your Lord and then slaughtering the Udhiyah sacrifice afterward.
reference: Tafsir Ibn Kathir on Surah Al-Kawthar 108:2 & Sahih al-Bukhari (Al-Bara' ibn Azib)

questionEn: What ruling did Al-Bara' ibn Azib (RA) report from the Prophet's ﷺ Eid al-Adha Khutbah about someone who slaughtered their sacrificial animal BEFORE the Eid prayer?
optionsEn: Their sacrifice counts double
It counts as both Udhiyah and Zakat al-Fitr
It is merely ordinary meat for their family and does not count as the Eid sacrifice (Nusuk); they must sacrifice another afterward
They are excused from praying Eid al-Adha
explanationEn: When Abu Burdah slaughtered before the Eid prayer, the Prophet ﷺ told him: 'Your sheep is only meat,' establishing that the valid time for Udhiyah begins only after the Eid prayer.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Al-Bara' ibn Azib)

questionEn: What is the ruling on using loud Takbir during the walk to the Eid Musalla on the morning of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha?
optionsEn: It is strictly forbidden to raise the voice outdoors
Only children under ten may recite Takbir aloud
It must be whispered silently inside one's cloak
It is a praised Sunnah for men to recite the Takbir aloud on the way to the Eid prayer ground until the prayer starts
explanationEn: Ibn Umar used to proclaim the Takbir aloud while walking to the Eid prayer ground on both Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha until the Imam arrived, reviving an open display of gratitude and Tawhid.
reference: Sunan ad-Daraqutni & Sahih al-Bukhari (Chapter on Takbir to the Musalla)

questionEn: What special permission regarding clothing and adornment applies to Muslims on Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha?
optionsEn: Taking Ghusl, applying perfume (for men), and wearing one's finest clean garments out of gratitude for Allah's favor
Wearing torn, dusty rags as on Istisqa'
Wearing only dark black garments by obligation
Fasting throughout both Eid days in celebration
explanationEn: Ibn Umar and Jabir reported that the Prophet ﷺ kept a special fine cloak to wear on the two Eids and Friday, and Ibn Abbas and Nafi' reported that Ibn Umar bathed (took Ghusl) on Eid morning before going out.
reference: Al-Muwatta of Imam Malik & Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah

questionEn: Which two days of the entire Islamic year did the Prophet ﷺ strictly forbid Muslims from fasting?
optionsEn: Monday and Thursday
The Day of Eid al-Fitr (1st Shawwal) and the Day of Eid al-Adha (10th Dhul-Hijjah)
The Day of Arafah and the Day of Ashura
The 13th and 14th of Sha'ban
explanationEn: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated that the Prophet ﷺ forbade fasting on two days: the day of Fitr (breaking Ramadan's fast) and the day of Adha (eating from the sacrifice).
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri)

questionEn: If a person arrives late to the Eid prayer and misses one rak'ah or the entire congregation, how do scholars advise making it up?
optionsEn: They cannot pray Eid at all once missed
They must fast three days as compensation
They pray two rak'ahs in the manner of Eid (with the extra Takbirs according to the majority, or two standard rak'ahs per some scholars)
They pray four rak'ahs silently before Dhuhr
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik, when he missed the Eid prayer in Basra, gathered his family and freedmen and had his servant pray two rak'ahs with them just like the Eid prayer of the townspeople.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Ta'liq report of Anas ibn Malik)

questionEn: During the Eid prayer's extra Takbirs, how did the Companions (such as Ibn Umar and Ata') handle what to say briefly between each Takbir?
optionsEn: They recited the entire Surah Al-Fatihah between each Takbir
They sat down after every single Takbir
They said 'Allahu Akbar' while bowing seven times
They paused briefly praising Allah, glorifying Him, and sending peace upon the Prophet ﷺ (e.g., SubhanAllah walhamdulillah wa la ilaha illallah wallahu Akbar)
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud and subsequent scholars (like Imam Ahmad and Imam ash-Shafi'i) explained that between every two extra Takbirs of Eid, one pauses for the duration of a short verse to praise and glorify Allah and send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ.
reference: Sunan al-Bayhaqi (Report of Ibn Mas'ud) & Al-Mughni

questionEn: In Salat al-Janazah, why does the Sunnah emphasize forming straight rows and gathering a large number of pious believers (e.g. forty or a hundred) to pray?
optionsEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ promised that when forty (or one hundred) sincere Muslims who associate nothing with Allah pray over a deceased Muslim, Allah accepts their intercession for him
Because fewer than forty prayers are invalid
To make the grave deeper
So each person only needs to say one Takbir
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas narrated: 'No Muslim dies and forty men who associate nothing with Allah stand over his funeral prayer except that Allah accepts their intercession for him' (and Aisha narrated similarly for one hundred).
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Ibn Abbas & Aisha RA)

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach about mourning and wailing loudly (Niyahah) vs shedding quiet tears of mercy at a funeral?
optionsEn: Even quiet tears are strictly forbidden at a funeral
Quiet weeping comes from mercy in the heart (which the Prophet ﷺ himself showed at his son Ibrahim's death), whereas wailing loudly, slapping cheeks, and tearing garments are forbidden
Slapping cheeks is encouraged to show loyalty
One must laugh throughout a funeral
explanationEn: When his son Ibrahim passed away, the Prophet's ﷺ eyes shed tears and he said: 'The eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, yet we say nothing except what pleases our Lord'—while sternly prohibiting screaming, tearing clothes, and hitting cheeks.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Anas & Ibn Mas'ud)

questionEn: What is the ruling on praying Salat al-Janazah over a stillborn fetus vs a newborn baby who cried or showed clear signs of life at birth?
optionsEn: Neither receives any burial or prayer
Janazah is prayed only after a child reaches age seven

If the baby showed clear signs of life (like crying) before passing away, it is named, washed, shrouded, and prayed over with full Janazah; if stillborn before 4 months, it is buried respectfully without Janazah (with scholarly detail after 4 months)
Both receive a seven-Takbir prayer
explanationEn: Jabir and Al-Mughirah reported from the Prophet ﷺ: 'When a newborn cries (is born alive), prayer is offered over it and it inherits'—so signs of life mandate full Janazah, whereas an early miscarriage is wrapped cleanly and buried respectfully.
reference: Jami' at-Tirmidhi & Sunan Ibn Majah (Narrated by Jabir)

questionEn: When the funeral prayer ends and the deceased is placed in the grave, what did the Prophet ﷺ tell the Companions to stand at the graveside and do immediately after burial?
optionsEn: Walk away silently without making any supplication
Recite the Adhan inside the grave
Light candles around the headstone
Ask Allah to forgive the deceased and grant them firmness (Tathbit), for they are now being questioned
explanationEn: Uthman ibn Affan narrated that once a burial finished, the Prophet ﷺ would stand by the grave and say: 'Seek forgiveness for your brother and ask for his steadfastness, for now he is being questioned.'
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Narrated by Uthman ibn Affan)

questionEn: How should Muslims respond when a funeral procession passes by them in the street, according to the Prophet's ﷺ practice?
optionsEn: Stand up in respect (or reflect silently on death) until it passes or is set down—and follow it if able
Cross the street running in the opposite direction
Clap hands loudly
Turn their backs and shout
explanationEn: Amir ibn Rabi'ah and Jabir reported that the Prophet ﷺ stood up for a passing funeral procession (even when it belonged to a non-Muslim, saying 'Is it not a soul?'), teaching profound respect for the sanctity of the human soul and remembrance of the Hereafter.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Amir ibn Rabi'ah & Jabir)

questionEn: In the opening verses of Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:1–2), what is the very first quality of the believers whom Allah declares have attained true success?
optionsEn: Those who in their prayer have Khushu' (humble submissiveness and focused devotion)
Those who accumulate the largest farms
Those who travel across seven seas
Those who recite the fastest during prayer
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:1–2) opens: 'Certainly will the believers have succeeded: they who are during their prayer humbly submissive (khashi'un).'

questionEn: What does the spiritual quality of Khushu' in Salah encompass according to Qur'anic commentators like Ibn Rajab and Ibn Kathir?
optionsEn: Singing verses loudly with theatrical gestures
Stillness and humility of the heart before Allah's majesty, reflected in calm, attentive limbs and lowered gaze
Closing one's eyes throughout every prayer
Rushing through postures to finish quickly
explanationEn: Khushu' is anchored in the heart—feeling awe, tenderness, and total attentiveness toward Allah—which naturally produces physical calmness, stillness, and reverent postures.

questionEn: How did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ define Ihsan (spiritual excellence) in the famous Hadith of Jibril—the pinnacle of presence during Salah?
optionsEn: Praying only when other people are watching
Memorizing long books of poetry
"To worship Allah as though you see Him; and even though you do not see Him, know that He sees you"
Never making any mistakes in Arabic grammar
explanationEn: In Hadith Jibril, the Prophet ﷺ defined Ihsan as worshipping Allah with the vivid awareness that you stand directly before Him, and knowing with certainty that He sees every movement of your heart and limbs.

questionEn: What unforgettable advice on cultivating Khushu' did the Prophet ﷺ give to Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (RA) when asked for brief, life-changing counsel?
optionsEn: "Never pray more than three minutes"
"Only pray when you feel joyful"
"Think about your business while reciting"
"When you stand up for your prayer, pray the prayer of one bidding farewell (Salat Muwaddi')"
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ advised: 'When you stand to pray, pray as though it is your farewell prayer'—because imagining this might be one's final meeting with Allah transforms distraction into deep sincerity.
reference: Sunan Ibn Majah & Musnad Ahmad (Narrated by Abu Ayyub al-Ansari)

questionEn: What tender words did the Prophet ﷺ address to Bilal (RA) when prayer time arrived, revealing how Salah brought relief to his soul?
optionsEn: "O Bilal, call the prayer and give us comfort by it (Arihna biha)"
"O Bilal, let us finish this chore quickly"
"O Bilal, skip the call today so we can rest"
"O Bilal, make the Adhan silent"
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ used to say: 'O Bilal, call the Iqamah for prayer and bring us comfort/tranquility through it,' showing that Salah is a sanctuary of peace rather than a burden.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Musnad Ahmad (Authenticated from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd)

questionEn: In Sunan an-Nasa'i, alongside pleasant fragrance and righteous wives, where did the Prophet ﷺ declare 'the coolness (joy) of my eyes' was placed?
optionsEn: In accumulating silver
In Salah (prayer)
In building tall palaces
In winning debates
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Made beloved to me from your world are women and perfume, and the coolness of my eyes was placed in prayer (Salah).'
reference: Sunan an-Nasa'i & Musnad Ahmad (Narrated by Anas ibn Malik)

questionEn: What stern warning did the Prophet ﷺ issue regarding worshippers who lift their gaze upward toward the sky during Salah?
optionsEn: It doubles the reward of recitation
It is recommended during Dhuhr only
They must desist from raising their eyes toward the sky in prayer, lest their sight be snatched away (or not return to them)
It only applies when praying outdoors
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik reported that the Prophet ﷺ warned sternly: 'What is the matter with people who raise their eyes toward the sky during their prayer? Let them stop doing so, or their sight will surely be snatched away.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Anas & Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: Where did the Prophet ﷺ direct his gaze while standing in prayer, according to the narrations of Aisha (RA) and Ibn Abbas?
optionsEn: Directly at the ceiling corners
Sideways toward neighbors' feet
Tightly shut eyelids at all times
Downward toward the place of his prostration (sujud)
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ entered the Kaaba to pray, his gaze did not leave the spot of his prostration until he exited, teaching worshippers to keep their eyes lowered toward their prostration spot (and toward the index finger during Tashahhud).
reference: Al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim & Sunan al-Bayhaqi (Narrated by Aisha RA)

questionEn: What happens between Allah and His servant during prayer as long as the servant does not glance or turn away, according to Sunan Abi Dawud and At-Tirmidhi?
optionsEn: Allah keeps His Face turned toward the servant in prayer until the servant turns away
Angels leave the room after Al-Fatihah
The prayer ends automatically after two minutes
Only the Imam receives Allah's attention
explanationEn: Abu Dharr narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah continues to turn His Face toward His servant while he is in prayer so long as he does not turn away; when he turns away, Allah turns away from him.'
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Sunan an-Nasa'i (Narrated by Abu Dharr)

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ describe the 'turning away' (iltifat) that a person does during Salah when Aisha (RA) asked him about glancing around?
optionsEn: A harmless habit that adds concentration
"It is a snatching away (ikhtilas) by which Satan steals from the servant's prayer"
A Sunnah of the travelers
A cure for drowsiness
explanationEn: When Aisha (RA) asked about glancing around in prayer, the Prophet ﷺ replied: 'It is something that Satan snatches away from the servant's prayer.'

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ prohibit standing in prayer when dinner is served or while urgently needing to relieve oneself (al-akhbathan)?
optionsEn: Because food spoils during five minutes of prayer
Because Wudu is only valid on an empty stomach
Because physical discomfort or craving steals the heart's focus and Khushu' away from standing before Allah
Because mosques prohibit eating at any time
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) narrated: 'There is no [complete] prayer when food is served, nor while resisting the two urges (urine or stool),' teaching believers to clear pressing bodily distractions so the heart is free for Khushu'.

questionEn: When Uthman ibn Abi al-As complained to the Prophet ﷺ that Satan came between him and his prayer and confused his recitation, what did the Prophet ﷺ identify and prescribe?
optionsEn: Stop praying for a month until thoughts settle
Shout loudly to drown out thoughts
Repeat Wudu ten times before every rak'ah
He identified that devil as 'Khinzab' and told him: 'Seek refuge with Allah from him, and spit lightly dryly to your left three times'
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ named that distracting devil 'Khinzab' and taught Uthman: 'When you sense him, seek refuge in Allah from him and spit lightly (dry puff) to your left three times.' Uthman did so, and Allah removed it from him.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Uthman ibn Abi al-As)

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ call the worst kind of thief among people?
optionsEn: "The one who steals from his own prayer"—by failing to complete its bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujud) with tranquility
Someone who takes sandals from the mosque door
Someone who forgets to bring a prayer mat
A merchant who arrives late to Jumu'ah
explanationEn: Abu Qatadah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The worst thief among people is the one who steals from his prayer.' Asked how one steals from prayer, he replied: 'He does not perfect its bowing and its prostration.'
reference: Musnad Ahmad & Sahih Ibn Hibban (Narrated by Abu Qatadah)

questionEn: When a man prayed hurriedly before the Prophet ﷺ and was told thrice 'Go back and pray, for you have not prayed,' what essential pillar of Khushu' did the Prophet ﷺ teach him?
optionsEn: Reciting only the longest Surahs
Tranquility and stillness (Tuma'ninah) in every posture—standing, bowing, rising upright, prostrating, and sitting between prostrations
Holding one's breath during ruku'
Skipping Tashahhud to save time
explanationEn: In the Hadith of 'the one who prayed poorly' (Al-Musi' fi Salatihi), the Prophet ﷺ repeatedly commanded: 'Bow until you feel at ease (tatma'inna) in bowing... rise until you stand straight... prostrate until you feel at ease in prostration.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: Why does the Sunnah instruct a solitary worshipper or Imam to place a Sutrah (barrier) right in front of them before praying?
optionsEn: To mark private ownership of that mosque carpet forever
To lean against it whenever tired
To shield one's visual focus and prevent anyone from passing directly in front of the praying person
To replace the Qibla direction
explanationEn: Praying close to a Sutrah (like a pillar, wall, chair, or object at least a saddle-back's height) guards visual focus (Khushu') and deters passersby from cutting across the worshipper's space.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Sa'id & Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah)

questionEn: What severe warning did the Prophet ﷺ give to someone who walks directly in front of a person who is praying?
optionsEn: They must pay one gold dinar
Their shoes become impure
They lose one voluntary fast
If the passerby knew the gravity of the sin upon him, standing still for forty (days/months/years) would be better for him than passing in front
explanationEn: Abu Juhaym narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'If the one who passes in front of a praying person knew what [sin] is upon him, waiting for forty would be better for him than passing in front of him.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Juhaym)

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Baqarah (2:45–46) describe why Salah feels easy and uplifting to the humble (Al-Khashi'in), while feeling heavy to others?
optionsEn: Because the humble know with certainty that they will meet their Lord and that to Him they will return
Because the humble pray fewer daily prayers
Because the humble never face hardships in life
Because the humble only pray when wealthy
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:45–46) states: 'Seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive—who are certain that they will meet their Lord and that they will return to Him.'

questionEn: Which distracting posture—placing one's hands on the hips (Ikhtisar)—did the Prophet ﷺ specifically forbid during prayer?
optionsEn: Folding the right hand over the left on the chest
Resting the hands on the waist/hips (Ikhtisar) while standing in prayer
Placing palms flat on the knees during ruku'
Pointing the index finger in Tashahhud
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ forbade a person from praying with his hands on his hips (mutakhasiran), which scholars note resembles arrogance or the posture of those punished/resting casually.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: When Mu'ayqib (RA) asked the Prophet ﷺ about smoothing pebbles/gravel on the prayer spot while praying, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
optionsEn: "Smooth the pebbles continuously throughout every rak'ah"
"Never pray on natural ground"
"Do not wipe them while praying; if you must, then only once"
"Collect seven pebbles in your pocket"
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ discouraged unnecessary fidgeting with pebbles in Salah, telling Mu'ayqib: 'If you must level them, then just once'—protecting stillness and Khushu'.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Mu'ayqib)

questionEn: According to Ammar ibn Yasir (RA), how much of a person's prayer is actually recorded as reward for them when they finish?
optionsEn: Always 100% regardless of absent-mindedness
Only the portion recited aloud
None at all unless they cry continuously
Only the portion of it in which they were mindful and attentive (sometimes a tenth, a ninth, an eighth... up to half or full)
explanationEn: Ammar ibn Yasir heard the Prophet ﷺ say: 'A man finishes his prayer and nothing is written for him except a tenth of it, a ninth, an eighth, a seventh, a sixth, a fifth, a fourth, a third, or half of it'—meaning according to his mindfulness.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Musnad Ahmad (Narrated by Ammar ibn Yasir)

questionEn: Before saying Taslim at the end of Tashahhud, which FOUR things did the Prophet ﷺ command believers to seek Allah's refuge from?
optionsEn: Punishment of Hellfire, punishment of the grave, trials of life and death, and the evil trial of Al-Masih ad-Dajjal
Poverty, rainy weather, long journeys, and forgetfulness
Cold winters, hot summers, hunger, and thirst
Sickness, old age, sleeplessness, and debt only
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah narrated: 'When one of you finishes the final Tashahhud, let him seek refuge with Allah from four things: from the punishment of Hell, the punishment of the grave, the trials of life and death, and the evil of the trial of the False Messiah (Ad-Dajjal).'

questionEn: Which heartfelt dua for forgiveness did the Prophet ﷺ teach Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA) to recite inside his prayer before Salam?
optionsEn: "Allahumma barik lana fi Rajab wa Sha'ban..."
"Allahumma inni zalamtu nafsi zulman kathiran, wa la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa Anta, faghfir li maghfiratan min 'indika warhamni..."
"Subhana Rabbika Rabbil-'izzati 'amma yasifun..."
"Bismillahi tawakkaltu 'alallah..."
explanationEn: When Abu Bakr asked for a dua to recite in his prayer, the Prophet ﷺ taught him: 'O Allah, indeed I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins except You; so grant me forgiveness from Yourself and have mercy upon me, for You are the Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Bakr as-Siddiq)

questionEn: Holding Mu'adh ibn Jabal's (RA) hand and declaring 'By Allah, I love you,' what lifelong dua did the Prophet ﷺ advise him never to omit at the end (dubur) of every prayer?
optionsEn: "Allahumma urzuqni malan kathira"
"Allahumma qini sharra nafsiy"
"Allahumma a'inni 'ala dhikrika, wa shukrika, wa husni 'ibadatik" (O Allah, help me to remember You, thank You, and worship You well)
"Allahumma ahlikil-a'da'"
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ earnestly advised Mu'adh: 'Do not leave out saying at the end of every prayer: O Allah, assist me in remembering You, being grateful to You, and worshipping You in excellence.'
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Sunan an-Nasa'i (Narrated by Mu'adh ibn Jabal)

questionEn: What are the very first words the Prophet ﷺ uttered immediately after concluding an obligatory prayer with Taslim, repeated three times?
optionsEn: "SubhanAllah" three times
"Allahu Akbar" three times
"La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah" three times
"Astaghfirullah" (I seek Allah's forgiveness) three times
explanationEn: Thawban (RA) narrated that whenever the Prophet ﷺ finished his prayer, he would seek forgiveness three times ('Astaghfirullah, Astaghfirullah, Astaghfirullah')—acknowledging any shortcomings even after worship—before reciting 'Allahumma antas-Salam...'

questionEn: Immediately following the three-fold Istighfar after Salam, what authentic praise celebrating peace and majesty did the Prophet ﷺ recite?
optionsEn: "Allahumma Antas-Salam wa minkas-Salam, tabarakta ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram"
"Alhamdulillahil-ladhi at'amana wa saqana"
"Sami'Allahu liman hamidah, Rabbana wa lakal-hamd"
"Subhana man la yanam wa la yashu"
explanationEn: Right after saying Astaghfirullah three times, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'O Allah, You are Peace and from You comes peace; Blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor.'
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Thawban & Aisha RA)

questionEn: According to Aisha (RA), how long did the Prophet ﷺ remain sitting facing the Qibla after saying Taslim when leading the congregation, before turning to face the people?
optionsEn: He remained facing the Qibla for half an hour silently
Only long enough to recite 'Allahumma Antas-Salam wa minkas-Salam, tabarakta ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram'
He turned around before saying Taslim
He walked out immediately without sitting
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) narrated that once the Prophet ﷺ gave Salam, he sat facing the Qibla only long enough to say 'Allahumma Antas-Salam wa minkas-Salam, tabarakta Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram,' and then turned to face the congregation.

questionEn: In the post-Salah dhikr narrated by Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah (RA), after testifying 'La ilaha illallah wahdahu la sharika lah...', what powerful affirmation about Allah's decree follows?
optionsEn: "Allahumma zidni 'ilman wa fahma"
"Rabbana la tuzigh qulubana"
"Allahumma la mani'a lima a'tayta, wa la mu'tiya lima mana'ta, wa la yanfa'u dhal-jaddi minkal-jadd"
"Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal-wakil"
explanationEn: After every obligatory prayer, the Prophet ﷺ recited: 'O Allah, none can withhold what You give, and none can give what You withhold, and the wealth/fortune of a wealthy person cannot benefit him against You.'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah)

questionEn: What does the phrase 'La yanfa'u dhal-jaddi minkal-jadd' mean in the authentic post-Salah dhikr?
optionsEn: Grandparents cannot pray for grandchildren
Hard work is unnecessary after prayer
Only the oldest person in the mosque is rewarded
No person's worldly fortune, status, or power can benefit or protect them from Allah—only faith and righteous deeds benefit
explanationEn: In Arabic, 'al-jadd' here means worldly wealth, status, and good fortune; the believer affirms that no privilege or status protects anyone from Allah's decree except obedience to Him.

questionEn: What famous Tasbih combination—often called 'Tasbih Fatimi'—did the Prophet ﷺ teach for recitation after every obligatory prayer, promising forgiveness of sins even if like the foam of the sea?
optionsEn: 33 times SubhanAllah, 33 times Alhamdulillah, 33 times Allahu Akbar, completed to 100 with 'La ilaha illallah wahdahu la sharika lah...'
100 times SubhanAllah only
10 times Alhamdulillah and 90 times Astaghfirullah
50 times Allahu Akbar and 50 times Ameen
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah narrated that whoever says SubhanAllah 33 times, Alhamdulillah 33 times, and Allahu Akbar 33 times (making 99), and completes the hundredth with 'La ilaha illallah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir,' his sins will be forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea.

questionEn: Why is the 33-33-34 (or 33-33-33+1) Tasbih practice also fondly known as 'Tasbih Fatimi'?
optionsEn: Because it was revealed only in Surah Fatir
Because when Fatimah (RA) asked the Prophet ﷺ for a household helper due to exhausting chores, he gave her and Ali (RA) this Tasbih before sleep as something far better than a servant
Because Fatimah (RA) invented it after the Prophet's ﷺ passing
Because it is only recited by women
explanationEn: When Fatimah (RA) showed calluses from grinding grain and asked for a servant, the Prophet ﷺ visited her and Ali (RA) at bedtime and taught them to say SubhanAllah 33, Alhamdulillah 33, and Allahu Akbar 34 times—better for them than a servant. (A similar 33/33/33+1 formula is also taught after every Fard prayer.)
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Ali ibn Abi Talib)
