questionEn: Besides the 33-33-33+1 formula, what alternative authentic Tasbih count did Ka'b ibn Ujrah (RA) report from the Prophet ﷺ for after obligatory prayers ('mu'aqqibat')?
optionsEn: 5 times each
12 times each
33 SubhanAllah, 33 Alhamdulillah, and 34 Allahu Akbar (total 100)—or 25 of each including 'La ilaha illallah'
70 times SubhanAllah only
explanationEn: Ka'b ibn Ujrah narrated: 'There are follow-up phrases (mu'aqqibat) after every prescribed prayer whose reciter will never be disappointed: 33 SubhanAllah, 33 Alhamdulillah, and 34 Allahu Akbar.' Another narration in An-Nasa'i/At-Tirmidhi mentions 25 each of those three plus 'La ilaha illallah'.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Ka'b ibn Ujrah) & Sunan an-Nasa'i (Zayd ibn Thabit)

questionEn: When poor Companions lamented that wealthy Muslims gave charity they could not afford, how did the Prophet ﷺ comfort them regarding the post-Salah Tasbih?
optionsEn: He told them to borrow money to give charity
He told them prayer without charity is rejected
He advised them to stop working
He taught them to say SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, and Allahu Akbar 33 times after every prayer—a charity that lets them catch up with and surpass others
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, Abu Hurayrah narrated that the poor emigrants received this Tasbih counsel from the Prophet ﷺ as a spiritual charity equalizing them with wealthy believers.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: How did Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) witness the Prophet ﷺ counting his post-Salah Tasbih, and what reason did the Prophet ﷺ give to Yusayrah (RA) for counting on the fingers?
optionsEn: He counted on his right hand's fingers, explaining that the fingers will be questioned and made to speak (witness on Judgment Day)
He forbade using fingers and required wooden beads
He only counted silently without moving any finger
He used pebbles stacked on his knees
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Amr saw the Prophet ﷺ counting Tasbih on his right hand, and the Prophet ﷺ advised Yusayrah and the women: 'Keep to Tasbih, Tahlil, and Taqdis, and count them on the fingertips, for they will be questioned and made to speak.'
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Jami' at-Tirmidhi (Narrated by Yusayrah & Abdullah ibn Amr)

questionEn: According to Abu Umamah al-Bahili (RA), what extraordinary reward awaits the Muslim who recites Ayatul Kursi (Al-Baqarah 2:255) immediately after every obligatory prayer?
optionsEn: Guaranteed worldly wealth within forty days
Nothing stands between them and entering Paradise except death
They are excused from fasting Ramadan
Their prayer counts as Jumu'ah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ promised: 'Whoever recites Ayatul Kursi after every prescribed (obligatory) prayer, nothing prevents him from entering Paradise except that he dies.'
reference: Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra & At-Tabarani (Authenticated by Al-Albani & Ibn Hibban)

questionEn: What did Uqbah ibn Amir (RA) report that the Prophet ﷺ commanded him to recite immediately after every prayer?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Kahf in full
Surah Al-Fatihah seven times
Al-Mu'awwidhat (the protecting Surahs: Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, and An-Nas)
Only the first five verses of Surah Al-Baqarah
explanationEn: Uqbah ibn Amir narrated: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to recite Al-Mu'awwidhat (Surah Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, and An-Nas) at the end of every prayer' (and other narrations specify three times each after Fajr and Maghrib).
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud & Jami' at-Tirmidhi (Narrated by Uqbah ibn Amir)

questionEn: After which two daily obligatory prayers did the Prophet ﷺ teach reciting 'La ilaha illallah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu, yuhyi wa yumit, wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir' TEN times before changing one's seated posture or speaking?
optionsEn: Dhuhr and Asr
Asr and Isha
Only Jumu'ah
Fajr and Maghrib
explanationEn: Abu Dharr and Abdur-Rahman ibn Ghanm narrated that whoever recites this Tahlil ten times after Fajr and Maghrib before unfolding his legs or speaking has ten good deeds written, ten sins erased, is raised ten degrees, and is protected from every disliked harm and Satan until evening/morning.
reference: Jami' at-Tirmidhi & Musnad Ahmad (Narrated by Abu Dharr & Umarah ibn Shabib)

questionEn: What short dua did Umm Salamah (RA) report the Prophet ﷺ used to say right after the Taslim of the Fajr prayer?
optionsEn: "Allahumma inni as'aluka 'ilman nafi'an, wa rizqan tayyiban, wa 'amalan mutaqabbalan" (Beneficial knowledge, pure provision, and accepted deeds)
"Allahumma barik lana fi laylatina"
"SubhanAllah al-Azim wa bihamdihi"
"Rabbighfir li wa tub 'alayya"
explanationEn: Umm Salamah (RA) narrated that when the Prophet ﷺ finished Fajr prayer and said Salam, he would supplicate: 'O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good and pure provision, and deeds that are accepted.'
reference: Sunan Ibn Majah & Musnad Ahmad (Narrated by Umm Salamah)

questionEn: According to Anas ibn Malik (RA) in Jami' at-Tirmidhi, what tremendous reward is written for one who prays Fajr in congregation, sits remembering Allah until sunrise, and then prays two rak'ahs (Salat al-Ishraq)?
optionsEn: Equal to one day of voluntary charity
The reward of a complete, complete, complete Hajj and Umrah (without diminishing actual Hajj obligations)
Equal to freeing one sheep
Exemption from Dhuhr prayer that day
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever prays Fajr in congregation, then sits remembering Allah until the sun rises, then prays two rak'ahs, will have a reward like that of a Hajj and an Umrah—complete, complete, complete.'
reference: Jami' at-Tirmidhi (Narrated by Anas ibn Malik)

questionEn: How long should a worshipper wait after the sun rises before praying the two rak'ahs of Salat al-Ishraq (early Duha)?
optionsEn: Pray immediately the exact second the sun's top edge touches the horizon
Wait until two hours before Asr
Wait roughly 15–20 minutes after sunrise until the sun has risen the height of a spear above the horizon
Wait until after Zawal (midday)
explanationEn: Prayer is prohibited while the sun is actively rising until it climbs the height of a spear (~15–20 minutes after sunrise), which marks the valid entrance of Ishraq / early Duha.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Amr ibn Abasah & Uqbah ibn Amir)

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when someone sits in their prayer spot after an obligatory prayer without breaking Wudu, continuing in remembrance or waiting for the next prayer?
optionsEn: They lose half the reward of their prayer
They are prohibited from sitting on the prayer mat after Salam
They must stand up within five seconds
The angels continue praying for them: 'O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, have mercy on him,' as long as they remain in Wudu without harming anyone
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah narrated that the angels continuously supplicate for a believer who stays in their place of prayer in a state of Wudu: 'O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, have mercy on him!'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)

questionEn: What did Al-Bara' ibn Azib (RA) report hearing the Prophet ﷺ supplicate whenever the Prophet ﷺ turned from the Qibla toward his Companions after concluding a prayer?
optionsEn: "Rabbi qini 'adhabaka yawma tab'athu (or tajma'u) 'ibadak" (My Lord, protect me from Your punishment on the Day You resurrect Your servants)
"Allahumma a'tini al-mal"
"SubhanAllah walhamdulillah" once
"Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim" aloud
explanationEn: Al-Bara' ibn Azib narrated: 'When we prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we loved to be on his right side so he would turn toward us, and I heard him say: "Rabbi qini 'adhabaka yawma tab'athu 'ibadak."'
reference: Sahih Muslim (Narrated by Al-Bara' ibn Azib)
